view.rationale: Reported Q3 results exceeded expectations on both sales and margins, with clear productivity/volume recovery. Q4 margin and sales growth guidance is broadly in-line on the direction (mid-teen path) despite a step-down in Q4 incremental margin, which tempers upside, leading to a moderately positive expected reaction.

No pre-release consensus numbers or reported revenue/EPS levels were provided, but management messaging suggests a pressured consumer backdrop (flat dollars in NAR, modest gross margin pressure, pet shipment timing/inventory headwinds) that likely tempers near-term expectations; offset by continued cost-savings program credibility and some category/brand momentum (hot snacks, pizza). Option skew/vol implies a modest move with downside somewhat priced.

Strong growth and an uplift to FY26 outlook (to 22% sales growth and $2.60 EPS) are likely the primary drivers, but margin compression (GM down 3.6 pts) and negative OCF/inventory & receivables build temper the upside; no pre-release consensus is available to size the beats.

No pre-release expectations/consensus were provided, so surprises vs market cannot be quantified. Qualitatively, results show improving gross profit and a narrowing net loss, plus management expects break-even/positive adjusted EBITDA in Q1 FY27 aided by restructuring savings and tariff refunds, which typically supports a modestly positive reaction despite the still-difficult demand and limited visibility.

Fiscal 2026 revenue guidance was lowered (despite maintained adjusted EBITDA), largely due to timing and international weakness—offset by solid subscription/committed services invoicing growth and improving backlog. Net effect is likely mildly negative/uncertain because revenue softness dominates the headline while profitability guidance holds.

No pre-release note/consensus provided, but the release emphasized narrowing FY26 EPS to a tighter range, improved gross margin (14.1%) despite low production levels, and strong railcar orders/backlog with 99% lease utilization—likely supportive. The main potential drag is delivery timing shifting into FY27 and some uncertainty around tank demand/tariff pass-through, keeping reaction only mildly positive.

With Q3 revenues down 5% and operating margin compressing to 11.5% from 14% due to irrigation fixed-cost deleverage, the print likely disappoints on profitability/demand. Offsetting positives include continued growth in Infrastructure (+8% and third consecutive quarter), plus liquidity/buybacks, but Brazil financing constraints and near-term funding cuts temper the outlook; guidance is not quantified vs consensus, so reaction is mildly negative rather than extreme.

No pre-release note/consensus is provided, but the call signals notable operational softness (LAL unit sales down 10% YoY; only 11 LDDs vs ~25 expected, and competitive trialing persists). Offsetting this, management raised full-year gross margin guidance (73–75% vs 70–72%) on favorable mix, which likely cushions the reaction but is unlikely to fully offset the growth/investment and competitive headwinds.

Organic ASV growth acceleration to 7.1% (with >10% of ASV growth from AI SKUs and 13x API call momentum) supports a positive tape reaction, but the ~300 bps YOY adjusted operating margin decline (comp/investments + FX drag) tempers the upside. Guidance was reaffirmed and tracking toward the high end, so the net reaction is modestly positive versus a median outcome, though exact beat/miss cannot be quantified without consensus numbers.

No pre-release consensus/expectations were provided, so surprise classification is based only on internal directionality. Retail strength and 90 bps gross margin expansion (plus web sales acceleration) are positives, but operating income/wholesale softness and higher capex with margin mix headwinds (retail margins down; wholesale shipments down) are negatives, implying a roughly neutral-to-slightly positive reaction.

The key incremental negative is guidance: full-year revenue was cut (and restaurant-level margin guidance lowered) due to construction/fire-inspection delays and macro pressure, which typically drives downside despite margin/labor progress in the quarter.

Deal is clearly growth/strategic but near-term results are clouded: management cut FY26 organic growth to 1%-2% and flagged margin pressure from tariff mix/service dilution plus a greater-than-expected Middle East headwind expected to persist into Q4. Incremental positives (Cortland strength/product momentum) likely partially offset the guidance/margin concerns.

No pre-release expectations were provided, but results showed a steep YoY revenue decline and a wider net loss. Offsetting items were targeted: sequential brand partner growth driven by the March Pi Day promotion and an inventory-driven cash improvement, though gross margin recovery remains delayed and most results do not yet reflect newly launched titles.

No pre-release consensus/option expectations were provided, so beats/misses can’t be quantified. Qualitatively, Q3 delivery strength (lot deliveries + robust industrial water) and high gross margin (52% driven by low-cost asset appreciation) plus a potentially more aggressive buyback are positives, partially offset by the scaled-back single-family rental program and board resignations described as routine.

Without a pre-release note or consensus figures, surprise vs expectations is unknown. Qualitatively, results show strong top-line growth but significant gross margin compression from commodity/shipping disruptions and a net loss; management’s Q4 stronger/ sequential margin recovery may cushion sentiment, implying a mildly negative-to-mixed reaction.

Without a pre-release yardstick, the core results look weak: revenue down ~42% and a swing to a $10.1m net loss with a very large gross-margin collapse from one-time charges. Guidance is also clearly cautionary (no FY26 revenue growth; improvement pushed to Q4), which should drive a below-median reaction despite some offset from expanding conversion-focused programs and a small acquisition.

No pre-release consensus provided for net sales/EPS, but the call emphasized broad volume/penetration softness (Atkins decline, OWYN distribution losses) alongside margin compression and a sizable $82m impairment. Guidance framed FY26/FY27 volume hit and Q4 sharper decline via intentional under-shipment, likely limiting upside despite management calling results better than expectations.

No consensus/pre-release benchmarks were provided for revenue/EPS or guidance, so beat/miss cannot be quantified. Qualitatively, growth (net merchandise sales +12.5%, comp +10.7%), margin expansion (+20 bps gross margin; operating income +16.7%), strong membership renewal (90.5% all-time high) and record digital sales likely drove a modestly positive reaction; partially offset by higher warehouse/SG&A costs from Chile preopening and operating income decline in Colombia.

Management reaffirmed full-year guidance but guided EPS toward the low end of the range and organic sales to the low end of the 4–6% target, citing NA pressure from higher gas prices (Iran war) and Q2 margin weakness. Some offsets (tariff refunds ~1 point EPS growth; international margin expansion/$40B+ revenue path) help, but the low-end bias likely tempers near-term sentiment.

Reported Q2 adjusted EPS of $0.28 beat guidance and the company raised full-year guidance again, with clear margin expansion (70 bps in the quarter) and strong DTC comp momentum. Without a pre-release consensus table, the size of the beat vs expectations and guidance upside vs Street are not quantifiable, but the direction (raise + improving margins/FCF) supports an above-median positive reaction.

With no pre-release consensus provided, surprise quantification vs expectations is unknown. Qualitatively, results beat initial guidance despite a large fuel headwind and reiterated full-year EPS, which should be modestly positive; however, management flagged fare-driven growth and volume upside remains more uncertain, capping upside.

No pre-release consensus was provided, but results show improving margins (gross +30 bps; operating +70 bps) alongside a guidance raise (FY sales/EBITDA/EPS up, with EBITDA midpoint lifted). Strong end-market demand (notably Container) and additional liquidity/capital returns (dividend +20%, planned debt paydown) likely drove a moderately positive reaction, though the exact beat vs consensus cannot be quantified without expectations.

With no pre-release consensus provided, surprise assessment is limited. The quarter showed strong top-line and operating leverage (net sales +24%, op income +47%, non-GAAP EPS $2.33), but management also highlighted meaningful gross margin headwinds (input-cost drag and Q4 cost pressure) and pulled-forward sales, which likely tempers upside. Net effect suggests a modestly positive, slightly above-median reaction given the strong EPS/operating income despite margin/setup concerns.

With no pre-release consensus, results/guidance can’t be cleanly benchmarked, but the release showed clear positives (NanoKnife record volumes, Auryon double-digit growth streak, and 70 bps FY26 gross margin expansion despite tariff drag) alongside a softer Mechanical Thrombectomy/AngioVac trend. FY27 revenue looks modestly positive (5–6.5% growth) with improved EBITDA/leverage support, implying a mildly positive but not extreme reaction.

With no pre-release consensus provided, directional assessment relies on qualitative items: operating leverage and efficiency improved more than the internal/sustainable targets, investment banking/S&T posted strong growth with record equities and strongest FICC in a decade, and management raised full-year 2026 NII/operating leverage guidance to the upper end—supportive of an above-median positive reaction.

With no pre-release note/consensus, surprise can’t be quantified. Qualitatively, loan growth/NIM holding up alongside improved efficiency should support sentiment, but the higher provision (despite low charge-offs) and softer economic forecast are potential offsetting negatives.

No pre-release consensus/guidance provided, but the quarter showed substantial revenue decline (-18.2% YoY), GAAP and adjusted weakness (adjusted EPS still a loss in context of liquidity-driven reductions), and significant margin compression (gross margin 31.2% vs 36.4% YoY) alongside deteriorating credit metrics and a going-concern disclosure—driving a likely negative reaction.

Guidance was net constructive (raised full-year NII and expense guidance with limited specifics that suggest revenue outperformance), and credit quality/mix improved (lower card net charge-off outlook). Offsetting negatives include CET1 pressure from RWA growth and capital distributions, and management tempered sustainability of equity strength—keeping the reaction moderately positive rather than strongly upbeat.

With no consensus/EPS-revenue numbers provided, directionally the call points to strong top-line acceleration (double-digit growth, ~20% June YoY, higher high-value site spend and contract counts) and modest margin expansion via SG&A leverage despite gross margin headwinds. The main offset is continued price/cost negativity and a trimmed full-year digital penetration target, likely limiting upside reaction.

Strong beat-style messaging and broad-based records (IB, AWM inflows/AUS, alternatives fundraising) plus an efficiency ratio improvement and raised full-year alternatives fundraising guidance. With no pre-release consensus numbers provided, magnitude vs expectations is not quantifiable; option pricing suggests a modest move with limited downside skew, consistent with a positive but not extreme reaction.

Management reported record flows and strong profitability, including 260 bps margin expansion to 45.9% and raised buyback guidance (at least $550m/quarter). Without consensus figures, the surprise is primarily in the magnitude of margin/flow strength and the incremental buyback raise, which should skew reaction positive versus the typical median.

With no pre-release consensus provided, direction is inferred from fundamentals: ROTCE is improving and credit/loan growth looks strong (positive), but management guided to similar modest NII compression into Q3 and explicitly noted stabilization later—consistent with a limited/possibly negative market reaction. Overall expected reaction skews slightly below median.

Fiscal 2027 guidance is a major step-up (implying ~2.6–3.0x growth) alongside record backlog/booking acceleration, which should drive a strong positive tape reaction. Offsetting factors: gross margin/guidance profitability outlook is supported by growth but FY26 margins already contracted, and option skew is only modestly bearish.

With record EPS, sharply improved efficiency ratio (52.8% vs 58.3%), improved asset quality (net charge-offs 23 bps) and a more positive CRE backdrop, the fundamentals likely exceeded what the market had positioned for; partial offset came from the small CET1 decline (10.9%) and a cut to net charge-off guidance (though this is credit-positive, it signals prior uncertainty).

Key reported positives were strong revenue/operating leverage and improving efficiency (expenses up much less than revenue), but the stock likely capped upside given management’s maintained full-year RoTCE target implying weaker 2H and explicit warning that markets revenue could decline more than historical H1-to-H2 seasonality. With no consensus/guidance baseline provided, reaction is assessed mainly from relative strength/offsetting 2H caution and modestly negative option skew.

EPS beat in Q2 led by operating outperformance (MA and individual ACA) alongside a raised full-year 2026 adjusted EPS floor (at least $27) and higher cash flow guidance, supporting an upbeat near-term reaction. Offsets include a $0.80 below-the-line benefit (nonrecurring) and reiterated Medicaid margin trough/negative outlook (now with added market exits), tempering upside.

Without a pre-release consensus note, surprise vs expectations is hard to quantify; however, the release showed broad-based record results (Wealth + Institutional), improved mix/margins, and strong net new asset momentum, with only modest sequential NII guidance. Overall likely mildly-to-moderately positive reaction given strong fundamentals, tempered by ongoing below-historical M&A/IPO volumes.

With no pre-release consensus figures provided, the cleanest incremental signal is the full-year 2026 guidance raise (midpoint adjusted EPS +$0.18 and higher operational sales growth midpoint $100.6B) alongside margin/tax outlook improvement. Offsetting negatives were MedTech growth slowdown (cardio/electrophysiology/Abiomed) and STELARA decline, but oncology and new launches appear to be progressing faster than feared, likely supporting a moderately positive stock reaction.

No pre-release consensus/guidance yardstick was provided, so beats/misses can’t be quantified. Management reiterated full-year 2026 revenue growth (3%-7%) with flat expenses, but highlighted NIM compression and weaker expected 2H fixed income results, implying a roughly neutral-to-slightly positive reaction given continued loan/PPNR growth and stable capital.

No consensus/actual revenue or EPS figures were provided, but the release’s tone is mixed: margin guidance is pressured and volumes are projected to decline again (negative), partially offset by strong free-cash-flow conversion, inventory reductions, and specific balance-sheet/cash actions (dividend cut) plus added A&P/supply-chain investments. Net reaction is slightly below-median as near-term margin headwinds dominate.

CTAS posted strong top- and bottom-line growth with continued gross-margin expansion (51% in Q4, all-time-high) and strong segment organic growth. The main offset is management flagging an SAP-related ~100 bps headwind in Fire and the acquisition/FTC timing uncertainty (UniFirst), which should temper upside into a moderately positive reaction.

Even without consensus figures, the release points to strong top-line/operating leverage (intermodal volume record, operating income/EPS growth) alongside clear cost-to-serve improvements and a record Dedicated truck pipeline. Offsetting negatives include transitory margin pressure from higher spot purchase transportation rates in JBT and continued headwinds from fuel (~100 bps operating margin).

With no pre-release note/consensus provided, the reaction is based on directional signals: NIM expanded and efficiency improved alongside record loan production and a stronger pipeline, partially offset by rising NPAs. Margin guidance for 2H (4.25%-4.35%) suggests a contained burn-off and supports a mildly positive, not dramatic, market reaction.

No pre-release consensus or guidance vs-expected benchmarks were provided, so surprise assessment is necessarily limited. Qualitatively, the combination of record funded backlog/bookings and strong space contract win rate is offset by a sharply lower reported Q4 revenue and the restructuring-driven drag, leading to an overall near-median reaction unless investors focus more on backlog conversion.

With no pre-release consensus/guidance yardstick, beats vs Street can’t be quantified. Qualitatively, the quarter showed solid broad-based loan growth, stronger fee momentum (record M&A advisory) and improving credit (NPL down, net charge-offs ~steady), while management reaffirmed NIM>3% by year-end—supportive for reaction. Key downside risk is N3 guidance for fees down in Q3 due to a capital markets pull-through, keeping the expected move only moderately positive.

No pre-release note/consensus or explicit financial guidance/EPS/revenue were provided, but management highlighted multiple financing milestones (JV debt structure, Europe lender/down payment, NRC funding) and a sizable LOI at fixed price with a large long-run demand appetite, offset by continued long construction timelines (ops expected 2028/2030). Overall tone modestly positive, but quantified surprise is unknown.

Management raised full-year 2026 EPS and free cash flow meaningfully alongside stronger Commercial Services growth and strong spare-parts visibility (backlog and off-wing/removals). Offsetting negatives were margin pressure (operating/CES margin down) and a sequential deterioration in spare-parts delinquencies, keeping the reaction positive but not extreme.

EPS and operating earnings growth were strong and management raised full-year adjusted EPS guidance and key operating earnings components; medical cost trend improved versus the initial estimate and retention/outperformance in Medicare Advantage was better. Offsetting concerns were that margin recovery is being pushed beyond 2027 due to accelerating commercial cost and IDR/NIPA impacts, and Medicaid margins remain pressured with elevated trends not yet an inflection. With no pre-release consensus provided, reaction is estimated as moderately positive given the guidance raises and improving cost outlook.

Without a pre-release yardstick for consensus/expectations, the cleanest incremental signal is the raised full-year net revenue growth outlook plus clear operating leverage (efficiency ratio down, ROTCE up) and credit improvement. The main offset is the announced reserve build tied to the Amazon portfolio close in Q3, which adds near-term credit drag risk.

EPS missed management expectations and gross margin contracted sharply (690 bps) amid weak shipments paced by weather and project delays; guidance is essentially near-term gross margin stability rather than a clear upside, reinforcing a negative read-through.

Fuel headwinds were expected to pressure results, but management both tightened full-year to the high end and guided recovery of most increased fuel expense, alongside stronger-than-expected TRASM/RASM tone and improving CASM-ex; net effect should be modestly positive versus consensus despite uncertainty on the exact expectation levels.

STT delivered strong operating leverage (645 bps ex-notables) with record fee revenue and raised full-year 2026 fee and NII growth outlook, plus $1B run-rate benefit medium-term targets—factors likely supportive for the stock. However, without a pre-release note/consensus, magnitude of the surprise vs expectations is uncertain.

Without a pre-release note or stated consensus, upside/downside vs expectations can’t be quantified. Qualitatively, results look strong: record adjusted earnings, stable NIM, improved efficiency, better-than-forecast loan growth (legacy loans) leading to stopping loan-growth forecasting, earlier/stronger acquisition contribution, and improving asset quality—likely supportive for the stock, with most of the surprise coming from the loan growth swing and Mountain Commerce timing.

EPS of $0.99 exceeded the $0.96 midpoint (about +3%), while Q2 commentary indicates stronger demand (U.S. growth accelerating to 16% and organic days-adjusted growth holding at ~6%) and expanding margins. Q3 guidance was maintained with 6% organic revenue growth at the midpoint and an improving EBITA margin tone, which should limit downside despite a high effective tax rate.

With no pre-release consensus and limited expectation detail, the reaction is judged primarily on directional signals: NIM improved but management guided margin to remain roughly stable, while loans and deposits declined and earnings included notable one-time costs—likely leaving investors broadly neutral to slightly cautious.

Abbott reported stronger-than-expected adjusted EPS and accelerated growth alongside a 100 bps gross margin expansion, and importantly raised full-year EPS guidance. The one offsetting negative was a 8% decline in Rapid & Molecular Diagnostics from a weaker respiratory season. With options implying only a mid-sized move and downside skew, the net effect should be moderately positive.

Without consensus figures, the best read is guidance stability: Q3 operating expense and NIM guidance were reiterated/defined without a clear beat. The main potential negative surprise is the elevated IT remediation/material-weakness costs, even if management frames them as one-time noise; overall expected reaction is slightly below median but close to neutral given ongoing loan growth pipeline and core yield strength.

Even without a pre-release consensus, management highlighted multiple quality positives (record capital markets fees/wealth all-time high, strong operating leverage with efficiency down to 61%, improved net charge-offs and stable ROTCE trajectory). Q3 guidance also implies modestly higher NII growth (2.5–3.5%) with stable-to-slightly-up expenses, supporting a favorable setup, though CET1 is slightly below target in the quarter.

With no pre-release consensus figures provided, the only clear expectation-relative items are qualitative. Gross margin and full-year non-GAAP gross margin were improved (supportive), procedures grew strongly with continued da Vinci 5 system placement (supportive), but management said full-year da Vinci growth results are closer to the midpoint (a mild demand/pace headwind), partially offsetting the positive margin story.

No pre-release consensus/earnings figures were provided for revenue/EPS, but guidance appears largely reaffirmed (Q3 ~12% growth; FY26 13%-14%), with positive color around improved season-2 falloff and narrowing ad-tier ARM gap supporting sentiment. Content spend growth is forecast to rise (~10% in 2026) but framed as slower than revenue, implying no major margin shock.

Despite strong operating momentum (record revenue and higher Aluminum adjusted EBITDA/margins), Alcoa reported modestly below-consensus adjusted net income tied to LME price weakness and also lowered full-year alumina production/shipment guidance due to Pinjarra instability and gas curtailment—offsetting much of the positive sentiment. Options imply a ~6-7% absolute move with no skew, suggesting a slightly negative but not extreme reaction.

No pre-release note/consensus was provided, but management lowered full-year NII guidance (range revised downward) alongside a smaller reset to full-year provisions. Offsetting positives were strong deposit-cost improvement and resilient revenue with solid capital/TBV growth, likely leading to a mildly negative-to-neutral reaction.

No pre-release yardstick or consensus numbers were provided, limiting precision. Operationally, the quarter showed margin expansion and record cash flow/leverage improvement, but the full-year outlook is reiterated flat organic sales and a wide restructuring/production-headwind backdrop (Turkey discontinuation, worse light-vehicle production assumption), likely keeping the market response modestly positive rather than a clear beat.

No pre-release research/consensus provided, so surprises vs expectations can’t be quantified. Qualitatively, deposits/BOH integration look solid (positive), but loan growth is largely acquisition-driven with elevated payoffs still a headwind (negative); management reaffirmed full-year loan growth guidance and expects deal costs to ease in Q3.

Even without consensus/research-note benchmarks, the release showed clearly strong fundamentals (core ROE above target, improving combined ratio, record segments and capital returns) plus modestly positive investment income guidance for Q3/Q4, which typically supports an above-median reaction. The main offset is tempered pricing/renewal premium changes in Personal Insurance and ongoing catastrophe/reinsurance positioning (cat XOL non-renewal; uncertainty reserve maintained).

Inflows were strong (highest in 4.5 years) with operating margin expansion, likely supportive for sentiment, but reported one-year investment performance declined sharply (41% of AUM), which is a key offset. Guidance details were provided but expected benchmarks/consensus were not available, limiting conviction.

Quarterly earnings momentum (37% YoY net income and improving ROTCE) is partially offset by softer guidance drivers—trimmed net interest income growth and revenue growth, plus lower NIM—though fee strength and improved credit quality limit downside. Without consensus revenue/EPS or a pre-release yardstick, the net reaction is likely modestly mixed.

With no pre-release note and no reported revenue/EPS figures, the actionable read-through is guidance/margin/delivering drivers: management reaffirmed 2026 NII growth at the top end and reiterated expectations for exceeding noninterest expense growth guidance and generating operating leverage—constructive for sentiment. Offsetting is credit deterioration (construction borrower migrated to nonperforming status with 11% specific reserve) and repricing back-book tailwind being tempered by low yields; overall this points to a mildly positive, roughly median-to-above-median reaction.

With no pre-release note or consensus figures provided, the clearest incremental signal is fundamentally positive: improving core NIM (+4 bps) alongside low charge-offs and a sharp jump in approved commercial pipeline (+63%). The main potential overhang (elevated CRE/Construction payoffs and modestly higher NPAs) sounds contained by criticized/classified declines and updated loan-growth outlook.

No pre-release note/consensus provided, so EPS/revenue beats can’t be quantified; however, management raised full-year NII guidance and noninterest income/expense targets while showing stronger-than-expected Southwest deposit inflows and best-in-recent periods credit metrics. Guidance also includes a partially offsetting credit headwind via a lower charge-off outlook. Overall likely positive reaction.

No pre-release consensus/guidance targets were provided, so surprises vs expectations can’t be quantified. Qualitatively, credit metrics improved (lower charge-offs/NPLs, normalized credit, stronger investment-grade pipeline) and NIM guidance supports a modest sequential improvement into the 3.70% exit level, which should be mildly positive for the stock absent any offsetting negatives.

Quarter delivered broad beats (revenue and adjusted EBITDA) plus major margin expansion (up ~650 bps) and strong FCF, but management’s leverage/interest savings and added auditorium plan were at least partially contemplated—thus upside reaction is positive but not extreme. Lack of numeric consensus/guidance makes surprise sizing uncertain.

With no pre-release consensus/guidance provided, I can only infer tone from fundamentals: record pretax net investment income and underwriting profitability (88.1% ex-cat combined, cat losses down) alongside continued premium growth and expense discipline (expense ratio targeted ≤30%) are likely supportive, but the lack of explicit consensus limits conviction.

Key negative was the trimmed U.S. net store growth outlook (pipeline pressure / franchisee profitability strain) after weak Q2 same-store sales driven by a controllable ticket issue; order counts improved but didn’t offset the ticket miss. With volatility/absolute move moderate (~6.1%), the market reaction likely leaned negative but not extreme.

No pre-release consensus/option expectations were provided, so surprise quantification is limited. Operationally, SFBS reported strong loan growth with record pipeline, expanding NIM (+10 bps) and improved efficiency (<30%), but deposits were pressured by tax payments and CRE concentration rose—likely keeping the reaction moderately positive rather than extreme.

No pre-release note or consensus EPS/NII/NII-growth expectations were provided, so beats/misses cannot be quantified. Management reaffirmed full-year 2026 operating leverage (100–150 bps) while highlighting stable-to-improving fundamentals (NIM stable/up YoY, low charge-offs, fee growth), which suggests a mildly positive but not outsized reaction.

No consensus/option expectations were provided to quantify beats/misses, but management reiterated Q2 sales/EBITDA within the upper end of recent expectations while citing improving gross margin from mix (ablative higher-margin) and strong firm LEAP-1A orders, with new longer-dated C2B/Aerion and Tulsa capacity/lease announcements supporting sentiment.

Guidance was raised for full-year 2026 adjusted EPS (to $8.45-$8.60) alongside solid free cash flow and improving Life Sciences momentum; offset by a notable bioprocessing revenue timing shift out of Q2/Q3 into 2027. With no consensus numbers provided, reaction skew is estimated from the directionally positive guidance and volatility/skew implying meaningful but not one-sided upside.

Revenue and adjusted EPS both edged above the April guidance midpoint, while margins (ex-FICO) beat the company’s 75 bps target and improved. Offsetting negatives include a $40m legal settlement charge and softer mortgage origination driven by higher rates, keeping the net reaction closer to the median.

With no pre-release consensus provided, the clearest angle is fundamental: purchase volume hit an all-time high (+8% YoY to ~$50B) and net charge-offs improved (5.43%), supportive of credit quality; however NIM fell sequentially (-42 bps) to 15.08% (though framed as the trough). The guidance was raised/narrowed to $9.25–$9.50, likely limiting downside and driving a modestly positive reaction.

The key surprise is management trimming full-year delivery guidance (~3%) citing softer demand and rising cancellations/qualification issues, which is directionally negative. Offsetting that, home sales gross margin exceeded the high end of guidance and pretax margin outlook is still in a tight range, limiting downside.

Revenue, non-GAAP EPS, and free cash flow all exceeded guidance, and management pointed to another software margin record in Q3 plus accelerating RPO—supportive of a positive tape reaction. Offsetting negative is the sequential decline in appliance gross margin (memory costs), though management framed it as bottoming in Q3.

Without consensus numbers, surprises are inferred from narrative: gross margin expanded sequentially and backlog/book-to-bill improved, supporting positive demand tone, but management flagged product gross margin pressure from relocation costs and the new licensing revenue timing is back-end loaded (Q2 accounting won’t fully repeat). Management also raised long-term targets meaningfully, which should drive a more positive than median reaction.

GM raised full-year 2026 guidance for a second time, with improving regional margins (NA back to target range) and stronger-in-year EPS/FCF dynamics, which should support a moderately positive reaction. Offsetting negative: additional EV-related restructuring charges, though management framed cash-materiality as substantially completed.

Despite a small EPS miss from a non-cash impairment and margin compression, management raised full-year Wizards outlook and the broader company guidance (revenue growth, operating margin/EBITDA) with cyber losses coming in well below the earlier estimate. Strong Magic demand/record set performance and better-than-expected cyber impact likely dominate, implying a modestly positive next-day reaction.

No pre-release expectations or consensus figures were provided, but the release includes multiple credit/efficiency positives (lower net charge-offs, low NPA, strong ROA/ROTCE) alongside some offset from deposit-cost pressure and guidance-tightening around NIM/FTE NII. Overall tone is modestly positive on fundamentals with uncertain magnitude given missing consensus/revenue data.

No pre-release note was provided, so beats/misses vs consensus can’t be quantified. Qualitatively, Industrial/Motion and NA Automotive showed margin expansion and solid growth, but Automotive was pressured by the Iran-related fuel/consumer headwind and management lowered the global Automotive revenue outlook and flagged incremental second-half costs—likely keeping the net reaction modestly positive/near-median.

No pre-release note/consensus was provided, but the release included a full-year adjusted diluted EPS raise ($8.30-$8.50 from $7.90-$8.30) and improving leverage/FCF outlook, partly offset by guidance for Q3 sequential EPS decline and management caution in Latin America/Brazil volumes plus higher Middle East conflict cost headwinds for H2.

Reported profitability and credit trends were broadly supportive (ROTC strong, NCOs improving, CET1 up), but management also flagged a meaningful CECL reserve build and originated-yield pressure from higher S-tier mix; overall the guidance update (earnings-asset growth range raised and NCO range tightened) likely offsets the headwinds, implying a moderately positive reaction.

No consensus/preceding expectations were provided, so beats/misses vs street cannot be quantified. However, management guided Q3 margins higher (C&P +125–175 bps; D&E +25–75 bps) and reiterated international growth engine upside (now ahead of schedule), with Middle East weakness framed as steady-activity assumptions—supportive for a modestly positive reaction.

Key positives were record wealth AUM with improving NIM (2.73% and guided higher to 2.75% in Q3) alongside loan/ deposit momentum; the main offset was a sharp deterioration in past-due metrics from a single CRE office exposure and higher noninterest expense expected for Q3. With no pre-release expectations provided, the net surprise is assessed as modestly positive but not high-conviction.

With no pre-release consensus, EPS/revenue beats or misses can’t be quantified, but the call emphasized solid operating profitability, sustained NIM expansion (6th straight quarter), and accelerating organic loan growth. Offsetting items include one-time legal expense and management flagging a modest sequential margin downtick in Q3 (~20–25 bps) as Navitas proceeds are reinvested.

Management raised full-year net sales and EPS guidance, with notable margin expansion (+130 bps) and strong North America Utility demand (pricing + volume + grid modernization). Offsetting negatives include sharp Telecom contraction and continued cost pressure (steel/diesel) with some international agriculture delay risk, keeping the reaction positive but not extreme.

Even without a pre-release consensus package, EPS and organic growth beat expectations and management raised full-year organic growth, EPS, and free cash flow. Strong order/backlog and expanding operating margin point to upside, offset by a notable Consumer weakness and larger oil/tariff input headwinds.

Raised full-year 2026 sales and EPS guidance alongside record backlog/book-to-bill (positive), partially offset by pressured space margins from unfavorable EAC adjustments. Without consensus/research-note baselines for revenue/EPS, the reaction is inferred mainly from the clear guidance raise and backlog quality.

No pre-release consensus provided, but management raised full-year average loan growth guidance (to 4–5% from 2–4%) and increased full-year revenue (to 7–8%) and net interest income (to 9–11%) alongside a sequential NIM expansion and supportive fixed-asset repricing. Offset came from investment banking/debt placement fees missing expectations and modest deterioration in nonperforming assets/credit watch items.

EPS of $1.84 beat consensus ($1.27–$1.28), and—more importantly—FY26 adjusted EPS guidance was raised to $5.15–$5.60 (midpoint $5.375), well above the market’s already-high $4.15–$4.70 range and above the $4.80 sell-side embed. Management also cited constructive biofuels, higher 45Z net benefit (~$250M), and strong AS&O/Nutrition operating profit, partially offset by ~$100M of positive MTM/timing impacts that are expected to reverse.

Quarter delivered upside on both sales and EPS, plus record orders/backlog and stronger core margin and FCF. However, the pre-release note framed the setup as “beat and raise is needed” with consensus already at the top of range, so much of the beat was largely priced in; the primary new positive is the raised FY guidance midpoint and the magnitude above the already-top-of-range expectation.

Despite no EPS/revenue consensus provided, the release showed clear upside in profitability (Adjusted EBITDA +160% and gross margin expanding YoY for the first time in 4+ quarters) alongside strong demand (Nielsen growth and accelerating DTC). Guidance was maintained, so the reaction is likely driven by earnings-quality/operating leverage rather than forward revisions.

Q2 showed clear quality beats versus the pre-release bar on profitability (adj. EBITDA margin 6.9% = best since 2021) and cash generation (FCF $301M), with strong orders/AOV/active customer momentum. Most importantly, Q3 revenue growth was guided to high single digits (above the pre-release expectation of mid-single digits), and gross margin was reiterated to the low end of the 29.5–30.5% range while EBITDA margin stays 6–7%; net effect is a likely modestly positive, partially already-priced reaction.

Revenue growth and category-specific outperformance (Premier Protein/Dymatize exceeding expectations) were partially supportive, but the release confirmed severe margin pressure (27.7% adjusted gross margin) and heavy second-half margin headwinds (Q4 ~10% adjusted EBITDA margin) while also calling for net leverage to rise to ~4x. Guidance net sales were raised, but EPS is unknown and the market focus remains on margins/financing, limiting upside.

EPS and the broader volume/demand picture were largely consistent with the preview (growth continues; FY2026 algorithm reaffirmed). The key negative surprise was North America comparable operating earnings declining (down 2.4% YoY) versus the note’s expectation of ~+8% growth, while the Millersburg start-up/capacity constraint was only partly anticipated.

EPS came in roughly inline/slightly below the consensus ANI/share range (reported $2.11 vs ~$2.18 to beat; the alt-income print was already pre-announced). Offsetting that, the key upside items—record capital solutions fees ($277M) and origination/organic capital formation strength—came through while management reaffirmed FY20%+ FRE growth and the 10% SRE growth/120–125bps spread outlook (net spread 124 bps on the normalized alt assumption), supporting a modestly positive but not outsized reaction.

Quarterly EPS (reported FY26 adj. EPS $9.60) came in slightly above the note’s implied high-end/consensus frame (consensus $3.75 vs implied Q4 $3.59–$3.76), while FY27 guidance was effectively better than the note’s “needs ≥7% recurring” setup: management guided 6%-8% recurring growth (with strong onboarding/pipeline visibility) and lifted margin to ~21% with higher EPS growth (8%-12%). Demand/pipeline and capital allocation (raised buyback authorization) further reduce tail risk, supporting a moderately positive reaction.

CAT delivered a clear upside surprise on both revenue and EPS versus consensus, plus a major backlog/earnings-quality catalyst (tariff recoveries). Most importantly, it raised FY2026 sales/revenue growth guidance to mid- to high-teens and lowered the FY tariff-cost outlook to the low end, supporting expanding margins; strong demand commentary (data-center-driven Power & Energy and out to 2030 order visibility) reduces the chance of a disappointment fade.

No pre-release consensus/option expectations were provided, so surprise is hard to quantify. Qualitatively, the release highlights strong hardware/DMP-SLA momentum and a large industrial order, but Industrial/legacy weakness and margin pressure from printer-heavy mix/tariff-related offsets temper the upbeat story; guidance is framed as a sequential step-up with improving EBITDA vs prior year.

Despite raised full-year 2026 net sales and adjusted EBITDA guidance, results show EBITDA margin contraction (tariff-related gross margin pressure, lower adjusted EBITDA growth vs revenue). The Cambridge acquisition is a large positive strategic catalyst, but near-term leverage/FCF impact tempers reaction.

With no pre-release note/consensus, the clearest new information is materially raised 2026 revenue and adjusted EBITDA guidance alongside improving gross margins and falling leverage. The main offset is a widening adjusted net loss and a slight year-over-year decline in adjusted EBITDA margin, suggesting some margin/earnings pressure despite top-line strength.

EPS and near-term revenue were effectively in-line versus a low-information consensus (EPS at the prior midpoint). The clear swing factor was the raise to full-year FCF guidance (positive), but full-year adjusted revenue growth was lowered and Capital Markets guidance was cut (negative), partially offsetting the FCF beat.

Revenue was largely preannounced (de-risked) so the main upside vector was already priced in; reported EPS strength via higher net income is offset by a notable COGS deleveraging/royalty drag (COGS 24.2% vs 19%) and the market’s main uncertainty around opex/R&D wasn’t clearly resolved. Guidance was reaffirmed, so the event likely produced a near-median reaction rather than a large directional repricing.

EPS and organic revenue growth came in ahead of the pre-print bar (Street was essentially at guide with no positive drift). Management also raised FY26 EPS and revenue, with expanding comparable margins and inVue Dx placements still on pace for the 5,500 unit goal; however, the quarter’s outcome is partly consistent with the conservative setup and Investor Day 9 days later likely tempers incremental repricing.

EPS beat (adjusted $3.38 vs ~$3.32 consensus), but demand momentum disappointed (US comps ~0.8% and July slightly negative) and management cut the FY26 FX tailwind to ~$0.15 (vs prior $0.20–$0.30), while also pushing restaurant openings out by one year—limiting upside despite the EPS cushion.

Q2 revenue ($93.3M) and adjusted EPS ($0.08) both missed the already-low consensus ($98.1M, $0.10). Although full-year revenue guidance was reaffirmed (0–4% growth), management cut FY EBITDA margin guidance (to 29–31% from 30–32%) and reported services softness (down YoY, weaker book-to-bill), which likely outweighs the modest positives (software stability and improving bookings ex-acq).

Revenue and margin improved (gross margin 64% vs 47%), but the pre-release note expected a revenue miss/weak compute backdrop and downbeat EPS cuts; on EPS, adjusted EBITDA more than doubled on the call while the large GAAP loss was driven by BTC MTM (expected). The main potential incremental negatives are the sizable G&A increase (largely non-cash) and limited unrestricted corporate cash, partially offset by the strong project financing/leasing updates already largely priced in. Overall reaction likely modest/mixed given expectations already incorporated the BTC/GAAP noise and the big contracted value items.

Q2 revenue ($338.8M) and EPS ($2.50) both exceeded the pre-release consensus floor, and management delivered a second full-year guidance raise with FY adj. EPS now $9.30–$9.80 (midpoint ~$9.55) vs Street ~$8.85–$9.50. The stock’s upside tone is supported by continued AST margin/outlook strength and improving leverage/FCF despite the non-cash reserve build.

ROK reported Q3 sales and adjusted EPS above consensus, helped by strong Software & Control and data-center/semi demand and expanding enterprise margin. The key offset is that FY26 adjusted EPS guidance was raised but the new midpoint ($13.15) is roughly in-line with/only modestly above the $13.03–$13.06 consensus range, so upside reaction is likely limited.

NDA timing and cash runway met the stated baseline (full submission in 2H26; approval targeted 1H27; cash ~$251M), and SELVA Phase 3 efficacy details were strong, but the notable financial swing was a higher FY26 cash spend guide ($85–95M) consistent with the market’s burn/raise overhang rather than a new negative. BTD was declined for the cVM program, but that was not a consensus-expected surprise in the pre-release framing.

Reported Q2 results show strong sequential momentum (GOV + operating leverage; adjusted EBITDA +33%) and cash held up with a credit-facility renewal. Guidance was raised for FY26, but the midpoint sits broadly within the pre-release expectation range (largely expected reaffirm/upper-end outcome), while revenue beat appears driven by the World Cup backdrop already anticipated.

Strong Q2 organic growth (broad-based) and record adjusted EPS with expanding gross margin likely drove a positive reaction. However, management explicitly cautioned that the double-digit growth is not sustainable and cited ongoing margin pressure at AJR (delayed Dominican Republic transfers), partially offsetting upside.

Q2 SaaS revenue/ARPU/subscriber trends broadly align with the pre-release frame, but management **lowered FY SaaS revenue (to $453–457 vs prior ~$463–471)** and **FY SaaS EBITDA to $42–44** while citing first-half sales/marketing underinvestment; together with weaker marketing services billings and a large restructuring charge, this shifts the key 2H SaaS EBITDA credibility risk toward the bear/base downside despite new platform/integrations.

Q2 results were broadly in line on revenue (~5.2% vs ~$813.6M consensus/$814M implied) while adjusted EPS was effectively at the functional EPS bar from the note (reported $0.59 vs derived $0.59–$0.62), plus EBITDA margin expanded to 26.8% (helping sentiment). The key is guidance: management affirmed FY organic growth and ~27% adj. EBITDA margin rather than raising to ~27.5%, capping upside and keeping the reaction near the cross-event median.

Results delivered a clear beat on revenue (record + sequential growth) alongside a much stronger profitability profile (near breakeven adjusted EBITDA) versus expectations of another cash/earnings overhang. Most importantly, FY2026 guidance was raised to a higher range and gross margin guidance improved (exiting 2026 at 60%+; mid-60s over time), which the pre-release note flagged as the key credibility/cash-driver. The release also provided incremental demand strength (record CTD volume) that was not anticipated to the same degree.

Revenue and marketplace growth materially beat what the note implied (~$215M consensus/guide-midpoint), and—more importantly—management raised FY26 revenue guidance to 33–34% (above the feared 27–28% deceleration). Margin expansion and strong buyer metrics (net adds and 21% revenue/active buyer) support the upside reaction; EPS was not provided versus consensus in the facts.

Despite a strong Engineered Composites quarter (record revenue and nearly doubled segment EBITDA), consolidated revenue and Q3 adjusted EPS guidance both undershot the pre-release anchors ($339.2M revenue; $0.75 EPS). With the stock already priced for another beat, the downside guidance skew dominates reaction.

EPS beat was sizable (operating margin/gross margin expansion) while revenue came in at the low end; however, full-year non-GAAP EPS guidance was reiterated (not raised) with organic/revenue guide unchanged and only FX assumption modestly improved vs the May note. The market reaction likely skews modestly positive given strength in bookings/margin, but the lack of guidance upside caps upside.

Q2 beat on both sales and non-GAAP EPS versus the high end of expectations, but the key upside driver is much stronger margins: EBITDA margin at 27.7% vs expectations of ~22%, aided by a $73M tariff recovery not in prior guidance. The company also raised FY26 sales and EPS guidance with stronger memory/pricing offsets, which should drive a positive (though not euphoric) tape given the market already expected a beatable quarter.

Q2 delivered upside on both revenue and adjusted EPS versus ~$376.2–$376.3M and ~$1.69–$1.70 expectations, alongside improving operational metrics (Personal Care fill rate, Hospice census growth). The main offset was the Ohio Medicare Cap accrual pressuring hospice margins, though management guided full-year EBITDA margin toward the top end (13% upper range) consistent with a margin expansion story.

No pre-release consensus was provided, but management raised full-year 2026 revenue and adjusted EBITDA guidance and showed strong utilization/OEC growth plus expanding SER margins, likely outweighing the tempered Q3 timing and the NOx penalty headwind.

No revenue/EPS figures or explicit 2027 guidance changes were provided, so the main incremental items are operational (production/cost progress, Waha turning positive) offset by removal of the minimum free-cash-flow return commitment (capital allocation flexibility), suggesting a modestly positive but mixed reaction.

Q2 outperformed on both revenue and non-GAAP EPS versus a tight top-end setup, with gross margin at the highest since 2022 and leverage improving to 3.4x. The key is guidance quality: Q3 implies stronger growth and higher gross margin/EPS than the already-demanding consensus framework, while management also raised MSI growth and shifted leverage expectations to a faster deleveraging path.

Revenue and profitability came in strong with margin expanding, and full-year revenue guidance was raised, which should support sentiment. Offsetting negatives were a slightly trimmed net income outlook due to higher hiring/investment spend plus a disclosed cybersecurity incident (even if non-material), likely limiting the upside reaction.

Net sales slightly exceeded consensus, but adjusted EPS missed (Argo + Mexico macro pressure) and segment operating income remained weak. Management reaffirmed FY adjusted EPS, broadly in line with/above expectations, offsetting some downside; tone stayed cautious on near-term margins (tapioca price pass-through) and Argo credibility despite recovery at June rates.

No pre-release consensus figures were provided, but the release highlighted Q2 results at the high end of guidance and a Q3 outlook that reflects acquisition-driven step-up (TCO) and removal of seasonal drag—supportive of a modestly positive reaction. Offsetting this, EBITDA margin ticked down (20% vs 21%) due to Middle East logistics cost pressure, which tempers the beat.

Revenue and EPS beat the pre-release setup: reported revenue topped the low-end consensus and adjusted EBITDA margin expanded to 23.4% (above the 22–23% need). Even with some Patient Services gross margin softness (mix/pump costs), upside from wound care (+154% to $2.1M) and Oncology reaching $20M likely drives a modestly positive reaction, while guidance was only reaffirmed (already largely expected).

Quarterly revenue modestly beat (but EPS headline is dominated by the already-expected Terns one-time charge, leaving EPS effectively inline). The main upside surprise is modestly stronger FY revenue guidance at the midpoint vs consensus, but negatives include tax rate impact (very high due to the acquisition charge) and gross margin guidance lowered to ~81% from higher prior expectations, plus management tempering U.S. KEYTRUDA growth.

Without a pre-release consensus/guidance yardstick, surprise is judged from call commentary: demand/order visibility improved materially (order book +50% YoY, lead times into late Q4’26; industrial backlog nearly doubled) and EBITDA is up 9% YoY on shipments/pricing/mix, but utilization came in below plan (74% limited cost offsets), capping margin upside. Management guided Q3 adjusted EBITDA slightly higher sequentially and YoY, implying a modestly positive but not a large beat-driven reaction.

Q2 revenue and adjusted EPS beat consensus despite the stock’s recent weakness, and management raised full-year 2026 guidance (adj. EPS midpoint above the Street’s prior consensus). Backlog expansion and strong E-Infrastructure/CE C momentum supported expanding margins; the main caution was order-timing lumpiness, but it was framed as timing rather than demand deterioration.

Quarter prints look roughly in-line with the heavily de-risked setup, with the key variable (guidance) reaffirmed exactly at $280–300M. However, volumes/NICU days were weaker (patient service volumes -2%, NICU days -3%) versus what the note’s base case framed as likely +2.5–3.5% same-unit with volumes ~flat-to-down, creating incremental downside narrative despite the pricing strength.

While NRG secured a major BYOP Texas hyperscaler project (1.2 GW, expandable) that is a genuine upside narrative catalyst, Q2 adjusted EPS fell to $1.49 vs ~$1.80 consensus and management reaffirmed 2026 guidance while signaling tracking below the midpoint due to softer Texas power/load, Winter Storm Fern costs, and incremental RGGI—keeping the market focused on guidance slope rather than the headline EBITDA jump.

PRKS missed on revenue (=$483.3M vs ~$493–494M consensus; about a ~2% shortfall) and reported weaker profitability (adj. EBITDA down to $195.5M) alongside continued attendance declines. While management reiterated remaining on pace for 2026 cost savings and noted strong in-park per-capita and buyback momentum, the fundamental demand/attendance softness plus margin contraction points to a negative earnings reaction versus expectations given the recent history of misses.

Top-line Modern Oral growth was strong, and the company raised Modern Oral net and gross guidance. However, Q2 adjusted EBITDA dropped 50% to $15M (11% margin), with full-year EBITDA guidance maintained at $70–90M—so the market reaction is likely muted-to-negative versus expectations that the spend would translate into narrowing downside to EBITDA.

With no pre-release consensus provided, the key actionable surprise is the raised 2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance ($8.3–$8.5B, +$0.2B at midpoint) tied to improved base performance and the Momentum acquisition, alongside strong execution (Phase 1 Socrates in-service on time/within budget) and additional growth signals (11%+ long-term EBITDA CAGR target). These incremental positives likely drive a moderately positive next-day reaction, though lack of revenue/EPS consensus limits precision.

With no pre-release consensus provided, directionally the report includes a margin decline (gross margin -120 bps) and book-to-bill below 1x in both divisions (backlog drawdown), which should temper sentiment. Offsetting positives include improved adjusted EPS and continued in-line acquisition execution, but the Q2-to-H2 sequential decline outlook and weak order trends likely cap upside.

Revenue and adjusted EBITDA came in around expectations (EBITDA ~in-line vs the ~$50M target), but the call added meaningful negatives: Q3 EBITDA step-down tied to sand completion breaks and wide volume/soft timing risk. Offsetting positives were the first behind-the-meter 120MW PPA with strong stated FCF/payback, though management also flagged limited additional contractability (2–4 projects vs prior 8–10), tempering near-term sentiment.

Management reiterated FY2026 sales guidance (flat to up ~5%), aligning with the pre-release yardstick; the upside came from gross margin improving to 20.3% at the high end of the 17–19% range and strong diversification/new business wins. The main downside surprise vs expectations was weaker profitability optics (operating income down on elevated SG&A) and ROCE far below target, which likely kept the reaction near-median rather than meaningfully positive.

Revenue and EPS beat the pre-release yardstick, but Q2 EBITDA margin fell on tariffs/incentives. The key market-moving item is guidance: full-year revenue growth was raised to 10–13% (above prior 8–11%), and the EBITDA midpoint moved up to 18–18.5%, which should support a mildly positive tape given the Street’s emphasis on H2 margin/guidance.

Q2 margin came in at the top of guidance (11.3%, sequential expansion), but EPS of $0.14 missed consensus (~$0.19). The bigger issue versus expectations was guidance: FY adjusted EBITDA was pushed to the low end of $1.05–$1.25B on markedly higher inflation (~$150M vs $60–$65M) and FY adjusted cash flow was lowered to $600–$700M, a combination that undercuts the H1→H2 step-up the market was relying on—driving a negative reaction despite solid Q2 profitability.

Pre-release positioning centered on a Q3 “inflection” and reaffirmation/“high-end” FY26 delivery. Instead, management lowered back-half organic growth to flat-to-up ~1% (from ~4% expected) and flagged a 200–300 bps battery-category softening versus prior expectations—an incremental downside to the growth leg of the thesis. EPS/Q3 prints and revenue vs consensus were not provided in the facts, so the reaction setup hinges primarily on the guidance reset, which should be negative but not extreme given some margin progress and continued tariff cash collection.

No reported revenue/EPS or explicit 2026–2027 guidance numbers vs consensus were provided, so the surprise call is driven by qualitative items: materially better-than-expected D&C cost performance on the new Marcellus pad and constructive basis tightening/transportation actions, which should be perceived as upside. However, magnitude is uncertain given missing hard guidance and consensus data.

Q2 adj. EPS of $1.43 beat the effective $1.30 whisper consensus by ~10.8% while management reaffirmed FY2026 guidance ($6.55–$6.80) exactly in line with expectations. Strong ESA/data-center demand (7.8 GW secured) and conversion of the pipeline are supportive; no offsetting negative guidance language or implied cuts were noted.

Q2 beat on adjusted EPS ($0.58 vs $0.40 consensus) alongside a gross margin above guidance (40.7% vs ~38.5% consensus view, helped by tariff refunds), while bookings stayed above 1.0. Q3 guidance appears broadly in line on the midpoint, so the main upside driver is the Q2 margin/EPS strength rather than a material guide raise—supporting a modestly positive-to-above-median reaction.

Q2 revenue and adjusted EPS beat the anchored consensus ($836M/$0.20 vs. $962M/$0.24), but the release confirms the market’s core margin worry: base gross margin fell to 7.9% (and U.S. Gas margin to 4.2% vs. 7.8% last year), which is not what bulls needed for near-term cash/profit conversion. Offsettingly, management raised FY26 revenue guidance (midpoint up vs. consensus) and highlighted 2H gas margin visibility (~7.5%) plus continued strong backlog/bookings, making the net setup moderately positive for the next-day move.

Revenue was essentially in line with the ~$987.5M consensus setup (only a modest miss vs consensus), but the call delivered a third consecutive $1B+ orders quarter with double-digit Prepared Food & Beverage growth and improved facility/automation savings targets. Offsetting that, Prepared Food revenue lagged ~mid-$20M with logistics/inefficiency pushback into the second half.

Q2 delivered strong operating momentum (comps +8% and written growth well above the pre-release base case) and EPS beat driven by leverage, while management reaffirmed the key gross margin range (60.5–61.0%)—a critical guardrail the market feared could be trimmed given new tariff/cost pressure. The main offset is management’s explicit worsening fuel/container/input headwinds and gross margin flat ex-tariff refunds.

EPS and operating earnings growth were strong (record adjusted operating EPS; sizable spread-based mix and annuity sales growth), which should support a positive reaction. However, limited partnerships underperformed the long-term return assumption (unfavorable notable-item impact) and full-year targets were merely reaffirmed, limiting upside surprise versus what the market likely expected.

With no pre-release expectations or consensus provided, the clearest actionable item is the guidance improvement: NJR tightened fiscal 2026 NFEPS guidance while raising the midpoint and also lifted the fiscal 2026 CapEx range, alongside a FERC certificate received ahead of schedule—factors that likely support a moderately positive earnings reaction.

Q2 adj. EPS ($0.77) beat expectations, helped by stronger non-COVID/launch performance and cost actions, and FY26 revenue guidance was raised at the midpoint despite a COVID cut—offset by large impairment charges (including sigvotatug vedotin/oxbryta) and reaffirmed FY26 EPS after a small AIPRD headwind. Overall should beat a mostly low-volatility, reaffirm-led setup.

Without consensus/guidance figures, reaction is based on qualitative deltas: record profitability metrics (net income, net written premium, investment income) and an unusually low catastrophe loss ratio likely drove a positive tape, partially offset by specialty E&S premium declines and a temporary expense ratio uptick from the Houston lease buyout.

Q4 topped tight consensus (EPS and revenue), helped by USFS local volume accelerating to 2.6% and an International margin/operating income rebound. Despite gross margin contracting and a somewhat weaker margin narrative, FY2027 EPS guide of $5.02–$5.12 better than expected versus the pre-release view that buyback pause would pressure outcomes; net result should drive a modestly positive tape move.

UONEK lowered FY26 adjusted EBITDA guidance to mid-$50M (from $60M), a clear deterioration versus the market setup emphasizing that a $60M reaffirm would be the key upside. Operating results also confirm weakness (Q2 revenue -6.4% YoY; adj. EBITDA down to $11.7M) alongside sharp linear subscriber decline and weaker political outlook, which likely drives a meaningfully negative repricing.

Revenue was essentially in line with the thin consensus and organic growth met the pre-release base case (6% vs a ~mid-single-digit concern). The main beat was EPS (breakeven diluted EPS vs consensus -$0.01), alongside stronger Recorded Music and sync momentum, while the main offset was no strategic-review update (supportive but not a new deal catalyst) and net debt rose further.

No pre-release consensus/expectations were provided, so surprises vs market can’t be quantified. Qualitatively, Q3 BMD EBITDA guidance implies a sizable sequential step-down (margin/earnings contraction) tied to supplier transition and soft end markets, partially offset by supportive EWP pricing/order file and strong plywood price benefits.

Revenue growth and improving net leverage (0.4x) plus strong international/offshore outperformance likely supported sentiment, but adjusted EBITDA margin contracted (17.2% vs 20.8%) due to a non-repeating project headwind, tempering the upside. No consensus/EPS/guidance benchmarks were provided, so overall reaction is only mildly positive/inline.

Q1 printed strong on both lines versus the pre-release base case: FRE margin expanded to 53% (vs 51%) and management delivered GAAP/non-GAAP EPS ~$1.94, well above the $1.52 consensus. The credibility debate was largely defused by near-unanimous evergreen net inflows (10/12 positive) and nearly $640M net inflows while AUM topped $19B, plus higher fee-related performance revenues driving the margin beat.

With no pre-release consensus given, the clearest incremental positives are the raised full-year production range, improved operating expense per boe, and a materially upgraded Permian synergy target to $250–300M (vs $90–100M originally), supporting higher-than-expected free cash flow/margins. Capital spending was maintained, and balance-sheet actions (debt redemption) further support sentiment, implying a modestly positive reaction rather than an outsized upside beat.

Consensus called for $0.90 EPS (split-adjusted), but reported diluted EPS was $1.31—however the pre-release note’s baseline implies a different split-adjustment convention versus the reported quarter EPS (and the call notes did not provide a revenue/EPS reconciliation versus the stated consensus). Operating tone was mixed-to-weak: maintenance reserve revenues fell and utilization declined to 85% vs 87.2% YoY, partially offset by higher AUM and better adjusted EBITDA (+4%). Overall, the market reaction is likely negative-to-moderately negative given weaker utilization/maintenance dynamics, despite AUM and embedded gains.

EPS of $12.01 beat ~$11.28–$11.30 consensus (≈+6.2% vs midpoint), and management raised full-year EPS guidance to $45.50–$47.25 (midpoint $46.375), above the prior guidance midpoint and above consensus. Gross margin expansion and segment momentum were supportive, though MonotaRO’s growth benefit from customer prebuying is described as fully subsided (a modest offset).

Top-line largely met expectations (13% YoY revenue growth; FY revenue raised to $3.4–$3.6B, consistent with being toward/above consensus), but margins disappointed: adjusted EBITDA was flat (reporting distortion notwithstanding), external headwinds were quantified (~$24M), and management lowered aggregate margin expansion to ~100 bps (from ~200 bps) and said results are trending to the midpoint rather than the upper end—likely tempering the reaction despite the revenue raise.

Quarterly performance and, more importantly, the second 2026 guidance raise (EBITDA/net income/EPS midpoints) with materially higher cumulative cash tax benefits were likely net positives. Offsets include margin softening in NGL due to mix (higher ethane recovery/lower C3+ margins) and expectations for Natural Gas Pipeline earnings decline in 2H as systems normalize.

EPS ($17.73) materially exceeded the top-end pre-release consensus ($14.52), driven by upside refining economics with R&M capture at 112% (vs the note’s base of 95–100% and high-end bull framework of 100%+). Q3 guidance described throughput/unplanned capture headwinds via higher turnaround spend, which was largely consistent with the note’s “base tell,” so the reaction should be positive but not extreme versus the EPS beat already partially reflected in positioning.

While the quarter showed weaker adjusted EPS driven by lower PVC pipe prices, management raised full-year EPS guidance and highlighted a strong (though likely pull-forward) PVC sales volume backdrop plus a growing load pipeline. The large antitrust settlement charge and expectation of softer 2H volumes likely cap upside, implying a roughly median/modestly positive reaction.

Q2 non-GAAP EPS of $0.86 beat the ~$0.80 consensus from the pre-release note, while FY2026 non-GAAP EPS guidance was reaffirmed ($4.28–$4.40) and thus largely met expectations. Offsetting factors include additional 2027 headwind risk (RTO transmission incentive elimination) and mixed nuclear monetization detail (uncapped price scenario vs collar ceiling), keeping the reaction near-median despite the EPS beat.

Q2 revenue was slightly above the $110.4M consensus, but EPS missed badly on extremely weak adjusted earnings optics and, more importantly, full-year guidance was materially lowered (deliveries, revenue, and adj. EBITDA) due to a delayed second-half ramp. Gross margin collapsed to 5.5% and cost/volume fixed-cost absorption weighed on profitability, outweighing backlog growth and aftermarket momentum.

Although the quarter delivered major upside in orders/backlog (record new orders $934M and backlog $2.4B), revenue ($312M) and diluted EPS ($1.42) both fell short of consensus ($318.3M and $1.49). With elevated options-implied volatility already pricing a large move and call skew for downside protection, the net reaction is likely modestly negative/near-median despite the strong demand signals.

TDG raised FY26 guidance (notably EBITDA midpoint and adjusted EPS to $41.04) and indicated improving margin (Q3 52.8% up sequentially) with strong commercial aftermarket and OEM trends. With the Street largely expecting solid but sensitive back-half optics, the guidance raise and margin resilience likely drive a modestly positive reaction despite some dilution from acquisitions.

Q2 beat on both revenue and adjusted EPS, helped by strong Industrial Motion (record sales and sharply higher margin). More importantly, FY adj. EPS guidance was raised to $6.05–$6.35 (midpoint $6.20), modestly above the pre-release expectation that the bar was guidance-consistent/low-hurdle—supporting an upside-biased reaction despite investors’ caution around belts/divestiture timing.

Q2 delivered a revenue and EBITDA beat (record $63.5M adj. EBITDA; 12.1% margin), improving the key margin narrative versus the note’s risk of continued contraction. However, EPS was essentially in line with the $1.39–$1.42 band and full-year guidance was merely maintained (11–12% EBITDA margin and low-to-mid single-digit sales growth), limiting upside reaction.

No revenue/EPS or explicit consensus comparisons were provided. The main incremental news is the more shareholder-friendly capital return framework (32% higher base dividend with a protected floor) alongside solid Q3 production growth (incl. organic contribution), which should be viewed as sentiment-positive even if the exact magnitude vs market expectations is uncertain.

Pre-release note and consensus expectations for revenue/EPS aren’t provided, limiting surprise attribution. However, management narrowed 2026 production guidance and raised the bottom end of total cash capex while affirming strong liquidity/net leverage and favorable hedge pricing, which likely supports a mildly positive market reaction.

Q2 EPS came in meaningfully above the pre-release base-case implied by the note (using ~$1.35), supported by a sharp rebound in PEM EBITDA and ~$150M contribution from the profitability plan. Offsets: HIP EBITDA was essentially flat with margin compression, and management flagged a modest Q3 pipe volume headwind from pull-forward, while guidance was reaffirmed (full-year cost plan $600M) and HIP revenue/margin outlook was reset toward the low end as expected.

No pre-release expectations/consensus are provided, so EPS/revenue beats can’t be quantified. Management maintained 2026 EPS guidance at the same range while reporting strong O&M control (ex-acquisition) and expanding gross margin, which should be modestly supportive; capital plan and acquisition/rate timing add some uncertainty.

TPG beat the market on both fee-related revenue ($628M vs ~$573.5M consensus; ~+9.5%) and after-tax DE ($0.69 vs ~$0.62–$0.64 consensus; ~+8% at mid), but the FRE margin normalized to “pulled-forward” levels (reported 50% vs a ~47% target with explicit caveat) and management guided a step-down in transaction/monitoring/capital markets fees in 2H due to pulled-forward closes—tempering the upside. Raised growth signals from fundraising ($16B Q2; >$50B target reaffirmed) were already a key focus, so the overall reaction skewed only slightly positive.

EPS of $1.43 missed the ~$1.48–$1.49 consensus, despite stronger-than-expected weather-normalized sales (+9.6%) and customer growth (2.1%). Guidance was effectively reaffirmed (still $4.55–$4.75) with management expecting the FY end at the top of range, but the Q2 earnings shortfall plus concerns around higher interest expense/ depreciation offset the favorable demand narrative; rate-case remains pending but decision timing aligns with expectations.

Q2 results beat the pre-release setup on revenue (reported $308M vs ~$288M estimate). The bigger surprise versus expectations was DAYBUE execution—STIX adoption (40% of U.S. patients) and referrals (STIX ~60% in June)—plus an upward raise of 2026 DAYBUE sales guidance, which supports the back-half ramp the note stressed. Offsetting EPS isn’t provided, and remlifanserin timing shifted only slightly but was already treated as the key variance item.

Q2 delivered a clear beat on both revenue (+8.9% vs consensus) and non-GAAP EPS (+15.9% vs consensus), and Scorpio accelerated to become the largest product line earlier than expected. However, Q3 revenue and EPS guidance are materially above consensus, while gross margin guidance resets lower to ~72% on mix—likely capping upside versus the magnitude implied by the beats.

Revenue, EBITDA and Illinois hold-per-day came in strong and Chicago licensing/near-term operating timeline appears to be pulled forward versus the market’s already-optimistic late-2026/early-2027 expectations—supporting upside. However, diluted GAAP EPS ($0.15) lagged the consensus EPS range cited in the pre-note (even adjusted would be at/above the weaker base), which tempers the immediate reaction; overall guidance/capex stayed in the same band.

Revenue came in above expectations (driven by recurring + projects), but adjusted EBITDA/margins remained weak with sharp YoY decline and adjusted EPS fell far below consensus. Importantly, management still guided to very low Q3 EBITDA, keeping the turnaround/margin inflection risk front and center despite liquidity support and higher full-year revenue/EBITDA ranges.

EPS is effectively de-risked versus the pre-announced line, and the release leaned positive (record revenue/TRASM strength and a best-in-class operating margin). However, Q3 guides a consolidated loss (~$0.50) with peak nonfuel cost inflation (CASM ex-cargo) and leverage pressure from a ~$275M pilot retention bonus, which should offset much of the positive sentiment; overall the market reaction is likely muted-to-slightly positive given the guidance largely met expectations.

Q2 revenue and EPS both beat the pre-release expectations, and Q2 gross margin (63.4%) improved QoQ. However, the key yardstick—the FY26 guidance reset—was a meaningful raise (~$12.6B vs ~$11.6B consensus/expectations), but at this stock price/volatility a lot of the upside was already in the run-up; only one notable negative surrounds the higher commitment level framing (aggressive supply securing) that could raise margin/recognition risk. Overall reaction expected to be mildly positive-to-mixed rather than outsized.

Q2 showed strong growth drivers (Repatha, UPLIZNA/IMDELLTRA/PAVBLU) and an above-consensus margin print (non-GAAP op margin 48% with full-year ~45–46%), plus a revenue/EPS guidance raise. However, EPS upside is partially offset versus the note’s bar given that consensus had already been near the top of the FY range, and management also flagged higher Q3 operating expenses (and CFO transition), plus the still-unquantified cybersecurity overhang remained a known risk.

Q1 revenue ($166M) and EPS ($0.19 non-GAAP) beat the pre-release consensus ($149.8M; $0.14) with clear margin expansion (adj. EBITDA margin +640 bps to 25.6%). The main incremental positive catalyst was guidance: FY2027 revenue raised to $650–670M and adj. EBITDA to $145–155M (midpoints above the previously guided range/market expectations), supporting a above-median post-earnings reaction despite already-elevated expectations after the stock’s strong YTD run.

Q2 revenue largely matches the pre-set ~$212M bar (and surgical strength with 17% growth/24% adoption supports durability). The key upside is margin expansion (gross +260 bps; adj. EBITDA up 53%) and raising full-year adj. EBITDA to ~$140M, but credibility remains tied to biologics and EOS timing (EOS $17M, essentially flat YoY; revenue/case and biologics commentary still constrain the story), keeping the net reaction near-median rather than strongly positive.

Q2 performance beat on adj. EPS ($2.54 vs $2.44–$2.46 implied) and revenue (+8% y/y) with ~40 bps margin expansion, but the key guidance disappointment was Q3 room nights (3%-5% vs the expected +5% to +7%) alongside a lowered FY gross bookings outlook (high-single-digit). With the market already sensitive to the 2H recovery slope, the net reaction is modestly negative to slightly below-median.

Revenue was broadly in line with the pre-release bridge expectation (the market largely assumed the April 2 TBHC consolidation would drive the step-up), while gross margin expanded to 26.8% versus the previously emphasized 24–26% constraint—an incremental positive. Offsetting that, adjusted EBITDA remained negative (–$12M) and EPS losses deepened vs the preview’s implied base-case signal that profitability could be near break-even, keeping the reaction close to median despite better margins.

The quarter added major de-risking Phase 3 efficacy confirmation and reiterated an sHTG sNDA submission before year-end with potential accelerated launch in 2Q27, plus REDEMPLO scaling (commercial revenue ~$2.4M; prescriptions up; >400 unique prescribers). However, the call also reported a widened net loss (-$194.3M / -$1.36), and the biggest “catalyst” was already de-risked by the recent SHASTA data per the pre-release note, limiting upside surprise; net result is likely a modestly negative-to-neutral reaction around the median.

EPS of $1.71 beat the $1.68 consensus and, more importantly, management raised full-year adjusted EPS guidance to ~ $6.55 on top of strong underlying orders (+7%) and accelerating ACV/software growth. Revenue was roughly in line, but the raised EPS/FCF outlook and margin expansion support an above-median post-print reaction.

Revenue beat the (stale) consensus, while non-GAAP EPS beat by a wide margin; importantly, reported consolidated gross margin jumped to 66% and organic growth ex-ESI was 7% reported (11% YTD) with ESI at $6.9M (supporting the acquisition thesis). Management maintained the $100M run-rate target despite having already reached it in implied run-rate terms—so the main upside comes from margin/EBITDA quality rather than new guidance.

Revenue and EPS both beat the pre-release setup (expecting roughly $262–265M revenue and ~$0.95 EPS). More importantly, FY26 guidance was raised to $1.085–$1.095B revenue, with adj. EPS growth guidance also upgraded vs the prior $3.86–$3.98 window. Despite margin slip (39.8% vs 40.3%) and higher leverage from Dimensa, the raised top-line/earnings trajectory should drive a positive reaction.

Jacobs delivered a strong operational quarter with margin expansion (15.2% adj. EBITDA) and a large backlog/book-to-bill, plus raised FY26 guidance again. The quarter’s adj. EPS ($1.84) was essentially in-line with pre-release expectations, but the raised FY outlook (revenue growth and FCF margin) and improving deleveraging/demand tone support an above-median reaction.
