Underlying operating performance was better than feared (base business ex-Veklury +10% YoY, HIV +12%, Trodelvy +26%, PrEP >$1B run-rate; Yeztugo maintained ~$1B FY guide), but headline/non-GAAP EPS was still very ugly due to acquired IPR&D (~$11.2B vs already-expected ~$11.5B), and cell therapy revenue declined as expected (–14% YoY with full-year guidance for a mid-teens % decline). Net: fewer negatives than the bearish setup, but the big EPS swing was largely priced in, leading to a roughly median reaction.

Q2 revenue and adjusted EBITDA both came in above what the pre-release note framed as the likely base/consensus band, and management raised FY26 revenue to the top part of the expected range while maintaining the ~$25M EBITDA target. Despite scoliosis weakness from zero 7D sales (already a watch item), the overall back-half credibility improved via gross margin expansion and stronger-than-expected EBITDA/free-cash-flow framing.

Revenue beat is largely merger/mechanical, but management raised the cost synergy target and provided 2H 2026 guidance with EBITDA/margin above the pre-release combined build; offsetting negatives include clear American Woodmark underperformance vs expectations (low EBITDA margin/absorption), partially muting the reaction.

Q2 revenue and GAAP EPS were materially below the pre-release working expectations (revenue ~$29.8M vs ~$33.5M; EPS $0.01 vs $0.04–$0.06). While management reiterated FY2026 e-commerce growth (10–15%), the ingredient business declined, S&M intensity stayed elevated, and cashflow stays supported mainly by the pharma investment narrative—limiting upside and driving a likely negative next-day move.

Q2 delivered a modest revenue and strong profitability beat (GAAP profitability continued; adj. EBITDA growth ahead of expectations) while management raised FY outlook and narrowed ranges. However, the market’s core question—the H2 gross profit bridge—was answered with a sharp Q3 deceleration (6–8% revenue, 5–7% GP) and a ~2-point second-half GP drag from Cash App new-issuance softness, limiting upside.

Revenue was broadly in line and subscription/ARR trends were supportive, but margins contracted and Cybersecurity income dropped with a $3M headwind still biting. The key incremental upside was raising FY revenue and EBITDA guidance (and hardware guidance) above prior levels, likely offsetting the margin optics, leading to a near-median to modestly positive reaction.

Open orders and managed-services momentum were supportive, but consolidated gross margin (23.3%) and adjusted EBITDA (47.8M) declined, and professional services revenue fell on project delays with revenue timing pushed to the back half/later—offsetting the modest demand positives. Guidance was maintained, which limits upside versus what was already anticipated.

Top-line slightly beat consensus, but the bigger swing was guidance: management lowered FY2026 revenue range (midpoint below the street expectation) after already-pressured EXPAREL volume growth (3% net sales; elective softness). EPS also missed due to lower-than-expected adjusted profitability despite cash strength and payer/reimbursement tailwinds.

Q2 delivered above the pre-release Street bar with record MAU and accelerating UCAN, plus the company raised FY26 adjusted EBITDA margin guidance to ~30% (from 29%), supporting the margin ramp narrative. The Q3 top-line guide decelerates but still brackets reasonably around the implied bar in the note, so most of the upside comes from higher margin/engagement quality rather than a guide collapse.

EPS came in sharply above the pre-release consensus loss (reported +$0.05 vs expected -$0.01), driven by operating profitability before the first FDA-approval anniversary. Guidance on funding operations to cash-flow breakeven by end of 2026 was reiterated, limiting downside from a projection standpoint despite the high-88% to low-90% steady-state margin commentary.

Q2 revenue slightly beat consensus and gross margin expanded, but the key overhang is guidance: management lowered full-year US procedure guidance to 54,000–56,000 (midpoint down ~7,000 vs the note’s consensus/expected path), which is the likely driver of a muted-to-negative reaction despite maintained total revenue and Q4 positive adjusted EBITDA commitment.

The key post-release change was a guidance update: Rigel raised the upper end of full-year guidance by ~$5M due to stronger contract revenue (~$30M vs $20–30M). Management maintained product sales guidance and declined near-term Vepinu launch guidance (consistent with the note’s focus), so the setup points to a modestly positive, but largely expected, reaction driven by the contract-revenue lift.

EPS of about -$0.11 is roughly in line with the -$0.12 consensus, but revenue came in far below expectations due to a $1.2M non-cash reversal tied to SK On milestone assumptions. Offsetting positives included equipment installed and commissioning starting in Q4 plus renewed discussions/catalyst expectations around a Korea joint venture by year-end, likely keeping reaction closer to median.

Revenue came in above the ~$500.1M consensus (~+2% vs expectations) largely helped by disruption coming in below the $9M drag guide, but consolidated adjusted EBITDA/margins contracted more than the Street modeled and the release still centered on a trough-quarter narrative. Full-year capex guidance was reaffirmed, so upside from the quarter is partially offset by margin weakness and only moderate operating leverage.

Q2 net sales (+12% Y/Y to $347M) and EPS ($0.26, with tariff-refund benefits) land roughly where the pre-release note said guidance/carryover implied (no clear beat vs the model). The key swing item—gross margin—was strong on an underlying basis but the main risk (FY/Q3 gross margin path) was not improved: Q3 GM guided to 53.5–54.0% and full-year GM maintained, consistent with expectations, leading to a modestly positive but not outsized reaction.

Q2 revenue came in above the pre-release $188.4M expectation (driven by 10% organic + Freedom). Management also raised FY26 guidance (midpoint sales growth and adj. EBITDA growth higher), which is a net positive versus what the note framed as a guidance-driven debate. However, gross margin fell more than expected (35.5% vs ~37.5–38% modeled) from a demand/ramp mismatch, and EPS was materially below what the note’s normalized $0.17 implied—partially offset by adjusted EBITDA improvement.

EPS and margins came in strong, and FY26 non-GAAP EPS/FCF guidance was raised versus the street’s already-high bar. However, cloud ARR growth missed the low-double-digit target and management downplayed AI product monetization (not material to Q2 / largely not baked into 2026), limiting upside.

Revenue came in modestly above the ~$184.2M Street expectation (reported ~$190M), supported by strong service/logistics growth and higher fleet utilization. However, FY26 adjusted operating margin guidance was cut materially (to ~12.5%-14% ex-PAD vs prior ~16%), with PAD/Ops investment and OCS Kidney expected to pressure margins—likely offsetting the revenue beat and keeping the stock reaction below-median despite the raised low-end revenue guide.

Revenue came in below the $79.4M consensus setup (reported $72.8M; shortfall versus the ~$79M expectation), and new patient starts declined sequentially (250; management called it temporary), which reinforces the “revuforj ramp gap” the market was trading. On the positive side, Revuforj net revenue of $55M slightly exceeds the note’s implied ~$56–58M whisper downside framing but still comes in below the consensus bar, so the dominant reaction driver is the continued revenue miss rather than EPS (not provided). Guidance/funding and the 70%-80% return-to-therapy target were reiterated/consistent, limiting upside.

Revenue beat (total revenue $169.6M vs $157.3M consensus) driven by strong FILSPARI/FSGS and higher collaboration revenue, but GAAP EPS missed ($-0.13 expected vs worse/unknown exact reported, implied ~7% below). Margins likely pressured by higher R&D/SG&A and non-cash charges, partially offsetting the launch momentum; FSGS launch strength was already a key narrative input, so upside is tempered.

Despite reiterating full-year guidance (inline to expectations), management reported a sharp margin inflection (21% EBITDA margin vs 13% in Q1; contribution margin 55% vs 50%) and GAAP profitability—offset by a slower July YoY origination growth rate driven by UMI rising to the top of its range, keeping reaction closer to modest-positive.

Adjusted EPS of $0.51 beat the $0.38 consensus estimate, helped by 13% organic service growth and 90 bps service gross margin expansion. Management also increased confidence and guided to continued high-single-digit service organic growth and service gross margin expansion—more supportive than the market’s already-priced track record narrative, though distribution margin fell sharply (vendor rebate timing).

Q2 revenue and margins deteriorated versus what was expected to be an inflection quarter (gross margin 39.3% vs ~43–44% consensus; adjusted EBITDA essentially zero). More importantly, FY26 guidance was sharply cut to $100–110M (midpoint $105M) from $130–135M, largely driven by delayed EG4/ITC-qualified inverter and slower GO ESS ramp—an outcome the market was sensitized to, driving a highly negative but not tail-risk reaction given expectations were already focused on the back-half bridge.

Q2 revenue and profitability beat the release’s own guidance and exceeded the pre-release setup (the note implied “inline to slight miss” vs the ~437M whisper), and FY revenue/EBITDA/FCF guidance were raised at a meaningful magnitude, with superscale ARPU/customer growth and pipeline cross-sell strength supporting the update. GAAP EPS guidance improved, but the note already expected EPS to be strong, keeping the beat from becoming a maximum-upside gap.

Margins disappointed versus the yardstick: gross margin fell to 21.6% YoY (though still above the note’s ~19% base-bar), with inflation/conversion cost pressure; however, upside came from strong adjusted EBITDA (positive $1.5M) and a record $140M pipeline with above-benchmark conversion. Guidance was consistent (moderate Q4 contraction), limiting upside follow-through.

The market largely expected a modest UAE delay within 1H27, but management pushed Wynn Al Marjan opening to Sept 2027 and increased the project budget ~+$600m (plus added equity needs), which is a larger-than-anticipated capex/cost overhang and drives the negative reaction. Offsetting positives were (i) Vegas revenue up with only small unfavorable hold and (ii) modest Macau mass improvement into late July/early August, but hold pressure and updated cost/cash requirements overwhelm.

Q2 revenue ($11.5B) and gross margin (~56%) were broadly in line with what the Street was underwriting, while the key decision number—Q3 revenue guidance of ~$13.0B—was not a clear upside vs the pre-release setup’s $12.5B focus. Upside came from Data Center strength (DC $6.7B; mix improving) and margin expansion, offset by softer Gaming and no meaningfully better-than-expected guidance action.

Revenue and full-year guidance were essentially aligned with the guidance-anchored setup, so the print likely trades more on narrative than on the numbers. Upside came from faster platform conversion (>17% of eligible ARR vs 15–16% needed) plus Verity monetization details; the main negative was the elongated mega-enterprise deal timing (slips past quarter-end) alongside modest ARR/NRR deceleration from the unlimited-user platform shift.

Quarterly revenue came in above the $49.9M consensus despite continued Y/Y decline, and adjusted EBITDA loss narrowed to near break-even with improving gross margin. More importantly, management supported positive trajectory via the $Q3 and full-year guidance prints and disclosed a sole-source DHA intent to award a multi-year direct contract—addressing the key unresolved catalyst from the preview—so the stock should skew modestly positive versus the market’s already-cautious setup.

No consensus revenue figure was available pre-release, and EPS consensus was based on limited coverage; however, reported Q2 revenue fell 21.8% y/y and adjusted EBITDA turned negative, while guidance remains withheld—both reinforce the market’s already-skeptical setup rather than providing a clear upside catalyst.

Revenue ($158K) was well below the ~$75K expectation (and far below the $50K–$100K Q2 guide range), while losses worsened (non-GAAP loss $5.0M vs. ~–$0.13 consensus). Qualitatively, Atomera did cite important technical milestones (GAA linearity, NAND TAM expansion, manufacturability milestone), but the call also flagged a missed PowerAmerica program, no new STMicro update, and a cash decline alongside higher 2026 opex guidance—overall more negative than the market’s already-skeptical base case.

EPS performance appears broadly in line with fragile adjusted consensus (no explicit revenue beat/miss disclosed in the facts). The biggest incremental positives vs the preview are the sharper-than-expected volume moderation/recovery (June positive, July up >20%) and continued record-setting dealer activity; offsetting that, forecasted net cash flows still declined and the provision/forecast gap widened on slower-than-forecast prepayments, limiting upside.

Revenue missed versus the pre-release/whisper setup (down ~9% YoY; product revenue down 22%), while EPS was mechanically boosted but still landed above the $0.04 consensus print. The key reaction driver is profit held largely on IEPA refund/royalty reserve one-offs, with underlying margins (~58.9% ex one-time) broadly flat and products weakness persisting.

Q2 revenue and (especially) adjusted EBITDA handily exceeded the already-too-high guidance hurdle, but the main offset is the Q3 revenue and EBITDA guide coming in below the Q2 run-rate/seasonal expectations. Net is likely a modestly positive but not a major re-rating into the print, with some pull-through concern around forward profitability timing.

Results were close to expectations (reaffirmed FY guidance) but the key swing factor—margins—beat via a sharp sequential recovery (12.5% vs 6.6% in Q1) alongside a newly announced restructuring plan for 2027. Offsetting negatives were weaker China order timing and Life Science softness, keeping the overall reaction near-median rather than strongly positive.

Quarterly EPS/FCF and reconfirmed FY guidance are largely in line with the pre-release setup (consensus was mechanically anchored to guidance, and the note expected no meaningful beat-and-hike). Incremental positives came from IKC exceeding expectations and strong leverage discipline/buybacks, but the key swing items (RPT decelerating sequentially with ACA commercial-mix headwinds) reinforce a limited upside reaction.

Q1 revenue ($190.2M) and service revenue exceeded both the company’s raised Q1 guidance and the Street’s ~$182M range, but gross margin fell to 61.6% on a mix shift (below the market’s expectation given prior margin sensitivity). The key upside driver is that full-year revenue guidance was raised (total revenue midpoint up; service revenue midpoint up), offset by margin/mix concerns and largely inline non-GAAP EPS vs the ~$0.07 consensus.

Q2 revenue ($33.6M) matched the pre-release expectation for a scripted ~45% y/y down quarter, and management reaffirmed FY26 guidance. The notable negatives versus what the note framed as the main swing factors were (1) tail (net adjustment) revenue falling and (2) a lowered full-year net adjustment revenue outlook (to $16–$20M), alongside weaker enrollment/unit economics (submissions down 44%, CAC up 16%).

Q2 EPS beat expectations largely due to a large, explicitly disclosed $122M gross tariff refund benefit (+$0.52 EPS, +700 bps margin), while underlying fundamentals were weaker (Water volume down high-single digits; ex-refund Water margin down ~700 bps). The key negative for valuation is guidance: full-year EPS excluding tariff benefits was cut to $2.70–$3.00 (midpoint ~$2.85), ~9–10% below the prior consensus range $3.15–$3.20; Q3 EPS and margins also imply continued pressure. Overall mix suggests a down-to-moderately negative reaction despite the headline EPS beat.

Q2 revenue and non-GAAP EPS beat the pre-release consensus (revenue +~1.7%, EPS +~30.8%), with Rule-of-40 profitability/margin strength and steady EX-led demand. However, FY2026 guidance appears reaffirmed/inline versus the $958–964M revenue and ~$0.61–0.63 EPS expectations in the preview, which typically limits upside and keeps reaction near the median-to-slightly-positive range given recent beat history and existing positioning.

Q2 RLA (164m) beat the guidance midpoint and came in above the pre-release expectations level, helped by travel/hospitality strength. However, adjusted gross margin fell ~450 bps to 56.6% despite EBITDA upside, and the quarter still reflects mix headwinds. The main potential driver of a positive reaction is raised full-year guidance (EBITDA expansion and top-line growth), though margin dilution limits upside.

Revenue beat the $377.4M consensus while ADS momentum continued into Q3. EPS surprise is unknown/likely muted because the release emphasizes margin compression to 34.7% (in line with the Street’s ~35% expectation) while affirming gross margins to stay ~34.7%–34.8%. Strong Canada/GPO demand and cash/repurchase support offset the weaker margin narrative, implying a roughly median/slightly positive reaction.

Q2 landed essentially at the guidance midpoint (EPS $0.34) and revenue was slightly below the low end but not a clear new downside surprise. The key trade—Q3 inflection—was supported with guidance revenue $68–70M and adjusted EPS $0.37–$0.39 (midpoint ~$0.38) plus a further gross margin step-up to ~46–47%, while management added more specific AI-delivery capture progress and delivered strong Q2 operating cash flow/buybacks.

Revenue and organic growth materially exceeded the already-top-of-range expectations, and FY26 organic growth guidance was raised beyond the prior range, supporting a positive tape. However, full-year margin tailwinds look limited by FX-driven EBITDA headwinds and cash flow remained negative due to higher receivables and long-lead prepayments, tempering the magnitude of upside.

Q4 topped consensus on both revenue and EPS, but the real driver is the first FY2027 guide: revenue midpoint ($658.5M) is slightly above the $656.3M expected in the pre-release note and EPS midpoint ($1.60) is above the $1.55 consensus, with continued strong cloud momentum (cloud ARR +29%, NRR ~123%). The main offset is the sharper-than-normal near-term license drag (Q4 license -25%), which was expected to be a headwind but came in as a notable negative against a quarter framed as stable.

Q2 improved vs its prior quarter (loss narrowed to $29M) and delivered a GOS margin jump to 345 bps with Q3 guide up to 360–390 bps, which partially addresses the market’s core “330–360 bps” worry. However, consensus revenue/EPS were low-confidence in the pre-note and the release did not clearly neutralize the liquidity/binary 2027-notes overhang beyond monetizing ~$10B MSR and buying notes at discounts.

Revenue and especially operational EBITDA substantially exceeded the pre-release model ($311M vs $276M; $36M vs ~$23M base) with margins expanding to 26%. The GAAP swing to profit is also a positive offset, but without reliable consensus EPS and given the model’s emphasis on GAAP being distortion-prone, confidence in magnitude/direction of EPS surprise is limited; inventory build tied to silver under new terms is the main negative.

Q4 lines were largely pre-set via the July 30 prelim, so there’s limited incremental upside in the reported quarter. The main incremental items are FY2027 framing—revenue per enrollment guided flat to up slightly with flattish margins (generally what the note anticipated), while gross margin fell 140 bps and applications are slightly behind, offset by ahead-of-prior conversion activity and $189M buybacks.

Despite strong gross margin and record operating income, LMAT guided FY revenue and organic growth down to reflect Q2 export/orders and RFA supply weakness, and reported EPS ($0.74) below the ~$0.81 consensus implied by the pre-release note. With sales being the key driver the note flagged as most asymmetrically risky, the mix of revenue miss + softer FY sales outlook should drive a below-median stock reaction.

Q2 beat was ahead of the already-expected de-risked quarter, and more importantly Q3 consolidated guidance was raised to $245–265M (midpoint $255M) and non-GAAP EPS $0.54–0.58—well above the note’s $228–243M framing and supporting accretive AMI assumptions. Despite this, the release comes after a strong run-up/positioning, tempering upside.

EPS of $0.84 materially undercut the Q2 $1.09 consensus in the preview (about -23%), driven by unusual GAAP/non-cash items and a weaker adjusted EPS outcome versus what the back-half bridge implied. However, funded volume grew (+21% y/y to $730M) and FY funded volume/$4.50–$5.00 adj. EPS guidance was reaffirmed, keeping the reaction muted rather than sharply negative.

The quarter was broadly in line on revenue and adjusted EPS versus the pre-release framework, with EBITDA/margins pressured by prior F2F-sale and mix (margin contracting). Offsetting the bearish setup, management announced incremental $13B of new PCF deals and strong PCF activity (notably $476M PCF cash and $91M Q2 PCF revenue with a pulled-forward California milestone), plus clear NaaS momentum—positive deal/demand headlines likely drive a modestly favorable reaction versus the base case.

Net sales beat the ~$1.08B consensus, but adjusted EPS ($0.01) missed expectations ($0.03) by far due to margin compression (48.6% vs ~48.5% whisper not the issue; the level plus higher opex/royalties/tariffs hit EPS). Guidance was reaffirmed at FY26 adj. EPS $1.27-$1.39, limiting upside and reinforcing the market’s margin/EPS sensitivity.

The market largely expected revenue to be in the ~$900M area and the key debate was credibility of the profitability path. OPEN delivered strong unit economics (CM 5.8%, marketing sharply lower, acquisition pace/contracting strong) but Q3 contribution margin guided to ~4–4.5% (below the Q2 5%–7% range), so the reaction should be moderately positive rather than a major beat.

Q4 revenue and adjusted EBITDA both beat the top end of guidance. However, FY27 total revenue guidance ($1.880–$1.895B) and recurring growth (~8%) align with the preview’s base case rather than delivering the more bullish FY27 step-up the market was implicitly positioning for after the pre-run; the disclosed deferred-cost accounting change also partially explains margin strength, offsetting the need for “core” margin upside.

Qualys beat on both revenue and EPS versus the pre-release bar that required more than modest outperformance, and it raised full-year guidance (revenue and EPS) with improving NDR (105%) and better EBITDA/FCF margins. Demand was described as early-stage for Mythos AI in Q2, but the operational KPIs and the higher FY guide likely dominate the reaction.

Revenue came in well above the ~$181–182M consensus (largest quarterly revenue, driven by CRYSVITA rebound) and EPS loss was much smaller than expected, while management reaffirmed full-year revenue and opex guidance. Despite reaffirmation, the size of the beat and improved cash/operating burn likely drive a moderately positive next-day reaction.

Revenue was essentially in line with the live-consensus model, but adjusted EBITDA/margins came in ahead (39% vs ~38.3% modeled) and Tinder/hinge momentum was solid (Tinder DAU/major MAU improvement; Hinge 22% growth). Offsetting negatives included continued E&E/Azar drag and the lack of clear evidence of upside beyond what the note already framed (Tinder payers still down 5–8.5% and MAU only improving toward flat by 2027). Overall reaction is likely near-median/slightly positive given the notes’ “binary guidance/momentum” setup and the strong margin beat.

Revenue beat expectations (company-driven outperformance), and demand/on-demand stabilized with PeopleReady growth acceleration. However, gross margin undershot the key 21.1%–21.5% setup (20.7%), and the net loss/write-down despite adjusted profitability plus margin pressure likely caps upside; Q3 revenue guidance appears broadly in-line with the base-case view.

Key positives vs expectations were a record 9,500 net location adds (vs ~8,400 consensus) and continued margin expansion (adj. EBITDA +240 bps to 37%) alongside 28%+ recurring gross profit growth. Offsets were GPV per location staying flat (World Cup as the only cited lift) and guidance nuance: EBITDA was raised by less than the Q2 beat due to reinvestment of a ~$10m tariff refund and hardware inventory build, keeping downside risk around the growth run-rate despite the higher FY recurring gross profit outlook.

Revenue ($255M) and subscription growth (+19%) beat the high end and key demand indicators (large cohorts, net new customers) were strong. The main incremental upside risk vs the note was whether cRPO/retention would confirm durable growth; reported retention exceeded targets and large-ACV cohorts grew ~33–34%. Guidance action was a margin/FCF lift (op margin to ~18% and FCF margin +100bp), which the note framed as potentially insufficient alone—here it came with a top-line beat, supporting a modestly positive-than-median reaction.

Headline revenue/units appear roughly in the expected $355–370M base-case (large uncertainty flagged pre-release), but management signaled production/deliveries will be below consensus and that formal FY guidance will be withheld—undercutting the key market variable. Margin deteriorated further (gross margin -105% with a large impairment), while liquidity runway was addressed but at the cost of continued heavy cash burn and more cautious volume trajectory.

Revenue and EPS strongly beat the pre-release setup (which assumed near-zero IP with dispersion around an R2 settlement). ACTG instead reported a large single-quarter Wi‑Fi 6 licensing settlement with $60.6M IP revenue and $10.9M IP segment adj. EBITDA, plus Benchmark delivering a record quarter; partially offset by Deflecto’s low adj. EBITDA and nonrecurring legacy litigation/parent expense pressure on GAAP.

Q2 beat was supported by margin expansion (+50 bps to 4.0%) and an improved turnaround/investment profile, but traffic remained slightly soft (industry lag, especially at Outback). The key surprise is the FY26 adj. EPS guide raised to $0.90-$1.00 versus the pre-release expectation of a high bar and likely reaffirm/limited upside, which should drive an above-median reaction despite Q3 tax-rate headwind.

Despite slightly softer residential AC demand hurting net sales, management delivered stronger-than-expected adj. EBITDA supported by improved APM mix/product execution and TiO2 pricing; however, full-year adjusted EBITDA guidance was maintained and largely aligned with the pre-release bar, limiting upside.

The pre-release note expected an EPS/ headline likely to look noisy due to reserve-development optics, but the release delivered a clear upside: management raised full-year 2026 outlook (mid-single-digit adj. EPS/EBITDA ex-cats with ~10% underlying growth) and reported record, excluding-cats growth with expanding segment earnings and stronger liquidity/capital return. Net effect should be modestly positive versus median.

The key upside was guidance: CVS raised FY26 adjusted EPS by $0.60 to $7.90–$8.10 (midpoint well above the pre-release expectation of ~$7.60+), alongside a $2B raise to OCF and higher PCW operating income. Q2 also beat, while the reported MBR of 87.4% included favorable prior-year development (less informative), limiting how much the quarter itself drives the reaction versus the guide.

Top-line and EBITDA largely tracked the pre-release setup (Q1 revenue ~in line; adjusted EBITDA down with specific headwinds; FY27 guidance reaffirmed). The key upside surprise was positive FCF ($72M, up 19%) and improved net leverage (net debt/EBITDA ~3.2x), but the call also confirmed ongoing fixed-service softness (subscriber decline, no stabilization until ViaSat-3 F2 enters) and no resolution on DAT separation/spectrum, which limits incremental upside after the stock’s recent run. Overall this is a modestly negative-to-neutral outcome versus the already-high expectations.

Despite active buyers down 10% (as expected), DIBS delivered a strong GMV (+7% YoY) and a major profitability beat (adj. EBITDA margin ~6%, far above the Q2 guidance range) alongside net revenue of $23.3M well above the (already low) consensus anchor. Most importantly, management upgraded full-year to expect GMV growth independent of macro, partially offset by a take-rate outlook reset lower and a shift likely eliminating 2026 FCF positivity.

Quarterly EPS landed essentially in the range the preview anticipated (flat YoY, and FY guidance reaffirmed), limiting upside. The key negative relative to the yardstick was adj. gross margin coming in ~30 bps down YoY versus the preview’s emphasis on meeting/clearing the ~44%+ margin pathway, adding concern that tariff/mix mitigation isn’t yet translating into the H2 EPS bridge; however, demand/margin and the deal-process headline kept reaction modestly negative to flat.

EPS came in essentially in line with expectations (reported $1.70 operating; notable-items $1.75) while management reiterated >15% full-year EPS growth, but investors had already heavily priced the merger close/timing. Offsetting positives were record AUM/A and broadly positive net flows plus higher AB performance-fee guidance; negatives included a below-plan alternatives drag (despite slight improvement vs plan) and the large GAAP net loss from hedge marks (less relevant to operating EPS).

Q1 P&L beat guidance and also exceeded the pre-release high-end expectations (revenue +100 bps above guidance; EPS $0.03 above high end). More importantly, management maintained the FY constant-currency ARR guide while raised full-year non-GAAP EPS to $1.97–$1.99 (above the note’s $1.93–$1.95), alongside strong demand signals (log consumption doubling in two quarters, net new ARR $85M up 66%)—supporting a modestly positive next-day reaction despite prior expectation that guidance might be unchanged.

Q2 results and FY guidance were a clear beat versus the pre-release setup: revenue/EBITDA/EPS all exceeded the stated expectations, the company raised full-year organic growth and (importantly) raised the innovation revenue target by $50M, while gross margin expanded (+80 bps) and net leverage improved faster than the prior range—offsetting the market’s concern about a low second-half bar.

Q2 charging revenue beat the low-bar setup (18th straight double-digit growth) but full-year adjusted EBITDA guidance was cut to -$25m to -$5m versus the note’s expectation of little-to-no change around roughly the guide midpoint; management also reiterated throughput softness and legacy/OEM-credit wind-down. Revenue was broadly in line (FY revenue midpoint modestly under the note’s ~$440m center) while the EBITDA reset is the main overhang for the next-day move.

Q4 revenue and gross margin beat, with strong Platform ONE progress and supply assurance. However, the key FY27 revenue guide ($1.38–$1.40B) is only modestly above/in-line with the $1.36B Street starting point and below the ~$1.40B+ “reacceleration” bogey highlighted pre-release, limiting upside for the already-rerated multiple.

Q2 EPS ($3.46) and margin expansion were broadly in line with the setup, but the release cut full-year outlook: FY2026 adj. EPS guide lowered to $13.60–$13.80 versus the market’s expected ~$13.80–$13.84 floor. Ongoing Middle East headwinds plus the guide reset likely outweigh otherwise-supportive Genius/segment momentum, implying a modestly negative tape after a big prior run.

Q2 RYTELO net revenue came in above the ~$55.3M consensus ($57.5M reported) while EPS was not clearly a surprise versus the -$0.01 consensus. The larger watch-item—FY26 total RYTELO range—was defended at the mid-to-high end, consistent with a positive tilt, though the gross-to-net widening (20.7% vs 15.3% YoY) remains a known risk that likely limited upside.

Q2 delivered a revenue beat and, more importantly, margin strength (adj. gross margin +170 bps to 48.6%) with raised full-year guidance (net sales growth now 10–12% and adj. EBITDA $210–220M). The only notable offset was higher logistics costs and quality-related tech commissioning costs, but the raised guide and 2027 gross margin floor lift should drive an above-median reaction.

Despite beating adjusted EPS on stronger digital subscription and ad performance, the release carries a negative incremental surprise vs the pre-read on Q3 digital subscription growth (guided 12–15% below the recent-trend/bullive expectations) and operating costs ran above the 8–9% guidance, tempering margin durability. Net: good quarter, likely modest/near-median reaction.

Despite a small same-store NOI decline, management beat on adjusted EBITDA and AFFO ($0.76/sh vs ~$0.73–$0.75 modeled), and—critically—raised full-year AFFO/share and lifted same-store NOI guidance. However, guidance also acknowledged a ~$15M adjusted EBITDA drag from the Big Bear fire and the GIS segment outlook worsened, tempering the upside; overall reaction likely around the median given the stock had already run and the release delivered a mix of beats and offsets.

Q2 results were strong (revenue and EPS growth, and margin expansion), but the market’s bigger focus—U.S. growth durability post-May recall—was hit: management cut the full-year U.S. Omnipod growth outlook to 17–19% from the prior 18–20%, attributing it to weaker Type 2 retention/utilization in the first 90 days. That guidance guide-down likely dominates any beat, keeping the reaction slightly below median despite upside gross margin.

Q2 revenue cleared the high end and, crucially, adjusted EBITDA came in far above both the range and the market’s implied profitability collapse, with margin expanding ~300 bps to 12%. Full-year adjusted EBITDA and subscription guidance were raised, and NDR improved sequentially, though M&T revenue still declined and PathFactory core attrition/headwinds were acknowledged.

The key pre-release swing factor was cash burn/runway and REC-4881 FDA specificity; management lowered FY26 cash opex guidance to $375M (below the <~$390M guide-implied expectation), which is a net positive vs what the market already positioned for, while the main clinical/regulatory items were mostly reaffirmed in timing/format (no explicitly new FDA endpoint agreement disclosed). Options priced a moderate absolute move (~5.6%), and the guidance beat supports a slightly above-median reaction.

Q2 showed modest upside on net sales and a key EBITDA print (385M, ~21.4% margin) that is stronger than the Street zone, while management kept the full-year adj. EBITDA range unchanged at $1.465B–$1.515B. With the direct-delivery recovery arriving early (vs breakeven expectations) but no guide raise on EBITDA, the setup points to a mildly positive/near-median reaction rather than a major re-rating.

Q2 delivered a clear upside on both revenue and profitability: non-GAAP EPS of $0.05 and operating income of $10.2M vs the preview’s mechanical view that consensus/normal midpoints implied EPS closer to breakeven to slightly negative. Gross margin also materially beat (28.6% vs a 23–27% guide) with tariff-refund benefit already embedded in expectations, and Q3 revenue guidance ($310–340M) skewed at the top end vs the preview’s ~flat/soft base-case framing—driving a modestly positive reaction despite the sequential decline outlook.

Revenue and Same-Shack trend largely track the pre-announced/setup quarter, but restaurant-level margin landed at 23.0%—consistent with the feared beef cost drag—while management guided full-year adj. EBITDA and net income to the low end of the already-cut range, reinforcing credibility risk. App momentum and record unit openings were positives, but not enough to offset margin/profit pressure; option market implied a sizable move with downside skew.

Results were modestly ahead on revenue and EPS landed essentially at the expected level, but the bigger surprise was backlog jumping ~40% to $421.8M (well above the ~$320–350M watch range), supporting the quarter’s demand narrative. Gross margin remains a headwind (Q2 GM guided 25–26% vs prior guide band implying ~200 bps YoY pressure), and ASP was only flat-to-slightly up with mix down-price, limiting upside despite stronger backlog.

Gross bookings grew to >$58B (above the high-end of pre-release guidance and above the ~$57.2B Street bar), and adj. EPS grew 35% YoY with free cash flow >$10B—both likely supportive vs a market focused on whether bookings/EBITDA could validate the narratives. Offset: mobility take rate declined ~500bps (with a large UK-model component), and AV remains <0.5% of volume, keeping some narrative risk alive; overall expected reaction modestly positive but not extreme given guidance/action details weren’t provided in the facts.

Q2 revenue ($277.8M) came in above the guide-mid/consensus (~$269.7M) while bookings ($295.9M) exceeded the ~guide-mid expectation (~$282.5M). The key upside was an FY26 FCF guidance raise to at least $480M (vs ≥$465M prior; consensus anchored ≥$465M), alongside a much stronger EBITDA margin (36.4% vs a ~35% target and expectation of ~~32% adj. margin). Q3 revenue/bookings show deceleration and a known negative FCF item from the Amex payout, but the operational/FCF upside likely dominates, supporting a moderately positive post-print move.

Quarterly top line and EPS were essentially in-line once the ODM net-commission accounting reset is accounted for. The main upside surprise was strong margin expansion/EBITDA ($98M, 18.7% margin) and progress toward VCP monetization (25 RCV at $286M, +65% YoY). The offsetting negative was Restaurants remaining soft with a decline in restaurant revenue and EBITDA (−6% ex-hardware; adj. EBITDA −15%), plus cited $20–$30M chip-cost headwind and delayed hardware refreshes—likely keeping investor focus on de-risking back-half vs the demanding Q4 EBITDA math. Full-year guidance was maintained, so the net reaction is modestly positive-to-neutral rather than a beat-driven rerating.

Revenue was essentially in-line/slightly above the $44.71M Zacks consensus (reported $44.8M) driven by HPC lease strength and newly operational CB-3, but adjusted EBITDA swung more negative to −$18.3M (pre-revenue costs) versus −$4.1M expected tone from the note. Guidance was reaffirmed (incremental 250–500 MW/yr), with the most material incremental items (Anthropic contract and Abernathy proceeds timing) largely aligned with the market’s framework, keeping the net reaction near median.

Q2 delivered a sizable upside versus consensus (revenue $34M vs ~$29.1M; GAAP EPS -$0.04 vs -$0.03). More importantly, management raised FY26 guidance again—revenue to at least $140M and gross margin to at least 28% (vs prior $130M)—which should resolve the market’s prior H2 ramp skepticism; demand/order momentum (Europe $24M order + major Stark Future contract) further supports the positive reaction.

On revenue, reported net revenues ($757M GAAP implied) landed close to what the preview framed as an “optically ugly but cadence-driven” setup. The key deltas were in profitability optics: adjusted EBITDA ($76M) was only modestly better than the guidance-implied band but still down YoY, with margin/FCF pressured by DSO (Q2 $19M unlevered FCF, 25% conversion). Management reiterated full-year revenue/adj. EBITDA and FCF ranges and reiterated 2H weighting (~53%), keeping the stock reaction modest-to-negative versus an already-prepped narrative.

Q3 revenue and non-GAAP EPS both beat the pre-release consensus, and management raised FY26 revenue guidance (including organic outlook from prior down to flat/up) while delivering a strong sequential EBITDA margin rebound. While Q4 organic is guided to low single-digit decline and Multiomics NA remains below prior-year levels, the guidance lift and improved margins are likely the dominant drivers for a positive reaction.

The key issue was guidance: FY2026 adjusted EBITDA was cut (top end lowered to $865–$885), below the note’s base case expectation that guidance would move to the upper half (or be raised). Q2 adjusted EPS of $0.38 undershot the $0.47 working consensus (roughly a 19% miss). Positives were supportive contract wins/renewal and margin holding above 70%, but the lowered EBITDA guide and aftermarket deferral outweighed.

Q2 ORLADEYO grew ~10% y/y on a comparable basis and pediatric prescriptions/persistence signals were strong, while non-GAAP costs were lowered and margin improved (non-GAAP op profit $113.2M). The key market-moving item was guidance: management raised full-year 2026 total revenue to $690–$715M (above the note’s street positioning), but ORLADEYO guidance was held, making the total reaction likely closer to median than a large beat.

The quarter lacked a reported revenue/EPS beat versus stale consensus, with network revenue down 34% and no guidance reinstatement. Offsetting positives were reaffirmed margin/cash-generation direction (July margin several hundred bps above Q2, targeting ~$50M annual adjusted EBITDA minus CapEx) and tangible Pro/AI progress (ChatGPT ad profitability, AI Front Desk live with ~80% retention, improved pro win rates/capacity), which should limit downside despite the large non-cash impairment.

Q2 top line and parts/services were better than the pre-print setup, but the quarter again underdelivered on the margin/joint thesis: adj. EBITDA margin (10.4%) fell short of the ~11% underwriting, and the key overhang was confirmed with a FY26 adj. EBITDA guide cut to $160M–$175M (below both the pre-note and narrowed H2 bridge), with heavy back-loading (1/3 in Q3, 2/3 in Q4).

Results and EPS exceeded a bar that was already set tightly by guidance/consensus, and importantly management raised FY gross profit and non-GAAP EPS outlook. However, gross margin fell more than expected (70 bps YoY to 20.1%) and services growth lagged, capping the upside and making the reaction likely positive but not a blowout.

Revenue and Land momentum were roughly in line with the preview, but the key downside came from cutting FY adjusted free cash flow to $70–$80M (vs prior $100–$115M) citing fuel and the nonrecurring self-insurance charge—exactly the 2H cash/EBITDA math risk highlighted pre-print. Reported adjusted EBITDA was also below the implied “ex-Fuel/Self-insurance” normalization, consistent with margin pressure and making the market less likely to re-rate on an otherwise solid top line.

Results and the call narrative came in stronger than the pre-release base case (notably Experiences: record revenue/OI with margin and raised OI guidance to the high end) alongside improved parks attendance. With revenue/EPS only modestly above the Street but guidance/segment mix clearer than expected, the release likely skews to a modestly positive next-day reaction versus the pre-print setup.

Q3 EPS ($+12% to $4.37) and revenue (+5% to $84.8B) are essentially in line with the pre-release consensus ($4.37; $84.89B). Guidance was raised slightly but not meaningfully versus expectations, while management lowered International revenue growth to ~8% (vs ~flat/positive expectations in the note), limiting upside and keeping reaction near median.

Revenue landed essentially in line with the pre-release range, and adjusted gross margin/product GM improved for the 7th straight quarter. The key negative was guidance: FY26 revenue was tightened to $300–350M (midpoint $325M), below the market’s low-end $311M and below what the note framed as the survivable/likely trimming path; additionally, EPS was pressured by warrant/derivative fair-value dynamics, reinforcing downside risk to headline earnings despite better operating conversion progress.

Revenue slightly beat the top end of guidance and management kept the FY2026 +40% growth framework, with additional coverage improving. However, liquidity/covenant risk was worse than the note’s ‘watch the cash line’ setup (unrestricted cash $11.2M < $15M and direct margin covenant breach), plus gross loss widened and EBITDA remains deeply negative—likely capping upside despite better bookings.

Revenue broadly met the Street view, while EPS benefited from the IEEPA tariff refund already part of the earnings-debate setup; the main incremental pressure/offset came from weaker-than-expected margin trends (gross and adj. EBITDA margins down sharply) despite leverage improving to 3.74x. FCF also looked strong, but the margin deterioration and American Performance decline were not fully anticipated, keeping the expected reaction near median. Guidance was reaffirmed, limiting upside.

EPS beat was driven by higher adjusted net income (+$0.12/sh vs prior-year) and lower FY interest expense, but EBITDA margin came in at 25.9% vs the market’s implied ~27%-plus trajectory for the “2H step-up.” Full-year revenue and $458M adj. EBITDA guidance were maintained (not increased), so reaction should be modestly positive rather than a rerating.

Results slightly topped EPS and reinforced growth momentum (record pipeline and strong commercial wins), but full-year guidance was largely held (tightened ranges with unchanged midpoints), limiting upside. With the market already pricing a ~4.6–4.9% move and prior beat expectations, the net reaction is likely mildly positive rather than a major rerating.

Revenue and adjusted pretax losses are in line with the trough-quarter setup (FCF usage and rebalancing charges largely as expected) and FY27 outlook was reaffirmed. A modest positive surprise came from stronger-than-anticipated Q1 signings trajectory (3.9B Q1) / mix commentary, but there were no guidance or cash-walk disappointments, keeping the reaction near median.

The release confirmed the key items the note focused on (BROADEN-2 accelerated to YE26 and cash runway into 2029; KT-579 timing in Q4 2026), which were largely expected; the main new upside is stronger-than-modeled Q2 collaboration revenue ($65M vs $32.8M consensus) driven by specific milestone timing. The primary offset is higher-than-expected operating expenses (R&D $119.5M, +22% sequential), implying margin pressure despite the non-core timing-driven P&L.

Q2 revenue and software both beat the pre-release bar (services-led beat with software also strong), and importantly FY26 guidance was raised (total and software) with better cash burn. EBITDA is still negative but the margin wasn’t a clear deterioration versus expectations, so the reaction should be moderately positive rather than euphoric.

Q2 adj. EPS of $2.70 beat the pre-release $2.42 whisper (despite revenue/units softness), supported by 110 bps margin expansion to 9.3% and self-help. However, full-year guidance was cut vs the note’s expectation framework (RV shipment forecast lowered; FY adj. EPS reduced to $8.25-$8.75), tempering the upside and likely limiting the stock move in a deal-compressed regime.

The big item (CMS reimbursement restored) largely matched what the Street was trading for, and FY26 net sales midpoint ($850M) remains essentially in-line with the ~$843M consensus from the pre-release note. Management did raise adjusted EBITDA guidance to $95–98M (consistent with restoration to pre-May levels), but Q2 gross margin (71.7%) was pressured by mix/credit and launches, limiting upside.

Q2 results beat the guided range with record adj. EBITDA ($10M, ~13% margin vs $4–6M; and WAU at an all-time high) and management raised FY2026 guidance to low-teens revenue growth and ~10% EBITDA margin. The size of the beats (especially profitability and WAU) goes beyond what was already framed as the 'beat cadence' in the note, supporting a moderately positive reaction rather than a fade.

Q2 delivered upside vs the pre-release yardstick (record revenue and higher-than-expected gross margin to 44.1%), and EPS of $0.65/$0.68 beat the ~$0.60 anchor; Q3 revenue guide ($137–$139M) is largely in line with what the note already assumed, so the primary incremental catalyst is margin/EPS quality rather than top-line guidance. Minor offsets were the explicit pull-ahead sales note and mixed regional weakness (notably India/Middle East down).

Q2 net sales beat and management raised FY26 organic cc revenue guidance (2.25–3.25% vs prior 1–3%), a bigger directional positive given the market’s low-bar setup tied to US/organic reacceleration. However, EPS was roughly in line and margins declined (gross -120 bps; operating -210 bps) amid channel/manufacturing investments, limiting upside despite the stronger demand/segment growth and higher buyback.

Revenue and EPS land essentially where the thin/low-confidence consensus range implied (EPS ~$0.00–$0.02; revenue ~$8.4–$8.9M). Main incremental upside is the large gross-margin recovery to 14.8%, but that is largely consistent with the expectation that Q1 was distorted by customer shortfall/margin compression; no clear guidance raise beyond “similar backlog pace.”

Q2 revenue/segment framing looked mixed versus the pre-announced setup (continuing ops revenue cited just under $2B; no explicit consensus-beating figure provided), but the company raised full-year guidance on sales and EBITDA. Management also provided incremental detail on stranded costs, working-capital benefits, and H2 headwinds (working capital separation headwind; synthetics normalization), yielding a modestly positive but not outsized expected reaction given much of the sequential Q2 weakness was already pre-priced.

With consensus describing a trough-year setup, the quarter’s key items (SNAP headwind absorbed, market-share losses narrowing, and free-cash-flow guidance essentially unchanged) read largely in-line. The incremental +$100M mostly-marketing spend and the improved market-share/near-term consumption trajectory are modest positives that weren’t fully the center of the base case, limiting upside reaction.

Operating EPS of $1.12 beat the $1.08 consensus despite a known weak variable investment income backdrop, but management also guided that VII will remain below target for the rest of the year (offset by strong Institutional Markets APTOI and Life run-rate ahead of guidance). Buyback guidance implied a lower 2H repurchase pace, tempering cash-return expectations; deal-close commentary was largely 'on track' and thus less likely to be a fresh upside catalyst.

Reported EPS of $2.13 grew 18% and appears modestly above the ~$2.05 consensus/“upper half of guide” bar, while EBITDA margin hit a record 18.5% (70 bps expansion). The key offset is organic revenue growth decelerating to ~4% with large AMS/DRS installations slipping into 2H—so the quarter’s momentum looks better on margins/EPS than on top-line demand. Guidance was raised for full-year profit and Q2 EBITDA cleared the prior midpoint, but the Malaysia/optics and merger-arb overhang likely capped upside, keeping the expected reaction near-median-positive rather than strong.

The key surprise was guidance: full-year NOI was cut to ~$36.2M (from $37.1M, ~-2.4%) citing delayed industrial lease-up and DC multifamily headwinds, while industrial leasing still hasn’t converted to signed leases (only ~20.7k sq ft signed vs 97.5k negotiating). Tailwinds from mining were mentioned but not enough to offset the demand/lease-up concerns, pointing to a likely negative-to-moderately negative post-earnings reaction.

Despite revenue growing to $173.5M (below the ~$177–179M expectation in the note) and bookings showing strength, gross margin (21.5% vs expectations ~mid-20s) and adjusted profitability deteriorated sharply (adj. EBITDA margin 8%). The key offsetting item—guidance reset—cuts FY26 adjusted EBITDA to $78–84M (below consensus in the note), which is the dominant driver of the likely negative reaction.

EPS beat is meaningful versus the pre-framed low bar (>$2.68 sequential floor) and full-year non-GAAP EPS guidance was raised to a midpoint of $11.30 versus the market’s ~$11.05 area; the upside narrative is reinforced by DSA net book-to-bill (1.9x) and backlog, though the operational beat still included notable nonoperating items and guidance tax-rate uncertainty added offsetting noise.

Q2 results beat on both revenue and adj. EPS (driven by tariff refunds and stronger Doors/EBITDA), but the key market yardsticks were margin and H2—management guided to weaker Q3 margin and specifically flagged Roofing volume/demand pull-forward into Q2 with Iran inflation worsening, which offsets the operational positives and drives an overall below-median reaction.

MTRN delivered record Q2 value-added sales ($308.2M), exceeding the note’s implied VA bar (~$305M) and reported a large EPS beat ($1.90 vs the note’s ~$1.60 management-implied bar). Most importantly, it raised FY26 adj. EPS guidance to $6.80–$7.20 (midpoint $7.00), clearly above the note’s $6.00–$6.50 setup, plus strong FCF and expanding margins/backlog—driving a likely above-median positive reaction.

Q2 delivered both upside revenue/EPS vs the pre-release consensus anchors and a material EBITDA margin expansion (350 bps sequential to 17.3%), plus a faster-than-planned synergy execution ($29.4M; ~$17M realized). However, demand was described as down mid-single digits in 1H with soft conditions expected to persist, and Ag-tech backlog fell sharply (-34% YoY), partially offsetting the operational beat. Guidance was reiterated at the same sales/EPS range, with the implied mix leaving some incremental conservatism vs the pre-release back-half bridge risk case.

Revenue and adjusted EBITDA inflected sharply higher (and margins expanded via High Purity Cellulose), offset by a worsening Paperboard/high-yield pulp adjusted loss. Guidance for FY2026 transition year/strategic review timing was not meaningfully changed vs expectations, so the reaction should be modestly positive rather than a blowout.

Reported operating EPS and revenue were broadly in line with the pre-release setup, but while margins improved (expense ratio down, strong NII), the key “ask” in this setup was a guidance raise/clear underwriting upside; management reaffirmed FY underwriting/fee guidance and noted a mix-driven non-cat loss ratio uptick. Net effect: modestly positive fundamentals offset by lack of guidance catalyst, consistent with a near-median reaction.

Q3 continued-ops adjusted EPS of –$0.26 was slightly worse than the –$0.24 consensus, but management reaffirmed FY26 adj. EPS $3.90–$4.10 and FY27 $5.40–$5.60, matching expectations; the main deltas were smaller-than-expected Gas Utilities loss (+) and higher corporate/interest-related pressure (–). With guidance unchanged, the tape reaction should be modestly positive.

Revenue of ~$783M was below the key sequential bar ($781.5M was the credibility threshold) and ~below the ~$804M consensus framing in the note, while management declined to reaffirm/update 2026 revenue growth guidance and acknowledged a narrowed path to the prior $4B-by-2027 run-rate. Offsetting positives were regulatory filings and strong patient starts/referrals, but the guidance/growth uncertainty and competitive pressure on nebulized Tyvaso likely dominate.

Revenue missed the guide/consensus (83.9M vs 87.44M consensus pinned to the 87.5M midpoint) and adjusted EPS (0.04 vs 0.19 consensus) undershot sharply, despite strong bookings/book-to-bill (1.14 consolidated; Sensors 1.44). Q3 revenue guidance ($84–89M) was broadly in line versus what the market had baked in, so the reaction should skew negative, driven by the earnings shortfall and KELK shipment delay.

Q2 topped the quarter setup (organic outgrowth; margins +100 bps to 11.3%) and EPS beat consensus. More importantly, FY adjusted EPS guidance was raised to $5.05–$5.30 versus $5.18 street, with sales/margin/FCF maintained—offset slightly by a lowered full-year margin midpoint from incremental industrial R&D.

Q2 revenue and EPS beat the already-expected upper band (revenue above the ~$895–897M consensus cluster; EPS well above the $0.15 consensus), while the bigger read-through was the strength in orders/margins: book-to-bill at 1.32 and gross margin expansion to 22.6% plus an upward-validated Q3 gross margin target. Q3 revenue guidance ($945–975M) lands above the ~$920–950M framing in the note, supporting a continued recovery slope.

Results beat on sales ($545M vs ~$531.7M) and EPS ($0.57 vs ~$0.50), with SSS at 8% matching the upper-end of what the note said could clear whispers. However, management tempered margin outlook wording: EBITDA guidance narrowed only modestly and full-year EPS remains $1.70–$1.75 (i.e., not pushed above the already-top-of-range consensus), while Q4 calls for 300–400 bps of margin compression tied to elevated base-oil/lubricant costs—tempering the upside reaction.

Q4 delivered a sizable EPS beat (record margins) driven by another large raw-material timing windfall, which the market largely expected given the pre-release framing. However, the key is FY27: the new FY27 EPS midpoint ($4.65) is below the market’s embedded ~$5.40–$5.50, with weak free-cash-flow conversion (~20% of adjusted NI) and an additional interest/FX headwind—likely muting upside despite the strong quarter.

Revenue was essentially in line with the ~$1.50B setup and EPS was not given in the pre-note as a reliable rebased consensus. The key surprise was the $90–$100M FY26 adj. EBITDA guide—raised vs the prior setup of a de-facto low bar—while downside was weaker-than-expected profitability for the quarter (adj. EBITDA $19.1M vs the $10–25M estimate range, and well below the prior-year pro forma), leaving a modestly positive but not outsized reaction.

Q2 revenue was roughly in-line and FY adjusted EBITDA guidance was reaffirmed within the expected $485–535M range, but the quarter’s adjusted EBITDA of $115M (below the ~$124M sequential step-up implied by the note) plus soft volume keeps sentiment constrained. Offsetting positives were the raised impact-program target (to at least $70M) and stronger-than-prior operating cash flow.

BXC delivered a clear upside on sales and—more importantly for this name—margin/EBITDA: gross margin expanded to 17.2% (above the market’s ~15.3–15.6% anchor) with structural and specialty margins beating, and adjusted EBITDA up ~33% despite the duty benefit. Management also guided Q3 specialty margin (18–19%) while indicating structural should normalize (8.5–9.5%), limiting downside surprises; net result should drive a positive re-rate versus the earnings setup.

Revenue came slightly above the $297.7M consensus ($305M vs. $297.7M), largely explained by the mechanical home-game swing already baked into expectations. The major surprise was profitability: Adjusted OIBDA fell to ~$12M (and operating loss vs. profit), far worse than the note’s ~$40–45M expected range, with BravesVision cash/timing and elevated expense commentary reinforcing downside margin risk. With no formal guidance, the reaction skews negative despite the revenue beat.

EPS was essentially in line with the market’s pre-sold setup, with FY26 EPS and FCF guidance maintained. Offsets: (1) Q2 FCF came in meaningfully higher than the note’s preoccupation with working-capital/FCF delivery (positive), but (2) incremental AC inventory absorption in H2 and the Ibn Sina JV downtime (equity earnings hit) are additional drags versus what the note framed as already-the-main risk, likely capping upside.

EPS ($5.07) was essentially in line with consensus ($5.10) but the call leaned positive (record FCF, strong well/test outperformance, cost reductions, and reaffirmed FY2026 capex/growth). With guidance maintained and the Street already primed for a beat from price capture/FCF, the incremental upside likely looks limited, implying a near-median reaction.

Q2 adjusted EPS and EBITDA beat the pre-release setup, but more importantly management raised FY26 guidance (EBITDA and U.S. RevPAR upward, plus global net rooms to ~1.5%), moving the market off a 'narrow/maintain' base case. Demand/unit commentary improved to nearly flat U.S. net rooms YoY, reinforcing the guidance raise.

Revenue and EPS land close to the market’s weak/low-quality Q2 anchor, with the bigger story being gross margin contraction (41% vs 46%) and execution/mix pressure in APC. While backlog is strong ($14.3M; largest since 2018, with $10.5M in next 12 months) and management maintained the “FY2026 revenues exceed 2025” guidance, much of the upside is still pushed into 2027 (APC and potential data center conversions), limiting near-term rerating.

The quarter was far stronger than the already-full-priced setup: revenue and especially Data Analytics growth/GP mix re-rated, and management raised FY2026 guidance materially (to $340–350M revenue and $47–51M adj. EBITDA) well above the pre-print base case. Despite the PREPA headline, management clarified no 2026 financial impact is included in guidance, limiting downside surprises; margins also improved with lower G&A and rising EBITDA.

Guidance delivered a clear upside versus what the note framed as the key binary (FY26 adjusted EBITDA update): adjusted EBITDA was raised to $270–280M (above the $236–247M baseline), alongside higher written premium growth (16–17% vs 15–16%). Operationally, loss ratio and marketplace trends looked disciplined/strong (upmarket sales and higher marketplace revenue), offsetting concerns around H2 conservatism.

Revenue missed expectations mainly from lower metal prices and a timing shift of Greens Creek concentrate sales into Q3, which the pre-release note flagged as a key headline risk. Offsetting that, management delivered strong cash generation (FCF nearly record; $500M+ FY FCF at current prices) with margin/cash flow strength, while guidance improved for Greens Creek and Lucky Friday costs—supportive for the stock despite the Keno Hill production cut.

Revenue outperformed the $462.35M consensus (reported $491.4M) but adjusted EPS landed essentially flat vs $1.06 expectation, while margins show mix-driven pressure (Fuel Specialties margin down; management flagged further sequential Fuel margin pressure in Q3). With guidance effectively matching the already-prepped ~$1.05–$1.07 EPS range, the setup points to a muted reaction rather than a sizable rerating.

Management raised FY revenue and non-GAAP EPS guidance and reported expanding performance margin (gross margin +1.3 pts; non-GAAP performance margin +9 pts). However, revenue/EPS beats are hard to score cleanly because the pre-release note flagged major EPS accounting ambiguity tied to the acquired IPR&D charge; guidance upside was broadly expected, implying a modest-to-moderate positive reaction rather than a sharp rerating.

Results landed near the market’s low expectations on revenue (only ~in-line vs $425.8M) but beat EPS (Adj. EPS $1.96 vs $1.81 consensus) despite EBITDA pressure. The key incremental upside was the Project Apollo raise (plant component $15M→at least $20M; annualized savings target to at least $25M) alongside 35.5% gross margin and commentary for further Q4 expansion; demand stayed mixed (frozen beverage down, but bakery headwind peaking and service gap expected to close).

Revenue beat (and demand/capital pipeline commentary was strong), but margins were weak with meaningful launch-cost drag and—most importantly—free cash flow guidance was cut (to $7–15M), worsening the already-problematic H2 cash/margin bridge despite raised sales and maintained adj. EBITDA.

Revenue and adjusted EBITDA materially exceeded the note’s base-case setup (operating leverage +7–9% above the mechanical $23.56M expectation) and management maintained FY27 guidance; however, gross margin upside was partially tariff/refund-related and Q1 implies slower intra-year ramp with backlog ($~24M) well below the ~$28–32M range flagged as validating for the FY27 cadence, adding headline risk.

Despite the expected margin normalization (gross margin below Q1), OSS delivered higher-than-modeled Q2 revenue (~$9.3M vs ~$8.8M base case) and record bookings (book-to-bill ~1.7), plus it raised FY2026 revenue growth guidance to 25–30% (above the prior 20–25% band where expectations already sat near the top). The legal settlement drove GAAP losses, but non-GAAP EPS was less negative than expected, supporting a modestly positive reaction percentile.

Q2 headline EPS was $10.10 vs $8.22 consensus, but this came off a quarter already framed by the note as requiring near-perfect capture (market priced-in ~97% capture). Reported capture was 125% system-wide (112% normalized) with notable Hawaii lag gain, yet management flagged Q3 Hawaii capture to fall below the typical 100–110% range due to turnaround costs/imports—an incremental downside to durability expectations that drives a modestly negative reaction despite the beat.

Operational demand/orders were solid (orders +8.8% YoY; AMC orders up 17.1%) but guidance disappointed: full-year ex-refunds adjusted EBITDA margin was cut to 21.3% and free cash flow guidance reduced by $50M to $600M, signaling working-capital drag and weakening H2 margin/FCF credibility vs what the market expected from an unchanged guide.

The key incremental positive vs the pre-release setup was operational/portfolio momentum: oil/BOE production exceeded guidance and Talos raised full-year 2026 stand-alone production guidance despite excluding the pending acquisition. Additionally, the BP preferential right was declined (removing the main deal-scope overhang) and balance sheet actions improved flexibility, supporting a mildly positive-to-positive tape reaction.

Adj. operating EPS printed $1.51 vs a ~$1.90 consensus yardstick in the preview note, but the shortfall is largely tied to the already-preannounced alts underperformance and includes severance drag that management said is offset by expense savings by year-end. The bigger incremental catalyst risk is the deal/strategic-review tone (not detailed in the provided facts), while operating momentum (excess capital, cash conversion, and strong retirement flows/fee-based revenue) should limit downside.

Revenue and gross margin came in materially worse than the pre-release setup (Energy margin pressure deeper; GM 4.9% vs ~6–6.5% expected). Management nonetheless maintained full-year 2026 adj EPS and adj EBITDA guidance and reiterated the renewables project completion timeline, with backlog nearly $14B beating expectations—offsetting the operating disappointment but leaving credibility/liquidity risk (FCF guide cut ~$200M).

FY26 total adj. EBITDA guidance was affirmed (no overall cut), which is directionally consistent with the note’s base case, but management raised Offshore Energy Services guidance and simultaneously flagged an ~$8M drag from supply-chain delays hitting Government Services profitability. With the key risk in the note centered on Government Services margin inflection and R&M/2H ramp, the net surprise is mixed—likely modestly negative/near-median reaction rather than a clear beat.

Revenue rose to $240.9M (+~2% vs the ~$236M consensus), but EPS was roughly flat at $1.16 vs expectations around ~$1.22 and margins/FCF deteriorated (YTD adj. FCF collapsed to $3.7M on higher capex). Guidance was maintained though management indicated trending toward the lower end, which offsets the revenue beat and tempers the market reaction.

Stub-period operational beat (top-end total volumes, oil at the high end) combined with a Q3 capital step-up and reaffirmation of ≥$1B 2027 synergies, plus improved capital allocation (43% reinvestment) and completed $1.25B 2026 debt reduction. Q2 revenue/EPS comparisons were largely pre-disclaimed as analytically noisy in the preview, so the market should react mainly to the new/changed forward guide and capital-return/deleveraging signals.

Q2 delivered a material revenue beat ($1.23B vs $1.0796B consensus) alongside strong margin expansion (EBITDA margin to 10.4%, E&M to 10.8% vs the anticipated ~8% core reversion). Management also raised FY26 revenue and EBITDA guidance (midpoints implying ~9% EBITDA margin; higher than the already-raised/expected guide in the note). With backlog up to $4.55B (supports the visibility thesis) and leverage very low, the release should clear well above the market’s base/bull setup.

Q2 EBITDA landed $53M (within the $50–55M range) with sales boosted by sulfur pass-through; however FY26 guidance was raised (adj. EBITDA to $195–207 and adj. FCF to $45–55) with stated legacy growth and Calabrian contributing synergies. Cash-flow and leverage optics were a check, but the guidance raise and firmer underlying demand/tailwinds likely drive a mildly positive, not outsized, reaction.

Adjusted EPS of $3.64 (and EBITDA $639M/$490M ex-50% RVO) materially exceeds the $2.39–$2.67 consensus range cited in the pre-release note, though the broader refining/margin backdrop and logistics tailwinds were largely anticipated. Guidance was reaffirmed for DKL (FY2026 EBITDA $520–$560M) with constructive Q3 throughput/margin commentary, so reaction is more moderate than a typical beat would be given the stock’s already high price and priced-in beat risk.

The note expected a Q2 headline beat driven largely by commodity/derivative effects, so the reported GAAP turnaround is mostly anticipated. However, the release delivered weaker-than-modeled production (41.5 kbbl/d, down sequentially and YoY) alongside higher capex (to $54M) which is a negative incremental surprise versus the base/bull setups; guidance action was not provided in the facts here, keeping conviction limited.

Revenue came in modestly above the pre-release consensus, while operating loss improved and cash flow turned positive—both consistent with the “Q2 trough” recovery setup. The key demand/backlog items (bookings growth) and tariff refund offset were in line with what the note highlighted, so upside is likely limited (guidance maintained as a moderate operating loss with stronger H2 weighting, no surprise cut).

Underlying underwriting held up (CY combined 94.7%, up on earned premium) and management reaffirmed ~15% Belmont Core GWP growth, but the expense ratio came in worse than target (40.9%, ~4.5 pts above long-term) and Specialty premiums fell sharply (-36%), with no evidence yet that premium acceleration is material enough to de-risk the back-half ramp—netting a slightly negative-to-neutral setup versus a fragile consensus where the big swing risk was Belmont credibility.

With Q2 revenue largely pre-baked ($341M) and FY guidance maintained at ~$1.48B/$4.85 versus consensus above it, the primary delta for the stock is downside margin/EPS optics: H1 operating margin compressed to 17.9% (vs 20%) on higher SG&A/A&P, despite tariff refunds already recognized in Q2 ($6.9M). The one standout positive was stronger H1 cash flow (OCF $46M) and inventory reduction, but it likely isn’t enough to overcome the conservative guidance vs Street.

Q2 handily beat consensus on both revenue and adjusted EPS (record results with expanding operating margins). More importantly for price reaction, FY2026 revenue guidance was raised above consensus and EPS range narrowed/shifted upward, while demand/backlog and aftermarket parts remained supportive; the main offset was weaker gross margin mix (capital-driven) and caution on capital project timing for Q3.

Q2 results were largely pre-positioned, and EPS sits essentially in-line with what the Street expected given prior curtailments. The key incremental negative was the Q3 phosphate volume guide cut (1.1–1.4 Mt) and sequential stripping-margin deterioration, partially offset by permanent SG&A savings and lower CapEx.

Q2 EPS and revenue were below the already-cut consensus, while guidance action was negative: full-year capex was cut (a partial offset), but OSB economics deteriorated further and management guided Siding/OSB such that consolidated earnings quality remains pressured. Despite a siding price/tenor-positive print (26% margin), the key narrative is OSB-driven weakness plus timing/weather-related caveats, which typically drives a downside reaction when the Street is already bearish on EBITDA durability.

EPS loss narrowed to -$0.26 vs -$0.29 a year ago, which is modestly better than the pre-release setup that anticipated a low-bar EPS print; however, the more decision-relevant item disappointed—full-year 2026 production and sales were cut and capex was raised (funding pressure vs the market’s “coal is noise; financing is key” framing). Brook Mine NPV/timeline was updated but largely treated as already known, and liquidity/share repurchases were supportive but not enough to offset the negative guidance impulse.

The key delta vs the pre-release setup is management shifting to the top half of FY26 EPS (improved H2 visibility), with SiEnergy showing >15% organic growth and a strong meter backlog. Q2 GAAP EPS/seasonality was already low-signal, but management also highlighted modestly softer first-half water performance, partially offsetting the bullish H2/visibility tone.

EPS was broadly in line with the pre-release band, and FY26 guidance ($525–575M) was maintained. The key incremental positive versus expectations was the Japan suspension impact coming in below the modeled quarter drag ($105M vs anticipated ~$140–160M), alongside stronger efficiency targets and record Group Insurance earnings, supporting a modestly positive reaction despite the lack of raised FY numbers.

Q2 adjusted and GAAP EPS came in well above the $0.65 consensus ($0.82 adjusted), and management attributed the outperformance to new rates plus stronger-than-anticipated Texas HB 4384 benefits. Despite the EPS beat, O&M growth remained a concern (sequential still expected to rise into/through the back half), and incremental tailwinds appear more back-half/phasing-related, implying a more moderate than outsized reaction.

Q2 adj. EPS of $0.16 missed the $0.17 consensus by ~6%, but guidance was reaffirmed at $2.02–$2.07 with a 2H-weighted earnings outlook—so the main rate/GenCo story didn’t change. O&M was pressured by storms and union negotiations (margin headwind), partially offset by cost optimizations and rate step-ins; revenue wasn’t provided, and guidance was already widely expected to be reaffirmed, limiting upside surprise.

The quarter’s headline EPS benefited from tariff refunds, but the magnitude ($15.3M recognized) appears somewhat below the note’s $18.6M base case; additionally, management flagged sustainability concerns (wholesale gross margin ex-refund materially lower) and raised 2H tariff uncertainty to 12.5% effective July 24. Overall reaction is likely modest because the refund was already a key, largely priced-in catalyst, offset by the still-strong reported EPS and inventory growth plan.

EPS (non-GAAP) of $0.38 matched the ~$0.38 consensus and management reaffirmed its 5–7% through-2027 EPS growth and the Q1 2027 deal-close framework. No new negative or positive regulatory/timing update beyond what the note already flagged as the key swing factor, so reaction is likely muted/near-median.

Adjusted EPS of $0.45 was slightly below the $0.47 consensus (~-4%), but the company reaffirmed FY26 and long-term growth targets and reiterated the California/Nevada timing within the original framework; key offset was stronger-than-expected Great Basin contracting (1.0 Bcf/d secured) and higher incremental margin expectations from the 48-inch conversion, likely limiting downside despite the modest EPS miss.

The quarter beat on the metric the note flagged as decisive: adjusted EBITDA $93M vs a $77–80M guide (~+16% at midpoint), alongside record Water Infrastructure revenue ($102M) and ~58% gross margin. Management also raised FY26 capex to $250–290M (supporting higher infrastructure awards) while reaffirming high-end Water Infrastructure growth, making the overall setup more bullish than what the note’s 'optical EPS risk' centered on.

The key incremental surprise vs the pre-release setup is management lowering FY26 outlook (driven by a more expensive HIYA DTC digital marketing environment, North Asia softness, and a packaging issue that reduced Rise guidance by ~$30–$40M with added margin pressure). The preliminary HIYA goodwill impairment and elevated persistent tax rate reinforce a weaker forward earnings profile; despite good news on cash/FCF and Rising door expansion, guidance disappointment should drive a below-median stock reaction.

Core and profitability momentum (core rev +14%, SaaS GM +75%, and third straight positive adj. EBITDA) were directionally supportive versus the note’s skepticism, and management reiterated the H2 > H1 inflection. However, the pre-release setup flagged headline revenue consensus as potentially too high due to hub-amortization runoff, limiting the magnitude of any “beat,” while EPS and detailed guidance (midpoint/quant change) were not provided for a clean consensus comparison.

Core EPS materially exceeded the pre-release $2.32 consensus on strong underwriting (combined ratio down to 91.5%) and especially record alternative-investment returns (7.1% vs 1.2% prior year). Premium growth/renewal rates were also stronger than the modest bar implied by guidance, while no guidance reset was indicated; the Charleston Harbor gain moved closer to expectations but was pushed to Q3, limiting downside.

Revenue of $260M (+11% YoY) beat the modeled bar (~$250–253M / ≥~7% growth), and underlying momentum (claims +8%, new sales +60%) supported it. EPS $0.63 also cleared the ~$0.58–$0.60 modeled range, but elevated by ~$0.07 of one-time CERIS settlement—still net income growth (+18% ex-items) reduces the risk of a pure timing beat. No guidance was provided, so the reaction is driven by growth/ramp signals and clean demand, not forward math.

PLMR beat on adjusted EPS and raised FY2026 adjusted net income again (to $270–$280M) above the already-high consensus expectation for a likely 9th raise. However, the adjusted combined ratio rose to 76.7% (worse than prior-year and at/above the market’s margin watch level), and crop/casualty mix continues pushing loss ratios higher, tempering upside.

Q4 delivered a record $8.3B revenue and $2.28 EPS, both well above the pre-release expectations anchored to guidance ceilings/whispers. Q1 FY27 guidance was raised versus what the note implied (notably $2.80–$2.90 EPS and $9.0–$9.3B revenue), while margin expansion, improved inventory/working capital, and solid book-to-bill further reduced downside risk.

Q2 results showed expanding profitability (GM +35%, adj. EBITDA up) and, crucially, guidance was raised for both potash and Trio production while keeping Q3 pricing ranges intact—supportive versus the preview’s base case of simply hitting guidance. The only offset is that reported EPS/revenue vs consensus is hard to compute precisely given the preview’s explicitly unreliable/dispersed EPS consensus, so directionality comes mainly from the raised production guidance and cost/throughput commentary.

Q2 delivered an upside beat on both revenue (+1% vs $1.41B consensus) and adjusted EPS ($0.63 vs $0.54; +17%), alongside a clear margin expansion (EBITDA margin +150 bps). The key new driver is guidance: management raised full-year 2026 revenue by $100M to $5.75–$5.85B (midpoint ~$5.80B) and raised adjusted EBITDAR to $640–$660M. Demand/occupancy trends and conservative leverage further reduce downside risk; no notable negatives were flagged.
