Q2 revenue ($121.4M) beat the note’s ~$117M base case (~+3.7%), but diluted EPS ($0.27) was essentially inline with the note’s ~$0.27 estimate. The key incremental positive was credit quality broadly holding/improving (30+ DQ 12.16%, NCOs 7.28% vs Q1’s 8.57%) alongside strong origination ($758M) and improving expense-to-portfolio, which should drive a moderately positive (but not outsized) reaction given guidance/consensus uncertainty and the already-priced growth narrative.

Adjusted EPS of $9.41 vs a stale working consensus midpoint of ~$7.40 is an apparent beat, but most of the outperformance is driven by favorable mark-to-market impacts already highlighted as a key swing factor in the preview; operationally refining capture/utilization guidance (~95% capture in Q3; mid-90s utilization) was broadly consistent with expectations. With little incremental negative information and upside largely already “priced” via the MTM/capture narrative, the expected next-day reaction skews slightly positive/near-median.

With no pre-release consensus provided, reaction is anchored to fundamentals: notable gross-margin expansion (beneficial mix/yield) is a positive, but adjusted net income growth lagged due to a sharp tax-rate jump, partially offsetting the profitability upside. Guidance was reiterated with management confidence and no apparent change in trajectory.

Q2 fundamentals dramatically beat the pre-release medical margin/EBITDA expectations and FY26 guidance was raised meaningfully (including medical margin and adjusted EBITDA), consistent with a bull-path resolution. The main offset is that MA membership still fell YoY and the guide still relies on conservatively reserving ~7% cost trend, tempering confidence in sustained H2 upside.

Q2 net sales were essentially flat vs the ~in-line $162.9M consensus, while adjusted EBITDA hit the high end (~$8.7M) and gross margin expanded materially to 61.1% (360 bps) vs the ~60% framework. Crucially, full-year net sales ($625–635M) and adjusted EBITDA ($30–32M) were reiterated, which the note treated as the main directional risk—so upside is modest and reaction likely stays near-median.

Revenue missed consensus (~$49.1M vs ~$52.0M base-case) despite strong Vafseo execution (21.3M revenue; >10,500 active patients), while Auryxia erosion was as expected from the new generic competitive regime. EPS was not clearly provided vs consensus in the facts, limiting certainty; the net loss and higher reorg expense likely tempered any optimism, keeping reaction near-median rather than sharply positive.

ARQT raised FY26 guidance meaningfully above the street (midpoint $532.5M vs ~$500.1M consensus) and reported very strong Q2 momentum (net product revenue +59% YoY/+23% QoQ) with a clear profitability swing ($15M net income). Record prescription demand and stable gross-to-net support the raise; the only potential offset (CCO resignation) is secondary versus the guidance and demand beats.

With no consensus/expected numbers provided, the only clear positives versus a typical setup are stronger-than-prior-period operating leverage (OPEX up 7% vs revenue up 34%), continued test volume acceleration, and improving losses; management also reiterated full-year revenue guidance (no guidance shock). Likely moderately positive reaction driven by demand/volume and margin improvement, partially capped by maintained guidance.

Top-line was down y/y but landed in the upper half of guidance, while adjusted EBITDA exceeded the high end despite lower margin. However, Q3 guidance implies a sharp margin step-down (~28% midpoint) tied to renewed marketing spend, which likely tempers the upside and keeps the net reaction near-median.

Q2 revenue and EPS beat the derived consensus/anchor, and management raised FY26 revenue (12–14% vs 10–12%) and EPS growth (14–16% vs 12–14%), which the pre-release note flagged as the key lever for a positive reaction; margin was steady (non-GAAP GM 80.3%) and demand/AI-led product strength was emphasized.

Q3 revenue and adjusted EBITDA beat the derived expectations for a Micro Bird-diluted quarter, and FY26 adjusted EBITDA guidance was raised (midpoint ~14% margin). However, unit sales fell and reported EBITDA margin remained pressured by integration, keeping the outcome largely in the 'base-to-mildly-bullish' range rather than a major re-rate.

Quarterly revenue growth and a higher (low-end) full-year revenue guide are positives, but profitability deteriorated with a wider GAAP net loss and an adjusted EBITDA loss, which likely limits upside despite the demand/order narrative and margin ex-tariff improvement.

Management said Q2 adjusted EBITDA materially exceeded the guidance range (ads unit economics, SumUp ahead, Deliveroo profit positive), but guided Q3 adjusted EBITDA to be within the range (no beat), tempering upside. Option markets implied a modest ~9% absolute move with downside protection (negative skew), suggesting a likely mildly positive but not outsized reaction.

Full-year 2026 revenue guidance was cut primarily due to MEATER softness and distribution-related disruption, which is the dominant negative. Offsetting positives include raised gross margin guidance and improved adjusted profitability (Q2 adjusted EBITDA up and adjusted net income positive), but the magnitude of the revenue reset likely drives a below-median reaction.

Key incremental catalyst was a clear upward revision to fiscal ’27 net sales growth (18%-20% vs 12%-14%) and adjusted EPS ($3.50-$3.55 vs $3.27-$3.32), alongside strong rhode and DTC momentum; partially offset by noted unit volume decline/pricing test need. Lack of consensus numbers for revenue/EPS prevents a precise beat/miss quantification, but guidance strength likely drives a moderately positive reaction.

Without a pre-release note, expected vs. reported cannot be quantified for revenue/EPS. The meaningful upgrade/raise in full-year revenue guidance midpoint and raised gross margin outlook—paired with continued positive adjusted EBITDA and Portfolio Growth Bundle traction—should drive a moderately positive reaction, partially offset by cash decline.

Expedia reported strong Q2 momentum (bookings/revenue/EBITDA all above the high end) and raised full-year guidance with continued margin expansion and marketing leverage. However, Q3 guidance flags decelerating bookings growth (tough comps/FX), limiting upside and making the reaction moderately positive rather than extreme.

Results showed broad upside versus provided guidance ranges (revenue, operating income, and record margins) and management raised full-year 2026 revenue and operating profit outlook. However, management flagged customer concentration increasing and episodic World Cup revenue as a portion of upside, tempering optimism.

No pre-release consensus was provided, limiting quantified beats/misses. Operationally, Galleri volume and cash appear supportive (positive), but adjusted EBITDA loss widened and the NHS-Galleri trial missed its primary endpoint (negative), likely leading to a mildly negative/neutral reaction consistent with priced-in uncertainty.

Record revenue and stronger segment EBITDA/margins (notably Expedited and Omni excluding impairment) are offset by a large $244m non-cash goodwill impairment that materially worsened reported operating results. With no pre-release expectations provided and no explicit EPS/guidance figures, overall reaction is likely near-median.

Without a pre-release benchmark, the only clear drivers are (i) very large one-time IEPA tariff refund boosting reported earnings/margins, which limits incremental upside, and (ii) underlying gross margin of 26.1% described as in line, with operating profit guidance (excluding the refund) improved from low-teens to high-single-digit decline—suggesting modestly better sentiment but largely expected tariff-related dynamics.

Results themselves largely match the pre-announced setup (revenue ~inline), but the key credibility questions were (i) NRR holding and (ii) Q3/strategic trajectory. NRR fell to 89% (bear trigger risk vs 90% floor) and downmarket ACV declined 12% and sales cycles lengthened—incremental negatives versus what was expected. Offsetting that, margins and cash flow improved (AOI margin +130 bps; uFCF +7%) and management raised FY26 guidance, which supports sentiment, keeping the reaction near-median rather than strongly positive.

Strong operating/margin improvements (EBITDA margin expanding to 31%, record volume, and sharply higher FCF) alongside raised full-year sales/production guidance likely drive an upside reaction, partially offset by weaker PLV realization and management warning of second-half pricing pressure.

With no pre-release note, I can only partially benchmark: management reaffirmed FY EBITDA ($112–$118m) while reporting a strong 45% margin (+1,000 bps YoY) and interactive EBITDA growth despite the UK remote gaming duty shock. The main offset is the duty-driven margin pressure and a one-time $7m pub restructuring outflow that reduced reported free cash flow.

No pre-release consensus/expectations were provided, so beats/misses can’t be quantified. Qualitatively, gross margin strength and raised gross margin guidance are positives, but revenue guidance was narrowed and the US FDA application withdrawal likely adds risk, implying a near-median to mildly positive reaction.

Revenue strength (text messaging/WhatsApp/analytics) and a higher full-year revenue midpoint likely drive a positive reaction, but the margin/gross margin decline and a $10M cut to non-GAAP operating income guidance temper the upside.

Quarterly revenue tracked guidance, but the key surprise is the sharp full-year and especially Q3 revenue deceleration tied to Google AI search—likely the dominant negative. Offsetting positives were stronger-than-expected profitability (adj. EBITDA above the high end with margin expansion) and continued subscription/mix durability, but the magnitude of the growth guide cut should keep the reaction modest-to-negative.

Revenue met the guided range but management cut full-year revenue and shifted adjusted EBITDA outlook to (near) break-even after citing a first-half shortfall and GLP-1 launch/cash-collection impacts. Despite improving gross margin and improving mix/retention from the new multi-month package strategy, the EBITDA loss and guidance reset likely drive a modestly negative reaction.

EPS and FY27 EPS guidance were both raised above already-high consensus (FY27 midpoint moved to ~$44.6 vs ~$44.28 consensus), while operating margin improved (~150 bps) and oncology/GLP-1 growth looked stronger than the cautious revenue/mix setup implied. Revenue was only modestly above expectations and FCF was still negative in the quarter, limiting upside.

Revenue momentum and RPO visibility were strong (record quarter, RPO acceleration, multiproduct growth), supporting an above-median positive reaction; however, profitability was pressured by noncash GAAP warrant charges and additional SkyWater-related costs, and consolidated forward guidance is delayed pending integration—offsetting some optimism.

Reported contribution ex-TAC and adjusted EBITDA beat consensus with margin expansion (37% vs 34%) and management raised full-year contribution ex-TAC growth guidance and EBITDA growth above prior targets. Despite Q3 CTV growth deceleration guidance, the balance of beats plus upward guidance likely drives a meaningfully positive reaction.

No consensus/guide figures were provided, but the call highlighted strong marketed-product and Afrezza pediatric uptake, while balance-sheet/income optics remained pressured by a large GAAP loss and sharply higher SG&A/R&D. Net: likely modestly positive, with reaction tempered by investment-year expense and uncertain insurance conversion through 2026.

Strong fundamentals (margin expansion to 72.1%, major EBITDA improvement, operating leverage, and record MyoPro orders) plus an upward full-year revenue guidance raise from $43–46M to $45–47M should drive a constructive reaction; however, without pre-release consensus/expectations, the magnitude of the beat vs Street is unknown.

Quarterly net product sales growth and a higher full-year net product sales range are supportive, and management highlighted improved cash contribution margins. However, the FDA’s recommendation for a new volixibat Phase 3 study pushes the NDA submission into H1’27, partially offsetting the sales/guidance positives; without consensus inputs, the magnitude of the beat vs expectations is uncertain.

Quarterly revenue/AFFO beat the (already guidance-derived) setup, and—most importantly—management raised FY2026 AFFO growth into the low-20s (vs the note’s expectation that an unchanged/reaffirm “high-teens” would be a cut). Margin and transit momentum also look stronger than the note’s caution, driving a likely above-median day-after reaction.

Operating margin expanded sharply (540 bps) and gross margin exceeded guidance, suggesting stronger profitability than already expected; however, the GaN-linked products are still several years away with no meaningful near-term revenue, and without consensus/expected figures the size of any beat vs market expectations is unclear.

The release included a clear full-year adjusted EBITDA guidance cut to $92–$96M alongside contracting restaurant-level margins and ongoing same-restaurant traffic headwinds (transactions down, traffic lapping issues). While cost actions and commodity hedging provide some offset, the demand/margin narrative and guide reduction likely drive a below-median reaction.

No consensus figures were provided for reported quarter EPS/revenue, but the release delivered clear negative guidance: FY2026 revenue guidance was lowered and cash flow breakeven pushed out to 2028, alongside restructuring and deteriorating gross margin (36% Q2 vs 38% prior year; FY GM guidance 35–37% pressured by compute/memory inflation and transition costs). Positives were limited to ongoing SparkNext adoption (software adoption >1/3 of install base; chemistry cost/usage improvements), which likely only partially offset the demand/funding headwinds and magnitude of guidance cuts, implying a below-median reaction.

Revenue landed above the low-signal deferred-revenue range implied in the preview, while the key execution/timeline items (PEAK-1 enrollment by YE2026; PEAK-20 to start by YE2026) were reaffirmed/advanced. No major new negative (e.g., cash guide deterioration or ARC-20 data deferral) was introduced, supporting a modestly positive reaction percentile.

The key incremental item was a sizable full-year 2026 cash generation and subscriber value guidance cut, driven by weaker affiliate volumes and a slower direct sales ramp plus higher rates—more negative than what the market would typically tolerate. Offsetting positives included a record 74% storage attachment rate and encouraging second-half direct volume growth trajectory.

Key upside is regulatory/expedited momentum: FDA acceptance of the daraxonrasib NDA with Phase 3 RASolute 302 efficacy and EMA high-priority designation, plus broad expanded-access uptake. Partial offset is financials—net loss widening with a large noncash warrant fair-value charge—even though operating expense guidance was raised for 2026.

Political advertising strength was reinforced with a meaningful raise to full-year political guidance (+13% to at least $375M) and adjusted EBITDA guidance raised despite core advertising being cut—suggesting leverage/earnings power resilience. Offsets include core ad crowd-out and a decline in Tennis segment EBITDA, but the net guidance tone is more constructive than typical for this setup.

Despite margin expansion and modest comparable-sales growth, the company cut full-year and Q3 adjusted EBITDA guidance after EBITDA missed prior guidance in Q2, driven largely by higher marketing spend and the delayed New York relocation—likely a negative net surprise vs what markets were positioned for.

ACV landed at $29.6M (+27% YoY) with the ex-contribution ACV at the upper end of expectations, and full-year ACV guidance was reaffirmed ($218–228M). The only notable upside was a higher drug discovery revenue guide ($65–75M vs $55–65M), but the call framed big EPS as largely Ajax-related (non-operational), and headline EPS/revenue optics were already expected to be distorted—limiting cross-sectional upside.

Headline Q2 sales were largely pre-paid by the known ERP/order pull-forward (expected), with Q2 reported up ~2.2% and organic strength reported, but modestly weaker than the note’s like-for-like setup. The material upside came from guidance: FY2026 adj. EPS and operating margin were raised meaningfully (vs consensus already near the top of the prior range), and buyback/Acera momentum supported; partially offset by management’s continued expectation that ERP orders reverse in Q3 (negative framing).

Strong growth in active buyers/orders and a clear gross margin improvement suggest execution momentum despite a stated promotional headwind. However, management lowered full-year revenue guidance for 2H promo headwinds, which likely offsets some of the positive quarter performance and keeps the reaction near-median.

No consensus/option “expected” figures for revenue/EPS were provided, but the company tightened expense guidance and raised collaboration/other revenue expectations while narrowing 2026 net product revenue toward the low end and guiding modestly lower 2H. Net effect suggests a roughly median-to-slightly negative reaction, with some offset from tighter cost outlook and ongoing FDA/process catalysts.

Pre-release framing was a Cornerstone-led guidance reset; while Q2 results were strong and management raised FY26 adj. EBITDA ($2.025–$2.225B) and FCF ($1.2–$1.35B), the net guidance outcome was broadly consistent with the note’s ~mid-$2.1B midpoint expectations. Upside likely came more from commentary/trajectory (2027/28 FCF/share bridge, AWS margin potential) than from a major incremental surprise, supporting a modestly positive reaction.

Margin and subscription profitability improved (subscription adjusted operating margin up to 15% and AOI up 24%), which is likely supportive. However, net income/EPS declined year-over-year (partly mix/one-time dynamics), the value proposition metric fell, and retention value proposition softness tempers enthusiasm—driving a roughly median-to-slightly positive expected reaction given lack of consensus/guidance benchmarks.

Quarterly starts/lead flow were mixed (UTI new starts up, but high school channel softness persists). The key incremental negative was management cutting FY2026 guidance (revenue and especially adjusted EBITDA), driven largely by Q4 high school auto/diesel starts weakness and margin-mix pressure—likely leading to a below-median reaction despite some offsetting campus execution wins.

Consensus in the preview anchored on ~low-$9M revenue and normalized adjusted EPS still around -$0.03 with heavy emphasis on proving cash/backlog; the print delivered $15.9M revenue with clear operating leverage, first-ever positive quarterly operating income, positive adjusted EBITDA, and RPO of $80.7M (at/above the preview’s >$80M watch level) plus Merlin on track for an October 2026 launch—overall a multi-metric upside relative to what was expected. Despite the GAAP loss, adjusted metrics were the focus pre-release and moved favorably; no guidance change was reported, so the reaction hinges on the revenue/RPO/cash-transition narrative.

Q2 delivered a clear beat vs the pre-release yardstick (revenue $1.0B vs $964.6M consensus; non-GAAP EPS $0.99 vs $0.92). More importantly, management raised FY26 sales guidance to ~$4.4B (above the prior ~$4.0B target) and guided a strong Q3 ramp (N+M mix shift and yields/margins improving), alongside record book-to-bill (1.49) and rising cancellable backlog—largely aligning with (but exceeding) what the market expected, though positioning should already have been helped by the prior drawdown.

Q4 revenue and EPS beat both the posted consensus and the guide high end, and—most importantly—Q1 FY27 guidance is meaningfully above the market’s flat-sequential setup (midpoint ~$455M vs ~$440M implied in the note) with higher operating margin and EPS. Demand/capacity narrative (50%+ data center mix, production testing, accelerating CPO) and margin expansion drive an above-median post-earnings repricing; no notable negatives were flagged versus expectations.

Reported cash/runway and reaffirmed ECLIPSE 1/Q4 2026 vs ECLIPSE 2/3/Q1 2027 timing matched the pre-release setup, while the quarter also showed meaningful Astellas license revenue recognition and a swing to positive net income. The only likely remaining delta for the stock is how much of the EPS/revenue accounting dispersion the market had already effectively priced.

Management raised full-year revenue guidance (and interventional dry eye guidance) alongside improving gross margin and a sharp net-loss narrowing; strong utilization/account growth in both dry eye and glaucoma supports a positive read-through. No consensus/option expectations were provided, so the magnitude of the surprise vs expectations is uncertain.

Q3 top-line/EPS were effectively known via the Aug 3 8-K, so there’s little incremental upside from the numbers themselves. What mattered versus the pre-release note was the call content: management reiterated the high-end FY26 margin framework and reinforced the operating cash flow/FC conversion and DSP/AI transition narratives, driving a modestly positive (but not outsized) reaction.

Q2 fundamentals were weaker than the market’s already-cautious setup: Nereus recognized only $1m vs expectations of a larger “first revenue datapoint,” Hetlios was hit by generic pressure plus a ~$7m timing shift, and the net loss more than doubled. While FY2026 revenue guidance was reiterated ($240–290m), cash declined faster than the preview’s runway math and operating costs accelerated, driving an overall negative reaction despite strong FNAPT prescription growth.

With no pre-release consensus/market targets provided, directionally WDC highlighted Q4 revenue/EPS at or above the high end of guidance, strong pricing (accelerating avg price/terabyte), improving margins, and upbeat Q1 FY2027 guidance with 25%+ exabyte growth durability—typically supportive for the stock, though magnitude is uncertain without consensus comps.

Q2 net sales landed at the high end of already-preannounced guidance and EBITDA beat the low bar, but gross margin came in at 48.9% with no price increases planned—so the key unresolved item (GM/margin pressure into Q3 and FY) largely tracked expectations. FY 2026 guidance was maintained; the new Q3 EBITDA loss and ~46% GM path were consistent with the pre-release risk framing, limiting upside beyond the modest EBITDA/flow-through beat.

No pre-release consensus or guidance was provided, so surprises vs expectations can’t be quantified. Directionally, reported revenue growth looks strong (U.S. MIPLYFFA sales up and inventory back to target), but the update includes meaningful negative catalysts (CHMP negative opinion/Europe MAA setback and slow DISCOVER event accrual), which likely offsets the near-term sales momentum.

Q2 organic revenue grew 6.7% versus consensus implied ~+4.3%, and underlying adj. gross margin (43.8%) plus EBITDA/margins materially strengthened. Management raised FY26 organic revenue growth to 5–7% (from 4–6%), adj. GM to mid-40s (from low-40s), and adj. EBITDA to $23–25M (from $20–23M), which de-risks the feared back-half ramp.

While Q2 profitability metrics were mixed (underlying strong combined ratio but reported combined ratio worsened sharply), the key driver is guidance: total revenue guidance was cut due to softening pricing. Offsetting positives include maintained pre-tax earnings guidance and capital returns/balance-sheet actions, but the E&S/ACES initiative running behind and increased hurricane retention cost are likely negative for sentiment.

No pre-release note/consensus was provided, but management guided to higher Q3 profitability (midpoint adj. EBITDA and EPS increases sequentially) alongside a known consumer sequential decline tied to supply/launch timing; the stock reaction is likely muted-to-slightly positive as pipeline/trial momentum offset margin pressure and consumer softness.

Without consensus/guide data, the best read is qualitative: revenue strength and multiple new commercial/partnership wins (optical connectivity JV + hyperscaler-focused JDA, Bendix/SICK/City of Fargo) are positives, but the quarter still reflects a sizable cash burn and the CFO departure adds execution risk—netting to a mildly positive expected reaction.

Q2 results and the third consecutive record order book show strong underlying demand (tracker growth + new bookings), and adjusted EBITDA/EPS and margins materially improved while full-year gross margin was raised. However, management flagged potential second-half headwinds (international mix, higher metals/logistics) and weaker free-cash-flow conversion from timing shifts, tempering upside.

Top-line and adjusted EBITDA landed slightly below the guidance midpoint/range, which is likely a modest disappointment. Offsetting positives include materially expanding margins (~+300 bps), record consumer/e-commerce advertiser spend, and reduced regulatory overhang, with Q3 start strength attributed to already-booked model improvements.

No pre-release consensus was provided, but the release highlights strong AI thermal processing momentum (AI revenue ~+120% YoY, book-to-bill ~1.4) and sizable margin expansion (~+400 bps to 50%), offset by continued weakness/no meaningful recovery expectations in SiC-related demand. Overall should skew positive versus a typical quarter, but magnitude of surprise is hard to quantify without benchmarks.

Despite gross margin contraction, the release paired record free cash flow and strong retention/multi-product adoption with a full-year revenue (and operating income) guidance raise, which should drive a moderately positive reaction; however, without pre-release consensus it’s unclear how large the beat/guide upside was versus expectations.

Q2 delivered a larger-than-expected top line ($246M vs ~$233M mid in the note) and a strong adj. EBITDA beat ($23.7M vs the ~$17–18M derived bar), driven by a major gross-profit swing and $5.1M of 45Z earnings. Key upside vs the note: 45Z is reaffirmed at 90M+ gallons with net income after monetization costs of $15–16M (above the note’s ~$15M base), while margin dynamics improved (crush to $0.33/gal) despite some export-volume softness that management attributed to freight/geopolitics.

EPS fell more than the pre-release base case driven by smaller favorable workers’ comp reserve development, and management narrowed guidance with cuts to both gross billings (midpoint slightly below consensus) and gross margin (2.7–2.75% vs prior 2.7–2.85%), reinforcing the margin overhang as 2026 is the low watermark.

No pre-release consensus provided, but the release featured raised full-year system comp guidance and reaffirmed strong 2026 shop growth/pipeline (positive). Offsetting factors were explicit deceleration in Q3 comps and net margin pressure from higher coffee and occupancy costs, limiting upside and pushing a moderately positive—rather than outsized—reaction.

With no pre-release consensus provided, directional read-through suggests upside: management raised full-year revenue growth (step-up vs prior range), gross margin expanded sequentially, and demand indicators (NRR 126%, bookings up strongly, international and enterprise momentum) support stronger-than-expected operating leverage. Continued FCF guidance and a new DHS counter-UAS award reduce downside, supporting a likely above-median positive reaction.

Shares likely react negatively primarily to the sharp FY2026 guidance cuts (revenue and adjusted EBITDA) and the reversal of the expected H2 YoY procedure-revenue growth, alongside gross margin contraction; supply continuity has improved but not enough to offset the demand/earnings deterioration.

Revenue and billings were weak YoY but within guided ranges, while adjusted contribution margin improved and churn/advertiser growth improved retention. However, free cash flow deteriorated sharply and MQUs declined due to bank-partner changes; with consensus expectations not provided, overall reaction skews modestly negative-to-mixed.

Revenue of $68.8M beat the guidance band and cleared the high end, but adjusted EBITDA loss widened as a % of revenue (margin pressure) and cash burn remains material; importantly, demand commentary is still impaired by domestic “misinformation” despite some international retail growth. Guidance direction for Q3 is consistent (implied sequential decline), so the tape likely focuses on operating deterioration and balance-sheet risk rather than the revenue beat.

LOQTORZI Q2 sales of $13.6M were slightly below the $14.41M consensus despite strong new-patient starts, and management’s FY2026 revenue guide ($57–62M) implies a weaker outcome than the pre-release setup suggested (consensus $73M with meaningful non-product assumptions). More importantly, casdo/tagmokitug timing pushed later (tagmokitug to October; casdozokitug initial data now Q4), which the market was already keying on, limiting upside despite Opex declines and improving cash visibility.

Revenue and EPS were not directly benchmarked to consensus (no pre-release note provided), but management lowered full-year revenue and EPS guidance and guided Q4 lower, driven by broadband demand constraints/BEAD delays and a customer strategy shift that led to backlog cancellation and an inventory write-off—offset somewhat by a first significant $22m hyperscale order. Overall reaction skewed negative given the guidance cut.

Clover raised full-year 2026 guidance across revenue and profitability while reporting strong operating leverage (gross profit and operating leverage up) and improved medical cost trends. Court/CMS 4.5-Star resolution is positive, though appeal risk likely limits upside and keeps some items partially priced.

No pre-release consensus provided, but management raised full-year guidance across revenue, EBITDA, and EPS while delivering strong margin expansion (EBITDA margin +600 bps; gross margin to 72%) alongside improving credit performance and monetization/advance-size initiatives—features that typically drive above-median post-earnings upside.

CAFD materially missed the pre-release setup driven by wind (Q2 CAFD $167M vs ~$190M expected), and—critically—FY2026 CAFD guidance was cut to $430–470M from $470–510M (midpoint down ~7.5%), outweighing positive mitigants like ERCOT PPA restructurings and reaffirmed 2027/2030 targets. Given seasonality-weighted importance of Q2, the release likely triggered a negative repricing despite flexibility on equity issuance.

With no pre-release consensus provided, the best anchor is guidance tone: Q2 revenue range and gross margin are broadly guided with an acknowledged one-time margin tailwind, while full-year PC business expectations were lowered due to constrained supply/timing and OpEx is set to rise. However, management also highlighted among-strongest HPMS pipeline and secured additional GlobalFoundries capacity/pricing, which may partially offset the margin and PC concern—implying roughly median-to-slightly positive reaction.

No pre-release note/consensus was provided, so beats vs expectations can’t be quantified; however, management raised both Q4 and full-year revenue/EBITDA/EPS guidance alongside expanding margins (29.1% adj. EBITDA margin) and improving cash generation, which should drive a positive, above-median reaction.

EPS (non-GAAP $0.09 vs $0.05 expected) beat materially, but revenue is effectively in line (~$31.4M reported vs ~$30.7M expected) while the key Dice signal worsened (bookings −14% and management says Dice bookings won’t return to growth in 2026). Guidance is maintained at $124–128M with a strong CJ bookings/pipeline narrative but weaker Dice demand/churn.

While exact consensus revenue/EPS aren’t provided, the release showed clear upside across operating metrics (23% YoY DAU growth, broad-based) and management raised full-year EBITDA margin to 26.5% (AI cost savings), with Q3/FT guidance implying continued growth. Margin expansion and higher profitability outlook are the likely drivers of a moderately positive reaction.

Q2 revenue was effectively in-line with the pre-release setup (Safeguard-driven headline decline; comparable up), while margins and Data Solutions growth came through positively. The key risk/reaction lever—FY2026 EPS—was held despite raised revenue/EBITDA guidance, keeping the outcome near the market’s base case.

No pre-release note or consensus numbers were provided, but the release featured strong Q2 growth and clear margin expansion, plus Q3 guidance calling for accelerating revenue growth and higher gross margin. The inventory/days commentary and automotive/AI content expansion further support a positive demand backdrop, likely translating into an above-median reaction.

Despite a very strong Q2 revenue/EBITDA beat driven by accelerated MCM deliveries and improving early liquidity, the company cut full-year revenue and adjusted EBITDA and guided Q3 to a sharp sequential drop—plus it flagged competitive price erosion from new naloxone entrants—so the market reaction is likely negative relative to expectations.

No consensus/reported revenue or EPS figures were provided, but the key incremental signal is management’s inability to reinstate guidance due to Iran/geopolitical uncertainty and communicated megaproject delays—likely negative for near-term visibility. Offsetting positives include a ‘uniquely strong’ MPD pipeline with up-to-5-year visibility and gradual margin improvement potential from the Saudi facility.

With no pre-release consensus/expectations provided, the key unanticipated negative is the full-year revenue guidance cut (midpoint -$50m) tied to slower NET indication ramp; EPS wasn’t flagged as cut and management offset via R&D reduction, but buyback support only partially offsets the demand/ramp concern.

Despite Q2 revenue landing above the top end of guidance, management cut full-year revenue and provided very weak Q3/near-term outlook (including negative adjusted EBITDA), explicitly driven by reversal of Q2 pull-forward orders and execution-driven delays. Net effect is likely a negative re-rating as forward visibility deteriorates.

Q2 revenue was inline, but adjusted EBITDA margin exceeded the guidance range (positive). The key negative is full-year guidance trending to the lower end of maintained ranges, driven by slower-than-expected new customer acquisition in EverPro—signaling pressured organic momentum despite expected acceleration later in 2026.

EPS landed around the low end of the market’s expectations, but the quality of earnings was strong: record collections and purchases, improved leverage and ROIC, cash efficiency running above guide, and (most importantly) raised FY EPS and collections with portfolio purchases guided to the top end. Offsetting it, a $30.5M refinancing charge dragged GAAP EPS materially.

With no pre-release note/consensus provided, reaction is inferred from the direction of results: gross margin contracted sharply (26% vs 31%) and full-year gross margin target was cut to low-to-mid-20% from mid-20% amid persistent pricing troughs—an overall negative. Partially offsetting positives included DLA contract reaward and indications of refrigerant pricing stabilizing around ~$6/lb, plus aftermarket opportunity momentum.

The key incremental positive was the full-year 2026 revenue guidance raise driven by Blade’s strength, alongside continued improving manufacturing/flight milestones (eIPP timing and expanding flight count). Offsetting negatives include a wider GAAP and adjusted EBITDA loss in Q2 and increased 2H 2026 cash burn, which likely tempers the upside despite demand indicators.

Revenue and non-GAAP EPS came in very strong versus company guidance, but since no pre-release consensus/market expectations were provided, the size of the beat vs the street is unclear. Demand commentary and subcontract-driven nonproduct growth are likely positives, partially offset by a disclosed margin headwind and litigation-related opex spike.

Results beat on both revenue and EPS, with a larger-than-expected margin expansion (32.9% non-GAAP op margin) and full-year guidance raised materially (revenue +$175M; EPS to $17.62–$17.72). Management also turned tariffs to net-neutral via IEPA refunds, reducing the main downside margin risk from the pre-release setup.

Revenue growth and operating margin came in better than the pre-release margin-and-EPS-risk setup (ops margin 6.7% vs implied ~6.7–7.1% and NIMAL improved to 21% with stronger Brazil unit economics). Also, adjusted free cash flow was positive ($214M) despite heavy investment, reducing the bear case that the investment cycle is worsening. No incremental guidance changes were provided in the facts, so the reaction should skew moderately positive rather than explosive.

Revenue beat and margins expanded, but the key expected catalyst (CT/NG InteliQuick FDA status) turned into a clear delay: OSUR withdrew its submission and now targets resubmission after FDA feedback with no 2026 clearance/launch. Q3 revenue guidance was reiterated essentially in line with what the note expected, so the downside is driven by the regulatory reset despite improved near-term numbers.

Q4 delivered a clear beat on both revenue ($2.3B vs $2.21B consensus) and adjusted EPS ($0.35 vs $0.21). The release also showed broad-based margin expansion (segment EBITDA margin to 18% FY; Q4 segment EBITDA +31%) plus exceptionally strong digital real estate and Dow Jones subscription/net-add momentum—more favorable than what the note framed as a modest beat with REA/rates and News Media as key risks. Guidance action not disclosed in the provided facts.

Q2 results were ahead on revenue (slightly above the top of the tight band) and delivered meaningful credit/outperformance (annualized NCO 12% vs 12.2%±15bps; delinquency 4.0% vs 4.1–4.2%). More importantly, FY adj. EBITDA guidance was raised ~6% at the midpoint, while FY adj. EPS was maintained (a deliberate offset, per management’s fair value headwinds), supporting a modest-to-positive reaction rather than a major upside rerating.

Revenue and adjusted EBITDA both beat the midpoint of guidance, with transaction margin dollars and margin expanding sharply. Full-year 2026 guidance was raised, but there was some softness in June high-value growth attributed to FX/RBI actions, limiting the upside.

Q2 reported both revenue ($731M vs ~$716–720M) and EPS ($0.41 vs $0.34) above expectations, and management raised FY26 adjusted EPS guide to $1.50-$1.55 (above the ~$1.35-$1.45 consensus base case in the note). Margin expansion (14.7% adj. EBITDA, +230 bps) and sharply higher FCF ($105M) plus a lowered tax rate further strengthen the raise, making the likely reaction meaningfully positive despite the quarter itself being less important than the guidance action.

Revenue beat the top of its own range and margins expanded sharply (gross and adjusted operating), while full-year revenue/EBITDA guidance was raised despite management flagging a Q4 EBITDA step-down. EPS surprise versus consensus cannot be quantified without external consensus numbers.

Q2 results beat consensus on both revenue and EPS, with adj. EBITDA margin expanding ~320 bps to 44.2%. The key positive surprise is the FY raise: revenue guidance lifted to $2.197–$2.212B and adj. EBITDA to $1.007–$1.022B (midpoint implying a ~46% margin), supporting upside follow-through despite the stock already running.

Headline Q2 revenue beat expectations (likely aided by Flyover timing already flagged), but the bigger tell is management also raised FY26 adjusted EBITDA to the consensus-aligned $128–138M range while acknowledging a margin decline from weather (margin down ~90 bps). Net: modestly positive setup with some quality concerns around margin/attractions softness; reaction likely near-median to slightly above.

Q2 delivered a clean beat on both revenue and EPS versus the pre-release consensus, with gross/operating margins expanding sharply. More importantly, Q3 combined revenue guide ($285–295M; midpoint $290M) and EPS guide ($3.50–3.65; midpoint $3.58) came in meaningfully above what the note implied the Street would likely underwrite, supporting a positive post-close re-rate.

Revenue (up ~2% Y/Y to $389M) roughly matches the pre-release $392.5M consensus expectation, so no top-line catalyst. Guidance tone is mixed-to-negative: management guided full-year PIF roughly flat vs 2025, which is softer than the note’s base-case expectation of low-single-digit improvement (and a likely risk to the bull/base scenarios). Margin/comps were also offset by management calling the 26% expense ratio unsustainable (normalizing toward ~29% per Q1/Q4), while GWP declined and average premiums fell—two additional negatives versus what the note framed as the key watch items.

Revenue came in extremely weak ($0.1M), consistent with the pre-release setup that near-term P&L would be largely non-informative without TVA definitization; on cash and strategic commentary, management framed progress without delivering a definitive TVA PPA date, leaving the market likely to trade the release mainly on sentiment rather than fundamentals.

Q2 delivered a large upside surprise (revenue $61.9M vs $52.5M consensus; adjusted EPS −$0.02 vs −$0.03 expected). Guidance was raised to $230–260M but the new midpoint ($245M) lands close to the Street/guide expectations in the pre-release note, so the main upside is execution (record quarter, margin improvement, strong customer commitments/channel wins).

No pre-release consensus was provided, but results were heavily negative on the core KPIs (large YoY/seq revenue and adjusted EBITDA declines) and guidance was withheld due to volatility. Some partial recovery in daily net revenue by end of June and continued sequential EBITDA expectation for the remainder of the year were the main offsets.

Revenue and gross margin were strong and broadly aligned with the pre-announced e-commerce momentum, but the adjusted EBITDA loss and cash runway/dilution risk remain the dominant overhang; adjusted EBITDA is worse than what was implied by the preview’s base-case framing, limiting upside despite the record top line.

Revenue and EBITDA margin came in above the top end of guidance (with a 70 bps EBITDA beat) and full-year 2026 revenue/FCF guidance was raised. Offsetting negatives include a ~22% decline from the largest client and cautious Q3 revenue/margin outlook reflecting continued client reductions and cost pressure.

No pre-release consensus figures were provided for revenue/EPS or for the guidance midpoint, limiting surprise assessment. Still, Q3 showed strong profitability with adjusted EBITDA more than doubled on expanding margins, but Q4 calls for roughly flat EBITDA margins and backlog slightly declined (with the 400 back-of-store contract delayed toward early 2028), likely tempering upside.

Core profitability and the credit/margin engine beat the pre-release setup: NIM printed 3.66% vs the 3.5% target and NPLs improved to 9.6% with resolutions clearing ~102.7% and minimal charge-offs. While origination dollars declined vs last year, unit production and Q2 momentum (submissions) supported the “2H re-acceleration” narrative; no formal guidance was issued, limiting incremental upside vs expectations.

TPC posted record results and, crucially, raised FY26 adjusted EPS guidance to $5.15-$5.45 (above the prior $4.90-$5.30 and the preview’s base expectation of at most conservatism/“no nudge”). Civil and Specialty margins beat the guided bands, backlog held up near $19.9B with book-to-burn ~1x, and the debt refi plus stronger cash flow reduce downside tail risk—driving a likely above-median positive reaction.

Q2 revenue ($193M) and non-GAAP EPS ($0.33) both beat the pre-release consensus (revenue $180.1M, EPS $0.26). Management also gave a Q3 guide at the top end of the ‘FY-critical’ band (revenue $200–220M, gross margin 41–42%), supporting the H2/FY math; key offset is non-GAAP FY EPS guidance was cut (to $1.36–1.61) despite revenue being raised (to $780–810M) due to growth investments.

No consensus/option expectations were provided, but the quarter showed sharp revenue and adjusted EBITDA year-over-year declines while reiterating full-year revenue and adjusted EBITDA guidance. Subscriber mix improved (clinical up strongly; Core+ sequential growth; ARPU up) and debt paydown supports cash interest, partially offset by behavioral subscriber and revenue contraction.

Despite some Q2 beats (management said revenue/EBITDA/EPS ahead of internal expectations) and customer renewals providing stability, the key overhang was the materially less favorable Avis/Hertz renewal economics and resulting guidance cut plus margin contraction—likely driving a negative, though not extreme, post-release reaction.

No pre-release consensus was provided, but results show strong YoY top-line growth (esp. advertising +54% and Connected Car +60%) and non-GAAP EPS more than doubling, alongside improving EBITDA margin (21% of revenue, +7pp). Offsetting negatives include Pay TV revenue decline (-11%) and the still-negative gross margin on advertising (-8%) which management only expects to turn positive entering 2027.

Raised full-year 2026 guidance (GP and adjusted EPS) with record margin/earnings momentum and strong GPV trends, which typically drives a positive reaction. Offsetting caution comes from Cash App transacting actives growing only low single digits and normalization expected in lending/borrow comps, limiting upside.

No pre-release note/consensus for revenue/EPS, but the release shows clear margin improvement (Adj. EBITDA margin 12% vs 8% a year ago) and raised full-year growth to low single-digit with higher margin outlook (12–14%), plus strong employer and paid-employer growth despite muted labor demand.

Results and cash EPS beat, with meaningful guidance raises for full-year 2026 (revenue and cash EPS). Incremental margin strength and continued organic growth/booking momentum likely outweighed the FTC settlement charge and expectation of slightly softer back-half margins.

No pre-release consensus provided, but results included an upsized full-year revenue outlook (midpoint growth lift to ~14%), improving gross margin and sharply reduced free cash outflow—partially offset by continued losses and adjusted EBITDA still negative.

Results exceeded the high end of guidance with upside momentum (revenue/GMV and non-GAAP EPS/operating income growth), and full-year FX-neutral GMV growth was raised—likely driving a moderately positive reaction. Q3 guidance implies deceleration and Depop dilution, but the guidance raise and margin/earnings strength likely outweighed near-term concern.

No pre-release consensus/guidance or option-implied expectations were provided, limiting precision. From the reported details, the main potential upside is Ting reaching its first-ever positive quarterly adjusted EBITDA and improving operating cash flow, partially offset by consolidated EBITDA decline and continued pressure in Wavelo/legacy mobile along with GAAP loss widening.

Q2 largely tracked the setup (lithium tight, lagged pricing) with revenue/EPS modestly above the cautious consensus expectations, but the net reaction should be dominated by guidance: management cut full-year energy storage volumes (flat to down 4% YoY; CGP3 fire) and guided sequential declines in Q3 despite raising stationary storage demand and stationary outlook. The guidance mix tempers upside, leaving a slightly negative-to-neutral cross-sectional tape reaction.

The print was largely a non-event on the P&L line versus what the note expected (cash around consensus; no revenue; EPS noise). The key tradeable item—confirming late Aug/early Sep 2026 topline timing—landed largely consistent with expectations, with only a modest positive from clarifying additional label-path efficiency (confirmatory sleeve-burden framing) and incremental collaboration momentum, keeping reaction near median.

The quarter beat on adjusted EPS ($1.26 vs ~$1.19–$1.21 expected) and management raised 2026 capital return guidance to $550–600M (vs $500M prior), which is a meaningful upside to the market’s base case of reaffirmation. Demand/volume (NIW $15B, persistency 80%) plus $1.9B PMIERs excess support the quality of the EPS, offset by only “normalizing” loss-ratio commentary.

EPS beat was expected given penny-guided quarters, but management disclosed a favorable volume swing (+~1% vs -1% to -2% expected) and—more importantly—raised FY26 guidance (adj. EBITDA to $575M–$603M and adj. EPS to $3.10–$3.25, above the prior reaffirm range). Record margins (18.3%, +110 bps) and a strong data/electronics narrative further support an above-median reaction.

Q3 results came in ahead of the pre-release yardstick (EPS $3.23 vs ~$3.14; revenue $5.0B vs ~$4.89B) and management raised the FY26 adj. EPS midpoint to $12.67, which the note expected to hinge on Q4 credibility—supportive for a modestly positive reaction. Offsets include margin pressure (24.9% down 130 bps; tariff drag) and messaging that FY27 starts with only low single-digit revenue growth and modest EPS leverage, limiting upside.

Quarter delivered strong operating signals (physical occupancy +~300 bps YoY sequentially strong and churn low), supporting AFFO. Most importantly, FY26 AFFO guidance was raised to $1.26–$1.32 ($1.29 midpoint) vs prior ~$1.25 midpoint expectation (~+1% beat), and the EQT JV regulatory approval/debt paydown mechanics remove a key uncertainty—likely driving an above-median positive reaction despite the non-cash impairment being pre-announced noise.

Revenue came in below the ~$874–$888M consensus range (reported $818M), but the call provided key offsets: Alani grew 21% YoY to $364M with 56% tracked retail growth and gross margin held at ~48% as guided. The main disappointment is CELSIUS net sales down ~12% (with only modestly better tracked retail and inventory rebalancing noted), which matches the pre-release bear framing, limiting upside.

FY27 guidance came in above the Street’s reference and was paired with a notably stronger capital structure/deleveraging path plus high-12% margin framing and outsized FCF support; together with award momentum (>$10B awards in FY26, large bid pipeline) this likely drives a modestly positive repricing despite Q4 EPS optics.

Q2 revenue was essentially in line and non-GAAP operating margin beat helped by profitability, but the key catalyst was management cutting FY2026 revenue guidance at the midpoint (from the pre-release implied ~$356M region down to ~$340.5M), which the market was not positioning for. Margin commentary also included sequential gross-margin decline (AI/hosting cost), partially offsetting the operating-income beat.

Top-line ($199.9M) was effectively inline versus the ~$200M setup, but adjusted EPS was a clear beat ($1.92 vs ~$1.70 expected). Guidance was mixed: Astaris/FY revenue was raised ($65–75M) yet total FY revenue guidance was lowered (to $825–855M) due to the Nuscenta drop, driving the net reaction to be modest rather than strongly positive.

Revenue was broadly in line with the note’s mechanical re-franchising expectation, while adjusted EBITDA ($28.8M) beat the note’s ~$30–32M working/implicit range less clearly but still reads as solid given the productivity/cost control and 340 bps margin expansion; importantly, guidance was maintained at $140–$150M adjusted EBITDA and net leverage improved to 5.4x. Net: modestly positive reaction versus median, with upside capped by guidance being unchanged.

Q2 revenue and EPS beat the pre-release bar (midpoint consensus anchored to guide) with a record $115M sequential add and a raised FY26 revenue guide above the ~$4.42B buy-side/whisper level. Despite the largest-customer usage reduction, management fully derisked FY26. Stock reaction should be moderately positive, but downside is cushioned by the decelerating Q3 guide and gross margin decline.

Q2 beat on both revenue (high end of range) and non-GAAP EPS, but the release disappoints on the items that mattered per the pre-note: full-year revenue growth was guided down to 3.2–4.2% (below the prior 4.0–6.5% framing) and Q3 revenue implies low growth with flattish Q3–Q4. Management also pushed meaningful AI-led deal revenue out to 1H’27 and cut FCF conversion guidance after weak Q2 cash flow/DSO.

On the key watch-items, results looked better than feared: same-park attendance +4% and same-park adjusted EBITDA +7% with ~120bp margin expansion, alongside a constructive demand/pass pricing commentary. Management also guided to YoY adjusted EBITDA growth in both Q3 and Q4 despite wildfire/July calendar headwinds, supporting an above-median reaction, though reported EPS/revenue vs the pre-note consensus can’t be precisely scored from the provided facts.

Even though EPS/reported revenue aren’t provided in the facts, the call delivered a materially stronger core/adj. EBITDA profile (ex-Longridge record $48.7M) and reinforced rail integration/synergy progress—supportive for the near-term. Offsetting that, Longridge still faced an outage with a lower-than-normal capacity factor (85%), and while the Longridge close timing was reiterated (end of Q3), the quarter itself was not a clear FERC/order beat given the pre-note’s emphasis on regulatory timing.

The quarter and especially FY 2026 guidance were upgraded (revenue raised; adj. EBITDA guide narrowed upward at the midpoint), which should drive a positive rerate versus the note’s 'operate off EBITDA/guidance' framing. However, Q2 MER rose to 95% (worse than the note’s improving path) and management pushed the revenue/launch ramp timing into H2 (and flagged broader Medicaid headwinds), muting the beat.

Despite record Q2 revenue and a better-than-expected 2.5% core organic growth, the key EPS sensitivity played out negatively (Q2 financing/equity drag and FY26 EPS guide implying additional pressure). Full-year core sales and adjusted EBITDA guidance were raised vs expectations, but the EPS guide (with assumed transitory price-cost neutrality drag) points to margin/EPS leverage being weaker than the market hoped, limiting upside and likely leading to a modestly negative-to-mixed reaction.

The key differentiator vs the pre-release setup was management providing the feared 'number'—raising FY26 BRINSUPRI revenue guidance to $1.25–$1.4B (vs prior >$1.0B) alongside improved gross-to-net and very strong organic patient adds (+7,000 vs 6,300 expectation). This should drive a meaningfully positive reaction despite limited disclosed EPS/reported total-revenue figures in the call facts provided.

Q1 revenue and adjusted EPS beat consensus, and—more importantly—management raised FY27 revenue growth guidance (5–8% reported / 4–7% organic vs the prior 4–7% / 3–6%). Despite the beat, gross and operating margins were down y/y (gross -40 bps, op margin -70 bps), which tempers the reaction versus a pure beat-and-raise.

Revenue beat the $193.2M consensus with strong adjusted EBITDA margin (31.8%). More importantly, full-year revenue and EBITDA guidance were raised to $790–805M and $240–250M (above the note’s tightening/raise expectations), and Pharma Direct growth was upgraded to >70%—offsetting the reported Rx slowdown. Key negative: MACs fell 12% Y/Y to 5.0M vs the note’s stabilization threshold (~5.3M), which keeps downside risk despite the positive Pharma/guide update.

This quarter appears to be more of a portfolio/cashflow and pipeline/timing update (no meaningful revenue and no decision-threshold EPS hurdle versus the preview). The new items (Moderna upfront cash, ongoing litigation, sarcoidosis Phase 3 initiation, and brepocitinib launch timing in dermatomyositis) are not the core RA/CLE timing driver emphasized in the pre-release note, which keeps the event close to ‘base-case / no re-rate’.

Q3 results were stronger than the already-guided bar (especially sequential growth), and, most importantly, management guided Q4 revenue to $375M with 48% gross margin—well above the pre-release implied ~$328M—while non-GAAP EPS guidance ($1.42) looks broadly aligned versus the market’s ~$1.13/derived bar directionally but revenue materially improves. The upside bias should be driven primarily by the raised Q4 top-line and stronger demand visibility (inbound POs into FYQ2 2027, >95% China utilization).

EPS and legacy/USRB momentum beat the pre-release setup, while management reaffirmed FY26 sales and low-double-digit CC EPS growth and framed leverage/FCF as on-track—limiting upside. Offsets were the expected weak U.S. Coffee/green inflation/tariff pressure and management warning JDE Peet’s profit could be a 2026 high watermark (though not a fresh negative vs the note). Net: a modestly positive reaction (beat but largely guided/anticipated).

EPS was far worse than the market’s $0.32–$0.33 adjusted operating EPS expectation because of a large $460m non-cash goodwill impairment. While underlying performance improved sequentially and commercial auto was solid, the call re-emphasized unprofitable CA personal auto and ongoing adverse reserve development—negative vs what the preview assumed would mainly be a “non-event” print. No formal EPS/revenue guidance exists, so reaction is driven by the unexpected impairment and continued CA/regulatory overhang.

Business update was largely in line with the pre-release playbook (BLA completion in H2’26 / runway into 2028), but the magnitude of lonvo-z efficacy (attack-free and “no SAEs” framing) and the lack of new hepatic safety signals vs the costly bear tails should drive a modestly positive next-day move, partially offset by the already-priced-in binary/regulatory narrative and ongoing cash burn.

Revenue came in above the median for the quarter, but the key narrative metrics (patient starts ~160, with first-line ~85% and growing first-line starts) appear broadly consistent with the pre-release setup emphasizing patient starts/stacking risk rather than a clear upside driver. No explicit FY26 guidance action and no EPS details were provided in the call facts, keeping the reaction near-median.

Quarterly results were modestly better than the pre-release expectations, but the key narrative stayed consistent: Q2 system SCS was only +1.7% (rate-driven) with member growth stalling sequentially and EBITDA margin declining. The main incremental positive was raising FY EPS growth outlook to ~6% (from ~4%), supported by buybacks; offsetting that, margin contraction and the focus on prioritizing growth over rate kept upside limited versus what was already priced.

Q2 showed clear operating leverage (adj. EBITDA +29% YoY and care margin +310 bps to 28.3%) and practice collections strength (+12.4% YoY) while management raised FY26 guidance with attributed lives now above the prior high end. Options suggested only ~±9% typical move, but the upside guidance revision plus margin expansion versus an already set guidance-implied bar points to a moderately positive tape reaction.

Revenue and FY26 top-line guidance were largely fully anticipated (pre-announced revenue; guidance reaffirmed). The reaction hinges on costs: GAAP EPS and cash burn came in worse than the pre-release model (burn $11.1M vs $8–9M guide and gross margin ~29% vs expected ~31–34%), offset by incremental backlog/new program awards that are more credibility-supportive than H2-recognizable.

Revenue landed essentially in line, but Q2 NA demand worsened (comps -8.3%) and—more importantly—2026 guidance was cut (adj. EBITDA to $180–190M and NA comps to -6% to -8%), with capital-allocation stress signaled by suspending the dividend. These are largely unanticipated versus the note’s base case, driving a likely negative reaction.

The release’s main incremental items were confirmatory-program momentum language (RGX-202 enrollment/dosing ahead of schedule and the Atlas/Ascent CERAVEC data timing reiterated for Q4 2026) while the key Q2 revenue/EPS line was largely a mechanical milestone/accounting topic already framed in the preview. Balance-sheet runway and regulatory timing readouts broadly match the setup, implying a near-median-to-slightly-positive reaction rather than a major beat-driven repricing.

Q2 prints were strong (revenue growth +70% and MLR 79.2% vs an implied ~83% anchored by consensus). More importantly, FY26 EFO was raised by $250M (and FY MLR/SG&A improved), which should be a ‘beat-and-raise’ for the story the Street was waiting on—offset only by churn timing commentary.

Revenue and especially adjusted EBITDA came in well above the pre-set base case (EBITDA $5.5M vs ~$5M implied), and MirrorEye hit a new sales record—supportive of the back-half EBITDA bridge. However, gross margin declined materially (~277 bps), and FY guidance was reaffirmed rather than raised, limiting upside despite the strong quarter.

Q2 revenue of $3.1M came in well below the ~$4.02–$4.03M consensus embedded in the pre-release note, while management kept the H2-weighted revenue framing (Q3 modestly up, Q4 significantly up with two systems shipping). On the positive side, bookings and backlog stepped up strongly (Q2 bookings not given, but H1 bookings +1,120% to $35.5M; RPO +668% to $40.7M with ~57% due within 12 months), which the market was specifically watching for. However, EBITDA loss widened materially (margin pressure), muting upside and keeping the expected reaction near the median.

Q2 delivered strong margin and earnings power (EBITDA above the high end of guidance; spot mix improving sharply and July momentum accelerating). However, Q3 outlook embeds headwinds (gross profit per load decline assumption, and Last Mile facing additional $3–5m sequential pressure; free cash flow still negative with leverage/cash constraints), limiting upside surprise versus what the market may have already priced.

The market thesis was that the Catalent Indiana FDA inspection classification would resolve (VAI/OAI) and de-risk the Sept 30 PDUFA. The call instead said Catalent Indiana classification remains pending (a key unresolved item), while reiterating launch readiness and keeping PDUFA on Sept 30—so outcomes were largely in line on timing but with a negative surprise versus the likely incremental expectation of clarity.

EPS matched the high end of the prior expectation (record $0.58; Q2 guide band included $0.58), but full-year adjusted EPS guide was cut to $2.85–$3.15 versus a $3.00–$3.40 baseline and Mattress Firm margins deleveraged (consumer financing + store investments + deleverage). Revenue also came in light versus the $1.89B consensus setup, with weak July 4 only partially offset by rebound after mid-July.

Q2 topped both revenue and adjusted EPS vs consensus, but the key miss was guidance: FY26 pro forma CC revenue growth was cut to 3.5%-4.5% (vs 4.5%-5.5%), blaming slower BIOTRONIK VI integration extending into 2H26. Despite a higher FY26 adj EPS guide supported by buybacks/lower interest/tax, the lowered revenue trajectory and margin pressure (280 bps GM down) likely caps upside reaction versus a market that largely expected guide credibility risk centered on the H2 EPS ramp.

Revenue ($16.7M) handily beat the pre-release $9.2M consensus and reset expectations for near-term demand (95% enterprise; >60k drones expected in Phase 2 H2 with most in Q4). Margins improved to 34.7% vs the prior quarter, but operating expenses rose sharply (incl. large stock comp), and the company disclosed supply-chain/vendor and motor quality disruptions—limiting upside for shares despite the strong print. EPS is treated as non-comparable mark-to-market in the note, so direction from EPS is uncertain.

Results beat the Street on both revenue and EPS, but the bigger upside catalyst was non-consensus magnitude in flows and margin: record net long-term inflows (+$4.2B) and adjusted EBITDA margin expanding to 55.8%, alongside a raised long-term adjusted EBITDA margin guide (49%→50%). With the stock already strong into the print, the reaction is likely positive but not maximal.

Q2 net revenue landed near the pre-release expectations, and adjusted EBITDA beat the guided midpoint, but the bigger watch items were largely only “on track”: digital accelerated (11% vs. the acceleration narrative) and management still expects stronger Q3 digital growth. The main negative is Townsquare Interactive revenue still fell 8.5% Y/Y and management’s turnaround remains dependent on Q3/yea-end, while leverage is a touch worse than the note’s implied 2H math risk. Overall, guidance is maintained, so the market reaction should be modestly positive rather than a sharp rerating.

Revenue was within guidance but specifically landed at the low end amid late-June softness, while management reaffirmed FY26 revenue and adj. EBITDA guidance and guided Q3 to heavy pre-launch investment with the toughest comps; downside tone from decelerating active customer growth likely offsets the strong initial EBITDA margin optics (tariff refund benefit).

ARR growth accelerated to 12% cc (vs the 11.5% streak in the preview), a constructive quality/tone positive. However, the company reaffirmed full-year FCF $500–$570M (no guidance raise) and margin commentary/mix implies continued front-loaded investment pressure with first-half margins trailing prior year, keeping the overall reaction near-median.

Q2 beat on revenue and EPS, and full-year revenue guidance was raised to mid-single-digit growth; Q3 guidance also came in stronger (revenue ~$230M, EPS ~$1.11). Offsetting note: Q2 gross margin missed slightly (~42.7% vs ~43%) due to CS&I mix/services costs, tempering the quality of the beat.

Revenue was essentially inline with the $430M consensus and the $420–440M guide. The key upside was a large adjusted EPS beat (not well-modeled pre-release), supported by EBITDA margin expansion (34% vs 32%) and a raised FY revenue/EBITDA guide. Offsetting negatives were weaker net new ARR/license-services bookings and Biller EBITDA softness (plus the terminated-partnership charge), which were only partially anticipated by the market focus on the Biller sale process—hence a near-median reaction rather than a strong re-rate.

Results beat on both revenue ($203.3M vs ~$193.4M consensus, +~5%) and earnings (non-GAAP EPS $0.31–0.35 guided with strong FY, with quarter level far above the ~$0.02 consensus; adj. EBITDA $16.2M vs ~$7M). More importantly, management raised FY26 cloud subscription guidance to $525–529M (vs $515–521M consensus) and guided Q3 revenue and EPS at/above the pre-release H2 math, with cloud NRR holding at 115% and AI monetization momentum (85% of new logos buying AI).

Core ‘fundamentals’ were largely mixed: streaming improved materially (strong EBITDA/margin and clearer retention tone) but linear ads fell ~30% with further international weakness, and the studio segment underperformed on a tough comp. Guidance/action appears directionally consistent with the pre-release expectation that streaming holds up while ad/Studio weakness persists; with the deal-arb event risk already dominating pricing, the net reaction is likely near-median to slightly positive.

Q2 revenue beat and, crucially vs the pre-release note, written comps surged +12.5% (vs expectation of at least flat-to-positive to validate the H2 bridge). Management also raised full-year net income and adjusted EBITDA while keeping revenue unchanged; the tariff recovery cash received ($37.8M requested; $23.8M COGS benefit in-quarter) provided offset as margins still compressed (GM ex-benefit down 70 bps, higher SG&A, fuel/shipping headwinds). Net effect should be a clearly positive next-day reaction, though tempered by margin pressure.

Q2 revenue came in above the already-low bottom-third expectations set by the plant-down/dirtiest-quarter framing, and management guided Q3 to a return to positive EBITDA (adj. EBITDA $7–$15M) versus the note’s implied risk to the H2 bridge. The main offset is very weak Q2 gross margin (7% with incident costs), which keeps confidence in near-term profitability limited despite the better top-line. No EPS vs consensus surprise can be scored because the release/quick facts don’t provide the reported EPS figure.

Results and, more importantly, guidance materially outperformed the pre-release setup: Q2 revenue/EBITDA beat, and full-year adj. EBITDA, adj. EPS, and FCF were raised well above the consensus ranges implied by the note, supported by record backlog, sharp AA&S margin expansion, and stronger defense/naval nuclear demand.

Q2 revenue of $33.3M exceeded the ~$29.8–$30.7M consensus range from the pre-release note, and adjusted EBITDA reached $4.7M (strong profitability inflection vs the note’s breakeven/slightly positive expectation). Full-year guidance was reaffirmed ($130–150M revenue, $12–24M adj. EBITDA), which limits upside; with the note already pricing a credibility risk, the upside should be muted-to-moderate rather than explosive.

Revenue came in essentially in line with consensus (slight beat), while adjusted EBITDA declined to $5.9M vs the market’s show-me level (~$6.8–$7.0M), and near-term margin/cash metrics were weak (cash/net working capital only $13.4M/$695k plus R&D step-up). Guidance was reaffirmed (no action), which likely limits downside, but the Q2 EBITDA softness is an incremental negative versus what investors were primed to judge.

BRLT delivered a clear margin/EBITDA beat versus the pre-release setup (Q2 gross margin +360 bps sequential and adj. EBITDA $5.8M vs a $0.5–2.0M guide) and raised full-year adj. EBITDA to $13–15M while also keeping net sales guidance near the top of the expected low-single-digit range. Demand/booking trends (fine jewelry +32% YoY, orders up ex-sub-$500) came in stronger than the market’s margin-and-H2-Ebitda stress test, supporting a likely positive re-rate despite EPS being low-confidence.

Revenue of $235.6M missed the $239.7M consensus in the pre-note (despite improved leverage and a 30.2% EBITDA margin). The release was still heavy on credit/cash cautions: no clear wavelength re-acceleration beyond $14.8M, and free-cash-flow remains negative ex-T-Mobile subsidy (plus ongoing sequential revenue decline), leaving investors cautious rather than surprised to the upside.

Q2 revenue beat consensus ($29.1M vs $26.6M). The key incremental surprise vs the pre-print is the full-year revenue raise to $104–108M (midpoint $106M) and raised gross margin/positive FY adjusted EBITDA expectation. Offset: despite the optimism, management flagged slower-than-expected enrollment in colorectal and breast cancer trials due to training challenges, and adjusted EBITDA declined Y/Y.

Quarter revenue cleared expectations ($51.8M vs $49.8M consensus) and cash improved, but the key overhang is Q3: adjusted EBITDA guided down sharply ($1–2M) versus the preview’s expectation of an EBITDA floor staying positive. Cash bridge / convert repayment in Q3 is a partial offset, but the margin/earnings power step-down was likely not fully anticipated.

Q2 came in at a record quarterly level with Adj. EBITDA margin of 32.2% (well above the guided midpoint) and Adj. EPS of $0.45 (+80% Y/Y), exceeding what the pre-release setup suggested was a relatively “priced” quarter and pointing to durable operating leverage. Most importantly, FY2026 guidance was raised (revenue and EPS both lifted) for the first time alongside results, and management also quantified a modest Q3 gross-margin headwind (~75 bps) framed as offset via pricing—reducing tail risk that Q3 guide could slip below the ~$280–285M zone highlighted in the note.

Q2 revenue and adjusted EPS were broadly in the expected/“pre-conditioned” band, with guidance reiterated (but guided results expected near the low end). The main incremental negatives vs the note were (1) Take 5 SSS of +3.6%—still fine but not clearly exceeding the mid-3%/traffic-led bull framing—and (2) restatement costs tracking at the top end and EBITDA margin pressure, which tightens confidence on the clean path to deleveraging/FCF. Net leverage improved to 3.1x and SSS cohorts stabilized, limiting downside reaction.

Revenue landed essentially at the pre-release working consensus (~$582M; $583M printed) with organic growth broadly in-line (5% vs expected ~5% range), but EPS came in meaningfully above the $0.84–$0.82 consensus band ($0.90 vs ~+6% y/y expectation). Guidance was reaffirmed and the quarter had some negative offsets (Middle East disruption; tariff/inflation headwinds), keeping the overall reaction modestly positive rather than a strong upside repricing.

Etsy delivered stronger-than-expected core growth: marketplace GMS rose 7.5% YoY to $2.6B (three straight quarters of YoY growth) with take rate up to 25.9% and sequential active buyers increasing. Guidance was raised to mid-single-digit full-year GMS growth and Q3 GMS guided to $2.53–$2.58B, which is an upside setup versus the note’s expectation that only an above-high-end GMS (and/or a FY raise) would move the stock.

Q2 beat consensus materially on both revenue and EPS ($449M vs $415M; $0.35 vs $0.29). More importantly, management raised full-year FY26 guidance across revenue/EBITDA/EPS despite already-strong expectations and reiterated a still-moderating (but not breaking) H2 growth profile. Also, demand/base strength looked better than framed in the preview (underlying base ~3.3% despite episodic initiatives; higher ex-initiative growth), supporting the rerating.

Q4 revenue and adjusted EPS both substantially exceeded the pre-release “real bar” (and consensus), with EBITDA up strongly and World Cup-driven advertising momentum validating the favorable phasing. Call also reinforced an attractive FY27 setup (midterms near/above the prior cycle and ongoing bottom-line improvement in digital) and did not introduce key downside guidance catalysts.

Management raised full-year sales and adjusted EBITDA guidance; the upside is partially driven by a tariff refund benefit and timing of the GTS metals launch, while the company also guided to low-single-digit 2H revenue decline and EBITDA down vs 2H 2025—so the setup likely supports a positive but not euphoric reaction.

Despite strong order momentum (record $1.44B orders; $850M data center/hyperscaler awards), Q3 revenue missed by ~90M on production delays and guidance was cut sharply (FY26 revenue midpoint down ~$400M and adj. EBITDA to negative), with margin/production timing risks (Houston facility now slips to Q1’27) reinforcing downside.

The quarter delivered mixed ops (mil/government strong; Galileo online and 5G C1 records), but management cut key full-year guidance—revenue and especially adjusted EBITDA—citing Galileo/5G timing slippage. The lowered EBITDA (with litigation driving a large portion) plus reduced Galileo online target is the incremental negative vs what was largely expected from the pre-release setup, likely weighing on the stock despite improved Q2 FCF.

Q2 topline/GRLNF and EBITDA beat, but FY guidance was reduced (notably non-GAAP EPS and FCF via higher net interest cost from the incremental term loan) and Q3 faces a larger Middle East travel disruption than the prior $20M embed. With the H2 ramp still the key swing factor, the guidance cut should drive a below-median reaction despite strong operating demand.

Despite a ~4% revenue miss vs the thin-published consensus, gross margin surged to 33.5% and EPS rose to $0.43 (well above expectations), driven by normalized GRE margins and a GREW profitability inflection. However, meter/RCE base contracted and SG&A increased materially for higher-cost acquisition, which caps the upside.

Q2 delivered stronger-than-feared operating momentum (adj. EBITDA $220M and gross margin 59% with 200bp+ margin expansion), alongside retention near highs and member growth finally turning positive Y/Y. Most importantly, management raised FY2026 revenue and EBITDA (vs consensus), though part of the beat is weather/cost timing that management flags as reversing in Q3, limiting upside.

Key market risk was a second Iraq-related EBITDA guide-down or further delay. Instead, management raised and narrowed FY2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance to $490–$515M (midpoint $502.5M), which is slightly above the pre-release $480–$510M expectation, while operational updates (Acadia deployed to Jordan; Iraq now expected early Q2 2027) reduced some timeline uncertainty.

Revenue and EPS were effectively in line with the pre-release bridge/consensus; the bigger swing factor—segment profitability—came in weak (SOI $36M; Americas and EMEA losses) while raw-material remains a key $200M H2 headwind. Guidance was reaffirmed (no cushion), but Asia-Pacific delivered a strong SOI offset, limiting downside versus an otherwise fragile setup.

Q2 delivered a large revenue beat versus the $87.3–$87.7M consensus bar and posted a major gross margin jump to 56% (vs 41% in Q1 and prior 50% peak). While guidance was signaled as an upcoming Q3 raise, the actual FY26 guidance change was not provided in this release, limiting the incremental upside beyond the quarter. Overall, the beat + margin credibility should drive an above-median positive reaction.

Raised full-year adjusted EPS guidance meaningfully (low end above prior high) alongside record revenue/orders and continued >100 bps margin expansion toward ~20.5% midpoint, which should drive a positive reaction despite no consensus/estimates provided in the prompt.

Management raised FY26 LINZESS net sales and company revenue/EBITDA guidance, but the core scoreable Q2 number in the pre-release note (company total revenue around ~$115M) was not met (reported $113M), creating a modest revenue offset. The call was still supportive on demand (TRx up; demand growth raised to mid-single-digit) and also de-risked financing (convert repaid; <1x gross leverage).

Revenue came in well above the $143.9M consensus ($176.1M, ~+22% vs expected), driven by contract/production and backlog-related recognition. However, the earnings setup emphasized margin/mix risk; call out on SWU margin compression and advanced-tech/SG&A cost pressure offset much of the upside, and guidance was reaffirmed at $450–$500M (with capex $350–$500M), limiting multiple expansion.

LFST delivered a larger-than-expected Q2 beat (revenue $435M vs $414.3M consensus; EBITDA nearly doubled to $66M with 15.2% margin) and, more importantly, raised FY26 guidance across revenue (+$45M at the midpoint to 20% growth) and Adj. EBITDA (+$15M at the midpoint to ~$225M), exceeding the pre-release base case. Q3 margin guidance moderates sequentially, but that downside was largely anticipated given planned 2H investments and the EHR transition narrative.

Q2 results modestly topped consensus revenue (mostly consistent with the pre-handicapped royalty expectation), but EPS beat meaningfully. More importantly for the stock, management lifted the full-year adjusted EPS guide low end to $9.00 (keeping $9.50), and reiterated royalty guidance—incremental upside vs the market’s de-risking expectations as the XOMA/H2 accretion and synergy narrative translated into cleaner EPS credibility.

Revenue and EPS were far below the ~$3.99M and −$0.05 consensus implied by the pre-release note (Q2 only $0.7M revenue; −$0.07 EPS).
