The major incremental negative surprise vs the note was the worse-than-modeled quarter-level outcome (and larger stated net loss), partially offset by constructive clarity: SONATA enrollment complete and, importantly, Zynquista resubmission now confirmed with a dated delay to end-October 2026, plus expectations for DKA safety in STENO1. Operating expense guidance was reiterated (no meaningful help to earnings trajectory).

Q2 revenue of $54.0M is broadly in line with the ~$49.35M consensus implied by the pre-release note, and management reaffirmed full-year RNG guidance ($175–190M revenue implied; production/throughput ranges reiterated). The key watch-items are mixed: realized RIN pricing ($2.45) lagged the ~$2.54 D3 index (weakness vs the note’s RIN-price focus), but RNG RIN monetization via GreenWave delivered a stronger than expected profit picture (net income turned positive) consistent with partially priced-in upside from distributions.

Top-line and adjusted EBITDA were stronger than modeled, but the quarter swung to an operating loss/EPS loss from $12m of solar impairment. More importantly, management guided full-year operating profit and net income below 2025 (solar-driven) and flagged possible additional curtailment/impairment in H2—an outcome not anticipated in the pre-release modeled base case, driving a negative skewed reaction despite the stronger Utility/Contract operating profits.

Q3 revenue and adjusted EPS both beat the pre-release consensus, while the standout driver is the Q4 guide: $415–$425M revenue and stronger margin/ops commentary support upside versus what the market was already anchored to. Record book-to-bill and record Data Center revenue further reduce downside risk.

The quarter and Q3 guide both beat the pre-release setup (revenue ~$1.25B vs ~$1.20B est; EPS $3.30 vs ~$2.93 est) and the Q3 guide holds accelerating growth with strong demand/visibility through 2027. Despite gross margin guiding down (47% vs 47.6% with known ramp/tariff effects), the market’s main swing factor—semi acceleration and the Q3 revenue/EPS trajectory—landed better than expected, supporting a meaningfully positive reaction.

Revenue and especially non-GAAP EPS beat the note’s “whisper” bar (EPS $0.52 vs ~$0.43–0.47), and margins expanded, but the company reaffirmed FY27 guidance and warned Q2 revenue is roughly flat due to Q1 government order pull-forward—limiting upside versus a full re-rating. Net effect points to a modestly positive, not euphoric, tape reaction.

Despite no pre-release note/consensus provided for revenue or EPS, the release highlighted clear margin expansion (adj. EBITDA margin +130 bps) and strong FCF (Q2 record $60m) alongside leverage improvement ahead of expectations. Offsetting negatives include the disclosed tornado impact (Q3 sales -$20–25m) and a higher-than-normal Q2 tax rate, likely limiting upside to what margins/FCF already signal.

Q2 revenue and EPS were directionally in the low-revenue/milestone-lottery range the note expected, with no identifiable incremental upside/downside from the quarter itself. The key update—raising FY26 adjusted revenue guidance to a $255M midpoint (+$5M)—is only a modest change and not above the market’s already-cautious expectation set in the pre-release note; margin commentary turned more favorable via >80% opex cuts.

The key miss was guidance/action: management lowered to the low end (operating ~9% vs 10%–15% prior framing), implying further deterioration in adjusted earnings power versus what the pre-release note viewed as the “~$20M adjusted pretax income floor.” Positives like >3x YoY origination adjusted pretax and improved refinance recapture rate helped, but servicing adjusted pretax income fell >60% YoY with MSR runoff up ~80% and asset fair value/legacy reverse-related costs added downside.

No meaningful beat/miss expected for a pre-revenue print, and the key valuation questions were FDA process/regulatory risk and runway. The release reinforced: no efficacy-significant issues, no AdCom, and no 483s across both programs (slightly positive vs the note’s focus on relutrigine amendment detail), while cash runway was reaffirmed into 2028. Incremental spend/burn rose with G&A acceleration—consistent with launch prep—so the main margin read-through is mildly negative but not a surprise.

Q4 revenue ($608M) beat the implied guide range (street $597M) but FY27 guidance was cut/positioned below what the market was prepared for: FY27 revenue implies ~-3.9% YoY at midpoint and churn rose in Q4 to 2.2%. Higher gross margin and stronger balance sheet/FCF were positives, but tougher demand/subscriber signals and conservative FY27 transition framing likely cap upside into the print.

Results/volumes were broadly in line with what the market had already framed as a Q2 trough: volumes within the -6% to -9% guide and FY guidance reaffirmed. The main incremental negative is the stronger-than-initial Midwest premium inflation outlook (now >$130M vs initial ≥$125M), reinforcing margin pressure despite the reaffirmation.

Q2 delivered the first positive operating EBITDA and EPS inflection, but the release lacked hard upside vs the pre-print on the near-term EPS/revenue lines; management also guided to more typical (less dramatic) YoY gains over the next three quarters, offsetting optimism. Key upside was continued strong Pier 17 sell-through (narrative supportive); key negative was entertainment segment EBITDA declining on higher costs and lost sponsorship renewal.

Revenue and especially adjusted EBITDA came in materially below the guided/expected range, and management went further than the market feared by suspending all guidance (including FY26 EBITDA). The only meaningful offset was strong CTV growth and rising enterprise/omnichannel mix, but the suspended outlook likely drives a negative re-rating given TEAD’s high sensitivity to the H2 EBITDA bridge.

Q1 revenue (+6.4% vs $249.7M consensus) and adj. EPS (+11.1% vs $0.88–0.89) beat a setup where quarter prints were expected to be “noise” versus the bigger guidance reset. However, the guide raise is largely acquisition-mechanical and is broadly in line with the note’s raised/pro-forma expectations; gross margin still declined (55% down 120 bps Y/Y) consistent with the market’s margin-watch concern, limiting upside.

Q2 revenue came in above the ~$255.8M–$258.1M market range on higher closings/ASP, but the quarter’s profitability was much worse than implied by the setup: EPS $0.03 vs ~$0.08 consensus, with margin deterioration (17.6% GAAP; 780 bps incentives) and large impairments/abandonments. Most importantly, Q3 gross margin guidance stepped down to 16%–16.5% and incentives expected to rise further, undercutting the note’s base case that required ~17.3%+ GM; this is the dominant driver for a negative reaction.

Revenue and profitability beat the preview’s centered view (Adj. EBITDA $206M and margin 28.2% vs modeled ~25%/mid ~180M), but management guided the full year toward the low end and explicitly warned of 2H SuperPlay declines from front-loaded UA tied to the earnout. Added demand/DAU deterioration (weaker MAUs/paying users) offsets the EBITDA upside, implying a roughly median-to-slightly-positive tape.

P&L largely matches the pre-release framing (no meaningful upside to the quarter), but the call added a key operational catalyst by indicating OCU410ST interim decision structure/timing and reaffirming multiple late-stage milestones. Still, cash dilution risk is mitigated mainly by the already-telegraphed convert, so the net setup looks closer to a base-case/coin-flip than a material beat.

Q2 revenue (including discontinued TheFork) came in modestly below the top of the guided/consensus band (~-1.5%), while margins and Hotels & Other profitability were largely in-line. However, Q3 guidance for continuing operations revenue implies a further deterioration (7–10% decline) rather than a simple “flat-through-the-year” feel, with experiences revenue lagging bookings (5–7% bookings vs -2% to +1% revenue), which likely drives a slightly negative-to-mixed reaction given the pre-release market left tail and already-low expectations.

Despite the pre-release flag that Q2 adj. EPS conversion could miss, management delivered a clearly stronger operating trajectory (Strategic Grow/Vector momentum, record 29% EBITDA margins, stronger FCF and net cash). Most importantly, Q3 strategic revenue guidance was materially above the setup’s ‘demanding ramp’ risk, supporting an upside-than-base stock reaction. Revenue/EPS numeric beats vs consensus are not provided in the facts, so those surprise fields are marked unknown/inline.

Q2 contract sales and VPG materially exceeded the pre-release setup (which focused on a potential H2 deceleration), and management raised FY adjusted EBITDA and contract-sales growth. Despite a higher reserve rate (a potential EPS risk), the combination of upside guide and accelerating sales/FCF is likely to drive a clearly positive tape reaction versus the already re-rated baseline.

Results beat the market bar on revenue and—most importantly—the margin step-up (Q2 adj. EBITDA margin 19.2% vs the note’s sub-18% risk). Management also raised FY26 revenue growth and adj. EBITDA margin ranges, and guided better deleveraging; EPS reaction is harder to underwrite because consensus/GAAP-versus-adjusted comparability in the note was flagged as unreliable.

Results beat (revenue and EPS) and—most importantly—management raised the full-year guidance midpoint across key metrics (unlike the pre-release setup where a reaffirm-only looked likely/was the market risk). Margin improved ~100 bps and Greater China demand strengthened, partially offset by disclosed H2 headwinds (Nashik fire/May FDA inspection) and China growth moderation due to channel policy.

EPS guidance was raised to $3.45–$3.55 (above the pre-release expectation set of ~$3.35–$3.50), but the call also flagged meaningful underlying margin pressure in Repair Solutions (leadership change and $7–8M revision) and a Mobility Tech headwind/guide trimming. With revenue quality flagged as potentially noisy by the Teletrac close timing, the net is a modestly positive reaction driven mainly by the EPS guide lift and strong buyback/cash flow.

Q2 revenue and EPS landed essentially in the middle of the pre-release consensus band, and FY26 revenue/adj. EBITDA guidance was reaffirmed exactly where the note expected—so the quarter itself was largely priced in. However, Q2 adjusted EBITDA was worse than the guided trough implied in the preview (-26.6M vs roughly -15M to -19M), and gross profit was heavily pressured by discrete costs (including excess breaker impact and butter exit), which adds downside risk sentiment despite the reaffirmed outlook. Balance-sheet action (revolver used, term loan added) and share repurchase termination are also incremental negatives vs the already-cautious setup, partially offset by retail share gains and narrowing price gaps.

EPS was not cleanly comparable to the pre-note’s ambiguous consensus basis, but the call disclosed additional Q3 credit-related charges ($12–$16M) and indicated the core business may land at the lower end of original guidance if conditions persist—both represent incremental negative surprises versus the note’s “no new charges / repurchases” setup, offset somewhat by durable servicing and constructive remaining GSE capacity.

Revenue outperformed the more relevant pre-release consensus bar ($18.6B vs ~$17.73B) largely aided by stronger net investment income. EPS/earnings quality was broadly in line with the market’s worked-for range, while the key margin debate landed as still-below-target auto profitability (auto combined 83.3%; mgmt flagged BI severity watch and potential normalization), limiting upside follow-through given the note’s ‘fade strength’ setup.

Q2 revenue $92.1M beat the ~$90.7M consensus setup, driven by Recorlev $56.8M (+81% YoY) and ~400bp gross margin expansion to ~86%. Most importantly, management raised the FY2026 revenue guide to $385–390M (tightened/raised bottom end), which—per the preview—was the key swing factor; the call also showed Adj. EBITDA +50% YoY to $19.3M while maintaining a strong demand narrative (record starts/referrals).

Q2 revenue was essentially inline, but EPS missed (adjusted EPS $1.87 vs ~$1.84–$1.86 expected) while U.S. Companion Animal and Dermatology weakened more than the pre-release setup implied. The key negative was full-year guidance: revenue and adjusted EPS were cut materially below the $9.68–$9.96B and $6.85–$7.00 bands in the note, confirming another credibility/growth-reset event. Options were pricing ~10% absolute movement, so the guidance miss supports an outsized downside reaction vs median.

Revenue was essentially in-line and full-year guidance was reaffirmed (flat–up 2% revenue; 29–30% EBITDA), limiting upside. However, EPS appears weaker than the pre-release consensus yardstick even as EBITDA margin beat (29.4% vs the high end), and guidance credibility centers on later margin/H2 ramp; partial offset suggests a roughly median-to-slightly positive reaction.

Q2 revenue of $102.9M missed the ~$109M consensus despite better-than-expected margin (EBITDA margin +70 bps to 32.3%) and insurance-driven pre-need growth. However, management lowered FY26 revenue guidance by ~$5M (to $435–445M), with volume still running negative Y/Y through 1H—more negative than the note’s base-case expectation of an unchanged $440–450M revenue stance and a modestly below-consensus quarter.

Q2 revenue came in well below the pre-release $24.5M expectation (reported $22.3M) on lower billed hours. FY guidance was maintained—revenue expected to stay roughly consistent with 2025 (implied below the preview’s low–mid single-digit growth setup)—and adjusted EBITDA was still negative, undermining the key breakeven/better profitability tail case; despite a GAAP loss narrowing vs the prior year, there was no upside in the demand/margins that the preview’s base/bull relied on.

Q2 sales and (implied) adjusted EPS were largely in line with the pre-release range, but the bigger swing was profitability: adjusted EBITDA missed on margin pressure from materials/wage/tariffs. Offsetting positives were free cash flow inflecting to +$16M and net new business awards staying ahead of the FY target; management also reaffirmed the full-year adjusted EBITDA midpoint, supporting the H2 margin/cash ramp despite the Q2 miss.

Q2 delivered revenue and adj. EBITDA margin above the pre-release implied bar, and management raised FY2026 sales/EBITDA and FCF guidance while citing stronger commercial vehicle demand. The key offset is that full-year EPS guidance was cut to ~$2 despite the operating/FCF lift, and EPS reported timing/definitions appear to differ from the street’s adjusted EPS setup.

EPS beat consensus ($0.47 vs $0.4057, ~+15.7%) with further core pawn strength (24% revenue / 28% GP; same-store core pawn GP +13%) and expanding adjusted EBITDA margin (+190 bps). Scrap margin fell to 26% as expected given gold pressure; management reiterated continued normalization toward 15%-20% if gold doesn’t rise, keeping guidance action effectively unchanged.

Adj. EPS of $0.88 was essentially in the modal/base case embedded in the pre-release note (stale consensus vs an effective whisper), with FY26 guidance reiterated at the $4.14–$4.34 range midpoint ($4.24). The clean upside was the reiterated/heightened conviction on at least one additional 2026 data-center ESA (pipeline not in the plan), but the quarter didn’t deliver a new quantified ‘beat’ versus what the note expected on weather-normalized demand and FY26 midpoint.

Adjusted EBITDA of $93.3M was essentially inline with the pre-release benchmark ($95–105M whisper; UBS ~$93M). However, management’s carbon EBITDA composition was strong (nearly $59M carbon net EBITDA) and Q3 crush margins were described as only slightly below Q2, which partially offsets the market’s key worry about maintenance-driven weakness. No new 45Z guidance raise was reported, limiting upside.

Q2 operating performance was mostly strong (revenue and EBITDA/margins above expectations; RPD/RPU beat) but the release included a meaningful FY26 EBITDA/liquidity guidance cut and heavy recall/usage headwinds. With the Q2 itself largely de-risked by the June 24 pre-announcement, the guidance downgrade dominates, keeping the reaction near-median/slightly negative.

Adjusted EPS of $0.65 missed the ~$0.78 consensus bar (and the pre-note flagged alts returns as the key swing). Management also guided Q3 alternatives returns to ~7–8% (below the 12–14% long-term target and consistent with recent weakness), which is a guidance-negative relative to what the note framed as beat risk vs potential re-baselining. Offsetting positives were record AUM growth and strong core FIA/UL/IOI sales, but the alts underperformance dominated the earnings bridge and outweighs the buyback/RBC/CLO mitigation reassurance.

Results materially validated the ERP stabilization thesis: Q2 revenue and (most importantly) adjusted EBITDA rose to $60M (4.6% margin) versus the guidance-implied ~$54–$65M band, and cash flow turned strongly positive with net leverage down. Management also raised FY2026 revenue to ~$5.0–$5.1B and reiterated stronger Q3 margin targets, providing upside vs an already-high bar after the stock run-up.

EPS and margins beat the functional whisper from the pre-release note (2.05 vs ~$1.45, ~+73%) and the combined ratio improved sharply (64.9% vs ~mid-70s base). However, the release still showed premium pressure (GPW -5.5% and policies in force -1.4%) that was a key overhang in the note, limiting upside.

Results beat on both revenue and profitability (adj. EBITDA margin +80 bps to 14.3%). Q3 guidance also lands toward the top of the preview’s implied range (revenue $63.5–64.5M; EBITDA $8.5–9.5M) with a continued growth/margin narrative. The only notable negative vs the note is APAC decline (-6.7% YoY), which fits the cautious geography setup.

Q2 revenue came in above the pre-release band (improving 500 bps vs Q1), while adjusted EBITDA margin hit 3% versus a ≥2.5% gate, indicating the operational inflection the market was waiting for. Most notably, management raised full-year revenue/EBITDA expectations and guided Q4 to growth with ~200 bps margin expansion (despite the 53rd-week distortion), which is a new positive versus the note’s base-case expectation of little net upside unless margins/2H language quantified.

Q2 revenue and EBITDA aligned with the pre-release setup (consensus sat near the top of the guided range, so an in-line quarter is largely expected). The key incremental positive was stronger-than-anticipated LEO/proof points—service gross margin ticked up to 36% and subscribing vessels ended at ~10,700 (above the ~10,300–10,600 watch window), with no guidance cut noted.

Adjusted EBITDA guidance was raised to $1.04–$1.1B (+$70M at the midpoint), which is a meaningful upside versus the preview’s emphasis that the low end was already hard to defend; additionally, Q2 delivered a record $281M and the company’s volume/Curtailment narrative improved (none assumed in Q4). With revenue/EPS not treated as decision-useful here, the read-through is a stronger-than-expected EBITDA/guidance and credibly improved leverage/FCF cadence.

Adjusted EPS of ~$2.43 beat the ~$2.30–$2.36 consensus range by ~5.5% (driven by strong Group Benefits mortality and ROE at the top of target), offset by a RIS investment-spread miss vs 100–120 bps (NII/variable investment income weakness). Management also announced a new $3B buyback authorization and kept full-year expense/risk-framing broadly aligned, keeping the net reaction modest around the median.

Revenue was essentially in line with the pre-release model, but EPS underperformed materially (non-GAAP $0.08 vs $0.12–$0.13 expected) as operating leverage didn’t materialize despite strong bookings ($13.6M TCV) and AI sequential growth. With no guidance, the market likely focuses on the miss and margin/SG&A pressure rather than the bookings narrative alone.

Q2 delivered a large upside versus pre-release expectations (revenue and especially adj. EPS), and the company raised FY26 adj. EPS guidance to $12.20–$12.70 (well above the ~$11.50 bar in the note). Cloud/services momentum and margin/cash priorities supported the raise, offset partly by weaker hardware gross margin and a cautioned Q4 growth profile.

With no pre-release yardstick, directionally the quarter and especially the raised full-year net sales/adjusted EPS/EBITDA margin guidance (plus backlog/bookings strength in Engineered Products) likely drove a positive reaction; partially offset by the under-review Southwest Steel Processing business generating a net loss and SG&A/interest headwinds.

Q2 revenue and (especially) adjusted EBITDA and margin came in stronger than the already-divergent/stale pre-release whisper, and—more importantly—management delivered the promised guidance update with a sales guide raised to $460–480M (vs $450–470M) plus higher EBITDA and new-wins guidance. Refinancing was also cleaner/more accretive than the feared overhang, and data-center/electric-grid metrics (T-12M ~$80M, pipeline ~$100M, installs into November) were supportive, limiting downside surprises.

EPS/revenue mechanics were widely expected to be strong given the known oil price unwind and the note’s framing; the incremental upside from Q2 production beating midpoint is partly offset by key negatives that the market was watching—Hai Su Vang-4X dry hole/resource revision—and management signaling higher (potentially materially higher) 2027 CapEx with possible periods of negative FCF. The main actionable surprise is the capex midpoint raise (signal of higher growth spend risk).

Retail delivered record results and PENN raised full-year 2026 retail revenue and retail adj. EBITDAR at the midpoint; however, consolidated EPS/revenue vs consensus and whether the Interactive revenue cut vs the note’s expectations drives a downside (despite maintaining Interactive adj. EBITDA) are less clean from the facts provided, making the net reaction likely modestly positive rather than a large beat.

Revenue and Q3 EPS landed around expectations, but guidance disappointed: full-year adjusted diluted EPS was cut (midpoint $8.05 vs expected ~$8.40), alongside a free-cash-flow reduction (to $425–$475m) and a slower-than-expected DSO (98 days in Q3) tied to federal customer administrative delays. Margin improved, but the net guidance/FCF credibility hit likely drove a sub-median move.

Revenue and profitability beat expectations driven by tariff refunds (+$3M; ~160 bps gross margin lift) and record H1 free cash flow. Management raised FY revenue and specifically increased FY free-cash-flow guidance to $45–$50M, while keeping adjusted EBITDA and leverage guidance unchanged; TRISM growth outlook (~20%) adds to the upside narrative.

Despite reaffirming FY26 revenue guidance (the key swing factor was not changed), RDW reported materially stronger Q2 growth, record revenue/backlog and a 1.42x book-to-bill, indicating demand/award strength beyond the pre-release setup; offsetting this, adjusted EBITDA remained negative and gross margin was guided back toward the low-to-mid 20s near term.

EPS of $1.00 lagged the (already-consensus) ~$1.14 expectation, with net income down 27% sequentially on moderating volatility—an item the note anticipated risk for. Offsetting positives (ROE above the 15% target; cost synergies ~$37–38m annualized) were mostly aligned with what was expected, while FX/CFD softness and weaker physical and sequential moderation drove the negative tilt.

Q2 revenue modestly beat ($712M vs $697.4M consensus) and, more importantly, normalized adjusted EBITDA beat the ~$130M guide by a wide margin (~$151M) with strong margin expansion. Guidance was raised for full-year pro forma adjusted EBITDA (~$600M vs ~$585M) and FCF improved (about -$65M vs -$70M), partially offset by still-soft bookings commentary (fuel/ME headwind) but bookings grew +1% and came in above the pre-reads ‘near flat’ risk.

The key overhang was FY26 guidance credibility; management reaffirmed $2.75–$2.90, which the pre-release note already expected as the likely base outcome. Operational updates (utilities settlement framed positively; AmeriGas attrition/leverage improving; slightly warmer-weather drag) did not change the guidance/timing narrative enough to create an incremental surprise versus what was modeled, so the reaction is near-median.

Q2 revenue ($321M) and adj. EPS ($0.26) beat the pre-release setup, and management raised FY26 outlooks by 25 bps (revenue/adj EBITDA growth and adj EPS). Margin expansion (+36 bps to 51.6%) plus leverage improvement and lower interest costs reinforced the upside, with little incremental negative commentary versus what was framed as the key risks.

Q1 performance beat the company’s prior mid-to-high single-digit revenue guide and came with broad-based demand strength (DTC comps +12%, Asia +25%, China >40%) alongside better-than-plan margin expansion (gross +130 bps, operating +150 bps). Most importantly for the stock, FY27 guidance was raised versus the pre-release expectation of a possible maintained guide (revenue +5–6% vs 4–5%, and operating margin expansion +60–80 bps vs 40–60 bps), which should drive a meaningfully positive relative reaction despite uncertainty on reported EPS versus consensus.

Q2 upside across revenue (~$219M vs ~$210M model whisper) and EPS ($0.39 vs $0.26 consensus) plus a strong EBITDA beat (~$108M vs $83–93M guide midpoint). Guidance is raised for Q3 (now $90–105M) and initial Q4 $100–120M, with added contract/ramp visibility (turnkey Hatchbo 660MW and more contracted MW), driving a likely positive but not blowout reaction given the stock’s already-risky, de-rated setup.

Q2 organic growth and data-center momentum were stronger than the pre-release setup suggested (record $763M organic; data center mix rising), and—critically—management raised FY26 organic sales guidance to 8–11% (above the prior midpoint/consensus debate). Despite a modest margin decline, EPS benefited from tax and strong demand/pull-forward, reducing the likelihood of the “beat-with-unchanged-guide” de-rating scenario.

Q3 headline is broadly in line with the note (quarter is information-light), but guidance improved: full-year consolidated adj. EBITDA midpoint was raised to $230M and Plant Nutrition guidance lifted, offset by Salt margin pressure (Goderich costs) and no new quantified FY27 bid-season commitments. Net: slightly positive but likely modest given expectations already leaned cautious and the quarter itself doesn’t settle the FY27 pricing question.

Revenue beat consensus ($153.8M vs $145.1M) alongside sharply stronger demand (orders +49% Y/Y to record $201.3M, book-to-bill 1.31x, backlog $298M). Margins and profitability also improved materially (gross margin record; operating margin 10.2%, EBITDA margin 15.4%) and STAND/operational gains supported the upside, offsetting the EPS math being only roughly inline given the expected tax/EPS sensitivity.

With no pre-release consensus provided, direction hinges on qualitative items: Q1 orders ($130M+) and backlog ($300M 12-month; $400M+ total) were very strong and support the stock, while GAAP and non-GAAP show a clear earnings/margin headwind (non-GAAP down y/y and gross margin hurt by purchase accounting and mix). Q2 revenue/gains guidance appears set up for a sequential dip, limiting upside vs expectations.

Management reaffirmed FY2026 EPS guidance ($8.40–$8.50) that the market largely already anticipated (consensus implied roughly a near-even Q3 and no big raise). However, the release adds a notable downside detail: the second-half APT uptick is now expected at the lower end of the $0.08–$0.12 range (despite $0.08 already captured in Q3), which is incremental to what was priced and limits upside.

Revenue came in materially above the market’s softer seasonal bar and record company history was confirmed, while non-GAAP EPS still failed to clear expectations (consistent with the note’s revenue-up/EPS-in-line-to-miss setup). The key incremental positive was the FY revenue guidance raise (to $805–820M), offset by continued margin/tax headwinds (tax rate up, DSO up).

Full-year adjusted EPS guidance was raised (midpoint $4.32; 2026 margin trajectory and margin expansion strong) and backlog/capacity/order visibility improved (SAT backlog record, orders into 2028). Some offsets were CPI hardware softness/retail weakness and leverage only modestly improving, but overall magnitude reads as an upside skew.

Q2 beat driven by upside EPS and a sizable FCF/cash-conversion improvement, plus operating margin expansion (19.4%) and orders with >1.1x book-to-bill. Critically, FY26 guidance was raised (sales +8–9%, EPS to $15.10–$15.40, and record op margin 19.1–19.3%), which is above what the pre-release note viewed as the modal base case (reaffirm/only modest uplift). Overall reaction likely modestly positive given expectations were already close to the consensus floor and the revenue print was essentially inline.

Insurance-related EBITDA uplift (Leer South settlement) drove strong headline profitability, but the key operational setup was mixed: HCV cash cost improved to $38.58/ton while management raised HCV full-year cost guidance, and met cash cost guidance was lowered. However, PRB coal sales were weaker (10.2Mt vs 11.9Mt in Q1) on weak shoulder-season demand and low gas prices—reducing conviction that the higher costs/realizations are fully supportive. Net: overall likely inline-to-slightly positive versus already reset expectations, with guidance action partially offset by weaker demand/PRB volumes.

Q2 delivered a clear revenue beat ($207.1M vs ~$178.3M expected) alongside much stronger margin performance (adj. EBITDA up 56% with gross margin up 120 bps to 42.6%), and management raised full-year net sales and adjusted EBITDA. The only offsetting negative is that FX headwinds still pressured Q2 earnings by $6.6M, but the raised guide and margin expansion likely drive an above-median reaction.

Q2 results beat mainly on stronger-than-expected EPS ($1.44 vs $1.37 est.) driven by meaningful fuel surcharge recovery (~70%) and record EBITDA margin expansion, while independent cases accelerated to 5.1%. However, FY guidance was maintained (4–6% net sales, 9–13% EBITDA, 18–24% EPS) and the note’s key risk was the unambiguous H2 bridge credibility with little room below the low-end EPS consensus—so upside is capped; net reaction is moderately positive rather than a large rerating.

EPS came in above the (ambiguous ex-Closed-Block) setup, but the print included a sharply worse Closed Block outcome with management warning that full-year A/E losses could run above expectations, and CareScout revenue/match pace remains behind required momentum. The stock likely still reacts modestly negatively despite the buyback raise because the major SOTP driver (legacy LTC tail) deteriorated while buyback support was at least partially anticipated.

CEG raised FY26 adjusted operating EPS guidance by $0.50 to $11.50–$12.50 (midpoint $12.00), moving above the affirmed consensus band ($11.00–$12.00 pre-release). The quarter also featured strong nuclear contracting (920MW of new long-term deals; 30% of output contracted) alongside better nuclear operating metrics, which should offset prior contracting-cycle anxiety and support a mildly positive reaction. (Revenue/EPS vs consensus cannot be scored from the provided facts.)

The release largely confirms the pre-announced “war-quarter” setup (race count down; Malaysia hosting in Oct; Apple TV viewership gains). With no explicit new guidance or upside/cost-flex surprise highlighted versus the pre-release framing, the expected tape effect is modest around a median reaction—slightly positive from the stronger-than-expected narrative on audience engagement/Las Vegas sales and the implied cost discipline (stable OIBDA decline vs revenue decline).

Power/CCUS and operational momentum were stronger than the pre-print narrative baseline (record adjusted EBITDAX/net income; Temple power output up with 70% capacity factor; PPA discussions narrowed). However, guidance action was partly offset by a much larger strategic power capital ramp (midpoint $400–$475 vs ~$280–$340 previously highlighted), raising the key funding/cadence concern that the preview flagged as a potential negative.

No pre-release consensus or reported revenue/EPS/guidance figures were provided, limiting surprise attribution. Key offsetting items likely drive a modestly positive but mixed reaction: underwriting current accident-year combined ratio improved (positive), but GAAP/group combined ratio deteriorated sharply due to catastrophe and adverse prior-year development (negative).

Q2 operating metrics broadly lined up with the preview (revenue/EPS beat derived consensus), but the release upgraded FY2026 guidance and added multiple quality details (occupancy/census, labor stabilization, MA pilot adjudication win rate). Offsetting negatives were the lower 2026 net provider-tax benefit (~$10m vs prior ~$21m) and the (implied) same-store discharge growth only ~5.6% vs the preview’s focus around ~2% and the deceleration watch.

The key market question in the preview was whether Lee would meaningfully improve the EBITDA trajectory and/or raise FY26 guidance given the “clean baseline.” Management raised FY26 adjusted EBITDA growth guidance to 22–28% and delivered a fifth consecutive quarter of comparable adjusted EBITDA growth with expanding margins and further cost/interest tailwinds, with no offsetting negatives on digital-only subs vs the expected trough baseline.

Q2 results exceeded even the top end of guidance (revenue, EBITDA margin and adj. EPS), and management raised FY and Q3 guidance meaningfully. However, the pre-release note flagged that consensus was already stretched and the stock was priced for a raise; with crowded positioning after two rewarded beats, the reaction is expected to be only modestly negative-to-neutral despite fundamentals.

Q2 revenue ($240M) beat the $210.8M consensus and management’s H2 revenue cadence ($~$250M/quarter) aligns with the pre-release range. Most importantly, Q2 diluted EPS ($0.63) substantially exceeded the $0.365 consensus and offsets the note’s key bearish EPS arithmetic; guidance reaffirmed FY26 revenue $850–$900M and kept EPS roughly flat vs 2023, implying less EPS reset risk than expected.

Q3 EBITDA was guided flat to slightly down, consistent with the note’s ‘guidance credibility’ bar, so the reaction is likely muted/slightly negative despite strong completion tools strength.

Q2 results beat the pre-release setup on both revenue and EPS, helped by heavy-commercial and other-segment growth. The key negative surprise was gross margin contracting (fuel and mix headwinds plus timing-lag on spray foam pass-through), but management framed foam as at least margin-neutral longer term and reiterated the main FY gross-margin framework rather than changing it—supporting a modestly positive tape reaction rather than a rerating.

Revenue was essentially in line with expectations on the consolidated print, with political pacing running ahead (a modest positive) but combined nonpolitical remaining soft versus the low bar. Management also reiterated the same limited forward-posture (no meaningful guidance change), reducing the incremental catalyst versus what the market already modeled given the TEGNA synergy/injunction overhang.

EPS beat was helped by a tax-equity/tax benefit and ISP strength (record AUM and net inflows), but insurance/Term volume deteriorated (issued premiums/policies down; B&C ratio up; smaller remeasurement) and management lowered the full-year sales-force outlook to flat-to-down 2%—a negative guidance/trajectory surprise versus expectations.

North America strength (142 rigs, $241M direct margin, $18.7k/day, and higher full-year NAS rig count guidance plus Q4 NAS direct margin $245–255M) was a key upside vs the note’s “in-line/uncertain trough” setup, supporting a modestly positive reaction. Offsetting negatives include International margin confidence framed via a broad run-rate target (Saudi reactivations lagging—2 rigs excluded from Q4), and EPS headline $0.74 being complicated by gains; excluding items management reported an adjusted loss (-$0.11), which is worse than the note’s consensus $0.11.

Q3 operating momentum was strong (record adjusted EBITDA, margin up), but management trimmed full-year adjusted EBITDA to the low end on inflation/macro uncertainty—consistent with the market waiting for a cash/FCF-leverage explanation. The key negative is the guidance action/cash conservatism rather than the quarter itself, limiting upside.

ORA beat revenue and expanded gross margin, and importantly raised FY26 revenue and adjusted EBITDA guidance—incremental to an expectations-reset quarter where a raise was the main upside lever. EPS direction isn’t fully comparable to the note’s adjusted EPS range (net income per share fell due to a storage write-off), while management also flagged H2 storage merchant normalization, limiting upside and keeping the reaction around the median.

Q2 top line and adjusted EPS were essentially in line with the pre-release range, but the release added margin-pressure detail: gross margin fell via both buyer-funded payables gross-basis accounting and interchange “double whammy.” Guidance was maintained (revenue high end) but adjusted EBITDA/gross profit were guided to the low end, which is a mild negative vs the note’s expectation of at least a midpoint nudge; leverage improved to 3.8x (a partial offset).

Q2 delivered record free cash flow ($751M) and EPS/FCF strength alongside a raised 2026 oil production guidance and lower CapEx midpoint, with only one notable negative being the still-challenging macro/commodity backdrop (negative Waha) tied to curtailments. Revenue was not explicitly quantified in the call facts, but the guidance/FCF direction suggests the tape reaction skews modestly positive versus a low-bar, strip-driven setup.

While management raised FY oil production guidance (midpoint) and provided a clearer forward oil roadmap (including Q3 oil and the Silverback/tighter workover economics), it also raised FY capex materially and guided pipeline/shift timing to early Q4 for Targa—offsetting positives. Net: likely near-median reaction, but with meaningful uncertainty because reported Q2 revenue/EPS numbers were not provided in the facts.

EPS was far worse than the (thin) $0.25 consensus framing, driven by a sharp collapse in tobacco/ingredients profitability and a net loss, despite management attributing the weakness to shipment timing. The pre-release note flagged inventory/range risk as the key swing factor; reported inventory dynamics still point toward slower normalization (unsold stocks higher), keeping the downside narrative more salient than upside.

Q3 operational metrics (record GMV, 10th straight YoY EBITDA growth, stronger RSCG and GovDeals execution) were broadly within the pre-release beat/meet rubric, and Q4 adj. EPS guide ($0.41–0.50) remains effectively in line with the ~$0.43 embedded expectation. Any upside is more about quality of execution than a new guidance step-up.

Revenue came in above the Street, but EPS missed meaningfully versus $1.38 consensus and the key driver—Specialty combined ratio—was worse than the low-90s softening framework. Guidance/buybacks and dividends were incrementally more constructive, yet the heavier Specialty reserve/combined ratio (98% vs mid/high-80s underlying) likely drove a below-median stock reaction.

Adjusted EPS/earnings power and cash flow came in stronger than the soft Q2 consensus implied, and LOE was slightly better than the note’s key $71–79M watchband (reported $72M vs expectation centered around the guide). Guidance was essentially reaffirmed/within expectations (Q3 production >35, FY capex $20–25M), so the upside is more about earnings quality (FCF, leverage down) than a major narrative reset.

EPS and cash returns were stronger than the pre-release setup, aided by firm EBITDAX and buyback/divestment-driven deleveraging, while full-year capex was reaffirmed and 2H production guidance was raised. The one notable negative is the reduced recurring G&A guidance (vs. a clean synergy/FCF narrative) and capex spending running below the midpoint due to timing—mitigated by reaffirmed FY capex and reaffirmed capital discipline.

EPS and EBITDA (and slipped the ERP timeline), moving profitability guidance below what the note implied as the minimum requirement for an “ERP recovery validated” quarter.

Revenue and especially adjusted EBITDA margin came in meaningfully strong versus the toughest seasonality comp, and mgmt acknowledged only a limited (known) Q2 pull-forward effect. However, FY27 guidance was maintained with an explicit sequential Q2 margin compression and resin headwinds, aligning with the note’s bear setup—so the net reaction is likely near-median.

Q2 revenue ($203M) and EPS ($0.10) substantially exceeded the pre-release consensus (about $194.3M and +$0.03). Revenue and key operating KPIs (record revenue/visit and highest daily visits) were slightly stronger than consensus, but adjusted profitability disappointed (adj. EPS down to $0.75 vs $0.85; adj. Operating metrics (notably gain margin and adjusted EBITDA) were better than the market’s worst-case read, but the equity/capital-structure shock dominated: a 10% preferred coupon on ~$1.65B plus ~330M warrants and the revealed hedge-loss/litigation kept residual common earnings power under pressure. Dividend suspension was expected, yet the disclosed preferred/warrant economics were an incremental negative beyond what the market had fully priced, driving a weak reaction percentile.

Revenue and total adjusted EBITDA margin improved versus Q1, but the key pricing benefit was pushed into Q3/Q4 (per management) and FCF was still negative (−$8M). With guidance largely maintained, the net setup is a modestly positive/neutral reaction rather than a clear re-rate.

Free cash flow beat and shareholder returns were strong, and guidance action was directionally supportive on capital allocation (75%+ return level). However, LOE guidance was raised (cost headwind) and margin trend is likely mixed despite operational volume support, limiting upside reaction versus what was already heavily centered on the 2H26 FCF/hedge bridge.

Q2 adjusted EPS of $0.54 beat the $0.40–$0.41 consensus in the preview note, while full-year guidance was reaffirmed at $4.25–$4.45 and the company reaffirmed advanced optimism on definitive data-center agreements in Q3. The revenue line is not provided, so the reaction driver is the EPS beat within broadly expected guidance.

Top-line came in record with strong New Afton/Rainy River contributions, but EPS was pressured by noncash acquisition accounting (Rainy River stockpile inventory) and consolidated CAS inflation, while guidance was effectively maintained with FY assumptions and heavy 2H weighting already framed in the pre-note. Net: limited upside versus what the market was prepared for, with some downside offset from margin/earnings optics.

Adjusted EPS of $1.39 beat the $1.26 consensus despite a 0% ESP setup, helped by an industry-leading adjusted pretax title margin of 17.8% (well above the 16.0–16.5% base). Adj. EBITDA came in at $49.7M vs the ~$48.5M expectation in the note (≈+2.5% beat) with margin up ~170 bps, and net leverage improved to 0.91x (strongly ahead of the sub-1.5x setup). The market’s main “upside trigger” was capital allocation; the repurchase authorization was expanded to $30M (positive), while FY26 adjusted EBITDA and capex guidance were reaffirmed (so no guidance shock).

EPS of $4.73 missed the pre-release $5.63–$5.71 consensus range (about -16.6% vs the midpoint), partially consistent with the note’s warning that the “whisper” implied a $5.75 beat threshold. However, the company raised baseline mid-cycle EBITDA to ~$2.9B and FCF to ~$1.7B (structural support for longer-cycle expectations), keeping the net reaction modestly negative rather than sharply down.

The quarter’s headline EPS was essentially in line with the pre-release yardstick (small upside), while the market’s focus was on forward guide/action versus the weaker H2 strip. Management offset key near-term risks with a higher cost-savings target (~$500M vs $450M prior) and raised Permian oil guidance (123 kb/d vs 120), supporting margins/FCF, but there was no major H2 FCF cut signaling a fresh bear trigger—hence a modestly positive but not outsized reaction versus expectations.

Revenue and adjusted EPS beat the (stale/ambiguous) $66.0M and $0.40 expectations, while backlog and space/order momentum were stronger than the note’s base case. Importantly, FY27 revenue/adj. EBITDA guidance was reaffirmed (no action), so the upside likely comes from verification of demand/backlog quality rather than guidance upside; one negative is gross margin slightly below the note’s base gross margin (~24% vs reported 25%, but defense mix was still a drag vs expectations).

KOP delivered modestly higher revenue (+~2.7% vs $506.1M) and meaningfully higher adjusted EPS ($1.37 vs $1.12, +~22%) while cash flow/FCF was record. Q2 core EPS beat consensus (and was not just cat-driven) alongside a materially better P&C combined ratio and higher P&C core earnings. Offsetting negatives were a lowered net investment income guide ($465–$475M) and management caution that favorable weather won’t persist into 2H.

Q2 revenue and adj. EBITDA/margin came in above the pre-release yardstick (record $66.8M; 89% margin; FCF strength), but full-year adj. EBITDA guidance was reaffirmed at $210–$230 (no raise to de-risk the back-half ramp). Additional positives—progress on multiple power/digital LOIs/late-stage negotiations and improved leverage/liquidity plus a larger revolver—support the upside more than a typical beat-and-raise setup, while the guidance unchanged keeps the reaction near-median to mildly positive.

Q2 revenue came in roughly in line with the soft-consensus setup, and the quarter’s profitability/gross margin was heavily driven by an IEPA tariff refund largely anticipated in the pre-note. The meaningful incremental item was the raise to full-year adjusted EBITDA and adjusted net income while net sales guidance was maintained; however, management also flagged potential startup/one-time cost pressure from the Hagerstown DC, keeping the net reaction near-median.

Q2 delivered a clear beat on both sales and adjusted EPS, while also expanding margins to a new record (40.5%)—above the already-constructive consensus setup. Guidance was raised for FY26 (EPS to $1.32–$1.36 and sales to $665–$675M), with management leaning toward conservatism (high-end 'meet or beat'), supporting a moderately positive next-day reaction despite some likely prior pricing-in.

Q4 EPS ($9.27) beat the $8.30 consensus backdrop, while FY27 adjusted EPS guidance ($34.75 midpoint) came in above expectations (vs ~$34.03 consensus anchor in the note). Demand/order/backlog commentary was strong and margins hit new highs, supporting a modestly positive, but not euphoric, reaction given guidance-setting risk already partially priced in.

Upside reaction driven mainly by a guidance raise: FY26 consolidated adj. EBITDA moved to $7.9–$8.4B and DCF to $5.3–$5.8B, with the new low end exceeding prior highs (clear above-consensus relative to the note’s $7.25–7.75B benchmark). With no pre-release note, the main actionable surprise is the raised 2026 stand-alone production growth guidance (from 5% to 6%) alongside strong FCF and margins, partially offset by the low D&C reinvestment rate (34%)—suggesting a near-term capital discipline/mix trade-off. Overall that mix points to a modestly positive setup for the next-day move.

Key upside vs the setup was operational/capital discipline: near-record Q2 free cash flow ($303M), debt paydown (RBL < $1B), and—most importantly—full-year oil growth guidance raised (to 4–7%) while reducing capex by 1%, plus strong early returns narrative (80%+ on new assets, $600/ft well costs). Revenue/EPS figures weren’t provided in the facts, so the earnings “beat” magnitude can’t be quantified, but the guidance package is incrementally positive relative to an already gas-sensitive street.

No explicit Q2 revenue/EPS print was provided versus consensus, but the key incremental datapoint vs the pre-release setup is that management reiterated/anchored a conservative back-half all-in fuel margin outlook (~$0.35/gal) while reporting controllables earning >$0.07/gal this quarter and continued tight supply duration. With limited upside confirmation beyond what the note already expected, the likely move skews mildly positive but not extreme.

Quarterly growth and strong EBITDA/margin expansion supported by higher pricing, but the margin beat appears largely driven by IEEPA tariff refunds that won’t repeat. Guidance was raised on adjusted EBITDA while net sales growth guidance was narrowed, plus management flagged Q4 margin pressure, tempering the reaction.

Q2 revenue (~$104.7M) landed slightly above the note’s $108M base-case expectation, and realized oil pricing/LOE trajectory were consistent with the market’s favorable oil-price setup. The key incremental item vs what the note flagged was the modest upward raise to 2H 2026 oil volume guidance (midpoint +~2%) alongside lower LOE guidance, but larger potential downside (hedge-settlement/FCF) did not surface in the provided call facts.

DE of $0.48 met the company’s guided/market-referenced dividend-coverage target, and Q4 guide (DE $0.48–$0.50; adj. EBITDA $19–21M) was maintained—so the headline should be largely expected. Incremental positives were incentive-fee momentum on pace for >$40M and reiterated valuation/liq optics, partially offset by the sizeable $19M non-cash OPI-related impairment and the note that recurring service revenue will be roughly flat at ~$45M next quarter as Greenwich/OPI fee roll-offs play through.

Adj. EBITDA of $1.603B (record) beat the pre-release ~$1.45B bar, and record Permian volumes plus stronger marketing ($~250M better H1 than expected) add upside beyond what was already modeled. However, FY26 EBITDA guidance was not raised beyond “top end” of the existing $5.7–$5.9B range, muting the potential magnitude of the reaction versus a guide raise.

Storage occupancy missed the pre-release watch (88.3% vs 86.1% Q4 but still pressured vs prior-year context, alongside management tightening delinquent policy) and EPS came in below the note’s expected ~0.80 (reported $0.63). Offsetting positives were improved disposal losses (+$24M YoY) and continued equipment rental growth with dealer/location gains; however, fleet depreciation still increased (+$13.5M) and expenses rose, weighing on margins.

Adj. The buyback step-up and self-funding Iraq narrative are incremental positives, though the release did not provide a comparable revenue line to judge vs consensus.

Revenue and EPS both beat consensus (not just inline): $576.5M vs $543.0M and $1.76 vs $1.59, with a material upside in EBITDA margin to a record 12.2% (vs ~11.4% expected). Management also framed strong demand/mix (Water nearing 70% of IPS) and delivered a large FCF rebound, which were key swing items in the pre-release setup.

Despite no pre-release consensus provided, the quarter showed strong operating momentum (45% revenue growth, 530 bps margin expansion) and management raised 2026 revenue, organic growth, and EBITDA margin guidance. With only limited offset in Q4 organic growth commentary, the magnitude of guidance upside and margin expansion points to a likely above-median positive next-day reaction.

EPS $2.56 vs consensus ~$2.50–2.72 range), and management did not deliver incremental guidance. The main incremental positive was operating cash flow of $335M (record, +119% YoY), while margin/EBITDA held at 83%.

Full-year guidance was raised and operations showed improving same-store margins/admissions growth, but the Hartford equity-method conversion (non-consolidated) and expected Q3/Q4 margin lumpiness/CapEx and higher debt temper enthusiasm.

Revenue and especially EPS beat the already-top-of-range Q2'26 expectations, driven by higher-than-modeled unit economics and strong cash generation tied to early workforce housing deliveries. However, inventory finance still declined sharply and the $48.6M matured note wasn’t repaid in full (forbearance/collateral), tempering the upside; net, the print should still be meaningfully positive given the shipment and profitability beats.

Adjusted EPS of $1.16 beat the ~$1.01 consensus, helped by a ~$50M Oncor catch-up and higher Texas earnings (+$138M YoY). However, guidance was reaffirmed (no upside revision vs expectations), and LNG Phase 1 substantial completion was pushed to Q4 (a negative), while ERCOT batch zero timing was delayed by the governor’s letter (further dampening near-term incremental Texas visibility).

Adjusted EPS of $2.40 materially beat the $1.84 consensus cluster from the pre-release note, driven by record midstream & marketing (~$960M) and upside production vs the Q2 midpoint. Guidance for the quarter was effectively maintained, but the capital-return/FCF framework and strong segment earnings provide an incremental positive catalyst despite the market’s oil-windfall skepticism.

DCO beat the pre-release revenue target (~$214M) with record $224.5M (+~5%), and gross/EBITDA margins came in stronger (28% GM, 17.1% adj. EBITDA) while backlog/RPO was also at a record. However, full-year revenue guidance was reiterated (mid-to-high single-digit growth), so upside is partially anticipated—offset by the stock being near highs and the market’s focus on future ramp timing (Vision 2027/Investor Day catalysts).

Even with EPS pressured by non-operating digital-asset and prior-year dividend timing, the quarter delivered the key operational inflection the setup note argued to watch: gross margin inflected sharply higher (40.6% vs 37.5%) and verification/certification rose (to $5.4M) alongside improving operating income. The big negative was net income/EPS softness from digital-asset fair value swings, while beef remains pressured; overall reaction likely modestly positive given the note lacked a usable reliable consensus bar.

No revenue/EPS or explicit guidance were provided versus consensus, but operating economics appear to weaken with the net loss widening and R&D/stock-based comp accelerating. Offsetting positives include a materially increased cash balance (longer runway) and progress on sample irradiation/examination and partner/MOU milestones, likely limiting downside reaction.

Revenue of $62.7M missed the stated $67.7M consensus, but the quarter showed a sizable margin/earnings swing (operating income +$5.8M; adjusted EBITDA +$9.7M) helped by $8.6M of 45Z credits—largely consistent with the note’s base case.
