Reported results broadly tracked the commodity-strip expectations embedded in the pre-release note (revenue/EPS not clearly beat vs the $59M/$0.75 adj. framework), but management delivered a supportive execution set: strong oil up move, maintained capital-return cadence with a regular + special dividend, and provided constructive Cherokee development/step-out upside while reaffirming a fully-funded $76–$97M 2026 program. With guidance action largely ‘none’ and the equity story already priced around hedges/capital returns, the expected reaction is near-median to modestly positive.

EPS of $1.09 beat the ~$0.93 consensus and the pre-print’s base expectation of $0.93–$0.96, helped by higher consumption and improved water supply mix (lower purchased-water reliance). Revenue came in roughly in-line (per the call’s YoY increase vs the note’s ~175M anchor). Management also cautioned the favorable mix may not persist, limiting upside beyond the beat; no change to ASUS FY2026 EPS range was indicated.

Q2 results beat the pre-release yardstick (revenue modestly above the ~$190–194M consensus band and EPS swung from a loss to +$0.06 vs +$0.02–$0.03 expected), and management delivered stronger 800G and CATV strength. However, the Q3 revenue guide ($255–290M) is notably below the ~$290–320M implied/expected ramp needed for the FY math, partially offset by continued reaffirmation of the FY26 ~$1.1B cap tied to capacity.

Q2 EPS ($0.10) appears roughly in line with the already-tight consensus band (0.08–0.09), and FY26 EPS guidance was reaffirmed ($0.93–$1.00), so the tape surprise is limited. Off-calendar, Bakken East specifics were more mixed than the preview expected: precedent agreements improved (nearly 1.2 Bcf/d), but the FERC 7(c) filing slipped to Q4 2026 (later than the preview’s Q3 timing), and pipeline segment earnings dipped, offsetting the otherwise constructive data-center/Badger wind updates.

AIP beat the quarter on both revenue ($24.1M vs ~$23.7M top-end) and ACV+royalties ($99.5M vs $99M guide top), and raised FY2026 revenue guidance to $95–$98M (above the prior/consensus range). Main offset was non-GAAP operating loss being pressured by unexpected payroll taxes, limiting margin improvement tone.

Results were broadly in line with what the pre-release note framed as “not about the quarter,” with CIS strength (99M, +39% YoY; GPUs sold out; acceleration into Q4) offset by ongoing Delivery weakness and margin compression. The key FY26 capex/revenue-math risk from the note appears largely managed: FY26 CapEx guidance sits ~at ~40% of revenue and Q3 capex steps up as expected, limiting unanticipated downside/upgrade catalysts.

The pre-release note argued the Aug 6 print/next-day reaction for LBRDK is largely information-free and the near-term stock is driven by CPUC/HSR timing (and CHTR beta). The reported quarter includes declining adjusted OIBDA (-11% YoY) and lower gross margin (to 75.5%) alongside mixed demand (broadband down organically, wireless up) and capex peaking in 2026—so fundamentals are not a clear upside shock versus what was effectively already “priced” for the trade; any incremental impact is likely modest.

Q2 revenue beat consensus, and AMDS momentum improved in the quarter (post-PMA blocker lifted). However, adjusted EBITDA margin fell ~90 bps to 21% due to higher R&D spend and free cash flow remained materially negative (transaction-related charges), while the full-year guidance was conservatively maintained at $480–$496M with no upside—limiting upside reaction versus what was already broadly expected.

Q2 revenue of $13.9M and reaffirmed FY26 revenue of $59–60M were largely in line with the note’s “modest beat / conservative guidance” setup, keeping the guidance-driven catalyst limited. Gross margin improved to 63.9% and the company provided clearer early traction for power liposuction on AYON (initial shipments, expected full launch in Q3), which offsets only partially any disappointment from not raising FY guidance.

Top-line SaaS/license beat was largely within the pre-release expectation (already flagged as likely), but management raised FY26 SaaS/license and total revenue guidance and lifted FY26 adj. EBITDA ~6.5M at the midpoint. Non-GAAP EPS of $0.77 is an upside surprise versus the $0.65 consensus reference, while GAAP EPS weakness appears accounting-driven (lower interest income) rather than operating deterioration. Overall, guidance improvement is positive but the market already penciled in a largely “flow-through” outcome, keeping the reaction closer to neutral-to-slightly positive.

Headline revenue and (implied) EPS disappointed vs the note, while management cut FY26 IBSRELA guidance to $350–$370M (below the $410–430M market expectation) and revised FY opex to below $500M after higher SG&A/R&D—together driving a downside reaction despite strong demand language and narrowing net loss.

The quarter’s revenue (~$3.0M) landed around where the pre-release note expected given the CSL wind-down, but management delivered a major negative fundamental: CSL Seqirus termination (replacing unmodeled future royalty/milestone upside with cash $12M and liability release) and reframed the key CF timeline to a Q4 2026 go/no-go decision. With guidance/guidance framing effectively worse for the post-H1 revenue ramp runway, the market reaction is expected to be meaningfully negative versus median.

Q2 revenue and adjusted EPS both missed the pre-release consensus that already assumed some high-margin transaction timing (absence of flight equipment sales drove results). Margin contracted sharply (22.9% vs 32.9%) and liquidity was still tight despite a 50% YoY rise in leasing; management did cite a $35M 737 sale plus expected engine closings in late Q3/early Q4, limiting downside.

Q2 revenue and non-GAAP op income cleared the top of guidance and were ahead of the pre-release setup, while total ARR growth accelerated and record net new ARR (29.9M, +35% y/y) exceeded what was largely a modest beat/base-case expectation. The key incremental positive was raised FY26 ARR guidance (midpoint 26% growth) despite noted FX headwinds, and margins landed above guidance with an expanding GAAP/NGAAP profile.

Q2 revenue ($10.0B) and non-GAAP EPS ($5.45) beat the pre-release whisper (~$9.9–10.1B sales and ~$5.00–$5.25 EPS) with expanding margins, plus demand/backlog signals (book-to-bill above parity; backlog at ECS all-time high). The main offset is the ECS $27M contract charge and expected additional charges, but Q3 guide (midpoint revenue/EPS) lands slightly above the Avnet-implied trajectory rather than below—supportive for a modest positive reaction.

Q2 topped near the top of the $32–34M range with non-GAAP operating income above the $5.5–6.5M guide, but the market’s key focus was the Q3 revenue guide versus the ~$33.9M implied consensus bar. Management guided Q3 revenue to $31.5–33.5M (midpoint $32.5M), which is below expectations and implies a weaker macro despite stronger Autopilot commercial progress; margins also step down to ~12% vs prior strength.

Revenue/loan volume were largely in-line with what the note expected (prelim Q2 revenue beat consensus slightly). The key new negative was guidance credibility: management confirmed it will miss the previously guided adjusted-EBITDA breakeven by September and declined to re-anchor a specific month, reinforcing the note’s downside skew despite cost-savings/opex improvement and higher HELOC share.

Q2 revenue and, more importantly, FY26 revenue guidance were cut sharply (midpoint ~$86.5M vs prior $110M and below what the market expected to require an H2 inflection). Offsetting positives: adjusted EBITDA loss narrowed materially and gross margin expanded strongly; however, the guidance reset and product-to-service mix deterioration likely drive a negative net reaction.

Headline Q2 results appear broadly in line with the pre-release framing (mechanically noisy Amicus stub), but the key differentiator was guidance—BioMarin raised FY26 revenue, VOXZOGO revenue, and non-GAAP EPS, supported by quantified cost synergies ($220M run-rate by 2028) and small stated VOXZOGO switching (~10%). Net effect should be modestly positive versus expectations rather than a large re-rating given uncertainty around the H2 bridge.

Revenue was in-line (high end of the already-guided $77–79M), and Q2 guidance was also broadly consistent with what was expected (reaffirmed full-year). The main upside surprise was improved adjusted EBITDA (~$0.6M) and better retention/LTV trends, while normalized gross margin was roughly stable (tariff recovery was a known distortion risk) and Commerce remained a mild concern but within expectations.

Q2 results and FY26 adj. EBITDA guidance were largely in-line, but the 45Z GREET benefit was pushed/qualified (could add up to $5M, with delay risk into 2027), tempering upside. Cash improved and upstream RNG neared breakeven (positive), while volume growth mix skewed toward conventional gas and X15N adoption remained slow (negative), leaving the net reaction near-median.

Revenue was essentially inline vs the pre-release expectation. The key upside was management providing concrete financing structure details (triple-net lease with near-100% NOI margin, tenant enabling non-dilutive/favorable financing) that the note flagged as the main catalyst; the key downside was weaker gross margin (38% vs 40% expected trend) and a still mechanically large GAAP BTC mark-to-market loss, partially offset by normalization.

Q3 revenue was in the expected $68–72M range, but adjusted EBITDA beat the $8–12M band (13.5M) with margin mix/OpEx improvements, connected services grew ~20% (15.5M), and management raised FY26 free-cash-flow guidance plus initiated a first-ever $30M buyback—these are incremental positives beyond what the pre-release note flagged as key risks. The main offset is variable license revenue falling 15% YoY and the Q4 guide ($61–65M) still pointing to a low EBITDA trough after the Q3 fixed license cadence.

Results were broadly in line with the pre-release framework: revenue was near the ~$9.3M expectation and margin expansion supported the operating loss narrowing. However, total cash at $5.9M (vs the note’s ~3.5–4.0M unrestricted/base-case focus) still leaves limited runway and the release did not meaningfully de-risk financing/going-concern language; the STAR-T data is a positive but the key “cash/burn credibility” detail is only partially better than feared, leading to a slightly negative-to-mixed reaction.

Q2 revenue broadly met expectations and gross margin improved (87% vs 84% prior year). However, management sharply cut FY26 revenue guidance to $58–60M (below the pre-release $63–67M ceiling/consensus mindset) citing onboarding/productivity drag from high manager turnover and persistent Medicare Advantage prior-auth approval issues—despite a modest Q2 approval-rate lift and strong Traditional Medicare reimbursement—driving a downside skew vs what the market was primarily debating (whether to raise/narrow FY guidance).

Pre-revenue results were broadly as expected for EPS/revenue (no meaningful beat vs consensus). The key incremental drivers versus the pre-release note were (1) Phase 2 AD enrollment completion now expected early-2027 with Q3 2027 topline (timing confirmation/new specificity), (2) Angel China cohort/enrollment and data timing refined for FDA filing use, and (3) HS/early asthma start timing before year-end 2026; partially offset by the reported Phase 3 PTCL interim futility analysis moving to Q1 2027 (incremental timing slip). With limited downside to P&L and a sizeable cash raise already priced, the net balance points to around-median/modestly positive reaction.

AVLAYAH/Ablea Q2 net product revenue of $3.6M materially beat the ~$2.15M consensus and the note’s ~“$0–$2.5M” launch framing, and management guided Q3 net product revenue to $10–12M vs the market’s ~~2–3x sequential expectation (implying a much steeper ramp). The key offset was a pipeline/timing overhang: DNL593 data moved further out to H1 2027 (later than the note’s “end of 2026” emphasis), which should cap upside.

Despite the depressed YoY headline revenue (prior-year Bayer milestone), MYQORZO delivered a strong $25.3M net product revenue and dispensed patient ramp (1,500 patients; >80% paid), both better than the pre-release product-revenue thresholds. The main push-pull was margin/earnings: GAAP net loss widened and EPS was still worse than consensus on the quarter, while OpEx was modestly raised (FY26 R&D+SG&A midpoint up to $875M), adding some dilution/runway overhang risk.

Revenue and GAAP EPS were essentially in line with the pre-release bar (low sequential expectations; EPS improvement largely matched). The main incremental support was the guidance raise (above what was already penciled in), but the tone still hinges on operating leverage/cash needs; cash guidance was not reassuring versus the note’s cash/balance-sheet binary, limiting the upside.

Q2 revenue and AI revenue were strong versus the already-low/managed Q2 bar, and management raised FY26 AI growth (to 60%+), plus guided Q3 revenue to a higher midpoint ($319M) consistent with the H2 ramp the Street wanted. Offsets were margin/EBITDA pressure (61% GM, 22% adj. EBITDA) and dilution from professional services expansion, but EPS guidance was left unchanged and the EPS line was effectively inline, supporting a moderately positive reaction rather than a blowout.

Q2 net sales were in line with the ~$13.8M consensus and with the ~$13.2M guide, and gross margin expanded (helped by a tariff refund), but the bigger issue is Q3 guidance: revenue was only modestly below the preview’s ~$14–16M base case range and adjusted EBITDA guided more negative than the market’s positioning around sequential stabilization, while the trucking ramp was described as beginning (not yet proving out at the Q3 EBITDA level). Netting cash/covenant concessions reduced solvency fear (partly priced in), keeping the reaction mildly negative rather than sharply so.

Operating tone was broadly constructive (American Place record-like performance; Chamonix near breakeven), but the key overhang—refinancing/construction financing—remains “still being documented” with closing expected in Q3 and no signed/committed terms yet, which the market largely pre-priced. Without confirmed financing terms, the reaction is more likely modest/median despite some incremental operational improvements.

Despite uneven U.S. growth, normalized gross margin (44.4%) and—crucially—adjusted EBITDA that exceeded even guidance (15M ex-tariff) drove a strong quarter. The key incremental catalyst vs the pre-release note is the raised FY26 adj. EBITDA guide to $100–$110M (and tariff-credit monetization/tariff-claim sale), which reduces the covenant/refinancing overhang that the market had already partially priced.

Revenue landed at the top of the guided range and slightly above consensus, while adjusted EBITDA beat despite margin still pressured by input-cost inflation. However, the key H2 margin step-up credibility is mixed: management narrowed EBITDA guidance upward but cut the implied full-year margin framework, and it highlighted ~$20M of inflation above plan and no underwriting of relief—so upside should be capped (more pop-and-fade than rerating).

Revenue was essentially in line with the ~$47M consensus set in the pre-release note, but the earnings print was dominated by the large non-cash Lake Preston impairment and a GAAP loss. The main true surprise was on guidance: full-year 2026 non-GAAP adjusted EBITDA was raised/quantified to “more than $60M,” exceeding the ~$55–65M range implied in the note. Carbon/45Z monetization mechanics looked consistent (including ~$17M banked CFR credits for Q3 and >$70M 45Z target), limiting additional upside beyond the guidance beat.

Q2 and FY guidance were both stronger than pre-release expectations: revenue and EPS beats versus consensus/preview, and management raised FY2026 guidance (not just reiterated), with EBITDA/margins expanding and additional collaboration upfronts supporting the royalty ramp.

Q2 gross profit (+18%) and gross margin (22.8%) and residents/scripts (high single-digit growth) beat the durability concerns in the note, and FY26 guidance was raised (revenue and EBITDA) versus consensus/near the top end. However, EPS and the quarter’s revenue were expected to be distorted by IRA pricing, limiting upside surprise versus the preview.

GMED posted a stronger-than-expected Q2 (revenue modestly above and, crucially, record non-GAAP EPS $1.34 with large margin expansion to 35.4%). Full-year non-GAAP EPS guidance was raised to $4.95–$5.05 (vs prior $4.70–$4.80), while revenue guidance was reaffirmed—aligning with the market’s core ask (a guidance lift) more than the pre-release base case; Enabling Tech revenue softness and Nevro declines were expected but didn’t offset the EPS/margin upside.

Q2 revenue was slightly below consensus but largely inline, while non-GAAP EPS beat meaningfully on lower tax and margin expansion. The bigger misses were operating quality vs the pre-release ramp story—book-to-bill fell to 0.85 and backlog slipped on slower federal awards—yet full-year guidance was reaffirmed unchanged, limiting upside and likely producing a mild-to-moderate negative/flat reaction versus the market’s hopes.

Q2 EPS materially beat the $1.91 consensus/management frame (+~24%) and management raised FY26 adjusted EPS guidance to $8.60–$9.00 vs $7.75–$8.45 prior (well above prior expectations). Revenue also topped consensus; the main offset is acknowledgment that Q2 IV Systems timing is aided by earlier installations, which should temper later-year growth and leaves some negative guidance-related risk around the pump cycle ramp.

Q2 results were roughly in line with the market’s thin-dispersion expectations (no guidance cut; FY26 revenue guide reiterated at $20–22M, implied H2 $12–14M). The main upside was demand/mix and execution (12 systems; Model 2 majority; gross margin above 50% for a fourth straight quarter plus improved cash burn excluding financing), while negatives were limited since losses and runway commentary held steady.

EPS/operating economics were better than the pre-release expectation largely due to the R&D rebate dynamic, but the big market question (UK MHRA submission) was not clearly re-confirmed as “filed/validated” versus already-priorized expectations. On top, management kept runway language through Q2’27 and reiterated low-increment ATM funding, limiting upside follow-through; net reaction likely near-median.

Q2 revenue of $1.5M versus the (pre-split) ~$1.0M consensus implies a clear beat (~+50%) and gross margin rebounded to 44% while management raised FY26 gross margin guidance to 40–45%. FY revenue guidance was reiterated, but improved profitability and a higher booking opportunity/defense traction are incremental positives not fully captured in the preview.

Despite a large revenue miss ($1.1M vs $1.84M consensus), the call delivered an incremental cash-runway positive ($50.8M into Q3’28, one quarter longer than prior runway) and EPS benefits from warrant remeasurement. Negatives were higher opex (R&D/G&A) and lack of any new OpRegen-controlled-trial timing language (the key upside catalyst highlighted pre-release).

Q2 revenue was essentially at consensus (~224M vs ~$219.3M), but management delivered a clear margin and cash upside (adj. EBITDA margin 19.3%, record +$37.5M FCF, gross margin 72.8%) and raised full-year 2026 revenue/EBITDA margin guidance; the guidance raise is largely in line with what the market already framed as the key variable, so the incremental surprise is more about quality/margins than the topline level.

Headline adjusted EPS ($0.30) modestly beat the ~$0.28 consensus, but the quarter’s growth was pricing/check-driven (transactions -0.9%) versus the note’s focus on traffic holding up. Offsetting this, management raised full-year system-wide comp guidance to 3.5–4.5% and raised FY adjusted EBITDA to $68–70M, aligning with the market’s key ask for a guidance lift; margin also improved to 19.5% (above the note’s flat 19.0–19.5% base-case).

Revenue came in well above the (derived) Q2 range and EPS/net income/EBITDA materially beat, but gross margin’s strength was partly flattered by tariff-refund timing (management cited ongoing margin pressure from the 10% tariff, stronger euro, shipping costs, and higher service mix). Overall reaction likely modestly positive given the size of the beat versus low expectations, but tempered by quality of margin and weaker operating cash flow.

Q3 comp accelerated to +1.2% with basket up but transaction count down (soft demand setup). Revenue of $334.7M trails the pre-release implied ~$343M estimate, while EPS ~$0.48 is effectively in line once accounting for the $2M insurance recovery that was already flagged as a key modeling nuance. Guidance was narrowed but not materially changed in the FY range (EPS midpoint roughly consistent), so the main incremental negative is the continued revenue/top-line softness alongside margin compression (down 60 bps).

EPS was essentially in line with Street ($0.47 vs $0.46). The key incremental item is management signaling a strategic shift toward holding more SBA 7(a) loans and re-evaluating prior Q4 guidance within 45–60 days—introducing downside/uncertainty on gain-on-sale and net interest income, partially offset by favorable deposit/core growth and declining deposit costs.

Q2 revenue ($13.4M) materially exceeded the ~ $5–6M derived consensus range, indicating stronger-than-feared milestone receipts. More importantly for the stock, FY26 revenue guidance was raised to $32–36M (above the prior $28–33M and above the market’s ~$30.8M expectation), while liquidity guidance to $37–41M cash end-year reduces financing/dilution fears.

Q2 revenue came in slightly above the pre-release implied $194M midpoint and non-GAAP operating income was above the guidance midpoint, but SMB weakness and the incremental customer acquisition spend (5x longer payback; $15–$20M NGOI headwind) temper the upside. Overall mix is modestly positive versus what was already largely anticipated to be a guided-down quarter.

Q2 revenue beat expectations materially (reported $31.6M vs consensus ~$28.97M; ~+8%) driven by better console/service. Management maintained FY26 revenue guidance ($125–130M) in line with expectations, while non-GAAP gross margin improved to 42.2% (up strongly YoY) and cash burn stayed on track—supporting a mildly positive reaction despite EPS being unavailable.

Revenue and, more importantly, Signatera unit growth (283k, +56% YoY and +34k sequential) and ASP strength (~$1,275) align with the note’s “$700M+ and 268–275k units” bar, but the quarter clears it meaningfully. Full-year revenue guidance was raised to $2.85–$2.91B (midpoint above the note’s ~$2.86–$2.94B expectation), supporting a modestly positive reaction; no material margin/op-ex deterioration was flagged.

Q2 printed above consensus on both revenue and GAAP EPS, and—more importantly—management raised FY net product revenue and net income. However, the tone was tempered by a sequential decline in new patient starts and the call also trimmed full-year royalties (partly a known risk in the note), keeping the reaction more constructive than extreme.

Q2 delivered a clear upside versus the pre-release setup (revenue above the already-tight guided range; EPS beat the high end by $0.20), and—more importantly—Q3 revenue guide was raised to $380–$400M versus an expected ~$350M bar from the H2 bridge. Management also materially upgraded H2 growth and advanced packaging growth, with gross margin/operating margin expansion and a stronger backlog/delivery visibility profile driving the likely outsized positive reaction.

Q2 revenue and—more importantly—adjusted EBITDA materially beat the setup (profitability is the swing metric), and management raised FY26 guidance (revenue to $516–$523M and adj. EBITDA to $50–$53M). Remaining caution: hardware is expected to normalize and Bridg reduced subscription margins near-term, limiting how far the margin expansion narrative can run.

Q2 adjusted EPS met the ~$0.80 yardstick and revenue was essentially inline. While the dividend was raised (positive), management also flagged softer CTU second-half enrollments and higher CTU legal costs; FY adjusted EPS and adjusted operating income guidance were set/kept consistent with the pre-release view, limiting upside and tempering the beat-driven optimism.

Despite a weaker-than-consensus Q2 loss profile, the release adds credible execution positives: enrollment completion pulled forward to early Oct 2026 (~3 months ahead), protocol amendment that still targets the same completion window, and balance-sheet strengthening to $101.6M cash with sizable net ATM proceeds—offset by the dilution/financing narrative risk and a widened GAAP/non-GAAP loss with higher clinical/comp spend. Overall reaction expected to be modestly positive/near-median given the timeline/financing items were already the core debate in the pre-release note.

Q2 results were solid with clear margin/FCF expansion and a demand mix shift (CTV/mobile/emerging), but the market trade was dominated by Q3 guidance. Q3 revenue guided $75–77M and adjusted EBITDA $17–19M, which is consistent with the pre-release bar (~$75M) rather than a clean upside raise. Overall, upside tone is present, but much of the good news was at least partly anticipated.

Revenue came in above the already-expected in-line ~$20.25M (reported $21.7M) and management raised FY26 revenue guidance to $86–89M (above the prior $80–85M range). Cash burn improved dramatically to ~$3.2M and operating loss narrowed, supporting the liquidity/breakeven narrative; the main offset is EPS still remains worse than the model/consensus directionally, so upside is capped versus a pure liquidity beat.

Revenue landed below the $22.65M broad-street consensus ($20.2M vs est.), but gross margin improved sequentially (16.1% vs 12.7%) and management reiterated FY26 $150–180M. The biggest incremental positivity was stronger margin and the cited $14–28M Q3 Drone Dominance contribution, partially offset by continued heavy opex (41.9M) and no clear delivery schedule detail beyond contingent shipment/competition timing.

No consensus/whisper was available in the pre-release note, but the call confirms a key downside already flagged—Gauzy production effectively stopped and REFR took reserves/going-concern treatment—offset only partially by incremental positives (new Klim license and additional aircraft program wins). Net: more negative than the base/non-event expectation; likely weak-to-mixed near-term reaction driven by cash/financing and collection risk into the November Nasdaq clock.

Print was largely mechanistic, but the release disappointed on the key binary: management attributed the Phase 3 IND/initialization slip to manufacturing schedule delays and said the originally guided YE-2026 initial 3-month complete-response disclosure is likely pushed to 1H 2027. With the catalyst timeline moved out, the market reaction should be meaningfully negative versus what was largely expected (pipeline start around mid-2026 and YE-2026 data reaffirmation).

Revenue and margins beat, but EPS significantly worsened (loss widened) on higher SG&A from the in-house commercialization ramp. The key driver is guidance: FY2026 net revenue and gross margin were raised above the prior range, partially offset by ongoing cash/opex concerns and outside-U.S. softness from delayed Europe tender updates, keeping the expected reaction near-median.

No reliable consensus EPS/revenue estimate was available in the pre-release note, so only qualitative guidance/financial tone can be judged. Management reported operating adjusted EBITDA of $66M (framing it as the best core quarter in ~3 years) and highlighted strong liquidity coverage for the ~$300M 2026 note maturities (investment securities plus cash), which aligns with the note’s key solvency trigger; however, trading gains and Babcock & Wilcox fair value were weaker than the modeled expectation (lower fair value driving a $14.8M drop in trading gains), offsetting some of the positive reaction. Overall, the setup implies a modestly positive-but-cautious market response.

Q2 results were largely in-line with the pre-release setup (adjusted revenue near the midpoint; EPS $0.16 vs $0.17 consensus and no clear upside gap). The key incremental item is the Q3 guide ($2.5–$2.7B), which is below the pre-release bear/base framing and reinforces rate-driven shrinking volumes, limiting upside despite improving margin and synergy progress. Overall reaction expected around the median, slightly negative/contained by priced-in volatility and the call-out that the Q3 outlook matters most.

Operationally strong: US comps +6.6% (above the pre-read mid-single-digit whisper) and Canada delivered profit/margin expansion despite near-flat comps. Guidance change was modest but positive—raised the low end of 2026 net sales/EPS/EBITDA (midpoint roughly in-line to slightly better), with commentary on margin expansion and debt savings supporting sentiment.

Q4 revenue (~$1.50B) and non-GAAP EPS ($2.95) slightly beat consensus, but the bigger driver is the new FY2027 guidance: EPS and revenue growth were guided below what the market’s base case implied, and the outlook includes a sizable Astral sales suspension headwind plus matrix/divestiture dilution. The quarter’s mask growth and GLP-1 co-prescription data are positives, but incremental negatives likely cap upside and keep reaction near-median/slightly negative.

Q2 delivered more product revenue and much higher EPS than the modeled preview (~$23M rev, ~$0.07 EPS), largely because IV+oral shipments came through as expected on timing while the company also emphasized completion of the 19C product obligations. With no new U.S. procurement contract still in place (key swing item), the reaction is likely modestly positive rather than a rerating blowout.

Revenue landed slightly below the already-low guided/consensus setup, and consumables/device weakness persisted. Offsetting that, adjusted EBITDA beat materially on margin expansion and cost discipline, and FY EBITDA guidance was raised—though FY revenue guidance was lowered (and the reverse-split/Nasdaq overhang remains), likely yielding an only mildly positive/relief reaction rather than a full upside rerating.

Q2 itself was largely de-risked, but the print still came in above the already-expected high end (revenue +1% vs consensus; EPS beat vs the $0.16 expectation). More importantly, full-year non-GAAP EPS and profitability guidance were raised and the exit-Q4 non-GAAP operating margin guide (~17%) supports margin expansion, partially offset by Q3 deceleration and acknowledgement that the sub-30K cohort turns slightly negative before stabilizing.

Q2 revenue essentially matches the ~$255M consensus framed in the pre-release note, while gross margin came in above the expected range (57% vs ~55–56%), supported by pharmacy pricing and scaling Mobi. The company reaffirmed FY sales/gross margin/adj. EBITDA guidance with no guidance reset, so upside is likely limited to the margin quality surprise rather than a re-rate on growth.

Revenues at $11.4M were roughly in the expected/consensus band, and FY2026 revenue guidance was reiterated ($54–57M), which matched the key yardstick in the pre-release note (no guidance reset). Offsetting negatives are that adjusted EBITDA loss widened and sales & marketing costs were very high (equal to quarterly revenue), while one notable positive is gross margin improvement to 86.8% and the July CMS G-code expansion (site-of-care access), which partially offsets the cost pressure.

Q2 revenue of $56.4M was essentially in line with expectations (~$60.5M consensus in the note), while margins were a bright spot (38.8% reported; underlying ~31.2% vs the Q1/previous run-rate), and adjusted EBITDA swung positive. However, EPS was still a loss and operating expenses/marketing intensity rose, and—critically—management reaffirmed the stretched FY26 revenue ($335–355M) and especially EBITDA ($44–48M) guide with only mid-to-high 20s% Q3 phasing, which the pre-note flagged as hard to deliver; that guidance-risk dominates the reaction.

Quarter delivered the core execution item that the market was underwriting—Phase 3 OCEAN-1 and Phase 2b LAKE both initiated in Q2, with LAKE SSRE framing (possible upsize via SSRE) portrayed as routine. With no revenue/guidance changes and no EPS surprise versus the already-predicted pre-revenue loss, the incremental news flow is modest but directionally supportive versus the note’s main fear of timing slippage, offset by remaining binary risk around the non-IPF ILD FDA meeting outcome.

Quarter fits the pre-guided trough (revenue cadence largely as expected) and Atera orders exceeded the ~40-unit FY plan despite capacity constraints—supportive for the Q4 bridge. The notable upside was gross margin expansion to 74% (helping the EPS outcome) and full-year revenue guidance raised to $610–630M versus maintained expectations, partially offsetting concerns about spatial instruments down ~47% YoY.

Q2 outperformed the pre-release bar materially on both revenue (+~13% vs expected ~$373M) and profitability (EPS about $0.71 vs an expected ~$-1.20), with major upside in DBM Global (record revenue, margin expansion). Incremental positive drivers were the much stronger Infrastructure backlog (~$2.7B vs ~$1.8B year-end 2025 base) and a completed Broadcasting refinancing plus the CONX transaction advance. The main negative was Life Sciences weakness tied to liquidity constraints.

UEIC missed on Q2 revenue ($73.2M vs $78.13M consensus) despite a large adjusted EPS beat due to a $5.1M tariff recovery that is excluded from FY guidance. Full-year 2026 EPS guidance ($0.45–$0.65) was reaffirmed and effectively aligns with expectations, so the reaction should be muted/coin-flip rather than a durable rerating.

Revenue was slightly above the $5.73M consensus, but EPS was far worse than the pre-release expectation (reported $-0.62 GAAP vs -$0.41 consensus). The key upside was improved liquidity/financing visibility: management secured a non-dilutive $27.5M credit facility and guided runway to 2028, which the note framed as the main risk, leading to an overall mixed reaction (still held back by the large EPS miss).

There was no Street consensus or guidance baseline in the pre-release note, so we can’t credit a beat/miss. Versus the note’s directional framework (base/bull assumed modest flows), results showed sizable AUM outflows (–$1.6B; institutional –$1.3B), led by legacy value performance and a shift toward passive—raising the risk that the next inflection (flows/MIS momentum) is delayed. While revenue and non-GAAP EPS were modestly solid, the flow damage and institutional outflows likely cap upside, keeping reaction near the median/slightly negative.

Revenue came in consistent with the pre-release “in-guide beat” bar, but the key disappointment was guidance: full-year revenue was lowered to $273–275M versus the market’s ~$276.9M midpoint expectation, introducing de facto 2H caution. Offsetting positives were a materially better-than-expected operating income / margin improvement and stronger operating efficiency plus first positive FCF for the first half.

Q2 revenue ($25.1M) landed roughly in the middle of the wide consensus range and therefore reads as inline to the pre-release setup. The key upside was EPS improvement on a narrowed non-GAAP loss and—more importantly—the non-dilutive $90M funding (plus management reiterating H2 self-sustaining), which materially reduces dilution/risk versus what was a live concern. The main negative is that R&D rose as expected and there was no overt evidence of an even steeper commercial ramp than the note’s base case, keeping upside capped.

Consolidated adjusted EBITDA of $21.3M is consistent with the note’s ~high-20s/low-20s expectation, and guidance was reaffirmed ($90–100M), keeping most outcomes priced. The key upside surprise was earlier-than-expected FCF (+$20.2M and positive H1 FCF) but margins/gross profit declined YoY on Conway depreciation/amortization and mark-to-market impacts, limiting upside on a near-term reaffirm print.

Q2 same-store sales missed and management materially cut FY2026 revenue and—more importantly—adjusted EBITDA, indicating the H2 bridge is deteriorating versus what the market was already bracing for. With margin compressing and leverage/cash down, the guidance reset drives a negative skew despite the on-balance revenue being near consensus.

Q2 growth and margin expansion were largely in line with the market’s setup (TOC comp drag resolved; gross margin up strongly). Management maintained full-year FY26 guidance and provided only expected-ish Q3 seasonal framing, while new-client commitments and 2027 retention derisking matched what the note had positioned as the key upside—limiting incremental surprises and keeping the reaction near median.

Q2 revenue ($475.5M) was roughly in the expected range, but adjusted EBITDA ($48.6M) and margins expanded more than the pre-release framework implied. Guidance was tightened to $167.5–$177.5M (upper end cut), with management emphasizing delivery-timing uncertainty (not demand), and the quarter’s EBITDA jump plus improved segments (notably Ecoverse margin pressure easing) reduced the key back-half ramp risk.

EPS came in at $5.60 vs $5.04 consensus (≈+11.2%), exceeding what the preview flagged as the likely debate (EPS vs unusually clean comps and Exzeo NCI headwind). Revenue growth at +11% was broadly consistent with the note’s low-information revenue range, while management reiterated (not dramatically changed) the margin/cost story via >10% ceded-premium cuts and guides Q3 ceded premiums around $96M; the market’s biggest swing factor (Exzeo distribution timing) was not evidenced by a concrete update in the facts provided.

Q2 revenue ($3.6B) cleared the top end of guidance and exceeded consensus anchored at ~$3.58B; adjusted EBITDA margin came in at ~35% with 100+ bps YoY expansion. Full-year guidance was raised (margin floor to ≥35.5%), while Q3 revenue guidance ($4.69–$4.77B) sits slightly above the ~$4.55–$4.65B consensus band; demand indicators (first-time bookers and nights acceleration) were stronger than the note’s nights-volume concern.

AMN delivered a sizeable upside vs Zacks on both revenue and adjusted EPS, helped by labor-disruption revenue coming in at $25M vs $10M in guidance; despite that, Q3 revenue ($640–655M) and core EBITDA margin (6.5–7%) were essentially in line with expectations. Demand tone improved (N&A volume growth; travel nurse orders up ~40% YoY), and the Q3 margin outlook suggests no deterioration from normalized levels.

Revenue of $898M was roughly in line with the ~$884M consensus (and the tape likely already anticipated FX/tariff noise). EPS came in far below the expected $0.36 consensus-equivalent: reported adjusted EPS was $0.52 but call framing explicitly excludes tariff impacts from the “underlying” line, and the note’s EPS math made the main risk the FY H2 step-up—while management reaffirmed FY guidance ($1.40–$1.50) without new quantification that resolves that arithmetical concern. OIS weakness and ongoing distributor inventory normalization point to demand uncertainty, driving a modestly negative-to-mixed reaction.

Revenue landed close to the ~$180M expectation (slight beat), while adjusted EPS materially beat the adjusted Street range driven by profitability/margin expansion. Offsetting items—ongoing BAQSIMI price/rebate pressure and continued IMS warning-letter costs—were largely framed in the preview, and full-year corporate sales guidance was reaffirmed (no guidance reset), keeping the likely reaction around neutral-to-mildly positive.

Q2 beat on both revenue and (pro forma) EPS, with stronger-than-expected paid adds and service momentum. Critically, management raised FY2026 revenue and non-GAAP EPS guidance (vs the note’s concern about an implied H2 revenue decline), supporting an above-median positive reaction despite some profit benefit from the tariff refund.

Q2 revenue landed essentially inline with the loose consensus anchor, but Adj. EBITDA fell to $8.1M (vs $10.8M) and EPS loss to -$0.13 exceeded the pre-release expectation of near-flat negative EPS. More importantly, management maintained FY26 revenue/EBITDA guidance rather than raising it—matching the note’s base case that a non-raise can disappoint—so the market reaction is likely modestly negative despite decent demand and long/extended U.S. Forest Service task orders.

EPS of $2.50 modestly beat the $2.41–$2.49 band, while revenue was essentially in line with the preview’s $716M expectation (well within definitional noise). Upside came from ROE staying far above the 20% target and a favorable Mercury contingent consideration adjustment; downside/quality risk was the negative fair value change and management flagging slightly rising delinquency/charge-offs next quarter.

Operations broadly matched the pre-announced setup, but the key incremental datapoint—Adjusted EBITDA margin at 49.7% vs the note’s ~50.8% expectation—was a downside on leverage math; additionally, no MBI financing/transaction update (explicit refusal to discuss) kept uncertainty elevated, offset only partially by slightly better-than-expected FCF/EBITDA-less-CapEx at $99.5M vs the note’s ~$80–88M proxy.

Q2 revenue and adjusted EBITDA landed at/near the top of the already-conservative guide, and U.S. dealer adds plus product adoption were supportive—offset by the still-visible margin compression. The key incremental positive vs expectations was management raising full-year profitability margin compression to only ~0.5–1.5 pts (vs the prior ~1.5–2.5 pts), while revenue and dealer-spend tone remained broadly as feared, keeping the net reaction modest.

Despite a stronger margin/earnings profile and better-than-expected Q3 adjusted EBITDA range ($325–345M vs $300M implied by the pre-release note’s math), revenue came in below the thin consensus ($752M vs $818.7M). Net debt improvement and earlier-than-scheduled capacity restarts were incremental positives not fully captured, but the magnitude of the revenue miss and mix/realization framing likely capped upside.

Top-line and GTV growth came in roughly in line with the pre-release expectations, but the more important margin signals moved the wrong way: gross profit as % of GTV fell and publisher-payment scaling persisted. Cash flow surged (OCF/FCF) and orders/AOV were strong, partially offsetting the margin disappointment; guidance was not a directional change versus expectations given the new widened-range approach.

Q2 revenue ($56.2M) came in above the low-end expectations, and management raised FY adjusted EBITDA guidance sharply (though a large portion is driven by the $6.1M IEEPA tariff refund and legal-expense offsets). Underlying demand stayed mixed (Adventure down materially), and Q3 EBITDA guidance implies limited follow-through—an offset to the headline upside.

Q2 revenue and GAAP/non-GAAP EPS beat expectations materially, with adjusted EBITDA clearing the high end despite memory-driven components softness. The key upside catalyst was raised FY2026 guidance (notably higher EBITDA midpoint) alongside strong cash generation; the main offset was that margin strength included a large tariff-refund benefit, but operational improvement remained given adjusted EBITDA outperformance.

Q2 revenue ($91.4M) came in above the ~$89.63M consensus (+~2%), and Corporate crossed $60M at record ~$60.5M with 103.1% NRR. However, management reaffirmed full-year revenue ($350–364M) and adjusted EPS ($5.55–$5.95), with 2026 EBITDA margin guided toward the lower end—exactly the key swing factor the pre-release note said the stock needs to change—so the guidance-driven downside case is avoided but upside is capped.

Revenue and the key EBITDA milestone beat the pre-print setup: positive adjusted EBITDA ($0.4M) and stronger Services/clinical-trial momentum versus the ~$50–51M revenue whisper. However, the company maintained FY26 revenue guidance ($192–$196M), and lack of an explicit guidance raise underwhelms versus the note’s expectation of flowing through the beat—likely keeping the reaction near-median to slightly positive.

The quarter’s P&L was weaker than the pre-release expectation (revenue fell to $1.4M vs $11.3M consensus; higher opex). While management reiterated key timing (registrational monotherapy in 1H27 and comprehensive dose-optimization update by year-end 2026), the cash burn was also worse than implied by the pre-note and there were no clear offsets—so reaction likely stayed muted-to-negative versus the market’s timing-driven base case.

Revenue and adjusted EBITDA both beat the high end of guidance, and FY27 revenue was raised (partly offset by a lower EBITDA margin guide due to higher AI investment). The main negative is the Q2 revenue guide implying ~flat YoY and zero AI-search revenue in Q1, which keeps forward-growth/earnings-quality concerns alive.

Paying-user growth (+96K to 18.9M) and a stronger-than-guided non-GAAP op margin (39.7% vs 38.5%) were the key swing variables the note flagged; additionally, management raised FY26 margin and lifted FCF. The revenue beat is modest vs the $625.6M consensus and margin/cost commentary implies some AI-driven volatility, keeping the tape closer to a moderate positive reaction.

Revenue was essentially in line with the ~$33.7M consensus anchor, but EPS/non-GAAP profitability flipped versus the prior year and, most importantly, management raised FY26 FCF guidance materially (midpoint ~$13M vs $7.5M prior), supported by a strong sequential FCF turnaround plus solid paid-member/engagement metrics and higher interchange. Upside is partially offset by continued y/y top-line pressure and lack of clear forecasting on when New Expensify growth fully offsets Classic churn.

EPS $2.20 beat the ~$2.12 consensus and, more importantly, management raised FY26 adj. EPS to $8.30–$8.40 (above the ~$8.19 consensus midpoint), alongside improving margins and record backlog (1.21 book-to-bill). Revenue growth was largely in line (~8% organic with Maritime still a driver), while Utility Solutions’ margin decline tied to NRG renewables remains the key offset.

Revenue essentially matched the already-stale consensus (and management confirmed the trough). The main surprise was profitability improvement (third consecutive positive adj. EBITDA) offset by weaker customer/order momentum and gross margin contraction; FY guidance was reaffirmed (no incremental upside).

Q2 net revenue and EPS beat the note’s already-high Q2 expectations, driven by a large IEEPA refund benefit that lifted gross margin/EBITDA meaningfully. More importantly, full-year FY26 net revenue growth guidance was raised to ~20% (above the prior 14–16% and above the note’s 'neutral-to-negative' reaffirm risk), which should overpower the partially mitigated Jordan supplier disruption.

Q2 revenue/EPS landed at the high end of the narrow range and adjusted EBITDA met the guide, so the quarter itself was not the surprise. The surprise was the FY26 guidance cut plus a very weak Q3 setup (revenue $55–56M; adj. EBITDA ~breakeven), and management also highlighted margin pressure and continued DOS→Ignite churn through 2027—tougher demand than the pre-print base-case framing.

Results largely track the note’s base case (revenue/margins improving with comps still mixed), but two incremental positives show up versus what was treated as the most likely path: Good Times turned positive (+0.6% SSS) and margin expanded via lower labor. The main negative is Bad Daddy’s weaker comps (-2.3% SSS) plus continued lack of pricing power on the back half, keeping the turnaround story incomplete; overall this points to a modestly positive, near-median reaction rather than a re-rating.

Q2 revenue came in meaningfully above the $131.4M consensus (and the note’s ~beatable bar), and—crucially—FY2026 guidance was raised to ~$540M revenue / ~$232M EBITDA (above the note’s expected floor of ≥$535M / ≥$227M). The only offset is a lower reported EBITDA margin (42% vs ~43% typical), but management attributed the raise to churn/price inelasticity rather than only tougher 2H assumptions.

Q2 revenue and EPS were essentially in line with the pre-release setup (high probability of hitting the quarter bar). The key new incremental positive was additional radar/iND880 commercialization/demand color (conversion speed, new wins), while guidance for Q3 (67–73M, core ~$40M; reduced loss per share ~$0.04) largely matched the market’s expectations, so the reaction is likely modestly positive rather than a re-rating.

Revenue was essentially in line with consensus, but the key surprise was a full-year revenue guide cut to $355–361M (mid ~$358M), below the prior consensus range implied by the pre-note. On top of that, international remains strong yet management flagged second-half distributor inventory pressure, while adjusted gross margin improved—supportive but not enough to offset the guidance reset, likely driving a negative tape reaction.

Q1 showed a clear upside with revenue $1.34B (+~1.5% vs the ~$1.312B consensus midpoint) and non-GAAP EPS $0.71 (+~3% vs the ~$0.69 consensus), and—critically—management raised FY27 guidance on both revenue and EPS (to $5.375–$5.475B and $2.87–$2.97 from 8–10% and mid-teens), flipping the key “maintain = disappointment” setup.

Q2 delivered a clear beat versus the (pre-release) $86.3M / $0.21 consensus—revenue +7% and EPS +95%—and gross margin printed above the company’s 40% target (49%). Management reiterated FY26 revenue growth of 40%+ (so no guide beat), but better-than-feared margin mix and concentration improvements likely drive an above-median positive reaction.

Top-line slightly above the ~$135.5M consensus, but EPS is effectively inline because the reported upside largely comes from the IEPA tariff refund that the market flagged as the key swing item. The bigger surprise is the refund being quantified/large (positive), offset by Q3 calling for normalization with gross margin only 35–37% and adjusted EBITDA 9–11% (negative for a stock already at a 52-week high).

Q2 delivered stronger operating leverage (Adj. EBITDA $1.5M vs very low prior year) and comp sales improved to -2.8% (slightly better than the -3% to -4% base case), supporting a modestly positive tape. However, the key downside surprise was new clinic openings guidance cut to 22–26 (vs 30–35 prior), and net clinic count ending lower than 2025, which dampens the upside despite reiterated FY sys-sales/EBITDA and the small spacing in revenue/EPS versus consensus.

Q2 revenue ($0.202M) beat the ~$0.183M preview number, and the call added continued customer engagement/proof-of-concept expansion plus a new $30K contract development stream. However, dilution/“2H hockey stick” risk remains: EPS was still a GAAP loss with operating cost pressure, and cash-use guidance was reaffirmed (no bridge on the back-half revenue requirement vs consensus).

EPS loss narrowed to -$0.01 versus consensus at the high end (+$0.02 / -$0.01 range), while consolidated adjusted EBITDA improved sharply and margins expanded. Q3 realized NdPr pricing guided to the high-$90s with a roughly $10/kg PPA (vs ~global ~$110 spot), appearing consistent/beneficial vs the preview setup, with no negative operational or run-rate slippage flagged.

Revenue and especially EPS came in well below even the already-discounted consensus range, but the core EBITDA/EPS weakness is largely attributed to known Bitcoin mark-to-market mechanics. The more incremental stock swing would come from AI/HPC disclosures: management reaffirms the 2+ leases by year-end and cites tenant demand exceeding initial expectations, yet it still did not provide the specific contracted lease/MW or Long Ridge close/capital structure details that the market’s valuation tail would require—keeping the reaction modestly negative rather than sharply worse.

Despite a strong gross margin and record Q2 sales ($117M), management cut full-year net sales and EBITDA guidance, with China sales down 20% operationally—directly contradicting the pre-release view that the key risk was a flat/raised guide. Lower guide dominates, driving a likely negative tape reaction.

Q2 revenue ($51.4M) and operating performance materially outperformed the pre-release setup, led by exceptionally strong growth in GMP consumables and an outsized adjusted EBITDA improvement. The key upside catalyst—raised FY26 adjusted EBITDA guide to $33–35M—was the market’s “want,” supporting a positive but not euphoric reaction given the already-crowded positioning and guidance still not a full runaway beat.

Q3 revenue and non-GAAP EPS beat the already-guidance-pinned consensus, and the company raised FY26 revenue and F&I guidance while also guiding/printing a higher EBITDA margin backdrop (38% adjusted EBITDA vs expectation of ~mid-30s). Despite some quality caveats (EMEA regulatory surge in SaaS; Check renewal timing), the Check ACV and reseller/bank wins reinforced the fraud franchise, driving a likely above-median positive next-day reaction.

Q2 revenue ($83M) beat the pre-release $78.59M consensus, but the bigger swing factor was Q3 guidance: midpoint $68M came in well below the ~$82M placeholder implied by the note (and downside skew was reinforced by softer volumes/EBITDA guide and a sequential product gross margin step-down from 43.6% to 41.2%). Management also flagged ~$17M of product revenue delayed from China supply chain disruptions, dampening near-term revenue visibility despite JLWS beginning to contribute.

Adjusted Q2 core EPS of $0.25 materially beat the $0.19 consensus despite the guidance framing largely staying intact; operating expenses were also better (down to ~$85M) with improving credit metrics. However, management disclosed new accounting that removes CECL for newly originated in-school loans (a mechanical offset that was a key uncertainty), and FY2026 core EPS credibility was not clearly raised beyond prior framework, limiting upside reaction versus a stock that is more sensitive to guidance signal than quarter beats.

Q2 delivered above the high-bar setup: revenue growth (36%) and DBNR (120%) accelerated vs the sequentially weaker Q1 backdrop and Q3 guidance implies only modest deceleration. EPS also beat non-GAAP expectations, while the main offset is the year-over-year gross/operating margin pressure tied to network cost allocation and higher-than-previous restructuring charges, limiting upside versus a fully clean print.

The call leaned bullish on ride quality (premium modes, partner-linked rides with higher-value skew) and repeated the expected narrative on the bookings-vs-rides gap; however, the pre-release note flagged that the trade hinges on Q3 guidance and the rides number, and the facts provided here don’t include reported revenue/EPS beats or any explicit Q3 guidance change to confirm a larger-than-expected upside. With wide ±14% options and downside skew priced, the base-case outcome is likely to be around median/only mildly positive.

Q2 revenue was essentially where expected (~$43.0M consensus vs $43.3M reported) but adjusted EBITDA loss narrowed to $0.9M (vs the guided midpoint), a genuine upside on profitability. The major negative surprise was guidance: FY26 revenue was cut to $168–175M (midpoint $171.5M), well below the $180–190M affirmed range in the pre-release note, and year-end cash guidance was also lowered to $30–32M, worsening solvency/burn optics into the reverse-split/delisting window; this overwhelms the operating beat and likely drives a below-median next-day reaction.

Q2 revenue ($42.8M) materially missed even the management-guided/consensus lower floor in the pre-release setup, while FY2026 revenue guidance was sharply cut to $179–215M (well below the pre-release $270–310M run-rate), signaling a delayed recovery. Despite some sequential share-gain signals and BLA acceptance, the new cash/dilution and worsened margin/burn risk dominate.

Quarter results beat (revenue above the high end of guide and non-GAAP EPS $0.16 vs ~$0.01 expected), driven by stronger-than-expected enterprise margins and contribution margin at cycle highs. However, guidance for Q3 revenue/non-GAAP operating margin is roughly in line with what the note framed as a low bar, and APAC enterprise revenue fell with restructuring plus continued consumer margin pressure, keeping the setup closer to median-positive than a blowout.

Revenue of ~$4.5M was below the Zacks $6.63M consensus and also below what the note flagged as the potential upside case tied to continued acceleration; however, management reaffirmed the cash-breakeven framing and raised full-year Thailand project spend guidance to $45–50M (from $39–45M), which partially offsets the revenue disappointment. Net loss/EBITDA stayed negative as expected given the ramp phase, driving a roughly median-to-slightly-negative reaction rather than a sharp rerating.

Revenue ($55.0M) was below the note’s “guide-high beat” bar ($52.5M guide high vs. $51.6–51.9 consensus) and the normalized GM still landed in the high-30s vs the framework, but the bigger swing factor (Q3 guide) was not raised and came in below the note’s ~$55–58M anchor. Management emphasized record sensor shipments/capacity scaling and Rev8 order momentum, partially offset by guidance/outlook rigidity.

Revenue and EPS materially exceeded the already-modestly bearish setup, driven by a large European ERC write-up (29% revenue growth) and net leverage improvements. Cash collections were slightly above expectations, and the company maintained its $1.0–$1.3B portfolio purchase target; with most of the upside perceived as ERC-accounting variability and the stock run-up already pricing a beat, the net reaction is likely limited/near-median.

Adj. EBITDA came in positive at $1.8M (highest since Q3’23; sixth consecutive sequential improvement), aligning with the market’s profitability/EBITDA focus from the preview. Revenue fell to $135.6M and was framed as intentional, but the bigger upside relative to the note was the more concrete progress on growth engines (A-Premium ~$50M run rate and JC Whitney ~$2.5M annualized run rate) plus IEEPA claims already received ($4.4M) even though EPS consensus is noisy in this microcap.

Revenue and EPS both beat the pre-release setup (which centered on a ~$129M flat-seq guide being met, and on weak consensus-quality EPS). However, management declined to provide formal 2026/2027 guidance and reiterated oil & gas softness, while gross margin improved sequentially but remained below prior-year levels—keeping the reaction near-median rather than decisively positive.

Results were broadly in line on revenue and beat on Q2 EBITDA margin, but management withdrew FCF guidance and sharply cut FY26 revenue/EBITDA/EPS (including a far lower FY EPS than implied by the pre-release H2 bridge risk). The combination of weak demand tone (respiratory modeled at the low end) and large guidance reset, plus negative FCF/OCF, drives a negative reaction despite the margin beat.

Q4 revenue and—more importantly—adj. EBITDA margin (11.1% vs expectations around the low 10.6–11.6% band) came in strong, and management provided FY27 guidance (revenue $1.45–1.55B; adj. EBITDA $150–160M) consistent with the high end of the pre-release “guide-is-the-bar” setup. The stock’s reaction should be meaningfully positive given margin delivery plus accretive M&A/capacity conversion tone.

EPS slightly beat ($0.27 vs $0.26 consensus), while revenue landed essentially in-line ($61.5M vs ~$61M). The key incremental factors versus the preview are stronger-than-feared backlog (~$271M vs the note’s ~$246M watch) and progress on eProbe (3 placed vs only 1 shipped YTD in the setup), offset by a gross-margin decline to 73% (vs ~76% est.)—with full-year revenue growth guidance reaffirmed (no action), keeping reaction near-median.

Revenue came in slightly above consensus and gross margin held up sequentially, but the key metric missed the pre-release gross profit dollars expectation (10.4M vs “should be ~11.2M”/~11.0M threshold) and EPS wasn’t a clear upside versus the already-loss-making setup. Guidance was broadly maintained (Q3 sequential growth, GM flat to slightly up), so reaction should be modest versus the mostly anticipated quarter.

Q2 delivered an all-time-high GMV and a meaningful EBITDA beat (margin expansion), plus management raised FY guidance across GMV, revenue, and notably adjusted EBITDA above the previously modeled bar after TDUP’s H2 cut. With the guidance action the key swing factor, the setup skews to a positive (but not assured) upside reaction.

Q2 headline delivered a clear EBITDA/margin beat (record 14.4%) and EPS strength ($0.40 vs ~$0.34-ish consensus). However, the pre-release thesis emphasized a binary Engine Services margin threshold and tougher cash/FCF credibility risk; while margins beat, Component Repair margin fell and military input delays persisted. FY guidance was raised, but mostly modestly (not a major upside catalyst versus what the note expected), leading to a roughly muted/mixed near-median reaction.

SEZL beat both revenue and EPS versus the pre-release bar and, crucially, guided FY26 higher (adj. EPS $5.25 vs $5.10 consensus; revenue growth 35% vs prior 30–35%). The quarter also delivered record engagement/subscribers and credit provisions within the target band (2.5–3% FY), reducing the key downside (worst-seasonal/credit-provision risk) the note highlighted.

Q2 results beat on adjusted EPS ($1.85 vs ~$1.81) with margins held at 32.1% and a yield/price story supporting underlying expansion. More importantly, management raised FY revenue/EBITDA/EPS/FCF guidance (vs the note’s expectation of either trim or a hold), with upside driven by commodity prices and acquisitions—partially offset by still-soft organic volumes (-1.6%). Overall reaction likely modestly positive given the earnings setup already telegraphed conservative revenue expectations.

Results were broadly in-line with the pre-release setup: revenue (~$5.1M) and non-GAAP EPS (-$0.05) match the $5.09–5.13M and -$0.05 consensus. The quarter showed margin improvement (43%), but the key market drivers were CHIPS definitiveness/dilution details and C-DAC Q4 acceptance timing; management reiterated the C-DAC recognition in Q4 2026 and provided no clear step-change beyond what was already expected from the LOI/roadmap risk. With no meaningful beats/misses versus consensus and guidance largely unchanged, the expected reaction is modestly positive/around median given gross margin improvement and upbeat technical fidelity context.

EPS was below the pre-release expectation centered around ~$0.52 ANI/share (reported $0.48), despite stronger-than-expected fee strength (FRE $106M, 39% margin) and very strong Private Wealth momentum (record $2.8B subscriptions; platform assets >$21B). The lack of new guidance means the reaction should be modest; markets likely already priced in decent fee performance, so the primary negative is the lower ANI/share and the headline GAAP loss optics.

Q4 revenue and cloud dynamics appear broadly consistent with the pre-release setup (cloud beat cited, DC/migration contribution in line). The larger swing factor—FY2027 guidance—was dominated by caution already priced (first-ever FY27 subscription/ARR framing and GAAP margin set low), so incremental surprises look limited; sentiment likely stays slightly negative/mixed rather than a major rerate.

Q2 beat the pre-set revenue growth narrative (~+4%) but still came in slightly below the $194.4M consensus. The bigger disappointment was margin/earnings: restaurant-level margin (13.1%) and adjusted EBITDA (–$0.2M) were far worse than what the note framed as a manageable trough, and guidance was cut sharply (FY comp decline widened to 8%–7% and FY EBITDA turned to a much larger loss), with cyclospora blamed for further 600–700 bps Q3 comp hit. While wraps showed some transaction stabilization, the magnitude of the guide revision dominates, implying a negative next-day reaction.

Q2 GAAP EPS ($0.10) and GAAP revenue ($14.3M) far exceeded the pre-release framework, largely due to the Dedeaux 1B land-sale (expected bull lever). However, the note flagged cash/liquidity as the key bear risk and TRC delivered the opposite there (liquidity down to ~$79M), with recurring quality weaker ex-land.

Revenue rose to $1.2M, materially above the pre-release model ($0.55–$0.65M) driven by stronger staking and digital lending. Despite the GAAP EPS “miss” implied by large non-cash MTM losses, the reported GAAP net loss ($18.9M, -$0.23) was less severe than the pre-release loss/EPS range (~-$26M to -$30M, -$0.34 to -$0.39), offsetting optics. Key downside: cash dropped to $3.1M (worse than the modeled low end), and there were sizable non-cash digital asset/receivable losses (Bluefin + returned tokens), plus legacy lending remains small with limited near-term originations.

The dominant miss was guidance: FY26 revenue was cut to $9–10M from ~$26M, far below what the pre-release note framed as a low bar (reaffirm ~$26M vs. at most a trim to $24–26M). Q2 revenue of $3.2M was roughly within directional expectations, but EPS losses and the much worse gross margin, alongside weaker Uber ramp and a broad strategic pivot, drive a strongly negative expected next-day reaction.

Q2 revenue of $715M missed the ~$751.6M consensus (and came in well below the pre-release setup), while Q3 revenue guidance of “at least $650M” implies a larger decline and weaker trajectory than what the note expected (~$800–810M). EPS was not clearly signaled versus consensus in the facts provided, but the drop in EBITDA/EBITDA and the guidance shortfall dominate the likely reaction.

Q2 revenue (~$17.8M) landed essentially at the pre-release $18.0M guide midpoint (no meaningful upside), but the non-GAAP operating profit milestone was delivered and margins/opex reductions improved (non-GAAP op profit +$0.635M; opex down 7.8% seq; gross margin 86.8% with mix-driven slight seq slip). Management also reiterated/kept the razor-thin profitability path while offering supportive forward framing (Q4 record >$18.7M and FY26 revenue >$70M), leading to a roughly median/only slightly positive reaction versus a market that already expected the milestone/guide.

Revenue growth and comps were broadly in line with the pre-release setup, but EPS came in below the note’s ~$1.90 base ($1.85 reported). The key upside—cutting FY26 commodity inflation guidance to ~5% and lowering Q3 inflation to 2–3%—was supportive, yet margin still compressed (down 66 bps to 16.4%), keeping the reaction muted-to-negative given negative positioning/pricing already priced in.

Revenue and the implied Q2 pattern largely matched the pre-release setup (Q2 revenue ~116M vs a ~$119M stale consensus), so the print’s battleground was FY26 adj. EBITDA guidance credibility. Guidance was reiterated at $95–$100M (not cut), but Q2 adjusted EBITDA and margin contracted (13%), increasing the burden on an acceleration in H2; demand/backlog commentary stayed broadly neutral rather than clearly improving.

Results and near-term demand metrics (organic rev +17% and DBNER 116%) came in above the already-high bar, and management raised FY organic and OpEx/FCF guidance. However, Q2 non-GAAP gross margin was pressured (49.1%) by carrier pass-through fees and management cautioned that the prior quarters’ beat cadence may not repeat, tempering the upside reaction.

Revenue beat the outlook and came in above the Q2 range, with other revenue also strong (record $33M; Hatch/data licensing tailwinds). However, core ad health remains mixed (PAL -1% vs prior -6%, but RR&O -10% and clicks -5% with only slight CPC growth), and the key risk is guidance: Q3 adjusted EBITDA $70–75M was broadly aligned with what the Street modeled while buybacks were paused—limiting upside and keeping the expected next-day reaction near median.

Revenue and EPS beat the company’s ~$585M/$0.246 setup, and management raised FY26 revenue and adjusted EBITDA. However, the key overhang was margin: Q2 adj. EBITDA margin fell to 37.2% (~-500 bps YoY), offsetting the beats and making the market’s reaction more mixed than a clean upside surprise.

ACMR beat revenue vs the ~($272M) working consensus and crushed EPS, but the key “shipments outpace revenue” demand signal weakened (shipments/rev 0.96 vs 1.04 in Q1) and gross margin continues to drift down (46.0%). Full-year revenue guidance was raised modestly (floor lifted) with the stock likely reacting positively given the magnitude of the earnings beat despite the shipment/margin flags.

The key upside was a raised FY26 adj. EBITDA guide (midpoint $267.5M vs consensus/preview expectation ~mid–$265M), which should drive a positive rerating; however, revenue came in below the preview-consensus $985.7M (reported $973M), and outpatient commercial cost trend was slightly above expectations—capping the beat despite near-high-end Q2 EBITDA.

Q2 revenue came in slightly above consensus, and gout launch early indicators were strong (supports demand/timing). However, management lowered full-year Cortrophin Gel guidance (to $520–540M) after previously implying a cleaner H2 ramp, which is a credibility/plan-risk negative versus what the market expected to be largely pre-guided; that should weigh more than the modest revenue beat.

Adj. EPS was $1.75 vs $1.77 consensus (slight miss), while revenue tracking was weak (FX/translation noise expected, but the guide tone worsened). Q2 revenue ($257.5M) and adjusted EBITDA ($155.8M at 60.5%) came in clearly above the pre-set revenue/EBITDA hurdle, and—more importantly—management raised FY revenue and lifted FY adj. Q2 net revenue and adjusted EPS both beat the pre-release consensus bar ($117M vs $102.27M; $2.07 vs $1.30). Q2 revenue ($45.4M) beat the ~$44.0M consensus, and management improved operating leverage (adj. EBITDA loss narrowed to $3.5M) alongside stronger surgeon adoption (LAPApasty 40% vs 35% in Q1). EPS were raised, partially offset by weak U.S./pen-needle mix commentary; the net tape impact is mildly positive given revenue guide credibility but with cautious demand signals and a slightly soft implied Q4 revenue.

EBITDA and the company’s key FY26 guide ($700M–$900M) were maintained, which the pre-release note said was the main driver; the big remaining bar was the ~$130–150M Q2 adjusted EBITDA whisper and the quarter’s demand/handle checks (11% YoY handle, July +20%, predictions growth and low overlap) support that. Despite a large adjusted EPS and EBITDA beat and strong new awards/backlog growth, guidance is the offset: the FY26 adjusted EBITDA range was revised down to $500–$525M versus the market’s $525–$560M embedded in the pre-release note, which keeps credibility risk alive. Relative to the pre-release setup, reported adjusted EPS (-$0.14) and the narrow vendor revenue line were roughly in-line, with some positives in National capital/leverage (leverage improved to 21:1; statutory capital up). North America/APAC). The big margin beat was heavily driven by IEEPA tariff refunds (timing-sensitive), tempering the quality of upside.

The key forward drivers largely met the pre-release bar: fundraising rose to $2.3B (supportive vs the $1.6B Q2 management guide) and fee-related/FRE rose (45% FRE margin). EPS/ANI growth came in ahead of the ~$0.18 ANI consensus, while reported revenue optics were effectively in line given the note’s incentive-fee lumpy expectations.

Revenue and full-year guidance were effectively in line with what the pre-release note framed as a likely ‘nudge/raise’ setup, but Q2 student starts materially underperformed expectations (headline starts +1% vs near-teens/high-single digits implied) and the quarter’s earnings power was held back by depreciation/new-campus losses. Counterbalancing upside came from improved cash generation (higher operating cash flow) and stronger adjusted EBITDA growth, but the increased CapEx (raised to $95–100M) is a new negative for cash/FCF expectations.

Results beat on revenue and helped demonstrate the promised Q2 EBITDA step-up (adj. EBITDA $99.7M vs ~mid-$90s bar), while the company raised 2026 imaging guidance and reiterated Digital Health. The main offset is Digital Health segment adj. EBITDA was still a small profit but below the prior-year level, adding some skepticism on the margin durability despite ARR exceeding expectations.

Despite a +40% YoY adjusted EBITDA beat driven by 45Z and FSS growth and guidance being maintained, revenue missed consensus materially, EBITDA was still at the bottom of the implied run-rate (with RNG production below management’s expectations/utilization only high-50%), and GAAP EPS was a large GAAP loss—keeping credibility risk and liquidity/cadence concerns in focus for the stock.

Revenue materially exceeded the pre-release bar (total rev $243.7M vs ~$232M trend/consensus-implied), with continued ≥$35M sequential Attruby adds and supportive first-line share/demand commentary. EPS and any explicit guidance change were not provided in the facts, limiting confidence on the reaction despite management reaffirming longer-term profitability/breakeven framing.

Revenue/EPS comparisons to consensus are not reliable in the pre-note and the release provides no EPS/revenue line items; however, reported portfolio fundamentals are stronger than the preview’s base framework: same-store occupancy at 87.8% (near/above base range) and NOI margin up to 32.6% (above the ~31.5–32.5% build). The key binary—refinancing the $170M bridge—was completed via a post-quarter $380M term loan, reducing near-term maturity risk, and the company reiterated it will defer formal 2027 FFO guidance until integration is complete.

Revenue was described as in line, and FY27 revenue/op income guidance was reaffirmed in line with consensus. The main negative versus the note was gross margin weakness (16.2% GAAP; adjusted 20.2%) with FX headwinds, which raises risk to the guide-critical margin trajectory even though full-year guidance was unchanged.

Despite largely in-line production and strong execution on cost synergies, Q2 adjusted EBITDAX of $338M sat below the $370–410M guidance band and effectively implies downside to the ~1.35 EPS consensus; with temporary constraints and differential pressures (only partially offset by hedges/realization discipline) reinforcing a weaker near-term margin profile. Capital allocation remains mixed (no buybacks) and the Crimson pipeline deal is growth/valuation-positive but not enough to offset the EBITDAX/FCF disappointment, consistent with a below-median tape reaction.

Q2 delivered a sharp revenue and EBITDA shortfall (sales -10% YoY to $117M; adj. EBITDA -40% to $6.6M), and cash fell materially to $43.9M with net debt rising to $224.7M despite guidance being reaffirmed at $44–48M/$530–550M. With the market already primed for GAAP EPS weakness due to the debt stack, the bigger incremental downside is the weaker-than-modeled quarterly operating/cash profile.

Q2 results beat the market’s “whisper” bar (47.7M vs ~47M) and—crucially—management raised FY adjusted EBITDA guidance to $23.6–28.6M (vs prior $20.6–28M; above the market’s trade-requiring higher low end). Margin quality strengthened (cash GM outlook 39–40%) and buybacks accelerated; the only headwind was a modest revenue reduction from phasing out low-margin resale, but it supported margin expansion rather than demand weakness.

Despite refinancing (a known risk-reducer) and incremental cash flow, Q2 revenue of $22.2M and especially adjusted EBITDA $4.4M came materially below the pre-release base, with management attributing the miss to continued traffic headwinds rather than stabilization—driving a likely negative tape reaction.

Headline revenue of $48.4M beat the $44.64M consensus (~+8%), driven by CMS revenue (+90% YoY to $30.5M) and a large gross margin expansion (+650 bps to 28.9%). CMS exited Q2 at >$125M run-rate and 34% media margin (vs the preview’s margin-threshold concern), partially offset by ongoing weak cash/OCF (~$0.3M H1) and a still-negative adjusted EBITDA (-$1.8M) with Q3 not guided to improve.

Revenue came in below the already-soft consensus and guidance was materially walked back: management withdrew the prior Q4 breakeven net income target and shifted to positive FCF, plus gross margin contracted with losses widening (-$0.12 vs -$0.13). The market likely priced a dull-to-flat quarter, but the Q4 breakeven reversal and international/CPA headwinds were not expected to that extent.

This is largely a low-information balance-sheet quarter for GUTS, and the release mainly reinforces the same runway/cash story (cash $47.1M into early 2027, no planned raise before pivotal data) rather than introducing a new funding risk or materially different pivotal timing. With clinical durability/AE safety commentary supportive but not a new consensus swing versus what the market was already positioning for the early-Q4 catalyst, the net move is modeled near-median/inline.

Q2 revenue beat consensus ($28.1M vs $27.29M) and gross margin printed a standout 92% (record), while FY26 revenue guidance was raised to $114–$117M—essentially in line with what the preview expected. EPS was worse than the expected loss magnitude (GAAP net loss $0.51 vs consensus -$0.47) and adjusted/GAAP loss optics remained a headwind, keeping the reaction only mildly positive rather than a clear upside shock.

Q2 revenue and profitability materially beat the thin/low-confidence preprint expectations ($8.1M vs $7.10M; adj EPS $0.23 vs the ~$0.15 whisper / $0.12 published). Despite systemwide sales declining reported, management delivered pro forma strength and operating leverage with SG&A down (no more TrueBlue legal fees), creating upside surprise for the turnaround narrative; main offset was cash down and receivables up.

On the surface, results align with the thin consensus (revenue ~in-line) but the release commentary underwhelms vs the pre-set high-signal bar: SDC organic declined again and past-due backlog rose (episodic recovery), while BPD rebounded only on easier comps/catch-up rather than a clean turnaround—offset by strong AOI/margin expansion and lower leverage. No FY27 guidance was provided (expected), limiting upside.

Q2 revenue of $8.2M beat the guided $7.5–$7.8M range (consensus-equivalent) while consumables (+30%) and record flow cells (9,219) cleared the market’s “runway/thesis” checklist. Full-year FY2026 revenue low end was raised to $31–$33M (vs the note’s $30M base), and gross margin hit a new record (53%). Offsets: cash/securities of $10.4M still implies financing risk despite saying runway into Q1’27, and software declined (-16%) with international systems growth slow (installed base +5%), limiting confidence in sustained growth without recapitalization.

Revenue ($229.1M) was below the pre-release “flat”/~$235M framing, and the call offered no Q2/JFY earnings guidance amid a deteriorating balance sheet (cash down to $51.6M, FCF deeply negative from the $110.9M judgment). Margin compressed further (27.2%) and management’s uncertainty/no guidance adds incremental downside versus the already-cautious financing/guidance-risk setup.
