Key driver is fundamentals lagging the preview: Q2 revenue came in far below the ~$3.3M consensus ($1.0M reported) and margins deteriorated (negative gross margin; cost of revenues up). While cash improved to $30.2M and wafer capacity prepayment was disclosed, customer deployment slips and a ~$20.4M net loss (driven by warrant fair value) reinforce the ramp/liquidity worry; the ATM expansion to $120M plus cash-burn guidance keeps the market focused on dilution risk rather than a clean beat.

Revenue was effectively in-line versus the pre-release setup and full-year Adj. EBITDA ($800M) plus FCF ($200M) were reaffirmed; the incremental swing is mixed (FCF swung positive and Digital Audio/Pocadsts were strong, but Multi-Platform EBITDA collapsed due to non-cash co-marketing and Q3 guide ($180–220M) plus low-Q4 confidence leaves the $800M math still fragile).

Revenue beat consensus while results and commentary confirm better-than-implied medical trend and a major EBITDA swing. Most importantly, management raised FY26 adjusted EBITDA guidance to $80–$110M (midpoint $95M), well above the ~$20–60M range implied in the pre-release note; however, liquidity remains tight ($21M cash) and at-risk membership declined with risk not expected to fully transfer until later (Nebraska services glidepath).

Revenue and adjusted EPS beat the pre-release consensus (revenue +~1% vs ~$320.5M; adjusted EPS reported $0.12 vs $0.06 consensus), but the quarter still showed margin contraction (gross margin to 17% and adjusted EBITDA margin down to 4.2%). No new FY guidance was provided; the market focus remains on the Sea Ray transaction mechanics and liquidity, so the net reaction is likely near-median rather than a large upside repricing.

Q2 revenue ($178.3M) and adjusted EPS (-$0.07) beat the pre-release consensus, and gross margin improved to near breakeven (-0.9%). More importantly, management raised FY revenue growth guidance to 15–16% (vs 13–15% prior), while demand/refresh activity and cash burn improved—together implying a modestly positive next-day reaction.

Headline revenue missed (~6–7% vs ~$103.9M consensus) on wholesale weakness, and management lowered FY26 revenue guidance to $420–$440M (below the prior $465–$485M implied by the pre-release note). Offsetting positives were strong margin/gross margin expansion (tariff refund) and improved adjusted EBITDA to +$2.1M, but demand response to mid-June price increases was described as more negative than expected, and GAAP EPS is not informative given prior-year non-cash/warrant dynamics.

Q2 revenue of $5.6M beat the pre-release $4.7M–$5.15M consensus range, and backlog rose to ~$42.5M (well above the ~$25M threshold the note flagged). Full-year revenue framework of legacy $20–$25M plus NHanced $7–$16M was reaffirmed (no guidance raise), but the disclosed cash runway and large backlog/contract visibility were incremental positives. EPS was not a clean beat because GAAP is dominated by mark-to-market items, and operating expenses rose sharply, partly offsetting the upside.

Despite an EPS beat (supported by strong Q2 operating income and collections), the key market focus was on ARR trajectory and Q3 implied further ARR decline (~$812M). The restructuring and margin/gross margin pressures appear more than offset by costs, while full-year revenue guidance is effectively reaffirmed, keeping the event’s upside constrained versus the already-negatively skewed setup.

Revenue and EPS beat a tight consensus band, and management raised FY sales growth guidance sharply. However, gross margin and the full-year margin outlook were cut ~200 bps and backlog/bookings showed sequential softening, creating a mixed quality-of-earnings setup that should temper the upside despite the strong top-line surprise.

Q2 revenue of $107M missed the $121.9M consensus in the pre-release note (~12% downside), which is the key near-term credibility test. However, management raised FY26 revenue guidance to $525–575M (midpoint ~$550M) above the ~$520M street number and delivered strong margin/earnings power (12% gross margin; adj. EBITDA $4M) alongside sizable backlog/book-to-burn momentum.

Revenues and margins significantly exceeded the pre-release setup (record 26.7M revenue +23% YoY and adjusted EBITDA margin +7 pts to 42%), plus record FCF/opex leverage. EPS also beat, though EPS was noted as less reliable pre-print. Guidance was maintained (high-30s adj. EBITDA margin), so the upside reaction is driven by operational outperformance and the acquisition/vertical expansion narrative rather than guidance changes; small negative was 2-point slip in gross retention.

Revenue came in below the ~$20.0M expectation and the PRS weakness (failed rep pilot/customer concentration) was worse than the note’s base-case setup. The key incremental issue was the full-year revenue guide being withdrawn (i.e., effectively below the ≥$86.7M path expected), while gross margin improved to 72% but didn’t offset the lost runway/financing overhang.

Despite GAAP/EPS remaining deeply negative, the print shows upside on top-line vs the (already shaky) consensus and better-than-expected data-center recurring lease contribution/margins, consistent with the landlord/ramp narrative. However, the release is also burdened by the call timing/postponement overhang and large noncash crypto-mark-to-market losses, keeping the net reaction near-median.

Revenue landed essentially in the expected range and full-year guidance was reaffirmed (so no valuation-reset catalyst). The main incremental positive vs the setup was a Q2 adjusted EBITDA beat to the high end with record EBITDA per unit, but management still flagged conversion/unit headwinds (price dislocation), keeping the likely reaction close to median.

Revenue ($58M) missed the $61.8M consensus anchor, though net client flows (~$700M) and AUM growth (51B, +8% YoY) were strong. Margin softened (adj. EBITDA margin 9.3% vs 9.5%), and the noted ~$19M unrealized loss plus Asian credit fund unwind is a negative narrative for distributions/incentives, while the strategic review added no new deal signal ("nothing further to report").

Revenue/EPS detail relative to consensus wasn’t cleanly provided vs the pre-release yardstick, but the key line—Q2 adjusted EBITDA at the better end of the stated range and Q3 guidance held in the same range—meets the expected burn trajectory rather than materially beating it. The major items were deal/strategy commentary (profitable Insitu, flat post-close cash burn) which were at least partially expected given the pre-announced acquisition framework, leading to a modestly positive but not outsized reaction amid already-high deal- and dilution-related expectations.

Q2 revenue landed at the high end of guidance and slightly above the $170.79M consensus, while adjusted EBITDA margin expanded 275 bps to the top of guidance (largely a beat versus the pre-release setup). Management also raised FY2026 guidance (revenue/EBITDA/EPS) and lowered capex, with Health+ and Military+ enrollment/registrations broadly consistent with targets and no cited operational deterioration; overall this should generate a moderately positive reaction despite earlier market skepticism around EPS being below-the-line dependent.

Q2 revenue $31.5M modestly missed the ~$34.1M consensus implied in the preview, but management reaffirmed FY2026 revenue $150–$200M with back-half weighting and added sizable funded government awards/backlog and a J-LEO Japan award; however, higher Q2 adj. OpEx and rising capex keep profitability/liquidity concerns intact, limiting upside versus what was already anticipated.

Q2 revenue (and adjusted EBITDA) cleared the top end and Q3 guidance shows acceleration (revenue +27% and contribution ex-TAC +25%)—all broadly supportive versus the base case. The main offset is the explicit 200bp Q3 EBITDA margin drag from TVision, which keeps reaction from being more strongly positive.

BODI beat the high end of its own Q2 guidance on net income/adj. EBITDA, but revenue landed only around the low/middle of the expected band and the key covenant-thesis metric deteriorated: digital subscriptions were 760k (down, and below the note’s ~780k stabilization trigger). Q3 revenue and EBITDA guided within the expected range, but net margin/gross margin is trending down (with further Q3 decline guided) and FCF was sharply negative on inventory build—limiting upside.

Revenue came in above the $99.65M consensus (reported $102M vs expected), aided by the quarter’s corporate liquidity events and non-cash items, while EPS direction/GAAP accounting was not meaningfully comparable given the market’s EPS skepticism. The key soft spot was the restaurant group: traffic-related impairments of $45M confirm the downside case, offset only partly by strong sports-related marks/operations (BKFC and Europa qualification) and the liquidity improvement after Watkins/Brasada transactions.

No meaningful consensus exists pre-release, so the print is mainly judged on narrative/liquidity. The release delivered (1) Truth API customer traction with signed high-tier agreements and (2) reiterated target to close the TAE deal by end-2026, partially offset by (3) continued heavy non-cash digital asset mark losses and (4) ongoing uncertainty around ~-$1B convertible note repayment despite only partial liquid/unenecumbered coverage—keeping likely next-day reaction near median with high dispersion.

Revenue (+130% YoY to $319.7M) handily beat the pre-release $196.97M consensus anchor, and management raised FY2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance to $80–$105M (above the $80–$100M midpoint $90M). The main offset is that first-half GAAP results remained pressured by sizable non-cash warrant/stock-related costs, keeping part of the credibility risk alive.

Q2 revenue was essentially inline with the ~$55.5M expectation, but EPS ($0.05) beat the ~$0.03 consensus. Management tightened FY26 revenue to $220–$222M (worse vs consensus ~$223.5M), while raising FY26 adjusted EBITDA guidance midpoint and indicating improving NDR and the strongest biopharma new-business quarter in three years; overall reaction likely modestly positive given the revenue guide disappointment is partially offset by margin/retention and the EPS beat.

Q2 revenue ($227.9M) and ATS revenue ($182.8M) beat the note’s ~mid-$219M base, but management explicitly guided a sequential decline Q2→Q3 and acknowledged the exceptional nature of the quarter—plus Media swung to an operating loss. The net is a modestly positive but largely expected outcome given the note’s thesis was already centered on the ATS run-rate and dilution of sustainability risk.

Top-line came in at the effective pre-release bar (~$18.5M floor), so there’s no revenue credibility beat. Offsets: gross margin and adj. EBITDA look materially better than the pre-release trough/concerns, and management reiterated the H2/EBITDA guidance (no hard slide), which should limit downside and support a slightly positive tape, though not a clear upside surprise given the guidance credibility framework.

Revenue of $26.2M is essentially in line with the pre-release ~ $26.5M expectation, but the call reinforced a transitional loss profile (adjusted EBITDA loss, large one-time costs) and flagged Monovate card issuance as still constrained and gated by a regulator issue—both negatives versus an already fragile setup. No formal revenue guidance was provided; the key item was cost savings (annualized $10–13M), which is broadly consistent with prior expectations that savings are back-end loaded.

Revenue/EPS surprise metrics are not usable versus the pre-release yardstick because the note flagged consensus as stale and guidance is already withdrawn/strategic process underway; relative to expectations, the main incremental positive was a clearly better subscriber attach rate (record 69%). With management providing no fresh margin/sell-through/2H color and keeping the sale-process as the dominant driver, the net reaction should be near-median to slightly positive rather than a broad beat-driven rerating.

Revenue came in slightly below the already-low street/preview ($55.7M vs $57.2M) and EPS loss was far worse than expected (−$0.14 vs −$0.08), despite a clear upside in CPG traction (341% sequential growth; ~2,000 doors). Margin stayed weak (restaurant-level adj. EBITDA 11.3% still below the preview’s ~10.5% base bridge expectations tied to a margin “bridge,” while COGS rose to 39.1% on CPG ramp), and FY revenue guidance was reaffirmed rather than improved.

Q2 revenue and adjusted EBITDA came in above the pre-release bar, and management raised FY26 revenue guidance with AI-driven engagement as a tangible operational catalyst. Offsetting negatives were continuing gross-margin compression and negative OCF/FCF plus explicit ongoing structural margin pressure, leading to a moderately positive but not outsized reaction versus the market’s already-consumed ramp expectations and heightened FTC overhang.

EPS/earnings power deteriorated sharply versus the pre-release EPS expectation (consensus -$0.10): reported Q2 was a materially larger loss, alongside negative adjusted EBITDA and a large operating cash flow swing. Positives were offset by equity/liquidity stress and the need for more capex; Turtle Creek guidance narrative was mixed (lower cost and operations pushed to H2 2028) but did not outweigh the quarter’s cash/earnings weakness. With low sell-side coverage and volatility skewed to the downside, the stock likely reacts below median, consistent with an already-expected weak quarter but worse-than-anchored details.

Revenue of ~$320.1M missed the ~$348.7M consensus, but adjusted EPS ($0.20) was inline with expectations; the dominant driver is guidance and growth outlook—FY26 revenue and adjusted EPS were cut and India launch slipped to H1’27, plus margin compression and continued under-investment in recruiting/leadership. Prism.io device placements/scans were a bright spot, but not enough to offset the guidance downgrade.

Despite a modest YoY revenue growth print, the quarter deteriorated on credit: net charge-offs jumped to ~52% (worse than the ~50% “bogey” in the note) while originations declined ~9% and adjusted EPS fell sharply. Most importantly, FY26 guidance was cut to adj. EPS $1.34–$1.51 and revenue $600–625M, materially below the note’s assumed reaffirm/maintain backdrop, driven by delayed line-of-credit launch and Lola migration—driving an outsized downside reaction.

Operationally, adjusted EBITDA loss narrowed sequentially and cash burn was framed as near-term peak; however, management reported RUO kit sales of only $21k (below the market’s expected ~$250k level) and—more importantly—raised H2 cash burn to ~$8M/quarter from ~ $6M previously, which worsens runway/dilution math. FDA remains “later in 2026” but timing is still cautioned, consistent with the note, so the reaction skews negative but not catastrophic.

Revenue growth came in strong (+51% YoY to $12.7M), driven by non-product microLED/Fabric.AI—consistent with the note’s low-quality beat risk but still above the (already noisy) $11.5–$13.8M range. More importantly, management said 2H results now exceed prior FY2026 $52–60M guidance (upside narrative beyond the note’s base case), while product gross margin improved to 14%, supporting earnings leverage; with implied move ~13% and no clear new negative, the market likely reacts positively though somewhat tempered by the note’s caution that much of the revenue is non-product/funded.

Revenue was slightly below the note’s $85M whisper and ~15% under the stale ~$103M consensus, while margins and profitability deteriorated sharply (gross margin 29.5% down and adjusted EBITDA collapsing). The key reprice levers (liquidity/going-concern and FY guidance) were not meaningfully resolved versus what the note flagged, keeping reaction modestly negative rather than an outsized beat.

Revenue and profitability surprised meaningfully versus the pre-release setup (revenue above the ~$75M midpoint guide; adjusted EBITDA well above the top end; gross margin reached 39.3% vs ~38% implied). Offsetting negatives include continued tape-supply constraints and a Q2 EBITDA guide down to $6M, which tempers the follow-through despite the higher Q2 revenue guide.

Revenue came in above the sell-side/guidance midpoint ($109.4M vs $106.8M consensus) and operating ratios improved sequentially (June 95.7%), but Q2 adjusted EBITDA missed the implied run-rate (fuel/driver cost pressure) and the company initiated a large M&A deal (Hansen & Adkins) that the market may discount for timing/synergy credibility despite 2H combined revenue guidance near ~97% OR / 8–9% margins.

Q2 delivered a top-line beat ($31.2M vs ~$29.7M consensus) and stronger profitability (Adj. EBITDA ~7.0M with ~22% margin vs $3.5M prior, plus operating income and near break-even net income). Importantly, Honey Birdette maintained the key “seventh consecutive double-digit comp” pillar and licensing was back to growth, with only a modest China step-down—no new guidance surprise was provided.

Quarter largely matches the note’s base case: ~$100.7M revenue versus the ~ $102M expectation and adj. EPS of $0.20 inline. Importantly, FY2026 revenue and adjusted EBITDA guidance was reaffirmed and margin decline is explained by KUBRA mix (not pricing), while synergy and cash conversion/rate-leverage commentary are supportive—consistent with a modestly positive/neutral tape reaction rather than a guidance-driven repricing.

Revenue landed inside prior guidance with strong contract/backlog momentum, and gross margins beat the stepped-down guide (tariff refund/inventory reserve effects). However, the key market sensitivities were margin trajectory and the Q3 guide: Q3 gross margin guidance was lowered versus the prior-year narrative and implies less favorable mix, while free cash flow deteriorated sharply—together pointing to a muted-to-slightly negative reaction given rich stock expectations and an options market implying only ~10–11% absolute movement.

Revenue beat the stub-period consensus estimate materially, and management also introduced credible Q3 guidance (>$87–$93M) that implies rapid post-stub ramp with Quake AI fully consolidated. The GAAP net loss widened substantially versus the already-weak EPS expectation, though adjusted EBITDA loss narrowed, keeping reaction likely net positive but with some drag from headline losses and early guidance uncertainty.

Pre-release benchmarks/consensus were not provided, so surprises vs expectations are difficult to quantify. Directionally, results were weaker (52% revenue decline and worsening operating/adjusted EBITDA losses), partially offset by meaningful regulatory approvals and still-on-track launch commentary; net impact likely mildly negative to near-median given the higher cash position but rising burn.

Q2 revenue was essentially inline to the pre-set guide/consensus and gross margin expanded to ~26% despite marketing, but the key issue was guidance: Q3 constant-currency revenue growth of 0.7–3.3% (and adj. EBITDA $0–$5M) is below the market’s needed acceleration for the “double-digit by exit” narrative. Japan remains the weak spot (cc -6.7% with MPU -9.5%).

Q2 revenue and adjusted EBITDA were above the already-expected range, and management raised full-year revenue growth guidance (3%-5% vs 2%-4%). However, guidance tightened on adjusted gross margin (cut 100 bps to 57%-59%) and the quarter’s gross margin fell with mix pressures plus higher China/CMT mix, and cash remained tight (only $6.5M).

The release disappoints on the core growth datapoint: Q2 TTV was only ~$169M and the company must generate ~$2.1B in 2H to hit the unchanged ~$2.5B target. Management also pushed monetization visibility toward break-even timing (4Q) and indicated effectively zero Bakkt Agent MAUs, while EPS/reported income is dominated by warrant fair-value effects—likely aligning with low-quality headline expectations and still leaving downside from the weaker TTV/launch credibility.

Q2 revenue of $29.5M landed at the high end of guidance (vs ~$29.3M stale consensus) with an EBITDA loss of -$10.5M within the expected range, but the bigger read-through was demand strength in Surf On Demand (record Q2, +67% departures) and incremental funding details (lower amortization, new asset-backed loan). Main negative vs the preview: NYSE deficiency notice timing was later than the preview assumed, keeping overhang alive despite the refinancing.

Despite backlog setting an all-time high and International returning to growth, the release disclosed a large Q3 P3 design-build construction management delay charge and revised full-year guidance down to ~$4.05 EPS (midpoint), well below the ~$1.49 adj. EPS consensus. Guidance reset appears to be driven by materially worse cash/CM project outlook into FY27, which is the dominant driver for this setup and likely drives a below-median (negative) reaction versus expectations that focused on NSR/FCF sustainability.

Q2 revenue and gross margin were essentially in-line-to-better (GM +180 bps), but EPS/Net income surged largely due to bottom-line improvement, while management guided FY revenue down the top end to $360–$366M citing a more conservative airway clearance (flat YOY) view. Guidance softness around airway plus prior-auth timing keeps the reaction closer to negative/neutral despite the strong margin/EBITDA beat.

Q2 revenue and profitability beat the (guide-based) bar with a record margin, but the key market focus was the FY guide: management cut FY2026 revenue and EBITDA materially below the pre-release yardstick ($760–790M and ~$250–260M), largely driven by worsening SEO and faster-than-expected low-value job erosion. Overall reaction likely near-median despite the Q2 outperformance because the guidance reset dominates.

Revenue was exactly in line, and R&D did inflect up as expected, but EPS/loss was worse than the preview (EPS -$1.11 vs -$0.87 consensus; net loss ~$3.0M vs ~$2.3–$2.4M implied). Cash landed near the expected band and trials restarted, tempering downside; lack of a clear funding/runway or partnering escalation likely keeps reaction near-median slightly negative.

Q2 revenue of $70.7M was slightly below the pre-release consensus (~$71.7M) but within the company’s $71M guidance floor, while GAAP EPS of –$0.18 is broadly in line with the –$0.18 consensus. The key—FY revenue $350–365M and FY adj. EBITDA $80–100M—was reaffirmed with no guidance reset; upside items (record Vevye/AIHESO and margin expectation toward high-70s H2) were largely offset by the still-negative Q2 adjusted EBITDA and cash/2H bridge risk already priced into the setup.

Key upside vs the pre-release setup: the company raised FY26 adjusted EBITDA guidance to ~$15M (from prior ~$14M) and reported a stronger balance sheet (cash $55.6M; net debt $29.8M), consistent with better-than-assumed liquidity/asset monetization. Revenue/EPS reported figures are not reliably comparable to the thin, noisy consensus noted in the pre-release note, so the reaction should be driven mainly by guidance and cash/debt.

Q3 beat consensus on both revenue and adjusted EPS, with organic growth (9%, ~11% ex calendar shift) and a stronger-than-modeled AOI (+13% to $261M). More importantly, FY26 organic revenue outlook was raised to 9–10% (above the prior high-end posture) and Aramark quantified Nexus scope/signed sites and ramp profile, reducing timing risk that the pre-release note highlighted.

Despite a margin beat (adj. EBITDA $9.8M vs ~$9M implied by the preview) and strong orders/backlog (+~50% orders to ~$144M and backlog to $385M, consistent with the setup), revenue ($102.9M) and EPS ($0.07) came in below what the market was positioned for (notably the preview’s $114M revenue and $0.08 EPS). Management’s H2 tone was “significantly stronger” but AP does not provide formal quantified guidance, limiting guidance-based upside.

P&L items were not the market focus (pre-revenue), and the key business-update gate—FORTIFI-HN01 on track for substantial enrollment by year-end enabling a mid-2027 interim and potential accelerated approval—matched the pre-release expectation. Operating expense ramp/upside durability language was broadly consistent, implying a near-median stock response.

The quarter delivered a key milestone (expanding to five Stage-3 customers) and an added/expanded foundry capacity narrative (positive), but it also showed widening losses and higher operating cash burn versus the pre-release modeled downside risk; with modeled revenue/EPS estimates having wide error bars and no explicit quantitative guidance, the net reaction is expected to be roughly median to slightly positive.

Q2 results were better than the main story line: adjusted EBITDA and gross margin benefited from absence of GAC start-up costs (a key pre-release risk). Management reaffirmed FY26 revenue and adjusted EBITDA guidance, limiting downside; offsetting items were balance-sheet optics (very low unrestricted cash at quarter-end) and no finalized GAC decision, which keeps uncertainty elevated.

Q3 revenue of ~$3.5B missed the ~$3.572B consensus due to procurement/material volume delays, but adjusted EPS of $0.67 beat consensus (~$0.611) alongside a margin beat (8.3% vs expectations). Guidance was mixed: FY26 revenue was cut to $13.8–$13.95B (~below the pre-release expectations) while FY26 EBITDA/EPS were raised, and FY27 revenue growth was clarified to be only 0–1% (with a larger 3% NASA headwind). Overall, the raised profitability and bookings/backlog support offset the revenue/guidance pressure, pointing to a slightly positive-to-neutral reaction rather than a sharp repricing.

Q2 revenue of $16.1M beat the $15.37M consensus and company narrative supported 57% gross margin (up ~85 bps) plus a material EBITDA loss improvement. Management also raised the full-year revenue low end to $68–$70M, but the call explicitly excluded AVCAD from guidance (reducing upside vs the market’s 2H bridge expectations), moderating the likely stock reaction.

Revenue of $5.2M missed the ~$6.07M consensus and the market’s key sequential-growth narrative, despite margin expansion to 62% and expense cuts. Management’s commentary on $13.1M contracted ARR converting starting in H2 (with most running into 2027) and the $36.8M pro forma cash largely tracks expectations, but the lower-than-expected Q2 print and the implied H2 ramp risk drive a modestly negative reaction.

Q4 EPS mechanically beat due to a disclosed nonrecurring IEEPA tariff refund, which was already the key swing risk in the pre-release note, limiting surprise. The bigger swing is the forward setup: FY27 EPS guide ($12.40–$12.60) is modestly above expectations/above the note’s base scenario, but management also guided lower FCF and described more normalized Pharma/GMPD profitability (Iran-conflict risk to the low end), tempering enthusiasm. Net expected reaction is mildly negative-to-neutral given the quarter’s quality concerns and buy-side sensitivity to cash flow.

Q2 headline revenue and adjusted performance were broadly in line with the pre-release frame (deal/stub timing), but the key event—FY26 adj. EBITDA guidance reset to $103–108M—was largely expected. Record utilization (88.3%) and operating leverage were incremental positives versus the note; offsetting that, GAAP EPS came in weak due to ~$3.3M transaction costs (priced to some degree), muting the equity read-through into the release.

Q2 revenue and EBITDA/op-profit were a clear beat driven by private-cloud timing, but management emphasized one-time pull-forward and left full-year guidance unchanged. The call added margin pressure (non-GAAP GM down) and negative FCF/OCF, offsetting the AMD AI deployment news—so the net reaction is likely muted to slightly positive versus a market that already discounted much of the beat.

Q2 revenue and EPS came in better than the pre-release bars, supported by a sharp gross margin expansion (51.1% vs ~48% needed for consensus). More importantly, FY26 revenue range narrowed slightly and gross margin guide was raised (48–50%), while cash increased meaningfully—reducing downside risk from the going-concern/covenant narrative. With downside risk already priced for this setup, the clean gross margin/EBITDA improvement and improved liquidity should drive an above-median positive reaction.

Q2 missed on both revenue ($455M vs $478.2M consensus) and especially EPS ($0.03 vs $0.253), driven by a sharp normalized tax/valuation allowance. More importantly, Engage guidance was cut (EBITDA margin down; revenue decline steeper), weakening the EBITDA/leverage trajectory despite some covenant flexibility and lower net leverage.

Despite a slight YoY revenue decline, Q3 EBITDA and margin beat the pre-release “~$79–80M bar” (reported ~$80.9M, ~12.2% margin) and management raised FY26 FCF guidance ($160–170M) and tightened FY26 adj. EBITDA to $310–315M (midpoint $312.5M) while outlining additional 2027 outsourcing savings and remaining transformation actions. Offsetting negatives were weaker reported revenue (-1.8% YoY) driven by lower pounds processed and removal of the top end of Q4 EBITDA guidance.

Q2 demand/operating quality broadly met expectations (RevPAR +8.2%, occupancy 82.4% already known), and Q2 Adj. EBITDA $122.1M was slightly ahead. The main negative was guidance nuance: full-year consolidated occupancy was lowered to ~83% (despite pre-announced occupancy being known) which the market feared could jeopardize the H2 bridge, though management offset with cost efficiencies and reaffirmed FY Adj. EBITDA $502–$516M.

Revenue landed essentially at the preview’s modeled ~$1.9–2.0M base (reported $1.93M), with mix-driven ASP and payer coverage progress broadly consistent. The main disappointment is EPS optics: reported EPS loss of −$0.19 vs a −$0.16 consensus setup, with GAAP dilution/burn dynamics likely contributing, keeping the expected reaction slightly negative-to-mixed.

Q2 revenue and gross margin missed the ~$24.9M / ~high-50s expectations, with EPS and adj. EBITDA far worse and liquidity tightening sharply. Most importantly, full-year revenue guidance was cut to $99–103M (below the prior $101–105M raise discussed in the pre-release note), undermining the needed H2 bridge; HEMOBLAST contribution was still small relative to the cost and orders initially flowing via Dilon.

Revenue of $5.6M is broadly in the $5.4–$5.6M “whisper” range despite the stale ~$6.0M consensus anchor, so the headline is not a true beat. Offsetting positives (retention up to 94%, net revenue retention 124%) are partly countered by gross margin compressing to 73% and adjusted EBITDA declining—implying the market will want clearer evidence of an inflection toward the high-70% margin recovery.

Q2 revenue landed at the high end of already-expected guidance, but adj. EPS beat the top end by $0.05 and margins expanded more than expected (IEEPA refunds cited). The key upside was the FY2026 raise to the $880–900M / $3.05–$3.25 range, though Q3 commentary points to decelerating momentum, keeping the reaction near-median rather than strongly positive.

Q2 revenue and margins undershot the model’s critical profit checkpoint: adjusted EBITDA fell to $13.7M (vs the pre-release framing that ~$26M was the key level to keep FY math intact) and turnaround revenue was down >50% plus Middle East-related deferrals hit 1H by >$20M. While management reaffirmed FY revenue and EBITDA ranges and disclosed a $20–$35M cost program, the call’s message leaned to the lower half of guidance, keeping the quarter-to-FY bridge risk high and likely driving a negative-than-median reaction.

Reported Q2 beat on both revenue ($193M vs $189.2M) and non-GAAP EPS ($0.28 vs $0.25), plus record adj. EBITDA ($25.8M) and margin expansion. Crucially, management raised FY26 guidance (revenue midpoint $747.5M and adj. EBITDA midpoint $93.5M vs consensus expectations), offsetting the expected oil & gas weakness with clear demand strength—driving a meaningfully positive next-day reaction versus the largely priced-in “reaffirm” base case.

Despite a >20% YoY jump in adjusted EBITDA (driven by Harsco Environmental) and cash flow improving, the quarter’s reported revenue ($187M) and adjusted EPS loss (-$0.63) were far below the thin consensus expectations (~$311M and -$0.31). Guidance was maintained (HE $170–180M; Rail loss $19–26M), so the reaction is driven mainly by the large headline/outcome misses rather than forward-looking changes.

Staking-driven fundamentals broadly landed in the expected “base-to-bull” range (revenue $15M vs $3M Q1; 230.5M gram; ~17% annualized yield), and the margin held ~95%. The main incremental negative was management caution on staking-yield durability plus additional legacy/stock-compensation charges, slightly lowering the bullish narrative versus what the market may have hoped on the call.

Q2 revenue modestly missed and, more importantly, adjusted EBITDA margin compressed ~430 bps to 17.2% and full-year guidance was cut (revenue to $925–945M and EBITDA to $150–170M) citing weaker-than-expected demand plus delays extending inorganic contribution. The only offset was the >500k smart-entry unit milestone, but segment weakness (commercial sheets/doors) dominated.

Q2 landed near the midpoint of expected revenue, while Adjusted EBITDA margin expanded to 11.2% (above the note’s ~10–11% implied consensus), supporting a modestly positive read-through. The main driver is balance-sheet/gearing optics: the $125M backstopped equity rights deal and raised WolfPack synergies likely help the 2H/2027 FCF narrative, but since Q2 revenue/guidance largely match expectations, reaction is only moderately positive rather than a large beat.

Standalone post-spin FY26 guidance (adj. EPS $6.73–6.89) appears broadly in line with the market’s recast range and is supported by strong Q2 CFS organic growth (+8.3%) and a raised CFS organic growth outlook (to 6–8%). However, margin commentary flags incremental H2 inflation pressure ($10–$15M) and CFS margins are held back by mix/new ramp-up, limiting upside and keeping EPS from being a clear beat versus expectations.

Adjusted EBITDA beat the ~$56–58M implied pre-print setup ($60.7M) with stronger Rockies/Mid-Con and improved realized prices. Guidance was tightened for FY adjusted EBITDA to $235–255M (midpoint $245M) and capex raised to $100–120M, which is consistent with the market’s Double E/FY build narrative rather than a credibility reset; buyback was small but not a major disappointment given the debt/dividend priority.

No published consensus/estimates existed pre-release, so surprise-vs-consensus is hard to quantify; however, the release largely confirms the expected sales pressure (-6% total; -11% LV; -10% FL) and reiterates ongoing litigation/casino delay risk. Margin cash flow improvements and Sequoia lease savings are positives, but the reported decline in EBITDA and gross margin (without payroll relief) plus the still-partial America closure in September tilt the tone toward downside.

Quarter benefitted from the expected realized-price tailwinds: production exceeded the high end of guidance and EBITDAX/free cash flow rose sequentially, while LOE was materially better than the full-year LOE midpoint (13% below). Offsets were the expected but still sizable hedge drag (~$55m net cash hedge losses) and rising caution on term-loan prepayment (limits balance-sheet upside timing).

Clinically, management reiterated multiple favorable efficacy/safety and enrollment acceleration (Ovation 3 ~0.5 pts/site/month), but the release re-highlighted a tight balance sheet—only $6.9M cash and an explicit need for additional capital—keeping solvency/dilution risk as the dominant overhang. Net: modestly supportive tone for the science, offset by funding/runway concerns, implying an approximately median-to-slightly-negative move.

While the company delivered strong margin improvement (biofuels and chemicals both to gross profit; revenue +120.7% YoY) and reported $34.3M cash with no revolver borrowings, the pre-release note lacked credible consensus/expectations for Q2 revenue/EPS and guidance direction/magnitude. The H2 45Z monetization ($22M gross proceeds) and the new $40M+ customer-funded capacity expansion are incremental positives versus the note’s watch items, offsetting uncertainty around how much was already priced.

Revenue of $24.3M was far below the ~$34.0M consensus bar, but the underlying demand/order engine was stronger than expected (Industrial Solutions + Gearing backlog up, book-to-bill 1.5x; orders surge in both segments). Management also kept guidance withdrawn through Q3, aligning with the note’s key expectation that guidance would remain absent until the Abilene wind-down ends, which likely caps upside despite improved operating momentum.

Revenue roughly matched the low $7–8M trough expectation, but losses worsened materially and liquidity tightened (only ~$0.9M cash; reliance on milestone-based restricted cash). Guidance pivots to cash-neutral/cash-positive only at mid-$20M (2027), and gross margin deteriorated further, reinforcing the bear case despite continued IntentKey growth.

This was primarily a milestone/cash-upgrade update rather than a meaningful earnings inflection. Reported cash ($201.1M) and the key ABS-201 interim PoC timing stayed consistent with the prior “2H 2026 / early 2027” expectations, limiting upside surprise; the main incremental item was the modeling/occupancy narrative rather than a new catalyst shift. Elevated R&D/SG&A supports a mild margin pressure backdrop, keeping reaction near median with slight downside skew given the name’s history.

Operational metrics were stronger than the note’s base case (same-location NOI +12% to $5.9M; RevPAS ~$225; higher utilization/parking), but revenue came in slightly below the note’s expected range and EPS details were not provided. FY26 guidance was reaffirmed (the note expected likely narrowing to the low end), which offsets some operational upside; overall, the stock reaction should be near-median given deal/IOI deadline timing rather than earnings alone.

Revenue came in below the Street ($383.3M vs ~$395–397M expected), and base business sales declined more than the note’s expectation of flat-to-slightly-down. However, adjusted EBITDA beat the note’s key bar (reported $60.4M vs the note’s ~$56–58M base case) with expanding margins, largely from higher-margin acquisitions and tariff refunds. Full-year guidance was reaffirmed in-line, leaving the market to focus on the mix/trajectory rather than a sustained earnings power reset.

Q2 revenue ($7.9M) and EPS (net income ~$0.1M; essentially far below a $0.008 EPS bar) came in well under the already-low consensus, but the bigger driver is guidance: management cut FY2026 revenue to $60M–$75M (midpoint ~$67.5M), far below both the company’s prior ~$125M guide and consensus (~$115M). While the DLA shipment timing and weak pricing were largely anticipated, the magnitude of the FY guide reduction and margin compression (to ~7% GM) should drive a downside reaction.

Revenue came in modestly above the thin consensus and, more importantly, the company raised both full-year revenue and year-end ARR guidance while showing a sharp Q2 adjusted EBITDA margin expansion (10.1%). eXpedite adoption also accelerated (100+ customers), offsetting the market’s margin-trough concerns tied to purchase-subscription mix.

Q2 revenue printed ~$14.9M, broadly consistent with the pre-release framing that looked for weakness/sequential decline but not a clear miss/beat; management reaffirmed FY26 revenue guidance $72–76M (H2-weighted) as expected. The notable upside was stronger gross margin (73%) and explicit GMP/scale execution color (permit imminent; one CDMO now in long-term contract talks), which likely offsets the lack of revenue upside and keeps the reaction near-median to slightly positive.

Fiscal 2026 results were strong, but the pre-release note framed Q4 as largely boxed in and highlighted FY2027 guidance—where management’s initial FY27 adjusted EPS/revenue and tax-rate normalization setup were broadly aligned with the expected range. The main differentiator is tone/operational progress (conversion/retention, assisted mix) and margin expansion, supporting a modestly positive reaction rather than a guidance shock.

Revenue came in modestly above the note’s ~$6.3M expectation, but margins were pressured by higher component/freight costs and shipment delays that pushed revenue out, leaving worse-than-expected adjusted EBITDA (–$0.6M vs –$0.05M modeled). Management reiterated the goal of positive adjusted EBITDA by Q4, so the market reaction likely stays mixed despite the top-line beat.

Revenue and gross margin came in comfortably above the pre-release setup, and adjusted EBITDA turned positive (also higher than what the EBITDA-to-net-loss math in the note implied). Most importantly, the company raised FY26 adjusted EBITDA guidance to $2–3M versus roughly breakeven expectations, though Q3 revenue guidance calls for YoY decline (partially expected as durable-goods comp/mix), limiting upside.

Q2 delivered a large revenue beat driven by both product momentum (~27k packs, +9% vs Q1) and meaningful ex-US milestones (~$3.8M). EPS was also materially better than the already-adjusted whisper, aided by sharply lower adjusted SG&A. Offsetting negatives: the company still characterized retail uptake as poor/limited and did not provide formal FY/Q3 revenue or opex ceilings—so the Street’s biggest uncertainty (runway/commitment) is only indirectly addressed via “more disciplined capital allocation.”

As expected for a pre-revenue quarter, revenue was effectively $0. The main surprise was EPS worsening due to the $200M upfront Tanabe payment flowing through the P&L (headline loss far more negative than the market had modeled as an expected accounting/timing noise). Guidance/cash runway was reaffirmed—cash supported funding into 2028—limiting downside beyond the initial EPS optics.

Q2 delivered a record $33.9M revenue (+29.9% YoY) versus $30.5M consensus, and—more importantly—raised FY26 adjusted EBITDA to $10.75–12.75M and gross margin to 53–55% while reaffirming revenue, indicating the profitability pivot is working. The main put (EBITDA phasing/weakness) was offset by strong subscription/subscriber growth and international momentum; Prime Day unit softness was noted but didn’t translate into a negative demand read or EBITDA disappointment.

Results and especially guidance improved versus the pre-print setup: Q2 revenue beat the thin ~$14.2M expectation, EPS loss was less bad than -$0.13 expected, and FY26 revenue guidance was raised to $270–310M (midpoint above the $225–300M range). Backlog growth and gross margin expansion further reinforce the “execution/2H cadence” thesis, limiting downside despite adjusted EBITDA loss widening.

Q2 revenue ($22.8M) and underlying RNS growth (21.3%) came in above the pre-release consensus ($22.6M), and—critically for the setup—the company raised FY2026 revenue ($99.5–$101.5M vs $99–$101M) along with improving adj. EBITDA and gross margin guidance. Despite the ongoing IGE PMA headwind, management provided a constructive path (SIR meeting in coming weeks; potential no full clock reset), supporting a mildly positive next-day reaction versus the note’s base/bear-weighted outlook.

Reported Q2 total revenue ($296.8M) comes in below the pre-release high/low consensus range (~$321–$330M), though adjusted profitability was solid: adj. EBITDA rose to $20.5M and SG&A improved to 74.1% of gross profit. Management’s demand commentary turned cautious (current-quarter same-store down low single digits) and refinancing/acquisition catalysts remain “nearing completion,” limiting upside; net effect looks modestly negative/near-neutral versus expectations.

Q2 results were modestly better on revenue (~$1.3M vs ~$1.25M consensus) and meaningfully stronger on gross margin (63.7% vs ~50–55% expected), but adjusted EBITDA improved only slightly while management declined to provide Q3 guidance (a key concern flagged in the preview) and there was no new quantified defense PO/strategy update.

Q2 revenue was essentially in line vs the Street ($3.10M vs $3.55M consensus, but the pre-release note flagged the stretched, 2H-heavy back-half math), and FY26 revenue guidance was reaffirmed $16–18M (inline vs ~$16.25M consensus). The main incremental positive was gross margin rebounding sequentially to 49% (though still below prior-year), partially offset by another negative demand/delayed sales-cycle tone and continued cash burn (6-month FCF about -$25.3M). Buyback activity was also a potential supportive governance signal, but not a clear beat to prior expectations given the bids were the dominant overhang.

Reported Q2 revenue ($452K) lands near the pre-release range implied by the $380–450K base case, and EPS comparisons are unhelpful given warrant/derivative noise noted in the preview; the bigger story is gross margin expansion (~61.5% vs ~38% prior-year) but the market’s key driver remains liquidity/equity-compliance risk. Guidance to Q3/Q4 implies a step-up in revenue versus the quarter, but the preview flagged that guidance was unlikely to be decisive versus solvency metrics and the report did not clarify the equity-compliance-plan status. Cash burn/working-capital use (cash $3.6M; operating cash use $5.3M; inventory up) is consistent with expectations, limiting upside.

Q2 revenue missed consensus ($7.7M vs $8.52M) and the quarter reinforced the supply-constrained catheter ramp (only ~dozen MAGIC-approved sites). Guidance was broadly maintained but Q3/Q4 recurring ($~$7M/$~$8M) and system ($~$3M each) sit slightly below the pre-release math/consensus trajectory, leaving less confidence in sustaining the previously emphasized H2 strength. Offsetting positives were strong MAGIC robotic catheter sequential growth (~270–300%) and a first U.S. GenesisX purchase announcement.

Consistent with expectations on key timeline (1H 2027 interim/FDA feedback) and no meaningful CMC critical-path shift, but the quarter’s EPS/net loss came in worse than the -$0.116 consensus. Positives included full dosing completion across REVEAL/ASPIRE and notably strong 12-month responder rates, partially offset by the new moderate Grade 2 neuropathy SAE in one REVEAL pivotal patient.

Revenue and gross margin confirm the pre-released ramp (limited incremental credit). The market will focus on liquidity/going-concern risk: cash remains very low ($1.2M) despite better Q2 operating cash burn, but first-half burn is worse and management avoided a clear sustained breakeven timing, making the overall setup skew downside versus the already-weak FY cash-flow expectations.

Revenue ($19.7M) and bookings ($21.8M) tracked below the pre-release yardstick (~$23.5M revenue, ~$25M bookings), consistent with the content-gap thesis—so the downside is largely expected. The call did, however, reinforce the key $11M deferred revenue shift to Q3 (supporting Q3 positioning) and showed margin improvement from the prior-year tax item plus a ~$1.5M/quarter ARK fee restructuring, which likely offsets part of the reaction.

Results were essentially in line on revenue and EPS versus the thin-stale consensus, but the key positive surprise was an adjusted EBITDA guidance raise (midpoint meaningfully above the pre-release expectation). Offsetting concerns were softer casino/gaming reported performance and the newly disclosed strategic review/divestiture optionality not fully offset by the tariff-adjusted numbers.

Q2 results beat the pre-release modeled setup on both top-line momentum and—most importantly—gross margin expansion (to ~75% vs ~48% prior-year), countering the margin-compression fears. Management reaffirmed ~100% FY26 revenue growth but added timing/Chile funding caveats; overall, the beat + margin relief should drive an above-median reaction, though guidance isn’t meaningfully upgraded.

Q2 handily beat the (restated) consensus on revenue ($260M vs $245.98M, +5.8%) and adjusted EPS (~$0.70 vs $0.53, +32%). More importantly, margins surged (19.8% EBITDA margin vs the note’s ~17% bar) and bookings hit an all-time high ($306M) while guidance was raised to $1.02-$1.04B (above the note’s $985M-$1.0B base case), driving a likely above-median positive reaction.

The key overhangs in the pre-release note—solvency/cash runway and non-committed LOIs—were confirmed or worsened: cash dropped to ~$5.6M (below the ~$9.5–10M straight-line red flag) and management added additional nonbinding LOIs/early-stage opportunities rather than committing orders. Operating loss/cash-burn deterioration signals reduced runway support, driving a modestly negative reaction after already-baked-in concerns.

Q2 results broadly matched what was expected given the quarter closed before the cyclospora outbreak; management reiterated full-year same-restaurant sales (4.5%-6.5%), restaurant-level margin (23.7%-24.3%), and Adj. EBITDA ($181-191M), limiting guidance-related upside/downside. The only tension vs. the note was that reported restaurant-level margin declined 60 bps on salmon/wage/delivery mix, but FY guidance was held.

Revenue of $1.5M was essentially in line with the pre-release framing (which modeled ~ $1.25–1.35M, but the note’s consensus bar was $1.50M), while EPS missed versus the note’s expected wider loss ($0.16–$0.18 vs reported $0.13). However, the release confirmed the key overhang—continued DOW funding delay—and disclosed very low cash ($0.2M) plus an explicit funding/ATM path, keeping liquidity/dilution risk front-and-center; margin also contracted.

Revenue (reported $5.8M) was close to the pre-release expectation range (~$6.8–$7.2M) but still slightly below; however the bigger negative surprise was Managed Services bookings falling to $4.5M (well below the $6.5M+ “needs to be healthy” threshold and the note’s $7.0–7.5M base expectation), alongside downside operating profitability (Adj. EBITDA -$0.4M vs +$1.3M prior year). EPS missed the thin consensus and cash draw continued, but margins held roughly steady.

The key deliverable (Q1 FY27 guide) came in above the pre-release yardstick: revenue midpoint ~$1.25B vs derived ~$1.15B+ consensus, and EPS guidance ($4.05–$4.35) implies an outcome well above the ~$3.55–$3.85 framing. Alongside record gross margin (50.4%) and operating margin expansion, the print should confirm pricing/supply improvements versus the supply-gated base case.

Revenue and EPS were broadly in line with the low-information consensus framework, and FY26 guidance was reaffirmed. The upside came from improved gross margin and more credible drone production/demand math (capacity scaling + demand > deliverables), but losses widened (and non-GAAP was pressured by bad debt), keeping the net reaction near median.

Q2 revenue of $3.5M is roughly in line with the pre-release $4.55M consensus on a narrowly watched, BARDA-driven quarter (small underperformance), while FY26 revenue guidance stays reiterated at ~$18.5M and is therefore not a new beat/miss. The key incremental detail was improved financing: higher reported cash ($14M) and an Avenue Capital tranche extension/drawdown, which offsets the weaker gross margin (31.6%) and helps keep the reaction near neutral to slightly negative given the market’s focus on guidance bridge and commercial order evidence beyond the P&L.

Revenue ($64K) came in above the stale $0.30M-directional expectation, while opex fell sharply to $3.4M and gross margin expanded to 60.9%. The key narrative catalysts—execution on licensing (first device licensee) and buyback ($3.2M)—were better than feared, partially offset by guidance being only sequential/lumpy and device licensee details remaining unspecified.

The release was largely about capital structure and regulatory/timeline language. Liquidity improved to ~$300M and debt was converted to equity with ~$170M warrant proceeds—largely in line with what the market was modeling after the Aug 10 run—limiting upside. However, the lower-900 MHz proposal was not included in the FCC final direct-to-device NPRM (a new negative vs what the preview framed as an open, time-sensitive upside catalyst), which likely offsets the otherwise supportive Safran partnership and keeps the expected next-day reaction near-median.

Q4 upside was largely already flagged by the July 21 pre-announcement (revenue near low end, margin reset), and management further confirmed strong order momentum (>$60B, backlog record). The main incremental positive was the magnitude of the gross margin/EPS beat (17.6% GM, $1.70 non-GAAP EPS) versus the still-stale Street EPS set; offsetting negatives were continued customer readiness delay in revenue timing and high concentration (one customer 28% of FY26 revenue). FY27 and Q1 guidance were broadly in line with the market setup (no clear guidance repricing).

As expected for a pre-revenue biotech, there was no revenue signal; the key variable (ALTITUDE-AD topline timing) was maintained as late 2026. Margin/run-rate improved (R&D down), but the cash/runway comment remains consistent with funding only into early 2027, keeping the financing overhang in place—slightly offsetting any positive tone.

Q2 revenue and adjusted OIBDA landed within guidance but slightly below the Street revenue number; however, local revenue outperformed sharply (48% vs. the already-strong consensus expectation). The offset is weaker national monetization yield (World Cup/film mix cited) and—most importantly—management paused dividend/repurchases to fund the Captivate deal, shifting near-term capital return expectations; no explicit Q3/Q4 guidance was provided, keeping the market focused on back-half trajectory.

Q2 revenue came in below the guidance midpoint (delay vs extension), and—critically—the Q3 guide is flat at $5.5M (implying H2 weakness) which undercuts the note’s expectation that Q3 revenue would support the high-end FY consensus. Offsetting positives were expanding gross margin to 46.8% and higher reported net cash (ATM-funded), but the guidance miss is the driver of a likely negative next-day reaction.

Revenue (and thus operating scale) came in above the thin consensus, and non-GAAP EBITDA loss improved more than the market’s low bar, but the headline loss was pressured by a one-time debt extinguishment. Guidance was reaffirmed at $46–50M revenue and $(30)–$(35)M adjusted EBITDA loss, matching expectations; the bigger swing factor (Anaphylm resubmission timing / Class 1 vs Class 2) was broadly consistent with the preview (on track by end of Q3).

Symbest revenue of $0.4M is directionally consistent with the pre-release “show me the units” setup (no clear beat vs the thin consensus), while cash/runway and the R&D/SNorth star narrative largely align. The key upside surprise is the trial readout detail (strong efficacy plus notably lower infection rate) and the fibrosis of the Phase 3 supports the launch timeline; the key downside surprise is cost/margin pressure with a sizable inventory reserve and unused capacity in COGS, which offsets the improving burn and keeps the market focused on execution rather than margin leverage.

On the desk’s model, revenue ($13.9M) is essentially in line, while adjusted EBITDA loss improved to about $5.8M (slightly better than the note’s -$5.2M directional path but not a clear operational “re-rate” given microcap noise). The key negative is cash burn: ending cash dropped to $10.1M versus ~$12.0M expected, increasing runway/financing risk; partially offset by management resolving the earlier margin packing inefficiency, but reported gross margin still fell to 27% (below the 29% expectation).

Q2 revenue and EPS materially beat the (already soft) consensus, driven by higher ElFabrio/Chiesi goods sales; however, management emphasized quarter-to-quarter lumpiness and flagged Chiesi inventory timing, and guidance appears reaffirmed/unchanged versus what the market already modeled for FY2026 H2 weighting—limiting upside and keeping reaction near-median.

Core inflection was narrative/catalyst-driven rather than earnings: PERFORMA Phase 3 enrollment scale and RECLAIM/AUD efficacy were already well telegraphed as upcoming. The key risk item for this event—cash runway through the 2029 MASH readout—was reaffirmed (cash $519M; funded through 2029), which was the market’s main concern, limiting downside surprise despite ongoing non-dilutive funding intent for AUD Phase 3.

TRMB beat Q2 revenue and EPS (also clearing the pre-set bar vs guide midpoint) and raised FY revenue (+$50M midpoint) and EPS (+$0.10) while delivering stronger margin (EBITDA +120 bps to 28.6%) and record organic ARR ($2.509B). Offset: Field Systems guidance was a notable headwind versus the pre-release “H2 conservatism” setup, as the company explicitly cut segment growth due to a white-label replacement/400–500 bps ARR headwind.

Q2 EPS ($0.25) beat consensus ($0.17) despite revenue/comp being broadly in line, but the major swing is guidance: management raised full-year adjusted operating income to $119–$139M while narrowing revenue and lowering the top end of comp guidance. The replatform drag and traffic softness remain, so the beat is partly offset by still-mixed demand quality.

The key upside was management raising FY26 adjusted EPS guidance to $5.25–$5.35 (above prior $5.15–$5.25) alongside higher gross margin guidance, consistent with the note’s tariff-relief upside but exceeding the degree implied by holding the range; incremental margin expansion and mostly stable Wrangler demand supported the raise. Overall reaction should be modestly positive given the market already anticipated tariff-related improvement and low-signal Q2 seasonality.

Commercial momentum (31% QoQ net product sales; 5,900 Rx / 5,000 starts) was broadly expected from the pre-print, but EPS came in below the tighter consensus bar and management offered no incremental guidance tightening—reaffirming only “>$1B in 2027” while asking investors to underwrite the patent timeline. Net: modestly negative reaction profile given the already-favorable setup and limited guidance uplift.

Revenue of $4.4M missed the ~$7.0M consensus and gross margin fell to 8.4%. More importantly, management cut FY26 revenue guidance to $20–23M after the delayed Water-for-Energy project, a guidance move beyond what was needed for the base case (while only a post-quarter $2.1M follow-on order was incremental positive).

Headline revenue/gains look broadly in line with the modeled ~$2M lease/amortization run-rate and noise around lumpy GAAP gains is already anticipated. Incremental positives were (1) clearer valuation framing ($1.40 vs FCC $2.50, with large remaining monetizable spectrum), (2) accelerating utility conversations and active opportunity set, and (3) supportive FCC/SpaceX-Lynk narrative alongside confidence on 10 MHz monetization (40% of counties cleared). Guidance was essentially maintained (next-quarter gains characterized as single-digit millions), so the reaction skews modestly positive rather than a large beat.

Revenue and profitability indicators (Adj. EBITDA back to breakeven; H2 >50% vs H1) largely met/cleared what the note’s base/bull scenarios framed, with the new “>50% H2 growth” and record-2027 narrative being broadly supportive. However, EPS materially missed (worse than consensus), tied to the ~$2.9M vessel charter cost exclusion/drag—likely a key overhang until clarified as one-time on the call.

Q4 operating results landed at the upper end of guidance with stronger-than-expected adjusted EBITDA (supportive of the already-anticipated FY27 inflection story), and FY27 adjusted EBITDA guidance ($2.125–$2.225B) is effectively modestly above the ~$2.10B bridge the market was watching. Offsets include lower EPS growth vs revenue/EBITDA and a noted diesel headwind, but overall the print de-risks demand/cost relief and keeps the margin/EBITDA trajectory intact, suggesting a roughly median-to-slightly-positive reaction.

Despite a large 45% YoY backlog rebound and improved sequential gross margin (+60 bps), Q2 revenue ($61.8M) and especially adjusted EPS ($0.15) were far below the pre-release expectation set around ~$65M revenue and ~$0.42 adj. EPS. Gross margin came in at 20.8% (below the expected ~21.5% and consistent with tariff/Big-3 runoff) and adjusted EBITDA dropped ~49%, overwhelming the positive backlog and cash-flow improvement; the company also signaled near-term margin pressure from newly acquired aerospace (~120 bps).

Q4 EPS of $3.07 is essentially in-line with the Street and the release largely confirms the preview’s “clearable company bar” narrative. The main incremental element is guidance: FY27 revenue/EPS were guided above the market-implied level in the preview (notably EPS at $12.60–$13.40), supported by accelerating July/August traffic and margin expansion (18% restaurant margin; +20 bps). With the market already positioned for a potential gap, this skews to a modestly positive but not outsized reaction.

Revenue came in essentially inline vs the pre-release base ($33.4M vs ~$32.7M est.), and margins look better (Q2 gross margin helped by SLS mix/profitability, with management reiterating a normalized SLS gross margin ~26%). The bigger swing factor vs the note is EPS/EBITDA vs the modeled range and whether SLS revenue weakness (10.1M vs 10.8M comp) was already the expected headwind; buybacks resuming is a positive relative to the note’s “credibility” watch item.

Q4 revenue of $196.3M beat the pre-release $184.7M consensus, driven by more Garden concerts (AOI swing to +$18.6M). Demand indicators (record Christmas Spectacular ticket sales; most concerts sold out) were broadly supportive, but weaker theater booking progress (~60% toward goal) is a tangible offset. EPS/guidance details weren’t provided in the call facts, limiting confidence in the exact price reaction direction beyond the revenue/AOI beats.

The key upside was guidance: FY26 revenue guidance was raised ~50% (to ~$15M) and cash-outlook improved, which the note flagged as the main asymmetry. Revenue also beat consensus for Q2 (lumpy ONR/Navy ramp) and the company added ~$50M of new military awards; partially offset by a still-large Q2 gross profit shortfall (gross profit only $0.37M) and a continued heavy net loss.

Q1 revenue ($16.1M) was slightly below the more realistic ~$16.8–17.5M bar but near the pre-release “stale consensus” level, while EPS/GaaP ($-0.05) underperformed the pre-release skew (near breakeven to -$0.01). EBITDA improved materially to $1.6M and contribution margin improved (positive), but the major risk remained guidance/AI monetization—no documented guidance raise was provided in the facts, leading to a modestly negative-to-neutral reaction given limited quarter upside vs expectations.

Revenue came in below the $21.23M consensus anchor ($19.3–19.4M) while consolidated adjusted EBITDA exceeded earlier expectations; however, Slacker’s margin was materially boosted by non-recurring stock-for-service and past-liability eliminations, raising durability concerns. PodcastOne posted record results and cash/equity improvements, but the lack of a consolidated high-quality earnings beat combined with a continued light quarter makes this more likely to be a modestly negative/only partially offset reaction.

The call largely de-risks regulatory timing (Shonin submission expected next quarter; FDA minutes supportive) versus the preview’s main near-term catalysts, but the enrollment tone stayed cautious ('resource-driven' with only four active sites) and the balance-sheet narrative (equity maintained for NASDAQ compliance, $5.4M cash) appears to align with the base case rather than the bull case of a surprise equity cushion. Overall, results/reveal are modestly supported with limited incremental upside.

While the call delivered strong de-risking commercialization/market-readiness commentary and reiterated a cash runway through 2027 (~in line with the note), the pivotal commercial swing factor—specific NDA timing tied to C-FORWARD—still implies a Q2 2027 submission and mid-2028 launch. With expectations already largely anchored on this setup (and guidance not meaningfully accelerated), the net reaction should be modestly positive/near-median rather than a re-rating beat.

Q4 results beat even the top-end of guidance (revenue and non-GAAP EPS). The bigger driver is FY27 guidance: revenue and EPS at the high end versus Street ($4.80 EPS target) supports a more bullish read-through, while management’s continued AI infrastructure framing remains a key upside catalyst. Negative offset: non-GAAP gross margin fell and management guided to slight further headwinds, capping upside.

Q4 printed a clear beat on both revenue ($2.05B vs ~$1.99B) and non-GAAP EPS ($1.74 vs ~$1.62), with margin tracking at 40.2% and demand/booking language reinforcing DC&C acceleration. The main swing vs expectations is Q1 FY27 guide: revenue midpoint $2.30B and EPS midpoint $1.95 both come in above the ~$2.15B/$1.86 effective street bar from the preview, while FY27-first-$3B framing and strong datacenter growth guidance add further upside.

Q2 results came in well ahead of the note’s “~$17.5–18.5M revenue / ~$(0.05) EPS” setup, showing strong Emrosi net revenue ($8.1M), higher prescriptions (~36k) and improving ASP with EBITDA turning positive. However, there was no mention of new formal FY26 guidance (the key binary), so the upside is tempered versus a guidance-driven re-rate.

Revenue was essentially inline vs the $14.5M consensus ($14.4M; slight miss). The meaningful disappointment was adjusted EBITDA dropping to ~$0.24M vs ~$0.6M implied by the pre-release math, alongside worsening losses and higher one-time/legal burden—this increases financing/cash-risk focus even though cash declined only moderately and no explicit numeric guidance was provided.

Q2 prints beat the pre-release yardstick (revenue slightly above consensus and adjusted EPS meaningfully above the $0.12 anchor) and gross margin exceeded the 29.8–30.0% outlook with sequential improvement. Most importantly, FY guidance was raised at the low end for comps and EBITDA/EPS (midpoints modestly above consensus), offset by the disclosed ~100bp Q3 cyclospora headwind and ongoing basket softness.

KOMZIFTI net product revenue of $9.1M and ~115 new starts (with ~60% prescriptions growth) exceeded the market’s key launch-quarter bar, indicating stronger-than-expected early commercial traction. Offsetting that, the company’s Q2 net loss widened due to higher SG&A, keeping EPS downside pressure, while formal guidance appears reiterated/unchanged versus the pre-release anchor—suggesting a modestly positive but not outsized reaction.

Revenue was already largely pre-announced (~$9M) so there was little upside surprise. The key deviation was fundamentals: gross margin was positive (~$7M) but cash ended at $8.2M (below the note’s ~$10–15M comfort range) and EPS losses/opex/dilution dynamics remain a concern; management also reaffirmed “each quarter better” milestones, providing limited incremental reassurance versus expectations.

Key regulatory items were broadly supportive versus the pre-note (PDUFA still October 30, late-cycle review completed, only one inspection observation addressed, and management signaled label negotiations in September). While the note expected “process updates” as likely, the reaffirmed on-track review posture plus cash runway into late Q1 2027 and the more favorable commercial differentiation framing likely drove a modest-to-positive reaction, not a full beat.

No reliable consensus numbers for revenue/EPS, but on the key modeled item (SaaS growth), Q2 came in at +4.2% YoY vs the note’s base-case expectation that results need to be nearer the +8%+ threshold to support the FY26 “double-digit” credibility. Guidance was reaffirmed, which limits upside, while worsening loss/adjusted EBITDA and an unfavorable margin/mix trend add downside pressure.

Revenue and hospital adoption came in stronger than the pre-release cash/burn-focused bar (Q2 revenue at $0.615M vs modeled ~$0.55M, and 20/50 hospitals now using vs the implied low-single digit incremental expectations). However, the operating spend jump drove a wider net loss and EPS worse than modeled, and the liquidity story is still delicate (cash ~ $7M; runway improved vs the bear red line of ~$5.5M, but still implies continued financing risk). Guidance was reaffirmed (FY $2M target stayed on track) and the biggest swing factor—going-concern/financing specifics—was not flagged as a surprise in the call.

Q2 results matched the pre-release build closely on total revenue (~$7.0M expected vs $7.3M reported) with the key upside—SPL revenue rising to $0.8M—already framed as a Casgevy-driven validation vector. Management reiterated FY2026 revenue guidance ($30–32M) with mid-70s gross margins expected in H2; gross margin did come in below year-ago (77% vs 82%), limiting upside.

Revenue was broadly in the expected sub-$1M range, but the key catalyst timing turned incrementally more cautious: topline data shifted to mid-September (vs the note’s ‘August/early September’ watch), while cash ($10.1M) implies a shorter runway (funding only into Q4) and losses widened with higher G&A/legal spend—together increasing financing/partnering urgency and the downside tilt into the next catalyst.

Despite an above-consensus backlog build and the Hanford H2C IDIQ headline that the market had already largely repriced, the quarter delivered a larger-than-expected EPS miss and a weak treatment revenue dynamic due to a customer-directed hold pushing revenue into 2H (with margin pressure). With no meaningful P&L upside to offset, reaction skews negative/mean-reverting after the pre-earnings re-rate.

Despite weak retention (NRR down to 90%) and sequential/per-customer declines, management reaffirmed FY26 revenue ($95–100M) and EBITDA ($21–25M) and raised gross margin guidance, which is the key priced-in hinge. The Q2 revenue and non-GAAP EPS also came in ahead of consensus, cushioning the negative demand signals.

Topline ($33.5M) beat the preview’s base-case (~$32.0M), and gross margin improved to 17% (above the preview’s ~16.2% base), but EPS was roughly in line (~$0.11 vs base ~$0.12) with operating income impacted by incentive compensation, and cash flow remained negative with a large working-capital build plus no tariff recoveries. Net: modestly positive but not a broad re-rating catalyst given profitability durability concerns.

On the numbers management reported, demand and margins were better than the pre-release bear framing (traffic effectively flat but best since Q1 2023; restaurant margin up 20 bps to 14.7%), but adjusted EBITDA was below the implied Q2 expectation in the note ($18.9M vs implied ~$21–22M) and marketing investment/lower profitability offset the improved operating margin. Importantly, full-year EBITDA and capex guidance was maintained ex the refranchising deals, which the note suggested could be a non-event if cleanly framed—so the guidance reset risk appears largely priced in, keeping the reaction near-median.

Revenue landed slightly below the model estimate, but operating EBITDA and the move back to GAAP profitability were better than what the note warned not to trade (EPS driven by non-cash items). The key refinancing/going-concern setup looked consistent with the bear/base narratives (only preliminary SP1 discussions; no committed refinancing), so the net reaction is likely mixed rather than sharply positive.

Revenue of $25.3M is right in the expected band (near the ~$24.1M consensus and within the ~$25.4M whisper range), but gross margin fell to 29% and Gen 3 timing is still contingent on regulatory approvals (no firm next-quarter launch). The quarter did, however, show improved operating cash burn ($3.7M vs $6.0M in Q1) while reiterating cash-flow-positive exiting 2026, which likely prevents a larger negative reaction.

No revenue and EPS is largely non-cash/FV-mark driven, so the actionable content is clinical/commercial timing. Compared with the preview, management delivered a more concrete operational update (75% enrollment with all sites active) and reinforced the 2H26-to-PMA timeline, plus added supportive market/clinical-tailwind points (updated 2027 U.S. procedure estimate and KDIGO accepting Nefamostat). Cash/runway/tranches language stayed consistent with the base case, implying a modestly positive net surprise and a near-median-to-above-median reaction.

Revenue strongly beat the pre-release ~$15.5M base case (Q2 net sales $28.5M) with strong ordering momentum (73 accounts, P&T uptake ~55–60%) and improved adult mix. EPS was largely non-comparable due to non-cash derivative effects (adjusted EPS near the deep-loss expectation per the note), so the reaction should be driven mainly by the revenue and commercial traction rather than headline earnings quality.

Quarterly numbers had little fundamental content vs the pre-release framework (pre-revenue/operating burn), and management mostly maintained the key ALPHA3 timeline. However, the call added constructive new specifics (site ramp to ~100 by year-end and strong MRD clearance/no hospitalizations narrative, plus ALLO-316 efficacy signal), partially offset by the market-sensitive item that interim EFS timing remains ~mid-2027 despite faster site activation.

Revenue came in below the ~$3.47M consensus anchor from the pre-release note (and below the ~$3.1M sequential expectation), while EPS (GAAP loss of $0.53) was broadly in line with the note’s rough anchor near -$0.21 (not a beat). Positives were customer diversification and the reiterated “no ATM” stance plus more detailed H2 deployment/pipeline framing (shorter sales cycle, FCC-certified ProPlus for 2H), but gross margin fell to 19% versus the note’s ~mid-30s implied level, creating an additional downside focus for the stock reaction.

With no reliable Street consensus, the key deltas versus the pre-release model are (1) much higher reported sales (+8% to $16.8M vs modeled ~$15.7M), (2) materially stronger gross margin (+290 bps to 25.6% vs modeled 24.0%), and (3) a sharp GAAP EPS reversal—though tariff-related adjustments and refunds meaningfully boost earnings. Offsetting the positives, management cut the quarterly dividend (to ~4% yield), which is a negative versus the note’s expectation of $0.08 staying and focuses attention on cash allocation away from shareholders.

Results showed an earnings power inflection (2nd straight GAAP profit, Adj. EBITDA +>2x YoY) alongside a meaningful gross-margin target confirmation (24% this quarter) and, most importantly, an upside guidance raise to 14%-16% from 10%-12%—above the market already pinned near the top of the prior range. Upside is concentrated in the guidance/margin validation rather than revenue alone, warranting a moderately positive repricing.

Q2 revenue ($23.2M) and licensing ($14.1M) cleared the key bar versus the pre-release hurdle (~$21.5M consensus and ~$19.8M guide floor), and profitability was far stronger (adj. EBITDA $11.4M; gross margin 73%). However, management guided H2 adj. EBITDA to $6M–$10M (a step-down), and also signaled conservative licensing assumptions via more rev-share terms, tempering upside.

Continuing-ops revenue (~$2.0M) and EPS loss (~$0.20) were broadly in line with the note’s low-expectations setup, but the release underdelivered on the key forward-looking metrics: orders (~$1.2M) and backlog ($3.9M) fell below the note’s ~$4.0–5.5M base case and were further threatened by the customer’s Chapter 11 filing. Balance-sheet cash rose and gross margin improved (16.8%), which offsets, but demand tone remained weak and no capital-allocation upside was announced.

Revenue and gross margin were already largely telegraphed by the July 30 pre-release (inline on revenue), but the magnitude/quality of losses improved versus the market’s low EPS noise: GAAP loss was driven by convertible accounting that appears largely non-cash, while Adjusted EBITDA improved to near breakeven. Bookings of $4.9M partially offset the backlog decline, and management’s acquisition narrative improved, reducing downside dispersion for the post-withheld items.

Q2 revenue was essentially flat ($0.961M) and EPS loss widened, versus a pre-release setup that already expected a double miss, but the going-concern disclosure and margin deterioration make the balance-sheet risk feel more acute than “priced in.” Product revenue remains explicitly lumpy/no recurring ramp, reinforcing the dilution/capital-solution overhang.

Revenue of $7.8M missed the already-stale but still-likely-relevant $9.90M consensus (and is directionally worse than the note’s base-case range). Liquidity tightened materially ($0.5M cash) and adjusted EBITDA loss widened, while gross margin softened—offset only partially by non-DSP growth and ~80% retention. With covenants still in play, the market likely leans bearish near-term absent clear refinancing/extension updates.

Q2 results and—more importantly—full-year guidance were upgraded (sales decline narrowed to -3% to -5% and adjusted op margin to 4%–6%), plus gross margin expanded to 62.4% with strong wholesale/traditional watch growth. The note expected guidance risk to drive the move; the raised guide plus stronger margin/wholesale tone likely drove a clearly positive but not extreme reaction.

Q2 printed near the top end of the already-expected range, with non-GAAP EPS and operating loss landing at the favorable end of guide; however, smart eyewear is explicitly guided to negative gross margin through 2026 and the Q3 revenue guide ($9–10M) remains below what’s needed to comfortably sustain FY26 consensus, keeping the story more “timing-dependent” than a clear Q3 beat. The release also improved Zone 1 dicing yield to 84% (a positive), but that was partly offset by gross margin pressure (14.4% GAAP / 19.9% non-GAAP) and ongoing margin drag guidance.

Q2 broadband revenue and EPS beat the already narrow/near-prepaid range, but the bigger positive surprise was the FY26 broadband revenue guidance raise to a higher midpoint (+~5% vs prior midpoint, and above consensus). Management also guided gross margins at ~51–52% despite memory-cost headwinds, improving the 2H bridge versus the note’s implied ~48.8% risk, with backlog staying record-high and book-to-bill well above 1.0.

Quarter’s core economics improved (adj. gross profit +20% QoQ to $1.2M; staking/yield enhancement growth), and management reiterated FY26 adjusted gross profit $5–7M with further Opex cuts—offset by disclosed DeFi monetization revenue pressure from the USDH→USDC transition (-36%) and wind-down of deployments. Since the key FY guidance matched what the note expected and most upside is token-price mark-related, the market reaction should be modestly positive rather than a major repricing.

Operationally, Q3 comps (-1.1%) and restaurant-level margin (17.6% vs prior 17.9%) tracked the note’s flat/pressure framework; FY26 adj. EBITDA guidance was held essentially within the $225–235M range (now $225–230M). The two new negative items were the margin/Chicago drag worsening and franchise margin/bad-debt step-down. The main positive was adjusted EBITDA rising to $61.2M and the clearer refinancing/leverage improvement (net debt/EBITDA 6.3x). Overall, with stub-leverage guidance still broadly intact, reaction skewed slightly below median but not sharply negative.
