Ahead of the note on margins (48.6% vs ~45.8% modeled) and cost/markdown discipline (regular-price shift, lower markdown sales), plus adjusted EBITDA at $1.0M clears the explicit +$0.5M bar. Offsets include revenue/orders down 17% YoY (we modeled ~-6.8%), return rates described as higher, and the stockholders’ equity listing risk backdrop remains—so net reaction skews roughly neutral-to-slightly positive.

Q3 missed on sales (-8.4% to $458.5M) with a large gross margin contraction (-310 bps) and adjusted EBITDA well below the ~$78–82M implied consensus. More importantly, the company withdrew full-year FY2026 sales and adj. EBITDA guidance amid weak peak-season traffic and balance-sheet/strategic-alternatives language, which was only partially anticipated (capital-structure risk was in focus from prior reporting, but the outright guidance withdrawal is the incremental negative).

Q2 revenue of $11.0M missed the $11.20M consensus from the pre-release note (inline cost story, but revenue still not fully stabilized). However, Q3 guidance revenue ($16.0–$16.5M) and adj. EBITDA ($2.3–$2.5M) exceeded the note’s ~$15M run-rate framing, while the cash decline was a negative check vs the higher-quality EBITDA narrative.

Management reiterated key NRC timing (EA Q1’27, safety Q3’27, H2’27 construction start) consistent with the pre-release framing. While liquidity was strong, operating expense growth widened the quarterly net loss more than the prior-year comparison implies and—critically—the STS revenue contributed only ~$0.2M to Nano post-close, providing no clear uplift versus what the note modeled. With limited clear upside catalysts beyond the reaffirmed schedule, reaction is likely slightly negative/near-median.

The quarter’s core earnings power deteriorated sharply (adj. EBITDA -85%, 1.7% margin) consistent with post-Movies operating leverage risk, but full-year guidance was lowered and explicitly framed as no near-term growth. That guidance downgrade is the key incremental negative versus the pre-release setup, driving a likely below-median stock reaction.

Revenue came in meaningfully above the loose $9.44M consensus anchor (and above the pre-release base expectations), while adjusted EBITDA improved (less negative) and management reaffirmed the key exit-run-rate framework ($42–46M annualized revenue; $4–6M adj. EBITDA). EPS remains a low-signal GAAP line, so the setup was already guidance-centric; with guidance maintained, the upside reaction is likely modest versus the concentrated expectation already priced into shares ahead of the print.

Reported Q2 showed record revenue and strong adj EPS/adj EBITDA, and P&S gross margin continued expanding (13th consecutive). However, guidance appears reaffirmed/inline to the note and management flagged an input-cost-driven risk to gross margin plus nonrecurring cash drag in Q2—limiting upside versus what the market already anchored on.

Q2 results largely matched the thin consensus backdrop (reaffirmed FY26 revenue guide). The key new datapoints were (1) contracted backlog rising to >85% (a positive versus the note’s H2-risk framework), partially offset by a sharp non-GAAP gross margin drop to 38% from 52% (raising execution/quality concerns), making the net reaction roughly median.

The micro-cap’s reported revenue and EPS remain in the noise versus an already “early commercialization / revenue miss” setup, so the main incremental signal is operational: payer conversations expanded to 20+ states and a 4th partnership launched (modest positive). Offsetting items—CE marking pushed into Q4 and net loss widening with higher opex—are likely negative/attenuate the balance-sheet narrative, resulting in a slightly below-median reaction.

Q2 revenue missed the derived street range (battery resale at $0.3M vs $~5M expectations) but profitability and cash improved (adj. EBITDA +6M, OCF breakeven). Full-year guidance was reaffirmed, limiting upside vs the market’s already-negative revenue expectations; the net read is slightly negative to modestly mixed.

The key market expectation was holding the near-term Delta/first commercial milestone; the company delayed the first commercial spaceflight to Feb 2027 (timeline slip) which is a meaningful negative surprise versus the pre-release scenario framing. Liquidity was still stronger than the note’s rough cash runway band (raised $134M and ended Q2 with $286M cash/securities), and upside demand/monetization improved via an oversubscribed $750k tranche (+$50M) and a plan for higher-price tranches. Net: more weight on the milestone delay and higher Q3 spend (FCF guided -$95 to -100M) driving a slightly negative/near-median reaction despite cash support.

Operating lines were broadly consistent with the pre-release setup (revenue decline and cost cuts delivering better Adj. EBITDA), but the release added an incremental positive via a large GAAP debt-restructuring gain (~$91.8M) and confirmed annualized savings. Offsetting negatives were weaker-than-ideal demand mix within same-station (national down sharply; agency down), limiting conviction that stabilization is accelerating.

Revenue landed at the high end of the already pre-announced/expected ~$90M+ range and management emphasized no distributor/inventory build while EVO+ gained mix and pricing held—supportive demand signals. The biggest potential market driver per the pre-release note was FY guidance/margin durability, which is not specified in the facts provided here, so reaction is assessed as roughly median.

Q2 revenue of $17.8M was essentially inline with the low end of the $17.8–18.2M consensus range, and EPS/net loss did not meaningfully beat expectations given the pre-release EPS dispersion/cleanliness issues. The main upside was a higher-than-prior gross margin (18% vs 17% in Q1) and $2.1M operating cash flow, while management reaffirmed FY2026 guidance (no action vs consensus), keeping the overall reaction near-median.

Q4 EPS ($1.32) beat guidance despite a $0.05 tax headwind, and FY27 EPS guidance ($7.80–$7.90) is above the ~$7.45–$7.50 consensus/amplify range in the pre-release note. Margin expansion (gross +180 bps; operating >23%) and strong new-customer acquisition support the beat; no offsetting negative surprises were flagged.

Core market focus was the call/catalyst framework (pro forma cash/runway, UTEBSI availability timing, and SP001 Phase II start). Management delivered runway extension into 2H29 and reiterated/kept SP001 Phase II starting Q2’27, aligning with the note. However, Q2 loss/operating burn was worse than the note’s modeled EPS range and reiterated no meaningful Q2 collaboration/approval-linked milestone revenue, so the P&L provided incremental downside into an already-risked setup.

Revenue modestly beat the ~$32.19M setup, but the core tape-driver was solvency/financing. Cash ended at $65.4M and operations are only funded into September 2026, with the Sep 10 $15.8M payment creating an imminent covenant-default risk if no waiver/financing is secured—more urgent than the note’s base case. Positively, FDA written feedback suggests SVR35 is a reasonably likely OS surrogate and supports the August sNDA submission, but guidance was reaffirmed and no new financing was disclosed, keeping the net reaction near-median/choppy.

Operating cash/going-concern risk and store trajectory were the core pre-release drivers; however, reported Q2 revenue ($2.9M) sits toward the lower end of the note’s base range, and Adjusted EBITDA and operating loss worsened despite gross loss narrowing. Management still points to ~5,000 stores by year-end but admits slower-than-planned margin improvement and customer churn from pricing, which likely reinforces dilution/liquidity concerns—more downside than a clean beat outcome, but not an extreme surprise given the note’s framing.

Revenue of $11.4M missed the ~$12.2M consensus, but the bigger scrutiny point was operational conversion; management’s shift to anchor on completed patients plus two cancelled biopsies and partial batch failures suggests only modest clarity versus what was already expected from the biopsy-to-treatment funnel. No guidance action or explicit profitability timeline change was provided in the facts given, keeping the likely reaction near median. Option market implied a ~14.8% absolute move, consistent with a limited surprise.

As expected for a pre-revenue clinical company, revenue remains effectively zero and the quarter’s EPS/net loss is largely noise around higher R&D. The key story—EMA/Phase 3 milestone cadence and any NDA timing update—did not provide the binary “submission-confirmed” catalyst emphasized in the preview; management reiterated Phase 3 site openings with first dosing late 2026/early 2027 and kept the NDA mid/late-6-month 2027 window, so the market reaction should be modestly mixed-to-neutral.

Revenue was $1.8M vs ~$2.0M guidance-implied (and below $2.30M consensus), and EPS loss slightly worsened; while gross margin improved to 13% and GPO/pipeline commentary was constructive, the biggest stock driver (Gen 2 timing) shifted later (now likely Q4), and the cash figure at 6/30 excludes the new financing—together likely keep the reaction only mildly below-median despite reaffirmed CY2026/CY2027 revenue targets.

Q2 EPS came in meaningfully above the pre-release consensus while gross margin expanded more than expected, and full-year gross margin and operating margin guidance were raised. The main offset is that management guided to a ~600 bps drag in 2026 U.S. drinkware growth (U.S. Drinkware flat in Q2), keeping the reaction only moderately positive versus a bigger upside that a demand/volume acceleration would imply.
